author: winter oak
title: A message from dreamland
content:
by Paul Cudenec, who reads the article

here


I had a couple of vivid and, I think, significant dreams the other night.


In the first of these my (deceased) parents turned up at my home bearing ancient suitcases and chests apparently full of my possessions. They looked very familiar and it seemed as if I knew what was inside each of them.


I felt I had to accept these items, even though I did not really have the free space – I managed to stuff one of them under my bed. I was left with the impression of being encumbered and cluttered, overwhelmed with

stuff

.


On awakening, my first reaction was that this was about the inter-generational mental baggage that is handed down to us all by our families.


I thought of a remark someone had made to me about the danger that the attitudes of our ancestors – a subject I had just

written about

 – might actually represent a

barrier

 to our direct individual connection to the Whole.


It was far too early to get up and so I went through a mental exercise of opening up each of these old suitcases in turn, sifting through the contents to check that there was nothing of importance, and then throwing everything into a skip outside.


Having achieved this to my satisfaction, I realised that there was probably a lot more in my own head that was responsible for this sensation of being cluttered and blocked.


I thought of what Malidoma Patrice Somé said, as cited in the aforementioned article, about his Western education preventing him from fully accessing traditional shamanic knowledge and I had to admit to myself how much my mind was full of incoming

information

,

news

 and

detail

.


When I slipped back into dreamland I found myself looking at a terrible landscape. It was the countryside – with no buildings in sight – but a

devastated, unrecognisable countryside

.


It had lost all aesthetic charm and was even

ugly

. Tree stumps were everywhere around. The distant hills were planted with row upon straight row of commercially lucrative pines and even the stunted and hacked-about oaks nearby were in a mechanical line stretching away from me, rather than in an organic copse.


I was surprised by a terrible roaring sound to my left and turned to see flames bursting up into the sky behind some other trees. Alongside, I noticed a drilling rig and other unidentifiable industrial structures.


A small girl-child had materialised in my arms and, as we looked out at this hideous scene, I said to her: “Oh my god, they really want to do this to us!”


I knew at this point that the people behind this desecration of nature did not so much

not care

 about the harm they were causing in their own self-interest, but that they actually took a

demonic delight

 in destroying all that is good and beautiful, all that means most to

us

.


A small boy was now holding my hand, as well, and I said to the little ones: “We’ve got to stop them!”. Suddenly aware that it seemed a bit too late for that, I added: “We have to go back in time and do everything we can. With love in our hearts!”


We stepped through the portal and I woke up in 2026. I am getting on a bit now, but those children have their whole lives ahead of them.

author: Poetry Collection
title: Remembering That Day (Revised) by TJ Hamilton
content:
Pale days had long begun to stretch out


Until an effigy in motion forgot


About weeks and hours and better days


Without the tedious dinners for one.


The wife failed to see, as wives often do,


Frailties writ large across a husband’s heart,


Or maybe she’d believed since a little girl


In her man would beat a heart of steel.


Meanwhile,


To an unsouled effigy


It would all have been the same


To her, to me, and to all the others.


I might have persisted a while longer,


If I hadn’t had to decide,


How best to escape


The confusion of being a man.


Odysseus sacrificed to souls grown pale,


Bored with life in the world to come,


A drop of blood, an offering of life.


What else is an effigy to do?


* * *


Using “effigy” to represent depersonalization, and in this case depersonalization as a prelude to cutting my wrists, is courtesy of “Tranz” by Gorillaz.

author: Mag
title: Die Form des Wirtschaftens ändern: Mit dem Sozialstaatsprinzip zu Vergesellschaftungen
content:
Dossier


„

… Vergesellschaftungen sind nicht mehr eine abstrakte Angelegenheit, ihre Notwendigkeit wird immer auffälliger. (…) Mit der Initiative »Deutsche Wohnen enteignen« in Berlin, die die Vergesellschaftung großer Wohnungsunternehmen erreichen will, wurden Vergesellschaftungen erstmals zu einem realistischen Szenario in der Politik. Die Corona-Krise zeigt, dass insbesondere im Gesundheitssektor ebenfalls über Vergesellschaftungen nachzudenken ist, denn der Markt regelt jedenfalls nicht, dass die Bedürfnisse befriedigt werden können. Wohlgemerkt, Vergesellschaftungen, nicht Enteignungen. (…) Wenn über Vergesellschaftungen gesprochen wird, dann geht es um die Erfüllung des Sozialstaatsgedankens des Grundgesetzes. Nicht alles kann oder sollte vergesellschaftet werden, aber wenn es um die Daseinsvorsorge geht und der Markt nachweislich keine Lösung bietet, müssen sie thematisiert werden…“

Artikel von Halina Wawzyniak aus PROKLA 199 vom Juni 2020


 – siehe weiter daraus und mehr dazu:


Offener Brief an die Bundesregierung: Unsere offene Gesellschaft braucht ein offenes Grundgesetz – Gegen die bundesgesetzliche Sperrung des Artikels 15 GG


„

Anfang Juli kündigte die Bundesregierung ein Gesetz an, das den Ländern die Kompetenz zur Vergesellschaftung privater Wohnungsbestände entziehen soll. Seit dem Wahlsieg der Linken in Berlin soll dieser Plan beschleunigt werden – er zielt direkt auf den Berliner Vergesellschaftungs-Volksentscheid von 2021 und soll dessen Umsetzung verhindern. Wir, die Unterzeichnenden, fordern die Bundesregierung und den Bundestag auf, Artikel 15 nicht durch ein Sperrgesetz auszuhebeln. Unabhängig von der inhaltlichen Position: Die Frage der Vergesellschaftung muss im demokratischen Prozess entschieden werden – ein Sperrgesetz verhindert genau das. Es wäre verfassungswidrig, widerspräche dem Gründungskonsens von 1949 und missachtete den Bevölkerungswillen

…“

Offener Brief auf communia.de

 


Die Argumentation lautet: Ein Sperrgesetz gegen Vergesellschaftung wäre verfassungswidrig, missachtet den Gründungskonsens des Grundgesetzes und den Willen der Bürger*innen des Volksentscheid von 2021 – siehe auch das Berlin-Dossier:

Gegen Mietpreisexplosion die Deutsche Wohnen enteignen: Ein guter Anfang


Soziologe Urban betont das Recht auf Vergesellschaftung


„

Gewerkschaftler und Soziologe Hans-Jürgen Urban hat das Recht auf Vergesellschaftung von Wohnraum verteidigt. Die Attacken aus Bayern auf die Berliner Koalitionspläne trügen autoritäre Züge. Das Grundgesetz sehe diese Möglichkeit ausdrücklich vor

.“

Audio des Interviews von Josephine Schulz vom 24. Oktober 2026 im Deutschlandfunk

 


Vergesellschaften – der letzte Einwand. Ökonomen warnen vor einem Vertrauensverlust der Investoren. Was ist damit gemeint?


„…

Bemerkenswert ist, wer sich hier gegenübersteht. IW und IfW argumentieren weniger als Vertreter der »Wirtschaft« oder der »Arbeitgeber«, sondern schlicht als Vertreter des Eigentums, und zwar des Eigentums an jenen Dingen, die die ganze Gesellschaft braucht: Wohnungen, Büros, Fabriken. Auf der anderen Seite steht das IMK als Vertreter der Lohnabhängigen, also der Nicht-Eigentümer. Die eine Seite repräsentiert jene, die von ihrer Arbeit – dem Lohn – leben. Die andere Seite jene, die von ihrem Eigentum – Miete, Zins, Dividenden – leben, also von der Arbeit der anderen. Der Reichtum der einen – teure Immobilien, hohe Aktienkurse, steigende Preise – ist die Armut der anderen.


Dass dieses Verhältnis Bestand hat, darin besteht letztlich das »Investorenvertrauen«, das eine Vergesellschaftung zu beschädigen droht. Nun könnte einem dieses Vertrauen der Eigentümer herzlich egal sein – wäre von ihm nicht alles abhängig im herrschenden System. Denn die erfolgreiche Investition, also die Kapitalrendite, ist die Quelle nicht nur für Gewinne, sondern auch für Arbeitsplätze, für Lohneinkommen, fürs Wachstum und damit auch für die Einnahmen des Staates, die die Basis seiner Verschuldungsfähigkeit bilden.


Insofern ist die Warnung vor Kapitalflucht und steigenden Zinsen nicht trivial. Sie verweist auf ein reales Problem bei dem Bemühen, die »Bezahlbarkeit« des Lebens für die breite Masse zu sichern und gleichzeitig die Eigentümer nicht zu verschrecken. Das IMK hält sich hier bedeckt: Es nennt einen Vertrauensverlust der Investoren im Zuge einer Vergesellschaftung zwar »theoretisch plausibel«. Praktisch aber sei das Ausmaß dieses Verlustes und seine Folgen »weitgehend offen«. Was aber, wenn …

author: Novara Media
title: The New Right Is Obsessed With AI, Israel and the Apocalypse
content:
In Brighton, for a special recording of Downstream IRL, Ash Sarkar sat down with Naomi Klein, and organiser, writer and co-founder of the Debt Collective, Astra Taylor. They gathered to discuss their new book, End Times Fascism: And the Fight for the Living World. 


An apocalyptic alliance of religious fundamentalists, billionaire Silicon Valley tech kings and ethno-nationalists is gathering momentum. They aren’t just exploiting collapse, they’re provoking and accelerating it, whilst protecting themselves from the fallout. The world’s fate is increasingly in the hands of men who are ambivalent about its survival and betting money on the end.


Already, anger at the building of data centres is cutting across left and right, in a way that climate politics rarely has – but how do we make sure that anger is heard? How do we separate necessary alarm from fatalism? And what can we prepare for the impending AI crash?

author: Unknown
title: Эррико Малатеста - Наконец-то! Что такое "диктатура пролетариата"
content:
Автор

: Эррико Малатеста

Название

: Наконец-то! Что такое "диктатура пролетариата"

Дата

: 28 сентября 1920

Источник

: Umanità Nova, год 1-й, №187


НАКОНЕЦ-ТО!

Что такое "диктатура пролетариата"


 Наконец-то появился тот, кто говорит ясно!


 До сих пор, когда мы говорили, что то, что социалисты называют

диктатурой пролетариата

, на самом деле есть не что иное, как диктатура некоторых людей, которые с поддержкой партии становятся над пролетариатом и навязывают себя ему, нас за это называли чуть ли не клеветниками.


 Вопреки всякой вероятности и всем установленным фактам утверждалось, что в России разрешена та квадратура круга, которой было бы правительство, действительно представляющее интересы и волю управляемых.


 Соответственно, Москва стала Меккой пролетариата: оттуда исходил свет, а вместе со светом – и категорические приказы относительно идей, которых должны придерживаться, и линии поведения, которой должны держаться те, кто с разрешения вышестоящих хотел называть себя коммунистами.


 Вследствие этого изумительного открытия, сделанного в России, – правительства, созданного по образу народа и для блага народа (или пролетариата, как угодно называть), – всё, что приходило из России, казалось обладающим чудотворной силой; и достаточно было назвать по-русски

советом

 любое собрание или комитет, чтобы он был возведён в верховный фактор революции.


 Но вот очарование разрушено.


 На этот раз не мы раскрываем секрет: мы, анархисты, злоязычные и непочтительные по убеждению. На этот раз это официальная газета Итальянской социалистической партии, до сих пор наиболее авторитетный орган московского слова.


 Это

Avanti!

 от 20-го числа текущего месяца, которая говорит:


 «....

В России при советском режиме Партия действительно направляет всю политику Государства, и вся общественная деятельность как отдельных лиц, так и коллективов подчинена решениям Партии, так что

 В САМОМ ДЕЛЕ ДИКТАТУРА ПРОЛЕТАРИАТА ЕСТЬ ДИКТАТУРА ПАРТИИ И, СЛЕДОВАТЕЛЬНО, САМОГО ЦЕНТРАЛЬНОГО КОМИТЕТА».


 Итак, теперь мы знаем, чего нам следует ожидать: диктатуры Руководящего органа Социалистической партии, или диктатуры нарождающейся Коммунистической партии, или даже диктатуры Д'Арагона и компании!


 Но руководители Социалистической партии, претендующие ввести Диктатуру, должны понять, что это, по крайней мере в Италии, невозможно: невозможно, потому что есть мы, анархисты и синдикалисты.


 Если бы мы находились в том же соотношении сил с социалистами, в каком, возможно, оказались наши товарищи в России, дело было бы простым: диктаторы избавились бы от нас средствами, дорогими всем диктатурам, – виселицами и тюрьмами, – и шли бы вперёд, пока не были бы свергнуты революцией или реакцией.


 Но мы уже сила, с которой необходимо считаться, и мы быстро развиваемся, чему благоприятствуют обстоятельства и то, что

Avanti!

 называет

необузданным темпераментом трудящихся масс

. И мы твёрдо решили не подчиняться.


 Не то чтобы мы верили, что массы всегда правы и что мы хотим всегда следовать за массами в их изменчивых настроениях. У нас есть программа, идеал, который мы хотим привести к победе, и поэтому мы отличаемся от массы, – мы люди определенного направления. Мы хотим воздействовать на массу, подталкивать её по пути, который считаем лучшим; но поскольку наша цель – освобождение, а не господство, мы хотим приучать массы к свободной инициативе и свободному действию.


 Мы верим, что свобода учит свободе и солидарности, и поэтому питаем отвращение к любому авторитарному устройству – как в обществе в целом, так и в любой отдельной партии или объединении.


 Социалисты хотели бы подготовить народ к свободе посредством власти.


 Но если бы, по предположению, которое мы отвергаем, было верно, что для торжества революции и устройства нового общества необходимо сосредоточить в немногих руках государственную власть, если бы было верно, что кто-то обязательно должен командовать, – тогда, пусть социалисты хорошенько поймут, – командовать хотели бы мы и не подчинились бы, разве что силой, командованию того, кто, по нашему мнению, заблуждается.


 Следствием чего было бы то, что революция, совершённая по авторитарным меркам и с диктаторскими целями, неизбежно привела бы в Италии к войне между одними революционерами и другими.


 Этого не хотели бы мы; этого не должны хотеть социалисты.


 Поэтому, оставив в стороне теории и судя о вещах реалистично, социалистам следовало бы отказаться от всяких диктаторских притязаний и принять либертарную …

author: Guerre de Classe
title: Towards the Hot Autumn 2026!
content:
Occupations of schools and squares, confrontations with police, strikes, blockades of roads and ports, burning State buildings, lootings… In France, in Belgium, in Spain, in Albania, in Argentina… in Italy…

Occupations of schools and squares, confrontations with police, strikes, blockades of roads and ports, burning State buildings, lootings… In France, in Belgium, in Spain, in Albania, in Argentina… in Italy…

High school students, university students, teachers, steel workers, dockers, farm workers, inhabitants of suburbs and “popular housing” – in short the working class – are revolting against this shitty capitalist reality!

The global Capital and its State can’t bring us anything else than always accelerating misery, life of exploitation and alienation or death.

A perspective it has for us is to be a cannon fodder in the capitalist war or to drain our life force “on the home front”. And if we are lucky not to live in the war zone and our limbs are not teared off by the killer drones, there is still a climate catastrophe, pollution and toxic food, poverty, prisons, state control, militarization, digital slavery…

Now the ruling class is starting to panic – they are afraid that we will overcome the categories to which they locked us in – students, workers, pensioners, unemployed, men or women, “Italians”, “French” or “Albanians”, white or black, local or immigrants, “Western” or “Eastern”… they are afraid that we realize that we have common class interests as proletarians across all the borders and categories. And on the contrary, we have opposing class interests to them, even if they happen to look the same or speak the same language.

They are afraid of ghosts of May 1968, the Hot Autumn in Italy of 1969-70, the Movement of ‘77, uprising in Albania in 97, the “Arab Spring”, the “Yellow Vests”, the “One Piece uprising” of 2025…

Their cops and thugs attack us and to repress our movement, but we are not afraid! On the contrary we pass into a counter-attack!

Their trade unions try to pacify our struggle, pretending that they can order us back to work, but we do not obey!

Their political parties try to fool us to give up our own class emancipation and let them “represent us”, but we spit on democracy! We do not trust these snake-oil merchants regardless if they are “right-wing”, “left-wing” or even pretending to be “communists” (by which they mean red painted capitalism in the style of Lenin, Mao or Hoxha)!

Their propagandists on social media or in TV try to misrepresent our interests and pit us against each other, but we laugh into their faces!

We inspire each other despite the national borders imposed on us by our class enemies. Let’s take it a step further and let’s organize ourselves internationally against all nation states! Against the State!!!

Let’s turn the schools, factories, offices, barracks, prisons, streets, squares and neighborhoods of every city into a battleground between us who struggle for a revolutionary change and them who want to preserve the World of exploitation!

Against the capitalist war and the capitalist peace – towards the global uprising for communism!

Source: https://tridnivalka2026.wordpress.com/2026/10/20/towards-the-hot-autumn-2026/ PDF: https://tridnivalka2026.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/towards-the-hot-autumn-2026-pdf.pdf

author: dev
title: La bande à « Balance ton Claude »
content:
Nous avons déjà longuement abordé les ressorts de l'« affaire Thélyson Orélien » dans nos pages (nous renvoyons, entre autres, à

cet excellent texte de Jean Claude Noel

). L'enquête qui suit porte sur ses délateurs, la bande à « Balance ton Claude » du nom du compte X à l'origine de la polémique. On y découvre que l'affaire Thélyson Orélien, est un double écran de fumée qui masque une convergence d'intérêts, financiers, idéologiques et géopolitiques, entre l'industrie de l'IA, les libertariens de la Silicon Valley, les christo-fascistes de l'administration Trump, et leurs imitateurs bien-de-chez-nous.


« Démarche complètement apolitique », « lanceur d'alerte », anonymat nécessaire pour éviter les attaques

ad hominem

… Toutes ces auto-justifications offertes par la bande à « Balance ton Claude », qui est derrière la polémique Thélyson Orélien, servent à ripoliner une opération idéologique, menée par un groupe de jeunes « libéraux-conservateurs » (doux euphémisme), très actifs dans l'espace médiatique, depuis les colonnes du Figaro, et les fabriques à propagande du projet Périclès. En outre, ces alarmes hypocrites s'inscrivent dans les récits

IApocalyptiques

 déployés par l'industrie pour faire gonfler investissements publics et privés. Une bulle profitant surtout aux nouveaux technoligarques, qui sont prêts à jeter la démocratie et l'humanité entière dans le chaudron de la valorisation et de la domination sans partage.


Les problèmes posés par la rédaction

I

A

ssistée

cachent une autre forme d'imposture : les allégations de neutralité politique répétées par la bande à « Balance ton Claude ». Une fine équipe, composée de cinq membres, d'après le premier accusateur anonyme sorti du bois

 [

1

]

, et qui n'a pas eu droit à la même attention que Thélyson Orélien.


«

Notre démarche était complètement apolitique

 [

]


 »

, déclarait ainsi Samuel Fitoussi dans

Le Point

, après avoir tombé le masque. Pourtant, le profil de nos Claudettes risque d'affoler votre détecteur à

bullshit

. Pas besoin du logiciel Pangram, vous allez voir, pour confondre ces immenses tartufes, présentés comme des «

lanceurs d'alerte

ayant

 l'amour de la vérité chevillé au coeur

et dénonçant les impostures intellectuelles

 [

3

]

 ».


Samuel Fitoussi


Commençons par vous donner une idée de l'honnêteté intellectuelle de M. Fitoussi. Quelques heures après avoir lancé la polémique sur le livre de Thélyson Orélien depuis le compte X « Balance ton Claude » (encore anonyme à ce moment-là), le chroniqueur du

Figaro

 intervient sur Radio J, où il déclare : «

comme aujourd'hui, le RN n'est pas un parti particulièrement violent ou antisémite ou quoi que ce soit, [renvoyer dos à dos les extrêmes] c'est en fait banaliser la dangerosité de cette gauche pro-Hamas...

 »


La journaliste lui fait alors remarquer que l'extrême-droite est quand même «

très proche de l'AfD, un parti néo-nazi

 ». Réponse de Samuel Fitoussi : «

J'ai beaucoup de critiques à l'égard de ces partis. Pour le RN, par exemple, je les trouve étatistes, socialistes, relativement incompétents

 […]

mais je pense qu'il faut reconnaître que les choses ont évolué, que le RN n'est plus le RN d'il y a 30 ans, et c'est même plus le RN d'il y a dix ans, qui voulait sortir de l'Union européenne, et c'est plus le RN antisémite

 [

4

]

 ».

L

'amour de la vérité chevillé au cœur

, on vous dit.


Par ailleurs, l'intérêt de M. Fitoussi pour les implications de l'IA générative n'est pas pure curiosité, étant donné qu'il travaille pour le fonds d'investissement FRST CAPITAL, spécialisé dans l'industrie naissante du

machine learning

(un des domaines informatiques que l'on trouve derrière la formule générique « IA », et dont les avancées ont notamment permis le développement des « grands modèles de langage » – ou

LLM

 – comme le célèbre ChatGPT).


Incidemment, FRST CAPITAL est une ancienne filiale d'OTIUM CAPITAL, la holding de Pierre-Edouard Stérin, milliardaire christo-libertarien qui utilise ses gains pour financer un projet de conquête politique par l'extrême-droite, baptisé « Périclès » (pour Patriotes, Enracinés, Résistants, Identitaires, Chrétiens, Libéraux, Européens, Souverainistes), et doté d'un budget de 150 millions d'euros

 [

5

]

.


Cerise sur le gâteau : FIRST CAPITAL n'investit pas seulement dans les « laboratoires d'IA », mais également dans la fabrique d'opinion, en produisant des sondages douteux sur la popularité d'Elon Musk ou …

author: Unknown
title: Cher·es collègues, il va falloir cesser d'être respectables...
content:
Le mouvement lycéen nous met face à nous-mêmes, nous, les profs : combien de temps allons-nous encore chercher à rester respectables

 

?


Quelques réflexions anonymes sur le mouvement lycéen de professeur-es en colère


CODE


GENERAL


DE


LA


FONCTION


PUBLIQUE

 (article L121-10) :


«

 

L'agent public doit se conformer aux instructions de son supérieur hiérarchique, sauf dans le cas où l'ordre donné est manifestement illégal et de nature à compromettre gravement un intérêt public.

 

»


1. Non, ce n'est pas «

 

leur

 

» mouvement : le mouvement des lycéens, en ce qu'il concorde précisément avec nos revendications, est aussi le nôtre. Il faut donc s'en sentir partie intégrante et se demander : que nous faut-il faire pour contribuer à faire triompher notre mouvement

 

?


2. D'abord, reconnaissons une chose : les lycéen·nes ont réussi là où les professeur·es ont échoué. Notre profession, corporatiste et «

 

bonne élève

 

» est si soucieuse d'être constructive et respectable qu'il y a bien longtemps qu'elle n'est plus prise au sérieux. Après des années de mobilisations de personnels de l'éducation, qui se sont révélées pour la plupart perdantes, car elles cherchaient à rester crédibles aux yeux du gouvernement, le mouvement lycéen nous met face à nous-mêmes : allons-nous, cette fois encore, rester respectables

 

?


3. Rester «

 

respectables

 

», c'est persister à «

 

remplir notre mission

 

» comme si de rien n'était. Ne surtout pas déroger à nos «

 

obligations légales

 

» : la place d'un·e professeur·e est dans sa salle de classe, n'est-ce pas

 

? et puisque certain·es élèves veulent faire cours, quel·le professeur·e serais-je si je ne les prenais pas

 

? C'est se persuader que sa place n'est pas dehors, avec les élèves qui bloquent, mais bien dedans, derrière la vitre, derrière la grille – il ne s'agirait pas de cautionner, par notre présence, des tirs de mortier ou des poubelles brûlées. C'est recommencer à placer des évaluations dès que l'occasion se présente parce qu'il faut bien les évaluer, les élèves…


4. Si nous sommes autant à être tenté·es par la respectabilité, c'est que, au-delà de la position de supériorité morale qu'elle semble nous conférer, le chantage de l'institution est fort. Cette période révèle en effet avec cruauté ce qu'elle attend réellement de nous, ce pour quoi nous sommes réellement payé·es : mettre des notes. Au-delà de nos envies si légitimes de retrouver nos élèves, de faire cours, de leur transmettre nos savoirs, telle est, in fine, notre crainte : ne pas pouvoir les évaluer. Même si nous savons qu'y procéder sans faire cours, sans passer de temps avec elleux, sans les préparer n'a pas de sens, nous persistons à vouloir le faire

 

; car l'absence de sens nous semble encore moins pire que le sentiment de les abandonner. Pris·es en tenaille par ces injonctions absurdes et culpabilisantes, dès lors que nous glissons dans un soutien marqué au mouvement, nous voilà réduit·es par les discours des proviseur·es, des médias des milliardaires, de certains parents et du gouvernement à la position intenable d'être des traîtres à la mission de l'école. Professeur·es soutenant les blocus, nous serions des opportunistes ou bien des fainéant·es, des gauchistes cherchant à «

 

manipuler les élèves

 

». Tous les jours où nous déciderons de débrayer, de nous mettre en grève, de soutenir les élèves face à la police, quelque bon serviteur zélé de l'institution sera là pour nous rappeler quelle est notre place, sans se gêner de nous rendre moralement responsables des «

 

débordements

 

».


5. Reconnaissons-le : l'institution, par le biais de ses directions d'établissement, exploite notre attachement à notre travail pour faire de nous, malgré nous, derrière la police, des agent·es de la casse du mouvement.


6. Mais la vérité, c'est que, si nous soulageons temporairement notre conscience professorale en programmant des évaluations ou en donnant du travail aux élèves pour «

 

rattraper le temps perdu

 

», ce même geste ne viendra jamais soulager notre conscience d'avoir vu nos élèves se faire gazer, matraquer, se faire mettre en joue, courser, charger, renverser, mutiler, interpeler, enfermer, insulter, brutaliser par la police de l'État. Il ne viendra pas effacer dans nos mémoires l'image des visages de nos élèves, de 14 ans, 15 ans, 16 ans, en pleurs, en rage, décontenancés, choqués, tout rouge et boursouflés du gaz, les bleus, les doigts, pieds …

title: Sırbistan’da Öğrenci Listesi seçimden zaferle çıktı
content:
Sırbistan’da erken genel seçimde, 12 yıldır iktidarda olan Aleksandar Vucic’in öncülük ettiği liste yenilgiye uğradı. Cumhurbaşkanlığından istifa ederek başbakan adayı olan Vucic, “Öğrenci Listesi”nin seçimleri kazandığını kabul etti. Novi Sad’daki tren istasyonu faciasının ardından başlayan öğrenci protestoları, seçim sonuçlarıyla birlikte ülke siyasetinde yeni bir dönemin kapısını araladı.


Anadolu Ajansı’nın (AA) haberine göre, Sırp İlerleme Partisi (SNS) öncülüğündeki “Aleksandar Vucic-Birleşmiş Sırbistan” listesinin başbakan adayı Vucic, seçim sonuçlarının dış destekli bir sürecin ürünü olduğunu öne sürdü. Vucic, yenilgiyi kabul etmesine rağmen muhalefette mücadele etmeyi sürdüreceklerini söyledi.


2014’te başbakanlık görevine gelen Vucic, 2017 ve 2022’de iki kez cumhurbaşkanı seçildi. Seçime başbakan adayı olarak katılabilmek için cumhurbaşkanlığından istifa eden Vucic, böylece 12 yıllık iktidarının ardından siyasi geleceği açısından önemli bir yenilgi aldı.


Öğrenci protestoları seçim sonucunu etkiledi


Novi Sad kentindeki tren istasyonunda 1 Kasım 2024’te beton sundurmanın çökmesi sonucu 16 kişinin hayatını kaybetmesi, hükümete yönelik tepkileri büyüttü. Facianın ardından başlayan öğrenci protestoları, yaklaşık iki yıl boyunca devam ederek Vucic yönetimi üzerindeki baskıyı artırdı.


“Öğrenci Listesi-Öğrenciler Kazanıyor” sloganıyla erken genel seçime katılan öğrenci hareketi, iktidara karşı yükselen toplumsal tepkiyi seçimlere taşıdı.


Öğrenci Listesi adına zafer konuşması yapan akademisyen Radomir Saicic, oy kullananlara teşekkür etti ve geleceği inşa etmeye başlayacaklarını söyledi.


Geleneksel siyasi partilerden farklı bir örgütlenme biçimine sahip olan hareketin, seçim başarısını nasıl bir hükümet programına ve yönetim modeline dönüştüreceği ise belirsizliğini koruyor.


Öğrenci Listesi yüzde 52 oy aldı


Aleksandar Vucic


Sırbistan Özgür Seçimler ve Demokrasi Merkezi’nin (CeSID) açıkladığı resmi olmayan sonuçlara göre, oyların yüzde 56’sı sayıldığında Öğrenci Listesi yüzde 52, SNS öncülüğündeki Vucic’in listesi ise yüzde 39 oy aldı.


Ülkede kayıtlı 6,4 milyondan fazla seçmen, 250 sandalyeli Sırbistan Ulusal Meclisinin yeni üyelerini belirlemek için sandık başına gitti.


Sırbistan Devlet Seçim Komisyonu (RIK), yerel saatle 19.00 itibarıyla seçime katılım oranının yüzde 67,6 olduğunu açıkladı. Ülke medyası, katılımın rekor seviyeye ulaşabileceğini bildirdi. 2023’teki seçimlerde katılım oranı yüzde 58 olarak kaydedilmişti.


Seçim günü usulsüzlük iddiaları


Erken genel seçim sırasında bazı sandık merkezlerinde şiddet olayları yaşandı. Sırbistan medyası, maskeli grupların oy kullanılan merkezlerden çıkan kişilere sopalarla saldırdığını aktardı.


İçişleri Bakanlığı, Lazarevac’ta yaşanan olaylarda iki polisin yaralandığını, bazı kişilerin polise taş ve tehlikeli maddeler fırlattığını duyurdu.


Bazı sandıklarda usulsüzlük yapıldığı da öne sürüldü. Oy pusulalarının fotoğraflandığı ve birden fazla oy kullanılmasını önlemesi gereken sistemlerin gerektiği gibi işletilmediği yönünde iddialar gündeme geldi.


Başkent Belgrad’da sandıkların kapanmasına yakın saatlerde çok sayıda zırhlı polis aracının görülmesi de güvenlik önlemlerini gündeme taşıdı.


Vucic’in İsrail ile yakın ilişkileri


Vucic yönetimi, İsrail ile yakın ilişkileri nedeniyle de dikkat çekiyordu. Vucic, Sırbistan’ın İsrail ile ortaklaşa savaş dronları üreteceğini açıklamış, ülkenin askeri kapasitesini güçlendirmek amacıyla İsrail yapımı insansız hava araçlarına (İHA) yönelik yeni bir montaj fabrikasının açılışına katılmıştı.


Vucic, İsrail Başbakanı Binyamin Netanyahu’dan da “dostum” diye söz etmişti.


Seçim yenilgisi, Sırbistan’ın dış politikasının geleceği açısından da soru işaretleri yarattı. Yeni siyasi hareketin Avrupa Birliği (AB) üyelik süreci, Brüksel ve Washington ile ilişkiler, Rusya ve Çin’le bağlar ve Kosova meselesi konusunda nasıl bir tutum alacağı merak ediliyor.


Öğrenci Listesi’ni şimdi ne bekliyor?


euronews'in yer verdiği habere göre, Öğrenci hareketinin önündeki en önemli sınav, sokak protestolarıyla büyüttüğü toplumsal desteği yönetim kapasitesine dönüştürmek olacak.


Yeni yönetimin ekonomi, dış politika, enerji, güvenlik ve kamu maliyesi gibi alanlarda kararlar alması gerekecek. Yargının ve kamu kurumlarının bağımsızlığı, yolsuzlukla mücadele, kamu yayıncılığı ve seçim koşullarının iyileştirilmesi de yeni dönemin temel başlıkları arasında yer alacak.


Öğrenci Listesi’nin geleneksel siyasi partilerden farklı …

title: Ephéméride des luttes : 26 octobre
content:
Dans l'éphéméride des luttes du 26 octobre, ce sont les bois de Sivens qui marquent le paysage, mais aussi les mémoires, puisqu'un des nôtres n'en est pas ressorti. Ciao Rémi, on n'oublie pas.


1876 :

 A Berne en Suisse, ouverture du huitième congrès général de l'Internationale Anti-Autoritaire.


1884 :

 A Paris, parution de la 'Revue Anti-patriote Révolutionnaire'.


1905 :

 A Saint-Petersbourg, création du premier Soviet.


1974 :

 A New York, plusieurs attaques menées en tant que premières actions des Fuerzas Armadas de Liberación Nacional (FALN) pour exiger l'indépendance de Puerto Rico et la libération de prisonniers politiques portoricains. En six ans, ce groupe mènera plus de 100 actions de ce style.


1977 :

 En Italie, de nombreux attentats frappent des entreprises liées à l'économie allemande, continuant à marquer le coup de la mort des militant-e-s de la Fraction Armée Rouge dans la prison de haute sécurité de Stammheim quelques jours plus tôt.


1981 :

 A Londres, un soldat de l'armée britannique meurt alors qu'il tente de désamorcer une bombe placée dans Oxford Street par l'IRA Provisoire.


1983 :

 A Toulouse, le CLODO (Comité pour la Liquidation Ou la Destruction des Ordinateurs) incendie les bureaux de l'entreprise américaine Sperry Univac.


1989 :

 En Allemagne de l'Ouest, l'IRA abat un membre de la Royal Air Force anglaise.


2014 :

 A Sivens, mort de Rémi Fraisse au cours d'affrontements avec la police, alors que plusieurs milliers de personnes tentent de défendre la zone occupée contre la construction d'un barrage, revendiquée comme ZAD, de l'expulsion par les forces de l'ordre.


2016 :

 A Diyarbakir au Kurdistan turc, des affrontements très violents ont eu lieu entre la population et la police suite à

l'arrestation de plusieurs maires

 Kurdes.


Voir également

l'éphéméride anarchiste

 du 26 octobre.

author: Perseus
title: Έκρηξη οργής στα Εξάρχεια μετά το χτύπημα πορείας μνήμης και τον άγριο ξυλοδαρμό 14χρονου (Βίντεο)
content:
Έκρηξη οργής στα Εξάρχεια μετά το χτύπημα πορείας μνήμης και τον άγριο ξυλοδαρμό 14χρονου (Βίντεο)


Εξάρχεια

: Το βράδυ του Σαββάτου 24 Οκτώβρη τα ΜΑΤ έβαλαν “φωτιά” στο φυτίλι χτυπώντας την πορεία μνήμης στον Κυριάκο Ξυμητήρη, τον άγριο ξυλοδαρμό και τη σύλληψη ενός 14χρονου και την σύλληψη ενός ακόμη 18χρονου.


Όλα ξεκίνησαν στον πεζόδρομο της Μεσολογγίου, όπου μετά από κάλεσμα του Συντονιστικού δράσης για την υπεράσπιση των Εξαρχείων, πραγματοποιήθηκε συγκέντρωση μνήμης και αγώνα για τον αναρχικό Κυριάκο Ξυμητήρη και σε αλληλεγγύη με την Μαριάννα Μανουρά και Δήμητρα Ζαραφέτα, έγκλειστες για την υπόθεση των Αμπελοκήπων.


Μετά την ολοκλήρωση της μικροφωνικής, περισσότερα από 100 άτομα που είχαν συγκεντρωθεί αποφάσισαν να πραγματοποιήσουν πορεία στα Εξάρχεια φωνάζοντας συνθήματα μνήμης στον Κυριάκο Ξυμητήρη, για τα Εξάρχεια και το gentrification, για την ταξική και κοινωνική απελευθέρωση.


Η ένταση πυροδοτήθηκε όταν η πορεία έστριψε στη συμβολή των οδών Ζωοδόχου Πηγής και Βαλτετσίου, μπροστά από το κατάστημα «Χάρτες». Διμοιρία των ΜΑΤ, που βρισκόταν παρατεταγμένη μέσα στον πεζόδρομο της Βαλτετσίου, επιτέθηκε ξαφνικά στους διαδηλωτές τη στιγμή που το πανό περνούσε μπροστά από το μαγαζί.


Ακολούθησε άγρια καταστολή, με τα ΜΑΤ να διαλύουν την πορεία και να προχωρούν στη βίαιη σύλληψη δύο ατόμων. Ανάμεσα στους δύο συλληφθέντες ο ένας ήταν ένα 14χρονος παιδί, το οποίο, σύμφωνα με καταγγελίες διαδηλωτών και κατοίκων, ξυλοκοπήθηκε άγρια από τις αστυνομικές δυνάμεις, οι οποίες περιορίστηκαν μόνο όταν συνειδητοποίησαν ότι βιντεοσκοπούνται.


Η είδηση για τον άγριο ξυλοδαρμό του 14χρονου μαθητή διαδόθηκε γρήγορα, προκαλώντας την αντίδραση του κόσμου, που βγήκαν στους δρόμους και συγκρούστηκαν με τις αστυνομικές δυνάμεις που εισέβαλαν βίαια στη γειτονιά τουλάχιστον έως τις 3 μετά τα μεσάνυχτα από τη Ζωοδόχου Πηγής και τη Βαλτετσίου, στη Μεσολογγίου, στην Κωλέττη και τη Θεμιστοκλέους.


Σε ανακοίνωσή του, το Συντονιστικό δράσης για την υπεράσπιση των Εξαρχείων κατηγορεί την αστυνομία ότι λειτούργησε ως ιδιωτική φρουρά και μπράβοι στο μαγαζί “Χάρτες”, γεγονός που δεν αποτελεί μεμονωμένο περιστατικό, αλλά μέρος της βίαιης πολιτικής εξευγενισμού και εκτοπισμού που εφαρμόζεται στα Εξάρχεια.


“Αναπλάσεις και εξευγενισμός σημαίνουν βία και εκτοπισμός, ενώ κράτος και κεφαλαίο είναι μια συμπαγής συνεργασία που επιτίθεται σε ό,τι μπορεί να χαλάσει τη “φυσιολογική” ροή του κέρδους -ακόμα και αν αυτό είναι μια πορεία, Μπάτσοι και ρουφιάνοι έξω από τα Εξάρχεια”, γράφουν ολοκληρώνοντας την ανακοίνωσή τους.


Αξίζει να σημειωθεί ότι παρά τα μυθεύματα διαρροών από “πηγές” της αστυνομίας προς τα ΜΜΕ για να δικαιολογήσει τη βίαιη καταστολή μιας ολόκληρης γειτονιάς, κανένας πυροσβέστης δεν πειράχτηκε ή κινδύνευσε από τον κόσμο που συμμετείχε στις συγκρούσεις με την αστυνομία. Σε αντίθεση με τις ψευδείς πληροφορίες, με τις οποίες τροφοδοτήθηκαν τα ΜΜΕ και αναπαράχθησαν άκριτα από τα ίδια, χωρίς ρεπορτάζ ή μαρτυρίες, το τι πραγματικά συνέβη αποτυπώνεται ακριβώς σε αυτό το βίντεο.

author: Μπάμπης Μπίκας
title: Το ψηφοδέλτιο της Φοιτητικής Λίστας κέρδισε τις κοινοβουλευτικές εκλογές στη Σερβία!
content:
Ο συνδυασμός που συγκροτήθηκε από τους φοιτητές στη Σερβίας με υποψήφιους προσωπικότητες της κοινωνίας των πολιτών, όχι μόνο κέρδισε τις έκτακτες κοινοβουλευτικές εκλογές που προκήρυξε ο απερχόμενος πρόεδρος Αλεξάντερ Βούτσιτς, αλλά πέτυχε την απόλυτη πλειοψηφία των ψήφων με 52% και της βουλής με 138 έδρες στο σύνολο των 250. Το απερχόμενο κυβερνητικό κόμμα περιορίστηκε στο 40% και τις 104 έδρες.

ΟΙ ΠΡΩΤΕΣ ΜΕΤΑΔΟΣΕΙΣ ΑΝΕΞΑΡΤΗΤΩΝ ΜΜΕ


n1info.rs


CRTA: Η Φοιτητική Λίστα κέρδισε το 51,47% των ψήφων


Η φοιτητική λίστα κέρδισε το 51,47% των ψήφων, όπως ανακοινώθηκε απόψε από τον διευθυντή προγράμματος της Crta, Ράσα Νεδέλικοφ.


Η λίστα “Aleksandar Vučić – United Serbia” κέρδισε 40,42 τοις εκατό.


Όπως είπε ο Νεδέλικοφ, καμία άλλη εκλογική λίστα δεν πέρασε το όριο, εκτός από αυτές των μειονοτήτων.


Πρόσθεσε ότι υπήρχε 1,55% άκυρων ψηφοδελτίων.


Ο Νεδέλικοφ είπε ότι οι πολίτες έχουν το δικαίωμα να γιορτάζουν, αλλά κάλεσε όλους να το κάνουν με αξιοπρέπεια.


(ΒΙΝΤΕΟ) Πανηγυρισμοί στους δρόμους σε όλη τη Σερβία μετά τη νίκη της Φοιτητικής Λίστας


Σε όλη τη Σερβία πανηγυρίζουν μετά τη νίκη της Φοιτητικής Λίστας στις πρόωρες βουλευτικές εκλογές.


Παρακάτω, δείτε πώς είναι οι πανηγυρισμοί στους δρόμους σε όλη τη Σερβία.


Μεγάλος αριθμός πολιτών της Νις συγκεντρώθηκε, κατόπιν πρόσκλησης φοιτητών, μπροστά από το εκλογικό κέντρο της Φοιτητικής Λίστας στην οδό Στρατηγού Μπόζε Γιάνκοβιτς για να γιορτάσουν τη νίκη της Φοιτητικής Λίστας.


Nova.rs


Πρώτα αποτελέσματα εκλογών στη Σερβία: Φοιτητική λίστα 138 έδρες, Ενωμένη Σερβία 104


Τα εκλογικά τμήματα στη Σερβία έκλεισαν επίσημα και ο Αλεξάνταρ Βούτσιτς, πρώην πρόεδρος της Σερβίας και υποψήφιος για την πρωθυπουργία, παραδέχτηκε ότι έχασε τις εκλογές. Σύμφωνα με τις πρώτες προβλέψεις, η «Φοιτητική λίστα – Οι φοιτητές κερδίζουν» κέρδισε το 52% και 138 έδρες, ενώ η λίστα «Αλεξάνταρ Βούτσιτς – Ενωμένη Σερβία» κέρδισε το 39,3% των ψήφων και 104 έδρες.


Αυτά είναι δεδομένα που βασίζονται στο 49,8% του επεξεργασμένου δείγματος με 750 εκλογικά τμήματα.


Ο διευθυντής προγράμματος της Crta, Raša Nedeljkov, ανακοίνωσε ότι η Φοιτητική Λίστα κέρδισε το 51,47% των ψήφων.


Σύμφωνα με το Crta, η λίστα «Aleksandar Vučić – United Serbia» κέρδισε 40,42 τοις εκατό.


Άλλα κόμματα που συμμετείχαν στις εκλογές δεν πέρασαν την απογραφή, εκτός από τα κόμματα της μειοψηφίας.


ΖΩΝΤΑΝΑ ΕΚΛΟΓΕΣ Ο Βούτσιτς παραδέχτηκε την ήττα του, οι πολίτες πανηγυρίζουν σε όλη τη Σερβία: Αποκλεισμένη η Σλάβια ΒΙΝΤΕΟ


«Νίκη! Τρόμπα!»: Η πρώτη προσφώνηση από τα κεντρικά γραφεία της Φοιτητικής Λίστας


Βούτσιτς: Είναι σαφές ότι χάσαμε αυτές τις εκλογές


Οι εκπρόσωποι των φοιτητών και οι υποψήφιοι της «Φοιτητικής Λίστας – Φοιτητικής Λίστας» γιόρτασαν τη νίκη στις έκτακτες βουλευτικές εκλογές στα εκλογικά τους γραφεία.


Μαζί τραγούδησαν το τραγούδι «Srbija se budi».


Ο εορτασμός στο εκλογικό αρχηγείο της «Φοιτητικής Λίστας» ξεκίνησε αφότου ο κάτοχος της λίστας της «Ενωμένης Σερβίας», Αλεξάνταρ Βούτσιτς, παραδέχτηκε την ήττα του στις εκλογές.


Προηγουμένως, ο Αλεξάνταρ Βούτσιτς παραδέχτηκε την ήττα.


«Με βάση το δείγμα, στρωματοποιημένο, είναι σαφές ότι χάσαμε τις εκλογές. Η Φοιτητική Λίστα κέρδισε, θα έχει 135/140 έδρες, εμείς έχουμε περίπου 105. Κανείς άλλος δεν μπήκε στη Βουλή, το SVM μπήκε με τρεις έδρες, οι Αλβανοί με μία και το SDA, νομίζω», είπε ο Βούτσιτς.


Οι φοιτητές κονταροχτυπούν στα ίσα (και) εκλογικά το καθεστώς Βούτσιτς

author: Mada Masr
title: Organizations rally in support of Mada Masr, condemn ‘weaponization’ of media law against independent journalism
content:
Rallying in support of Mada Masr, statements of solidarity have emerged in recent days from domestic and international advocacy organizations, political figures and parties, journalists and media platforms, all expressing their backing for the independent journalistic website and for Editor-in-Chief Lina Attalah, following her referral to trial last week by prosecutors.


Though Mada Masr has been called in for questioning on an almost annual basis in relation to journalistic coverage, this is the first time prosecutors initiate a trial of this kind. Attalah is due to attend a misdemeanor court session in New Cairo on Tuesday on the charges of founding, managing and operating a website without a license.


During a gathering at the Journalists Syndicate on Saturday, several General Assembly members and independent journalists declared their support for Mada Masr and condemned what they described as an “assault on independent journalism,” referring to the escalation that began in September with the arrest of six journalists from the independent fact-checking platform Matsda2sh.


In the ensuing weeks, Attalah received a summons for investigation,

fielding

 six hours of questioning from the Supreme State Security Prosecution about her efforts to acquire a license for Mada Masr since 2018, the website’s operations, as well as questions concerning a recent report on protest actions taken by prisoners across the country and authorities’ response.


She was informed less than 24 hours after the investigation session that she has been referred to trial on charges of running an unlicensed website.


Following news of the trial referral, 119 human rights organizations and media institutions from around the world came together to condemn the “unprecedented attack on press freedom in Egypt,” in a Friday

statement

 calling for an end to the legal pursuit of Attalah and urging that Mada Masr be granted a license to operate following its multiple applications to media regulators.


They also called for Egypt’s authorities to halt the targeting of independent media outlets — including Matsda2sh — and to release all 26 journalists currently imprisoned in Egypt in relation to their work.


The list of signatories to the joint statement includes Amnesty International, Human Rights Watch, the Committee to Protect Journalists, PEN International, the International Federation for Human Rights, the Robert F. Kennedy Human Rights Center and the Electronic Frontier Foundation.


Also among the signatories are the International Fact-Checking Network, the Center for International Policy, the Tahrir Institute for Middle East Policy and dozens more Arab and international media platforms.


The signatories stated that Attalah’s trial threatens the future of independent journalism, knowledge production and civil society in Egypt. They warned that the potential penalties — fines ranging from LE1 to LE3 million and possible orders for the website’s closure — could effectively end the operations of one of the last remaining independent media institutions in the country.


Individual expressions of support were also forthcoming from Democratic United States’ Senator Chris Van Hollen, who called the charges against Attalah “baseless,” and described the events from Matsda2sh’s arrest to Attalah’s pursuit as “the most severe crackdown on the press seen in years.”


Van Hollen, a member of the US Senate Committee on Foreign Relations, called for an end to the assault.


Amnesty International had already demanded on Wednesday an end to what it described as the persistent judicial harassment of Attalah and Mada Masr’s journalists, prior to the trial referral, with Yasmin Ahmed, the organization’s regional impact director, stating that targeting the editor-in-chief for the journalistic work produced by her team is “outrageous” and pointing to the fact that this is the sixth case brought against the outlet and its journalists in the span of six years.


The Committee to Protect Journalists’ regional director, Sara Qudah, likewise

described

 these recent actions as a coordinated assault on the press, condemning Attalah’s referral to trial “for operating a website without a license that Egyptian authorities have themselves refused to grant for years.”

author: Abahlali_3
title: Worsening Violence as the Election Comes Closer
content:
25 October 2026 Abahlali baseMjondolo Press Statement

Worsening Violence as the Election Comes Closer

Our country is one of the most violent in the world, worse than some war zones. The rate of violence against women and the rate of murders committed by young men against other young men are among the highest in the world. There is violence in the home and in communities, violence from ordinary people, politicians, criminals and the armed forces in service of the state and the rich.

Our country and its people have been deeply damaged by generations of oppression, which has continued into the present for many people, especially the poor. The ANC has never pursued a project of healing, a project of restoring the humanity of our people and our society. They have just made themselves rich, leaving most of us poor and living in a broken society, a broken society in which the poor continue to be ruled with violence.

Things are getting worse. In KwaZulu-Natal armed mobs now parade through the streets accompanied by the police. People have been driven from their homes and livelihoods, assaulted and killed. The rise of the right, including violent fascist organisations, is a matter of grave concern for our movement and all people of good conscience.

As the election approaches, violence is worsening. So far 43 people have been killed, including people from the ANC, IFP and MKP. The political killings that are taking place are another grave concern for our movement. In a free, democratic country everyone should be free to campaign for election without fear. We know very well that the killing will not be confined to politicians. As killing becomes more common, more and more activists will be targeted in the years ahead.

Right now, the atmosphere in Durban is particularly threatening. Political intolerance has reached a fever pitch. The danger can be felt everywhere. Many politicians and parties have been complicit, and none have built a project in support of healing and a just peace. People are being assaulted and sometimes beaten to death in the streets. The political assassinations continue and will continue after the election as the politicians fight for power and money.

While the situation is at its worst in Durban and KwaZulu-Natal, it is moving into other parts of the country. ANC people have been killed in Katlehong.

People are being encouraged to hate, attack and kill as the election comes closer. But elections come and go. Every time there is an election, politicians come into our communities with promises, food and t-shirts and then they leave. We don’t see them until the next election comes. To them we are voting fodder, people who can be lied to and bribed, and not citizens of a democracy, or even just full human beings.

We have had elections for more than thirty years and the poor remain poor and without land, water, sanitation, electricity and housing. Our dignity continues to be vandalised by the state and the organised power of the rich. We continue to live with our suffering. This election will not resolve any of the problems that we face, and yet we are being encouraged to hate, attack and kill, and to support politicians and parties that are encouraging hate and are involved in political violence.

We cannot now glorify elections as the only thing that can resolve our problems and ensure that our dignity as human beings is recognised. Elections can be important, but all our advances as a movement and as a class have come from building our own power, popular democratic power. We must never allow politicians to divide us. We must never be divided by people who only come to our communities to lie to us when they seek power and then leave us poor and oppressed.

After careful discussions, we have agreed to encourage our members, and others who look to our movement for political direction, to vote according to their conscience if they wish to vote, but not to support those who have disappointed and betrayed them in the past, and who have made the poor suffer for more than thirty years. They must not vote for people who are trying to divide the poor with ethnic politics and political intolerance, for the corrupt who steal from the poor or for people who are xenophobic. They must not vote for any politicians or parties that encourage hate and violence.

When this election has passed, the oppressed will remain oppressed, there will be greater political intolerance and our society will be even more violent …

author: Ahmed Ismat Ahmed
title: How a child inherits care
content:
We are sitting at Gallal. It’s in Madinaty, on the edge of Cairo where the buildings are all new and the streets are too wide. The tea is too sweet the way Sudanese tea is supposed to be too sweet when someone else makes it for you. Mahmoud is across from me.

I don’t remember either of us standing up. Only the hug itself, which went on long enough that an Egyptian girl at the next table put down her phone and started crying. She didn’t know us. She cried because whatever passed between two men holding on to each other in the middle of that cafe was apparently visible even to a stranger who had no context at all.

Mahmoud went red immediately — a Sudanese man has no idea what to do with a stranger’s tears — so he pulled out his phone, opened Facebook, and muttered that she was probably crying over some relationship, while the screen in his hand played footage of Khartoum burning. We’re good at that silence now. The silence of being physically tethered to one place while completely living inside another. I kept thinking: Does everyone I love do the same? Carry so much that they stop feeling it, until a stranger has to cry for them?

The screen lights up. The wallpaper is a photo of my grandfather’s class in Wadi Halfa, built after the water took Halfa Dagheim. The first time my grandmother told me about it, she didn’t say “displacement.” She said, “We left the house, and the water took it.” Halfa Dagheim was going to drown for the High Dam — a decision made far away by people who would never bear its cost. When they moved to Wadi Halfa, there was only dust. The first shared project families built was a school. The teacher was my grandfather Ahmed, an English teacher. He gathered children under a tree and started. I inherited that before I understood it. Not money. Not land. The habit of starting under a tree when the official map says your town should no longer exist.

The waitress calls me

ya walad

 even though I am 29. That word makes me think of my mother. Her father died during her certificate exams. She carried grief silently and kept studying until she earned admission to veterinary school at the University of Khartoum. She graduated while pregnant with me. I came from that lineage of exhausted people who kept choosing endurance.

When I entered the University of Khartoum in 2015, I thought I was entering a sanctuary. The conversations that shaped us happened beside roads, under trees, around tea stalls that surrounded campus from every direction. The women who ran them knew who was always late, who never had money, who argued too much, who quietly listened. They knew us better than the administration.

For a long time I thought we had to be hard to win. I thought we had to stop feeling to keep going. I was wrong. The only thing that ever saved us was the opposite. The tea. The sitting together after. The hand that was out before you asked. They can turn violence into money. They can turn gold into weapons. They cannot turn care into money. Care refuses to be bought. That is why they fear it.

In the republic of the unimportant — at the tea stalls, in the resistance committees, in the unions that kept meeting in borrowed rooms after being banned — we kept a different ledger. Not gold. Who was missing, who needed medicine, who hadn’t eaten. That ledger didn’t make anyone rich. It kept people alive.

At Gallal, Mahmoud orders a second tea without asking me. He knows I will want it. We have this habit from Khartoum — you order for the other person before he finishes, so he doesn’t have to say he wants more but has no money. He pushes sugar toward me. That small push is the whole essay. You notice who needs sugar and you push it without making a speech.

And finally — to the child walking into a school that hasn’t been built yet, with a notebook slipping against his arm. Inside, a poster on the wall is crooked. Someone taped it in a hurry and left one corner hanging. He will stop, shift the notebook to the other arm, and straighten it without thinking. He learned that from someone who sat next to him when he cried. That is ordinary. That is how a child inherits care.

author: Ndivhuwo Mukwevho
title: Multi-million rand sports facility finally opens in Limpopo
content:
Finally, Waterval residents in Limpopo outside of Elim Hospital are now able to utilise their R55-million sports facility having waited for over a decade of delays. The Waterval facility is not the only one that has been neglected by Limpopo municipalities. Earlier this year,

Elitsha

reported on the R1.4-million upgrades to

Makwarela Stadium

 that never happened.


How it all started


The Waterval sports facility, which consists of a soccer field and a tennis court, was officially handed over to the Waterval community earlier this month. This came as welcome relief to local residents who had already lost hope that the facility would ever open. At one stage, it was left abandoned and turned into a drug den and a hiding place for criminals.


The facility is set to be utilised for various sporting codes by the local communities and schools. “At last, our children have got a ground where they can play their football with ease. Even though we had to wait for years for the facility to be completed, we are happy now that the ground is ours. To be honest, I am one of the people who had already lost hope that one day, the facility will ever be used for our benefit,” says Cedric Mulaudzi, a resident of Waterval.


Mulaudzi told

Elitsha

 that his 11-year-old son was not yet born when construction work began on the Waterval sports facility. “I am just happy that my son, who was not yet born when construction work started, will now have a place where he will be able to mature his football career,” says Mulaudzi.


The Waterval sports facility is the only decent, modern sports facility in the area and will be utilised by Mpheni, Shirly, Elim and other local communities.


Politically motivated?


“Why did it take too long for our government to complete this facility? This means that if it takes our government more than 10-years to complete just one stadium!” says Mulaudzi.


Nelson Mudzanani, who was born and raised in Waterval, also has questions about the timing of the project’s completion, while welcoming its completion. “For years, we have asked questions to the local municipality [Makhado] on why it was taking too long for them to complete the project and we never received any response. But now, we are due for elections in the coming weeks, and all of a sudden the stadium is finally completed. I just hope that the timing is not politically motivated,” says Mudzanani.


He believes that the sports facility will go a long way in empowering the local communities. “Those who want to exercise and those who want to play various sporting codes now have a decent place to do so. I just hope that the facility will be maintained accordingly,” he says.


During the handover of the Waterval sports facility, Makhado mayor, Dorcus Mboyi urged the local communities to utilise the facility properly and refrain from vandalising it. She also extended apologies for the delays they endured during the construction of the facility.

author: ROAPE
title: Life after Museveni
content:
I have argued before that moving forward, Uganda will need General Muhoozi Kainerugaba, son of current President Yoweri Museveni. Or a person like Gen. Kainerugaba. This is not necessarily about the man, Muhoozi Kainerugaba. More that the trajectory of Museveni’s politics needs a man of this texture.


My intention here is neither support nor endorsement. But acknowledging Muhoozi’s usefulness in the transitional phase which must happen soon – or that is already underway.  Of course, his autocratic display thus far, is difficult to ignore.  But we have to acknowledge that Gen. Kainerugaba is a very important actor in an ongoing transition.


As

the

 son of a sitting president, and current commander of the nation’s military, this is an unusual combination for anyone, and is therefore discussable on its merits. Especially with an octogenarian president, and a nervous country, surely this person – whoever they may be – is a key component.


I know, we are all running scared. Many comrades in the struggle for a good governance are still missing – Sam Mugumya. Many are rotting in jails and ‘safehouses’ across the country.  National Unity Platform (NUP)’s incarcerated supporters and leaders – Waiswa Mufumbiro, Eddie Mutwe, among others – are constantly threatened with public executions by the CDF himself, who is currently the president in waiting. We are all scared.


Exile has become an even more common word in our conversations. But I will say one more time, viewed comparatively, President Kainerugaba will never be as brutal as his father – even if he so badly wanted. But presently, the country needs him sober and rightly guided.


If we are looking towards a peaceful, gradual, no-deadline transition, Gen. Muhoozi features prominently – importantly.  This does not mean to suggest I’m anti-revolution, but instead aware, on the one hand, that most African countries do not have the critical mass for revolution, and on the other, that Africa remains a colonised continent with leaders being decided

elsewhere

. You should have read my disappointment when Mr Museveni refused to appoint him, Vice President.


Is Yoweri Museveni leaving?


It is no cynicism to say that opposition forces – mainstream opposition, civil society, activists – have struggled to challenge Gen. Museveni. In fact, as journalist Charles Onyango Obbo observed one time, most of us in Kampala on either side of the isle are resigned to the man’s death. Undoubtedly, Museveni – and his mostly Western backers – have proved too strong to beat. We have tried elections, and failed. Opposition leader, Dr Besigye led the country into peaceful protests and failed. We have tried the judicial route and failed.


Presently, a leading opposition candidate, Dr Kizza Besigye and his lawyer, and former Kampala City Lord Mayor, Eria Lukwago are fighting for their lives in an inhumane judicial system.  They are both in jail. Legal rebel and president of the Uganda Law Society, Isaac Ssemakadde, and leading human rights lawyer, Nicholas Opio were forced out of the country. Activist Male Mabirizi, a pioneering activist lawyer, is in jail.


Even when Museveni’s own comrades – Amama Mbabazi, Jaberi Bidandi Ssali, Miria Matembe, Eriya Kategaya, among others – nicely asked him not to stand again, and let them lead the transition, the man simply sidelined them.


In truth, besides our rhetorical belligerence, we have been defeated. Leading opposition figure, Bobi Wine is in exile, while the other key figure, Dr Kizza Besigye in jail. We on the outside are walking zombies, scared and talking in whispers. But in appreciating our blighted condition, we ought to find solace in the fact that we will have the chance to fight another day – maybe audition for a new opponent.


Indeed, it is here that I see Gen. Kainerugaba as the man of the moment. Not out of endorsement or affection, but Kainerugaba as the product of the contestations spelled out above. Indeed, Gen. Kainerugaba stands as ‘president-in-waiting’ as testimony of the success of his father’s politics – where all potential competitors in the race to replace him (inside and outside) have all been defeated, humiliated, exiled or thoroughly emasculated. Only one man is left standing.


To this end, I don’t see Gen. Kainerugaba withdrawing his preparation/candidacy for president, neither do I see Museveni seeking to fight a supposedly impatient son, say dropping him from the position of CDF.  Museveni has no other choice, but to …

author: Moussa Traoure
title: The Palace Guard Against the Trenches : What the Mutiny in Niamey Revealed
content:
The mutiny that broke out in

air base 101 in Niamey

 in the night of 29 August 2026 failed. The real question now is to understand why it took place. Those who took up arms against General Abdourahamane Tiani were young soldiers from the front lines, those who fought the ‘jihadists.’ For all of the Sahel, it’s a much more worrying sign than any plot from the army high command.


Until Saturday morning, fighting took place in the Nigerien capital near to Diori Hamani airport, the presidential palace, and the public television channel RTN.

Loyalists retook control only with the support of the Russian Africa Corps

.

The state television broadcast

 the live arrest of several tens of soldiers being arrested, most of them extremely young.


Three juntas, one promise


In Mali, in Burkina Faso, and in Niger, soldiers took power putting forward the same argument: civilian leaders had failed in front of the ‘jihadists,’ and the army would now do better. Assimi Goïta carried out two coups in Mali in 2020 and 2021. Ibrahim Traoré took control of Burkina Faso in September 2022 and overturned another putschist, Paul-Henri Damiba. Tiani deposed President Mohamed Bazoum in July 2023.


The French were asked to leave, and the Russians invited to come in. The three countries concerned founded the Alliance of Sahel States and

withdrew from ECOWAS in January 2025

. Each then solidified its grip on power through legislation. In Mali,

political parties were banned in 2025

, and the leadership was granted a

five-year renewable term in office

—without elections.

Until 2030, Tiani will remain president of the transition

. In Burkina Faso,

all political parties were dissolved in January 2026

, clearing the way for the regime to consolidate control.


The promised security, however, never materialised. This gap between promises and actions has fuelled anger—an anger that is now festering in the barracks.


Two armies in one


Niger effectively has two armies

: the Presidential Guard, and everyone else. Tiani commanded the Guard for twelve years; since the coup, it has received the best equipment and the most secure and comfortable postings. Meanwhile, regular units stationed in the southwest and along the Nier’s borders are losing personnel in the fight against the Islamic State in the Sahel and the al-Qaeda-linked JNIM.


According to observers, it is these soldiers who have mutinied. US researcher

Alex Thurston

 that most accounts align: regardless of infighting at the top, it is the anger of the rank-and-file that has driven the revolt.

Paul Melly, of Chatham House

, aptly summari the sentiment among young officers: three years ago, things seemed to be improving; today, the opposite is true.


When dealing with generals, a regime can either negotiate or simply swap out loyalists for other trusted figures. But for soldiers suffering from a lack of ammunition and reinforcements, a reshuffle within the high command changes nothing.


Niamey, Niger.


How the juntas protect themselves


The first pillar: the purges. In Mali, following a

reported coup attempt in August 2025

, two generals and more than fifty military personnel were arrested. At the end of December,

a decree mandated the forced retirement

 of several high-ranking officers, including the former intelligence chief. In Burkina Faso, after a plot was uncovered in January 2026, Damiba—identified by Ouagadougou as one of the organizers—

was extradited to Togo

. Tiani has taken a more cautious approach: on 11 September,

he replaced Chief of Staff Moussa Salaou Barmou with Mamane Sani Kiaou

. Former Defense Minister

Kalla Moutari has been arrested

, and former RFI journalist

Moussa Kaka

 has been shot. According to Thurston, this reaction suggests that

Tiani does not wish to appear fearful

.


The second pillar is the law. With political parties banned and terms of office extended, the opposition has no remaining legal path to power.


The third pillar is an external protector.

Between 200 and 300 fighters

 from the Russian African Corps are stationed in Niger, with their headquarters located south of Base 101. Russian Ambassador

Viktor Voropaev maintains that Niamey merely requested assistance

. According to Thurston,

the Algerian air force also provided support

author: Omar Kalinge-Nnyago
title: Uganda: The Entrenchment of a Hereditary Military Oligarchy
content:
Uganda is approaching one of the most precarious political transitions in its post-independence history. The likely trajectory is not democratic consolidation but the slow institutionalization of a hereditary military oligarchy. Four developments are driving this shift: President Yoweri Museveni’s advanced age; the elevation of his son, Gen. Muhoozi Kainerugaba, to Chief of Defence Forces (CDF); the operationalization of the Patriotic League of Uganda (PLU) as a parallel mobilization vehicle; and the legal entrenchment of military authority over civilian institutions. Taken together, these amount to what might be called a “slow-motion coup” already under way.


The most probable outcome is best described as contested dynastic authoritarianism, a system in which elections continue to serve as instruments of international legitimacy, while substantive power is contested within the first family and the military elite rather than at the ballot box. The formal opposition faces structural decapitation through repression and co-optation. Yet two under-examined institutions – the Anglican and Catholic Churches, and segments of Uganda’s Muslim community – offer potential, if imperfect, nonviolent pathways for mediation or resistance over the coming decade, complicated by the risk of Muslim youth radicalization.


A conventional, extra-constitutional military coup remains possible even as the regime works to secure de facto military dominance through promotions, strategic retirements of senior officers, legislative amendment, and patronage. The PLU’s grassroots strategy is designed to insulate the succession from exactly this risk, cultivating broad loyalty and framing dynastic continuity as patriotic inevitability rather than rupture. The principal danger to the plan, accordingly, lies less in popular revolt than in intra-elite fracture or palace intrigue should the succession falter.


Anatomy of a slow-motion coup


The regime has moved beyond personalist autocracy toward a durable, self-perpetuating system built on four pillars: fusion of military command with the first family, political mobilization through the PLU, subordination of parliament, and kleptocratic control of the state’s resources.


Uganda’s slide toward dynastic rule no longer needs to be projected; it can be observed directly. In 2024, Museveni handed his son the office of Chief of Defence Forces, together with an unusual personal grant of authority to promote senior officers – a clear departure from the constitutional design of a professional military answerable to civilian rather than familial command. Muhoozi has used this platform expansively, maintaining an active, often combative social media presence, intervening openly in partisan disputes, and, in June 2026, ordering troops to shut down Nation Media Group’s operations after critical coverage of his conduct. He has also directly ordered the arrest of opposition lawyer Erias Lukwago and the deportation of Kenyan lawyer Martha Karua, both members of Dr Kizza Besigye’s defence team – a signal that the regime now treats defence counsel, and not only defendants, as targets. In his national address of 4 July 2026, President Museveni appeared to defend his son’s actions, placing blame on Besigye for allegedly delaying court proceedings.


The institutional scaffolding around Muhoozi has matured alongside his personal profile. The Patriotic League of Uganda, rebranded in 2024 from an informal network of birthday rallies and fan clubs known as the “Muhoozi Project”, now runs village-level structures, community clean-up campaigns, and youth roadshows, and openly courts the same rural base the National Resistance Movement (NRM) has cultivated for four decades. It functions less as a political party than as an insurance policy: it absorbs potential rivals into patronage, builds a loyalty network running parallel to the NRM’s own, and softens the ground for a hereditary handover by presenting it as continuity rather than rupture. Leadership changes, such as the appointment of Hon. Fadil Twaha as Secretary General, signal a deliberate effort to deepen outreach among Muslim communities that feel marginalized in the League’s rise.


The 12

th

 Parliament offered an early demonstration of the PLU’s reach. The League withdrew its earlier backing for then Speaker Anita Among and her deputy, Thomas Tayebwa, clearing the way for Jacob Oboth-Oboth’s election as Speaker – a small but telling exercise of veto power …

author: AfricanFeminism
title: Morocco’s First Woman Prime Minister and the Terms of Freedom
content:
Something changes when a woman occupies an office men have treated as their natural inheritance. Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri’s

appointment

 on 29 September 2026 makes that change visible in Morocco. For women whose competence is routinely scrutinised, the pleasure is neither naïve nor trivial.


But the woman forming a government and the woman labouring in the fields, raising children without pay and denied an equal share of her inheritance encounter power differently. Representation changes who governs; emancipation changes what all women have the power to do. That distinction shifts our attention from PM Mansouri’s gender to the politics of the centre-right

 Party of Authenticity and Modernity (PAM

)

, which she leads. Will its programme redistribute the resources and rights on which women’s freedom depends?


The history beneath the headline


Calling women’s leadership foreign to Morocco requires forgetting its history. Historian Osire Glacier

documents

 women’s authority long before the contemporary premiership. Kenza al Awrabiya, the Amazigh mother of Idris II, helped secure the Idrisid dynasty, founded in the late eighth century in what is now Morocco. Zaynab al Nafzawiyya influenced eleventh-century Almoravid politics around Aghmat, near Marrakech. Sayyida al Hurra governed Tétouan, a city in northern Morocco, during the sixteenth century. Khnata bint Bakkar intervened in eighteenth-century dynastic politics.


Across the region,

Dihya

 is remembered as an Amazigh queen who led resistance to the Arab conquest in the Aurès, in present-day Algeria, during the late seventh century. Tuareg oral tradition remembers

Tin Hinan

 as a queen and founding ancestress of noble lineages in the Ahaggar, in present-day southern Algeria.


These histories expose how male authority is made to appear natural. Fatima Mernissi’s

The Forgotten Queens of Islam


challenges that selective memory. Colonialism also reorganised authority: French Protectorate administrators

reshaped

 customary courts around imperial priorities. What survives as tradition can carry the history of political intervention. 


Religious interpretation can give exclusion another claim to permanence. Islamist and other conservative opponents invoke this

hadith

 against women’s political authority:


«لَنْ يُفْلِحَ قَوْمٌ وَلَّوْا أَمْرَهُمُ امْرَأَةً»


Usually translated as saying that a people governed by a woman will not prosper, it becomes a prohibition irrespective of her competence. Asma Lamrabet, a

Moroccan Islamic feminist thinker

, questions turning a

narration linked

 to Persia’s dynastic succession into a universal ban. She reads it against the Qur’anic Queen of Sheba, whose judgement demonstrates capable leadership. Her argument contests male authority’s claim to divine necessity.


PAM’s promises and its record


Women have long contested how authority is distributed within the family. Fatima Sadiqi

documents

the Union de l’Action Féminine’s 1992 million-signature campaign to reform the Moudawana, Morocco’s family code. The 2004 reform abolished wives’ duty of obedience but retained unequal inheritance and exceptions to the marriage age of eighteen. Proposals announced in December 2024 left fundamental equality demands unresolved. In October 2025, more than sixty civil society organisations and public figures

joined to call for comprehensive reform

. Rights in Morocco have advanced through organised demands, not the gender of an officeholder.


PAM, a centre-right party founded in 2008,

advocates

 social modernisation and positions itself against the Islamist Justice and Development Party (PJD). It entered government in 2021 alongside the National Rally of Independents and conservative nationalist Istiqlal. Opposition to Islamist conservatism, however, does not itself entail reforming the laws and economic conditions that subordinate women.


PAM’s

2026 programme

 promises improved widow pensions, childcare, safe transport, a women’s enterprise fund and labour inspection. The commitments leave inheritance equality, abortion reform and decriminalisation of consensual same sex relations unaddressed. Mansouri called for

banning child marriage

 without exceptions in 2024, yet PAM’s electoral programme

omits that commitment

. Employment can support independence, but a wage does not cancel criminalisation or unequal property rights. The programme leaves those constraints intact.


Even PAM’s narrow promise to increase …

author: WoMin
title: Press Release | Women’s Climate Assembly strengthens Pan African solidarity, women-led resistance and the struggle for a just future
content:
“

Empowering women is a radical way to transform the world!

” –

Ivorian activist


The fourth regional

Women’s Climate Assembly

 (WCA), held in Yaoundé, Cameroon, from 5–8 October 2026, concluded with a powerful reaffirmation of African women’s determination to defend their lands, territories, livelihoods and communities, and to demand climate justice and reparations.


Under the theme, “

Our lands, our voices: African women united for climate justice and reparations!

”, the Assembly convened over 75 women community leaders, activists, feminist organisations, civil society groups and allies from twelve countries including Burkina Faso, Cameroon, Côte d’Ivoire, the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), Guinea-Conakry, Liberia, Namibia, Niger, Nigeria, Sierra Leone, Senegal and Zambia.


The gathering provided a vital space for women on the frontlines of the climate crisis, extractive industries, land dispossession and environmental destruction to share their experiences, strengthen relationships across borders and build collective strategies for change.


As the Assembly closed, one message rang clear: African women are not merely bearing the costs of the climate crisis. They are leading the struggle for solutions, defending their communities and shaping the future they want.


“

There’s an adage in my village that women cannot build a nation. The Women’s Climate Assembly has proved that women build nations. We counter this adage with the unity and solidarity of African women!”

 –

DRC activist-participant


Turning shared struggles into collective power


From communities confronting oil and gas expansion and destructive mining to women defending forests, seeds, water sources and ancestral lands, participants brought forward the lived realities of communities too often excluded from decisions about their territories and futures.


Through collective reflection, popular education and movement-building, women connected struggles that may take place in different countries but are rooted in common systems of exploitation, inequality and environmental destruction.


Designed by women activists and members of the WCA Steering Committee, the thematic teach-ins explored a range of political concepts, questions and practices, including:


The erosion of farmers’ seeds

: A challenge for building resilient and sustainable food systems. What solutions are there for preserving our seed heritage?  


Nature Commons

: The defence of the Congo Basin’s forests.


Counting the Costs of Mal/Bad Development and Demanding reparations

: The case of the African Development Bank campaign.


Fighting some of the false solutions to the climate crisis

: Gas extraction, enclosure of our forests and lands for carbon trading, green conservation and more.


Building democratic, accountable, ‘loving’ leadership

: Why are these principles so important to feminist leadership? What else do we feel is critical to leading as feminists?


Lessons on organising and movement building

: Growing National/sub-regional grassroots movements.


Building knowledge from what we know

: Building feminist popular knowledge as the basis for Building Women’s Power. How can we go about doing this locally in our communities and beyond that.


The WCA celebrated the knowledge, resistance and organising power of rural, Indigenous, peasant and working-class women. The

Each One, Teach One

 sessions embodied this spirit of knowledge-sharing, collective learning and liberation. On Day Two, participants exchanged practical skills, crafts and tools, sharing techniques for making baobab candies, producing eco-briquettes from cassava and creating seed bricks to cultivate and protect Indigenous seeds. Weaving, cloth-dyeing, beadwork and other practices also featured, affirming the value of knowledge held, practised and passed down through generations of women.


The gathering reaffirmed the importance of strengthening a Pan African ecofeminist movement that recognises the connections between the climate crisis, extractivism, gender injustice, food insecurity and the loss of community control over natural resources.


It also reinforced a fundamental principle: communities must have the power to determine their own futures, including the right to say NO to destructive development projects that threaten their lands, livelihoods and ways of life.


Climate justice means reparations, not empty promises
