author: anred
title: Continúa la limpieza étnica palestina: ahora Israel cerca Cisjordania y desplaza a 2 mil personas mientras destruye viviendas en Hebrón
content:
A dos días de las elecciones israelíes, el gobierno de Benjamin Netanyahu lanzó una nueva operación militar en Cisjordania ocupada. El operativo incluye el cerco de Hebrón, detenciones masivas, demoliciones y el desplazamiento forzado de miles de palestinos, bajo el argumento de responder a un ataque de la resistencia palestina. Mientras tanto, los ataques israelíes contra Gaza nunca cesaron, pese al alto el fuego anunciado en octubre de 2025. Por ANRed


El viernes 23 de octubre, dos combatientes palestinos atacaron un puesto de control militar israelí cerca de Hebrón, mataron a dos soldados e hirieron a otros tres. Los dos atacantes también murieron durante el enfrentamiento. El primer ministro israelí, Benjamin Netanyahu, ordenó una operación de gran escala y amenazó con destruir el barrio del que procedían los atacantes.


La ofensiva se concentra en los barrios de Al Jalda y Deir Bahha, en las inmediaciones del puesto de control, y en la zona de Ein Deir Bahha. Las fuerzas israelíes bloquearon accesos, realizaron registros casa por casa y anunciaron demoliciones. Según la Sociedad de Prisioneros Palestinos, para el sábado se habían allanado cientos de viviendas, decenas de ellas convertidas en centros militares de interrogatorio, y unas 70 personas habían sido detenidas en distintas localidades de Cisjordania.


Las cifras de desplazamiento aumentaron en pocas horas. Reuters informó inicialmente de unas 1.200 personas obligadas a abandonar sus hogares. El ministro de Defensa israelí, Israel Katz, reconoció después que alrededor de 2.000 palestinos habían sido desplazados. Este domingo, el diario

Haaretz

 publicó una cifra de 2.231 personas, atribuida a la vicealcaldesa de Hebrón. Las autoridades municipales habían informado, además, del desplazamiento de entre 200 y 300 familias de Deir Bahha y otros cuatro barrios durante la noche del viernes.


El cerco también restringe la circulación de la población palestina. Los controles y las puertas militares impiden el tránsito de vehículos, dificultan el acceso al trabajo y a los hospitales y obligan a las familias a trasladarse a pie. En algunos casos, los residentes debieron abandonar sus casas durante la noche sin poder llevar suficientes pertenencias.


La Autoridad Palestina denunció que estas medidas constituyen un castigo colectivo. La organización israelí de derechos humanos B’Tselem advirtió que la ofensiva podría implicar castigos colectivos y actos constitutivos de crímenes de guerra. El ministro de Finanzas, Bezalel Smotrich, anunció también la demolición de edificios palestinos supuestamente construidos sin permisos, sin demostrar que sus propietarios tuvieran relación con el ataque.


La operación ocurre a apenas dos días de las elecciones israelíes del martes 27 de octubre. Netanyahu y otros referentes de la derecha endurecieron sus declaraciones y prometieron una respuesta contundente contra los palestinos. El analista Amjad Iraqi, del International Crisis Group, señaló que este tipo de anuncios también funciona como una demostración de fuerza dirigida al electorado de derecha y a los colonos israelíes.


Gaza: los ataques nunca cesaron


Mientras la ofensiva avanza en Cisjordania, la Franja de Gaza continúa sufriendo ataques israelíes pese al alto el fuego anunciado el 10 de octubre de 2025. El último informe humanitario de Naciones Unidas, publicado el 19 de octubre, documentó bombardeos, fuego de artillería y disparos entre el 29 de septiembre y el 12 de octubre de 2026.


Según el Ministerio de Salud de Gaza, durante esas dos semanas murieron 57 palestinos y otros 319 resultaron heridos. Con esas cifras, el balance desde el anuncio del alto el fuego ascendía a 1.493 muertos y 5.299 heridos. La ONU también verificó 1.076 muertes relacionadas con el conflicto entre octubre de 2025 y finales de julio de 2026, incluidas 331 personas fallecidas cerca de la denominada «línea amarilla», que delimita zonas bajo control militar israelí.


A la violencia se suma la devastación material y humanitaria. Naciones Unidas estima que unas 950.000 personas desplazadas viven en asentamientos con riesgo medio o alto de inundación. La falta de refugios adecuados, combustible, medicamentos y materiales de reconstrucción agrava las condiciones de vida de una población que sigue sin poder regresar a sus hogares.


De Hebrón a Gaza, los desplazamientos, las demoliciones y los ataques contra zonas habitadas continúan marcando la vida palestina. La nueva ofensiva en …

author: CMI Argentina
title: Elecciones parlamentarias en Serbia: La Lista Estudiantil enfrenta al Gobierno
content:
Protestas contra el gobierno serbio en los días previos a las elecciones parlamentarias


Mario Hernandez


 


En los últimos días se llevaron a cabo distintas protestas en las principales ciudades de Serbia: Belgrado, Novi Sad, Nis, Kragujeva (entre varias otras) fueron testigos nuevamente de manifestaciones de miles de personas contra el gobierno de Aleksandar Vučić. Los manifestantes, la mayoría jóvenes universitarios, se enfrentaron contra la policía .


Paralelamente, la Lista Estudiantil, un movimiento de masas que lleva dos años sacudiendo Serbia con protestas constantes, este domingo presentará a sus propios candidatos a las elecciones parlamentarias y planteará el desafío más serio al que se ha enfrentado Aleksandar Vučić en sus 12 años en el poder


 


Los choques más fuertes se dieron en Vrbas. Lo sucedido en Vrbas generó que se convocaran nuevas movilizaciones en varios puntos del país, en donde se dieron escenas similares y se sumaron múltiples ataques a distintas sedes del partido gobernante, el Partido Progresista Serbio (SNS por sus siglas serbias).


Vučić, a través de sus redes sociales, llamó a la «calma» y a poner fin a la violencia «gratuita» y «completamente injustificada» contra la policía.


Frente a la acusación de la participación de matones progubernamentales en la represión, el ministro de Interior, Ivica Dacic, dijo que estas solo eran grupos de militantes defendiendo las sedes del SNS que fueron agredidos por los manifestantes.


La situación permanece tensa. El presidente serbio, mientras tanto, declaró que «no habrá una guerra civil».


Desde noviembre del año pasado, esta clase de protestas han sido parte de la vida cotidiana del pueblo serbio. Nueve meses en los que el gobierno de Vučic intentó (y falló) en ponerles un freno definitivo y calmar la situación del país.


 


La mayor ola de protestas en la historia de Serbia


 


El sábado 15 de marzo, tuvo lugar en Belgrado la mayor manifestación de la historia de Serbia. Fue la culminación de las actividades del movimiento de protesta estudiantil que ha estado activo desde noviembre del año pasado. «Soy un activista ambiental, así que he estado en muchas protestas. Pero por primera vez en mi vida, vi a personas de izquierda y derecha de pie una al lado de la otra, sin tratar de convencerse mutuamente de nada», dice Tijana, de 25 años y de Belgrado, describiendo el ambiente de la manifestación del sábado 15 de marzo. «Simplemente estaban allí para apoyar a los estudiantes. No he visto tanta tolerancia en muchos años».


Las protestas comenzaron debido a una tragedia que ocurrió en la segunda ciudad más grande, Novi Sad. El techo de un edificio de la estación de ferrocarril recientemente renovado se derrumbó, cobrándose un total de quince vidas. Los manifestantes inmediatamente enmarcaron este suceso como un problema sistémico relacionado con la enorme corrupción y la incompetencia de la administración estatal, rechazando la idea de que fuera un desafortunado accidente.


En noviembre, varias facultades de la Universidad de Belgrado fueron ocupadas en relación con las protestas. Los estudiantes se atrincheraron en los edificios de la universidad, que se convirtieron en los principales lugares donde los manifestantes se reunían y planeaban nuevas estrategias. Los bloqueos se extendieron a otras ciudades universitarias de Serbia, y los estudiantes gradualmente se ganaron a la mayoría de la sociedad serbia. Las decisiones sobre nuevas acciones se toman en sesiones plenarias públicas abiertas al público.


Los estudiantes están procediendo de una manera muy coordinada, no tienen líderes formales y exigen una investigación sobre todo el incidente en Novi Sad, así como cambios más profundos en el sistema político del país. Según la investigadora Nina Djukanović, este es el mayor movimiento de protesta estudiantil desde 1968.


Según la organización sin fines de lucro Archive of Public Gatherings, había casi 300.000 personas en las calles de Belgrado, mientras que los organizadores estudiantiles estimaron el número en 800.000. Las autoridades estatales informaron de cifras significativamente más bajas: según la policía, había 107.000 personas, según el ejército, solo 88.000. Sin embargo, los estudiantes afirman que tales números solo cuentan unas pocas calles y plazas principales.


Incluso según estimaciones moderadas, sería la mayor protesta en la historia del país. «Una gran parte del público esperaba una resolución política desde el …

author: Anikibawal
title: Lof Juan Currin de Temuco enfrenta una nueva orden de desalojo del único predio en reivindicación que queda de su territorio ancestral.
content:
Durante el mes de junio del año 2026, dos integrantes del Lof Juan Currin fueron denunciados ante el Juzgado de Garantía de Temuco por el empresario Pablo Jacobi Bauman por los delitos de Usurpación u ocupación violenta de inmueble, en el único predio que queda de su territorio ancestral, el cual figura en su Titulo de Merced. Los dos lamgen que se encuentran procesados en la causa son Leonardo Catrileo Chiguaihuan y Oscar Chiguaihuan Chiguaihuan, quien cumple el rol de Lonkopalife en su comunidad. Durante el mes de octubre, el lof y en particular, los lamgen Oscar y Leonardo han sido notificados con una orden de desalojo.


Este no es el primer proceso judicial que interpone el empresario en contra de la comunidad, durante el año 2001, Pablo Jacobi anuncio una querella por destrucción de propiedad privada, ante la negativa del Lof Juan Currin a la instalación de un cerco dentro del terreno que pretendía instalar el empresario para materializar un proyecto inmobiliario en el predio. Durante esos años, Mariquina Trecamán, dirigenta de la comunidad declaro que el empresario Jacobi tendría una visión parcial de la historia del conflicto, ya que este se remonta al año 1950, cuando Alfonso Taito Schneider llegó al lugar como arrendatario, donde instaló una fábrica de ladrillos, en palabras de Mariquina Trecamán «Este señor fue designado como tutor de un menor de la comunidad, quien al fallecer ambos padres quedó al desamparo. Valiéndose de esta situación, no sólo se apoderó del terreno del menor, sino que se apropió de casi todo el terreno de la comunidad Juan Currín utilizando distintas maniobras en tribunales» (fuente: https://mapuche.info/archivo/news02/austral010528.html).


El Lof Juan Currin lleva décadas resistiendo en este predio ante la usurpación y despojo de casi la totalidad de su territorio ancestral, arrinconados entre edificios y proyectos inmobiliarios han logrado mantener y preservar sus practiiicas sociales, políticas, culturales y espirituales, espacios ceremoniales como un un Rewe y Paliwe, ademas en el lugar se emplazan viviendas pertenecientes a las familias de la comunidad.


 A continuación, compartimos una declaración del lamgen Oscar Chiguaihuan Chiguaihuan, Lonkopalife de la comunidad:


«Bueno, yo soy Óscar Chiguaihuan. Hace tiempo atrás recibí una denuncia aquí en mi territorio, pertenezco a la comunidad Juan Currín. Hubo una denuncia hace tiempo atrás por usurpación violenta, según yo… le usurpé el territorio a Pablo Jacobi, me acusa de haber puesto un rewe, el rewe era de mi abuela y tiene más de 30 años,… me imagino yo que tiene, yo tengo 35 años… yo me crié ahí, siempre había un rewe ahí y el winka me echa la culpa a mí que yo puse un rewe. No es lógico lo que dice.

Esta comunidad es muy antigua, tengo documentos donde se registra la comunidad, el lof, el título de Merced tiene muchos años, documentos de 1922 hacia estos años, hay documentos de que la comunidad está asentada aquí en este territorio y sin embargo hoy día me acusan a mí de yo usurpar territorio donde yo he sido toda la vida de aquí.


Y pasa que después de la denuncia, hoy día llega otra mala noticia, de que el Winka y sus abogados pidieron una audiencia de urgencia en Fiscalía, no sé cómo se harán esos temas y llegaron un acuerdo de desalojar aquí a la comunidad, digamos, despojarnos de donde tenemos el Rewe, que es un lugar ancestral para nosotros lo tomamos como donde hacemos nuestras ceremonias, jugamos al palín, tenemos nuestra salida hacia digamos hacia la hacia la calle, mi familia circula por aquí todos los días y nos quieren encerrar prácticamente, nos aislarían, no tendríamos salida, nada. No entiendo lo que quieren hacer los Winka, pero nosotros queremos evitarlo realmente porque no sería lógico que nos dejen encerrados, sin salida, ni siquiera caminando.


Entonces pasa que salió la audiencia que pueden desalojarnos y nosotros estamos en contra y queremos apoyo, necesitamos que la gente haga visible todavía como el winka usurpa la tierra, se empeñan en despojarnos de nuestra forma de ser, se niegan a reconocer los que nosotros todavía hacemos, nuestro guillatü, nuestro palines, hacemos ceremonia, celebramos Wetripantü, entonces nos van a despojar de todo eso si logran su acometido los winka. Nosotros como comunidad, digamos, como familia siempre hemos sido afectados, siempre hemos tenido que estar luchando. Yo tengo 35 años, pero hay registro de lucha de mi comunidad mucho más de la edad que tengo yo, hay mucha …

author: Darío Aranda
title: Miguel Mirra: "Cuando la comunidad participa en contar su historia, la recupera para la lucha"
content:
Por Ivana Carino


Desde mediados de la década del 80 Miguel Mirra trabaja una filmografía que recupera lo que suele quedar por fuera del plano de las narrativas industriales: las luchas de los pueblos originarios, los conflictos territoriales y las resistencias socioambientales, entre otros temas. Director de cine, guionista y docente, se formó en historia y antropología antes de pasar por la escuela de cine de Avellaneda.


Nacido en Lanús en 1950, en el seno de una familia de clase trabajadora, Mirra relata su recorrido con calidez, humor y un particular gusto por las anécdotas. Entiende

la cámara como una herramienta de lucha

: no solo para registrar y visibilizar los conflictos, sino también para

construir memoria, poner en circulación experiencias y hacer cine junto a quienes protagonizan esas historias

. Desde

La máscara de la conquista

 (1985)

, hasta sus trabajos más recientes, hay una preocupación que atraviesa su recorrido: que el documental acompañe las resistencias y permita que quienes las protagonizan se reconozcan también en las imágenes.


Foto: Télam


Entre el documental y la ficción


“Llegué al documental porque no sabía hacer otra cosa”, bromea Mirra. En la escuela de cine de Avellaneda había dos vertientes, documental y ficción, y él probó las dos. Su primera realización con equipo completo fue una ficción de época ambientada en la mal llamada "Conquista de América",

La máscara de la conquista

, rodada en 16 milímetros en 1985, con escenas filmadas en Mar del Plata y Córdoba. “Para una escuela era un lujo”, recuerda.


Fue durante ese rodaje cuando comenzó a explorar el cruce entre ambos lenguajes. Había escenas que no sabía cómo resolver y decidió filmarlas como documental: “Les planteé a los actores que siguieran más o menos el guion y las filmamos en el aquí y ahora, donde había sucedido aquello”. El resultado funcionó mejor de lo que esperaba. “Me di cuenta que había quedado bueno”, recuerda. Allí comenzó a descubrir las posibilidades del documental.


Ese descubrimiento tomó forma con

Hombres de barro

, rodada entre 1986 y 1987, y estrenada en 1988. Mirra la define como “el puntapié” de sus trabajos como documentalista. Fue, dice, una experiencia extraordinaria. El equipo, de cinco personas, filmaba en las Sierras de Zenta, en el límite entre Jujuy y Salta, cuando se cruzó con una camioneta en la que uno de sus ocupantes llevaba una cámara. “Nos preguntamos ¿quiénes son estos?”, recuerda. Era Miguel Pereira, que estaba filmando

La deuda interna

 (1988).


A partir de entonces, Mirra fue y vino entre el documental y la ficción. En

Crónica de un extraño

 (1998)

 retomó la historia de Eulogio Frites, abogado kolla y referente del derecho indígena en América, a quien había entrevistado para

Hombres de barro

. Frites le había contado que su familia lo había entregado a la familia administradora de un ingenio, donde pudo estudiar y recibirse de abogado. A partir de esa historia, Mirra construyó un relato de ficción sobre un padre que viaja a Buenos Aires en busca de su hijo, un joven que se había alejado de su comunidad para probar suerte como boxeador. “Hay parte del documental anterior y otras son ficción”, explica.


Pero no todas las historias admiten ese cruce. En sus documentales biográficos sobre Adolfo Pérez Esquivel,

Otro mundo es posible

 (2010);

Darío Santillán,


la dignidad rebelde

 (2012); y

Norita, Nora Cortiñas

 (2013), la ficción no tuvo lugar. En el caso de Santillán, es categórico: “Ahí no correspondía meter ficción. Trabajamos con la gente que lo conoció”.


La exploración de esas formas híbridas continuó con

Fuego en Casabindo

 (2022). Mirra llegó a la historia a partir del descubrimiento de una ópera sobre la rebelión kolla de 1874 en la puna jujeña, cuando unos 2.000 kollas se enfrentaron primero al ejército provincial y luego al nacional, en la

Batalla de Quera

. La investigación lo llevó a escribir un guion que pone en diálogo la ópera con los acontecimientos históricos y construye un personaje ficcional que funciona como nexo entre ambos planos.


La película debía exhibirse en Casabindo, pero antes fue presentada en San Salvador de Jujuy. Mirra recuerda que, cuando estaba por entrar a la sala, vio llegar una columna de personas: eran kollas que iban a verla. Al finalizar la proyección le regalaron un pequeño toro de porcelana. “Es uno de los recuerdos más lindos que tengo de ese momento”, cuenta.


En paralelo, Mirra desarrolló una serie de …

author: La Zarzamora
title: DESPEDIR A JUAN…
content:
Esta mañana nuestro compañero Juan Aliste Vega ha partido de su cuerpo, cuerpo que el poder mantuvo en encierro los últimos 16 años, cuerpo que practicó el conflicto y lo materializó en acciones armadas, que acompañó su vida en el álgido recorrido de ser él. Fue en el hospital penitenciario de Santiago, donde en compañia y calma, se fugó definitivamente.

Aún no podemos confirmar donde ni como será su despedida, ló que sí sabemos es que serán muchas, en muchos territorios, en las calles, en los puentes, en las jaulas, en avenidas y carreteras.

Juan Aliste es y será reivindicado, pese a los esfuerzos incansables de la prensa del enemigo y de sus múltiples intentos de desprestigiarlo, nosotrxs sus compañerxs sabemos que en este momento estamos despidiendo a un guerrero de gran envergadura. Pese a sus miserables conjunciones de palabras, el mundo sabe quien es Juan y en todos los territorios se levantará fuego en su memoria.

Que desesperanza deben sentir los poderosos, al saber que amamos pese a estar en guerra, que nuestra historia es escrita por nosotrxs, pese a sus asquerosos relatos oficiales, tan indignos como ellos mismos.

Hoy es un día de nuestra propia historia, hoy parte el guerrero combatiente que se alzó en armas contra la dictadura y la pestilente democracia de burgueses y traidores, el que no se dejó abatir, el que atacó y acertó, el que siguió compartiendo conocimientos y enseñanzas pese al encierro, el que enviaba notas y saludos, el que hacía llegar sus palabras a actividades y espacios.

Cada vez es más difícil despedir, esto no es una noticia, ni tampoco un comunicado, es nuestro adiós a un hermano…

A nosotrxs ahora nos quedará volver a mirarnos, tensionar el encierro de nuestrxs compañerxs, cuestionarnos y autocriticarnos, dejar de hacernos tolerantes al encarcelamiento, dejar de normalizar la sociedad carcelaria y hacer. Arduo camino nos dejas.

Juan que tu fuga sea eterna querido compañero.

Ternura y ataque frontal por ti y por todxs nuestrxs muertxs.

author: Bruno Fonseca
title: Lula é reeleito presidente do Brasil. Pela 4ª vez. Em virada histórica.
content:
Investigamos o que importa para os brasileiros além do que passa na campanha eleitoral. Leia mais reportagens como essa clicando

aqui

.


Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) foi reeleito presidente do Brasil neste domingo, dia 25 de outubro de 2026. O resultado acontece em um dia de votação extremamente conturbado pela falta de ônibus para eleitores e a ampliação tardia do horário de votação.


A vitória de Lula é histórica: é a primeira vez no período democrático atual que um presidente é reeleito para um quarto mandato. Também é a primeira vez no período recente que um candidato à presidência que estava em segundo lugar no primeiro turno consegue virar o jogo e terminar em primeiro.


Outro fato histórico — e problemático — desde domingo foi a ampliação do horário de votação em duas horas. O presidente do Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF), Cristiano Zanin,

tomou a decisão

 nos minutos finais da votação, após pedidos das campanhas de Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro para que a votação fosse ampliada. O presidente do Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE) Kassio Nunes Marques não ampliou o horário, apesar do Tribunal ter sido acionado muitas horas antes do fim das votações.


O pedido da campanha de Lula se baseou nas inúmeras denúncias de falta de transporte público para que a população votasse em várias cidades do Brasil. Ao longo do domingo, a

Agência Pública


mostrou

 como a redução da oferta de ônibus dificultou o deslocamento dos eleitores.


Em São Paulo, a

Pública


encontrou

 pontos de ônibus lotados e eleitores enfrentando trajetos muito mais longos que o habitual. Um eleitor, ouvido pela reportagem, levou mais de duas horas para percorrer um trajeto que normalmente faria em cerca de 40 minutos e chegou a temer não conseguir votar antes do encerramento previsto para as 17h.


A situação ocorreu apesar de uma determinação para que a cidade mantivesse 100% da frota equivalente à de um dia útil. A denúncia do PT apontou que os ônibus circulavam com cerca de 70% da frota total. A redução do transporte também afetou eleitores que conseguiram votar, mas enfrentavam dificuldades para retornar para casa.


Em Salvador, o problema foi ainda mais explícito. A Secretaria Municipal de Mobilidade confirmou que pelo menos 75 ônibus foram impedidos de sair das garagens depois que foram encontrados adesivos com o número de Lula nos veículos. A apuração do governo estadual chegou a identificar 252 ônibus parados em três garagens.


A redução da frota provocou a reação do TRE-BA. O presidente do tribunal determinou a prisão em flagrante do secretário municipal de Mobilidade, Pablo Souza, que está em Paris. O tribunal também determinou a retomada de 100% dos ônibus, sob pena de multa de R$ 1 milhão por hora.


O prefeito Bruno Reis, responsável pela administração municipal, é aliado da candidatura de Flávio Bolsonaro. No primeiro turno, Lula obteve 65,26% dos votos em Salvador, contra 27,03% de Flávio.


A situação em São Paulo tem paralelo com a de Salvador: Lula também foi o candidato que mais teve votos no 1º turno na cidade. O petista teve quase 300 mil votos a mais que Flávio Bolsonaro na capital paulista, que é o maior colegiado eleitoral do país. Lula se saiu melhor, além do centro da cidade, em bairros da periferia, em especial os mais distantes do centro.

author: Administrador
title: Zapatistische Vorbereitungen für das umarmende Treffen mit den Familien Sucherinnen. Teil II. »Plan D«.
content:
»Die Delegation der Reise für das Leben – Kapitel Mexiko beim Ausüben der bekannten Spielvariante »Gemeinschaftlicher Fußball« oder »Massiver Fußball«. Kein Ball erlitt dabei einen Schaden … die Spieler*innen … nun, Ihr seht es im Video.«

Musik: Cuatro Pesos de Propina: »La Verdadera – Die Wahre« und »El Maleficio – Der Fluch«. Aufnahmen, Bearbeitung, Produktion: Terci@s Compas Zapatistas.

Zapatistische Vorbereitungen für das umarmende Treffen mit den Familien Sucherinnen.

Schwestern, Brüder, Schwestern-Brüder* der Familien Sucherinnen.

Compañeras, Compañeros und Compañeroas.

Comunidad originaria Otomí der Casa de los Pueblos Samir Flores Soberanes.

Wir informieren Euch darüber, dass der sogenannte Plan C gescheitert ist. Wir kommen jetzt nicht, wie wir gesagt haben, mit 1.509, nein, wir kommen nun mit 1.530. Hoffen wir, ein Plan E wird nicht notwendig sein, aber mensch weiß ja nie – nachher kommen welche mit dem Trick an: »Wir sind ja nur zum Abschiednehmen hier« – und steigen dann in die Busse: »Tja, nun seht mal zu«.

Wir haben uns als gesamte Delegation versammelt, um uns gut vorzubereiten und Euch ein gutes Wort der Ermutigung und Unterstützung zu bringen.

Viele* von uns können nicht gut castilla [spanisch]. Unsere Muttersprachen sind Maya-Sprachen. Somit müssen wir auch die vorbereiten, die übersetzen werden – und korrigieren, so weit wir können – damit unser Wort nicht falsch und verdreht herauskommt.

Wir sind froh, weil wir Euch zuhören, mit Euch sprechen, Euch umarmen werden können. Somit praktizieren wir. Lediglich die Umarmungen praktizieren wir nicht [vorher], denn wie Ihr wisst, nachher gibt es auf einmal eine*n Clevere*n, der*die befiehlt, das heißt, profitieren will.

Manchmal spielen wir zusammengeballt Fußball, falls dort [in Mexiko-Stadt] ein Spiel organisiert werden sollte.

Innerhalb der Delegation sind wir:

709 Männer, 622 Frauen und 2 Otroas-AnderE*.

24 des Comando Popcorn: 10 Jungen und 14 Mädchen.

110 der Comunidad Jugendliche Gemeinsam: 66 Männer und 43 Frauen. [Gesamtzahl?]

27 der Koordinierungsequipe: 7 Frauen und 20 Männer.

39 der Miliz [zapatistische zivile Selbstverteidigungsstruktur]: 16 Milicianos und 23 Milicianas.

Bis heute, 18. Oktober 2026, sind es insgesamt, ungefähr, 1.530 Delegierte* sowie verflixte Rasselbande aus Mädchen und Jungen. Somit seht zu.

Für den Moment ist das alles, Compañeras, Compañeroas und Compañeros, Schwestern-Brüder*, Brüder und Schwestern.

Falls es eine Änderung gibt (wir beten, es gibt keine), sagen wir Euch Bescheid. Wir werden Euch weitere Videos schicken, wie wir uns am Vorbereiten sind.

Wir senden Euch unsere gemeinschaftliche Umarmung, darauf hoffend, sie Euch bald persönlich zu geben.

Aus den Bergen des Südosten Mexikos.

Subcomandante Insurgente Moisés. Hauptkoordinator der Reise für das Leben – Kapitel Mexiko.

title: HPG guerrillas: Our decision to join the movement is a commitment to Leader Öcalan’s manifesto
content:
The peace and democratic society process initiated by Abdullah Öcalan on February 27, 2025, has sparked new political debates and discussions about social change within Kurdish society. Young people who have since joined the Kurdish freedom movement also cite the Kurdish leader’s paradigm and his

Peace and Democratic Society Manifesto

 when explaining their decisions.


Two members of the People’s Defense Forces (HPG), Şoreş Botan and Dilsoz Sînornenas, explained their motivations to ANF, speaking about the social circumstances of Kurdish youth, the manifesto’s influence on their political development, and the significance of the peace process for their future path.


Şoreş Botan: The system deliberately targets young people


Şoreş Botan described the social conditions in North Kurdistan as a decisive factor in his decision. His remarks focused on assimilation policies targeting the Kurdish population, the situation of young people, and the political perspectives outlined in the manifesto.


Botan stated the following:


“After the Peace and Democratic Society Manifesto reached the Kurdish people and their youth, it sparked extensive discussions. Its publication had a positive impact on society as a whole. Even before we joined the movement, discussions highlighted that the attacks of special warfare against our society had already begun. These attacks deliberately target young people in North Kurdistan in particular.


Young people are deliberately supplied with drugs on the streets to keep them away from the freedom movement. As a result, we become alienated from the social reality of our people. I witnessed this firsthand. Our aim was to avoid being drawn into this dirty system of genocide.


As Kurdish youth, we did not accept this. We had already adopted this stance before joining the movement. Our culture and language are under attack. In fact, the aim is to eradicate Kurdish society. We could not tolerate this. That is why I also decided to join the movement. The publication of the Peace and Democratic Society Manifesto generated positive momentum within society.


https://video.anf-news2.com/cdn77/firat/20261023161654_2026-10-23-behdinan-sores-botan-hpg-gerillasi-baris-ve-demokratik-toplum-manifestosu-uzerine-rop-1.mp4


Leader Apo [Abdullah Öcalan] has been held under severe isolation for 27 years. This system of isolation is unacceptable. Even before joining the movement, we opposed the existing system. Leader Apo initiated a process two years ago. Subsequently, the manifesto was written and made available to the Kurdish people. This had a very positive impact on society. Following its publication, our goal as Kurdish society became to respond appropriately to Leader Apo’s call through our struggle.


When one studies the manifesto in depth, it becomes clear that Leader Apo provides answers to all social problems and develops appropriate solutions. I continue to read his writings to properly understand his ideas and grasp the depth of his perspective. I regard my decision to join the movement as one made following the publication of the Peace and Democratic Society Manifesto. My efforts and struggle are aimed at living up to my leader’s expectations and supporting it.


With the publication of the manifesto, the women’s struggle has come even more prominently to the forefront, both as a social issue and in terms of its development. This has also become evident in various areas of the struggle. The manifesto has influenced the women’s struggle and society in many ways. The women’s struggle continues to expand day by day. We are convinced that the struggle and leading role of women will be further strengthened through the Peace and Democratic Society Manifesto. Leader Apo wants women to assume a leading role in society and throughout the world. Our struggle is also developing on this basis.


Kurdish youth in particular should engage with the social realities addressed in the Peace and Democratic Society Manifesto and make greater efforts to read and understand it. In this way, it can also have a positive impact on them. We call on Kurdish youth to read the manifesto themselves and engage with Leader Apo’s ideas. This is what we expect from Kurdish youth.”

author: Brian Hioe
title: Labor Groups Seek to Put Demands on Agenda Ahead of Election
content:
TAIWAN HAS SEEN a number of labor demonstrations in recent weeks.

A strike by workers at iconic snack Kuai Kuai’s Zhongli factory came to an end after five days earlier this month. Kuai Kuai is an iconic snack best known for a superstition that keeping bags of it near machinery keeps them running smoothly. Kuai Kuai operates one factory in Taoyuan, but 130 out of 155 union members voted in favor of a strike after the company decided to relocate to Hsinchu.

The two sites are 39 kilometers from each other, meaning that the move is untenable for many workers. Workers were only informed of the land scale on September 1st. According to the Ministry of Labor, the move was not expected for another two years. The factory has operated in Zhongli since 1968, and 1/3rd of workers at Kuai Kuai have worked there for more than thirty years, despite the fact that their wages are near minimum wage.

Though workers initially voted only for a one-day strike, the action was later extended indefinitely. After the strike, workers won four months’ wages plus severance pay if they are reassigned in the Zhongli factory and eight months’ wages plus severance pay if they have to leave their jobs because of the planned reassignment to Hsinchu and resign by September 30, 2028. Workers with twelve years of experience under the labor pension system will receive a further 100,000 NT. Kuai Kuai has stated that it will not lay off workers for two years and that workers who are laid off afterward will receive two months’ wages.

Workers have accused the San-Ti Group that owns Kuai Kuai of perhaps having only acquired the company with an eye on selling its land to Advanced Semiconductor Engineering Inc. Originally, Kuai Kuai workers were only offered a 5% pay increase and verbal assurances that they would be relocated to the new factory. It is to be seen if acquiring land to sell it to technology companies is a tactic increasingly adopted in corporate acquisitions going forward.

To this extent, migrant worker groups have criticized Singaporean company Sheffield Green and Indonesian company PT Kepodang Makmur Sejahtera, both offshore wind manufacturers, of violating the contracts of Indonesian migrant workers. Specifically, despite being skilled workers as fitters, such workers signed contracts that promised pay of 48,000 NT per month, but were later only paid between 100 NT and 143 NT per month. Such groups demonstrated earlier this month.

Such workers were part of projects run by Taiwanese company Century Energy Co., Ltd., but Century Energy has skirted responsibility by stating that it had no responsibility over contracts signed between workers and foreign contractors under a “contract performance” system that allows the company to bring over foreign workers to be part of projects. Under this system, the Indonesian workers were paid less than the minimum salary in the Labor Standards Act.

In response to such criticism, the Ministry of Labor has stated that it will step up inspections. It is to be seen if this actually takes place.

Likewise, the May 1 Action Alliance–a coalition of labor groups–demonstrated outside of the Executive Yuan on October 13th to call for employers to increase the amount of money they contribute to worker pensions. The Action Alliance cited that the mandatory employer contribution rate had remained at 6% since the current pension system was introduced in 2005, though expectations were originally that the rate would increase. As such, calls by labor groups were for the contribution rate to increase to at least 12%.

Though Lai Ching-te had previously pledged to increase the contribution rate as a campaign pledge, there has not yet been action on the issue.

The demonstration was followed up by another demonstration on October 19th. Labor groups, including the Taoyuan Confederation of Trade Unions, Chunghwa Telecom Union, and other organizations, pledged to strike if their demands were not met, calling for higher wages and an increase in employer contributions to worker pensions.

It is to be if labor becomes a campaign issue ahead of elections next month, then. This does not look likely at present, unless candidates are seeking new issues to brand themselves with, but it can be expected that labor groups will seek to pressure the government on the matter.

author: Kodao Productions
title: A hollow victory: On the SC decision declaring parts of the 2024-2026 budgets unconstitutional
content:
By

Atty. Ephraim B. Cortez


In a recent decision, the Supreme Court declared the Unprogrammed Appropriation in the 2024, 2025, and 2026 General Appropriations Acts (GAA) unconstitutional. The Court found that Congress and the Bicameral Conference Committee committed grave abuse of discretion amounting to a lack or excess of jurisdiction for the following reasons:


The grant of authority to avail of the Unprogrammed Appropriation by the mere existence of any excess revenues from a specific source without considering the aggregate amount of revenue generated from all other sources is unconstitutional.


The pertinent provision of the GAA providing the condition for availment states:


“1. Availment of the Unprogrammed Appropriations. The amounts authorized herein for purpose Nos. 2-4,6, and 9-10 may be used when any of the following exists:


“a. Excess revenue collections in any of the identified non-tax revenue sources from its corresponding revenue collection target, as reflected in the Budget of Expenditures and Sources of Financing (BESF);


“b. New revenue collections or those arising from new tax or non-tax sources which are not part of, nor included in, the original revenue sources reflected in the BESF;


“c. Approved loans for foreign-assisted projects.


As written, any excess revenue triggers the availment of the Unprogrammed Appropriations. However, in Araullo v. Aquino III, the Supreme Court held that Unprogrammed Appropriations may be used only after aggregate revenue collections from all sources exceed the projections in the BESF. They are not intended to be activated “when individual revenue sources exceed their targets or when new revenue sources become available.”


The Supreme Court emphasized that Unprogrammed Appropriations serve as standby authority and should be “deficit neutral.” Therefore, they may be used only after the budgetary deficit for Programmed Appropriations has been addressed.


They gave the executive department the discretion to allocate excess revenues to Unprogrammed Appropriation without providing sufficient standards to limit the exercise of such discretion.


Under the GAA, the availment of the Unprogrammed Appropriation is triggered by the mere existence of excess in revenue collections in any of the “non-tax revenue collection target” as indicated in the Budget of Expenditures and Sources of Financing (BESF), or revenue collections in any from new tax or non-taxes which are not included in the sources of revenues under the BESF. It is apparent from the language of the provision that once any of the two conditions exist, the executive department is given the authority and the discretion to determine how to allocate excess revenues for the implementation of the Unprogrammed Appropriations.


As explained by Supreme Court, we are running on an unbalanced budget, meaning the projected expenditures are usually in excess of the projected revenues. As such, if there are revenues generated in excess of the projected revenues, the same should be allocated to fill the revenue deficit for the Programmed Appropriations. The Unprogrammed Appropriations are merely a standby authority which cannot be prioritized over that of the Programmed Appropriations.


Under the subject GAAs, the executive department is given the discretion to prioritize Unprogrammed Appropriations over that of the Programmed Appropriations in the allocation of excess revenues.


Congress did not define the parameters and provide for sufficient standards on how excess revenues should be allocated for Unprogrammed Appropriations. This is tantamount to an undue delegation of power, and the President is given the unbridled discretion to allocate such excess revenues.


They increased the total national budget or the total appropriations proposed by the President in violation of the provisions of Art. VI, Sec. 25 (1) of the 1987 Constitution.


The Supreme Court clarified that “Appropriations” in contemplation of Sec. 29, (1), Art. VI of the 1987 Constitution refers to any legislated allocation of a “determinate or determinable amount of money” for a “particular public purpose.” It covers both “programmed” and “unprogrammed appropriations which are both subject to the same constitutional standards and limitations. As such, the limitation imposed by Art. VI, Sec. 25 (1) of the 1987 is likewise applicable to Unprogrammed Appropriations.

author: groundxero
title: The Twilight of Trumpism
content:
Contemporary Trumpism is not the conservative attempt to return US society back to the 1950s. It is the attempt to return US society back to the 1850s – an attempt which will fail completely, disastrously and totally.


 


By 

Dionysius


 


Between 2016 and 2026, the political system of the United States has been dominated by Trumpism, a.k.a. the US variant of billionaire fascism or plutofascism. Its domination was so complete that even when non-Trumpist politicians won elections, they did not question Trumpism’s single most compelling argument. This argument, in a nutshell, was that the United States could solve the 21st century problems of a

collapsing middle class

 and

an economy being looted by billionaire monopolists

 by a magical return to 19th century tariff walls, territorial imperialism and settler colonialism.


 


The year 2026 marks the moment when a majority of US citizens have stopped believing in 19th century magic. One of the most telling signs of this shift occurred on October 9, 2026, when Pete Hegseth, the Trumpist official in charge of the US military, announced that the US would broadcast the execution of a former US soldier on live television.


 


Hegseth had fully expected the announcement would create a wave of hurrah-patriotism. After all, the soldier in question, a former US Army major, had shot and killed 13 fellow soldiers and wounded 30 others at a military base in Fort Hood, Texas in 2009. The soldier also happened to be Muslim and the US-born son of Palestinian American immigrants, two groups which have been constantly scapegoated and persecuted by Trumpism.


 


Instead, the announcement triggered a firestorm of condemnation. Numerous former soldiers and Pentagon officials criticized the announcement as tantamount to a lynching, while human rights advocates pointed out that the only two countries which hold public executions are Taliban-ruled Afghanistan and theocrat-ruled Iran. Ten days later, overwhelming political pressure forced the Trump administration to back down and

call off the broadcast

.


 


To understand why Hegseth misread the situation so badly and why this moment is so significant, it is worth pausing for a moment to reflect on the group which forms the electoral core of Trumpism. This group consists of white males who are nostalgic for the settler colonial white masculinity which dominated US politics for almost two hundred years, i.e. between the creation of the US in 1783 and the civil rights and feminist struggles of the 1960s and early 1970s.


 


To understand why this group wants to return to the past, we must first understand that this white masculinity was responsible for 105 years of settler colonial land theft and genocide against the First Nations of North America. This period began with the 1785-1795 Northwest Indian War, and ended in the Wounded Knee Massacre in South Dakota committed by US soldiers against the Lakota people on December 29, 1890. Most of the surviving First Nations were confined to reservations thereafter, and none enjoyed full US citizenship rights until the Snyder Act of 1924.


 


This white masculinity was also crucial to perpetrating the horrors of 82 years of US chattel slavery (1783-1865) on African Americans and citizens kidnapped from Africa by slave traders. After the abolition of slavery in 1865, this white masculinity engineered systems of legal apartheid (commonly called “Jim Crow” laws) which privileged whites at the expense of African Americans. In addition to these laws, many US states had groups of white terrorists who regularly assaulted and murdered African Americans. The most notorious of these terrorists were the Klu Klux Klan, an organization so powerful that as late as August 12, 1925, an estimated 30,000 of their members marched openly through the US capital of Washington, DC without any legal repercussions whatsoever.


 


Official Jim Crow and unofficial racial terror ruled large parts of the US for 87 years (i.e. 1878-1965). They did not disappear until the 1965 Voting Rights Act granted African Americans the right to vote in all US states, and until Federal law enforcement agencies cracked down on white terrorist groups during the 1960s and 1970s.

author: Daniel Aloc
title: Ganggang ni JL Burgos bilang salamin ng lipunan
content:
Natatangi ang karanasan ng mga batang lumalaki sa kanayunan, malayo sa kalunsuran na may madaling access sa teknolohiya. Sa pagitan ng pagpasok sa paaralan at paglalaro sa mga burol at parang—kabilang na ang paghahanap ng mga gagambang panlaban sa kapwa gagamba—unti-unti nilang natututuhan ang mga realidad ng mundong kanyang ginagalawan. May nananalo, may natatalo; may nambubully, at may napipilitan lumaban upang hindi na lamang manatiling api.

Ngunit paano kung ang mga larong kinalakihan nila ay naging daan upang maaga silang mamulat sa karahasang umiiral sa lipunan? Paano kung ang mga batang dapat sana ay malayang naglalaro ay maagang nahaharap sa dahas, takot, at pang-aabuso.

Ilan lamang ito sa mga tanong na sinisikap sagutin ng Ganggang, ang kauna-unahang full-length narrative film ni JL Burgos, na unang ipinalabas sa Cinemalaya noong Agosto. Nitong Oktubre 21 ko lamang ito napanood sa Cinematheque Centre Manila, na ngayo’y matatagpuan sa bagong tahanan nito sa Philippine Film Heritage Building sa Intramuros, bilang bahagi ng Pelikula ng Bayan: Cinemalaya 22.

Hindi na katakataka ang tema at paksang tinatalakay ng pelikula, lalo na’t ang gumawa nito ay isang filmmaker na matagal nang nakatuon sa usapin ng karapatang pantao. Bago ang Ganggang, nakilala na si Burgos sa mga dokumentaryong Portraits of Mosquito Press at Alipato at Muog (2024). Ang huli ay nagwagi ng Best Picture, Best Documentary, at Best Editing sa ika-48 Gawad Urian noong 2025.

Hindi isang bagong proyektong biglaang nabuo ang Ganggang kasunod ng tagumpay ng Alipato at Muog. Ayon kay Burgos, isinulat niya ang kwento noon pang 2019. Sa halip na talikuran ang mga isyung matagal na niyang tinalakay sa kanyang mga dokumentaryo, pinili niyang ilahad ang mga ito sa pamamagitan ng naratibo ng isang pelikula—sa lente ng mga batang hindi pa lubusang nauunawaan ang bigat ng mga puwersang humuhubog sa kanilang buhay.

Sa pelikula, sina Ilay (Kenneth “Butchoy” Vincent Mendoza), Ten-ten (Don Rishmond Cerbito), at Mel (Raine Dela Cruz) ay tatlong batang naging magkaibigan sa paghahanap ng gagambang panlaban sa gagamba ni Anton (Prince Nathaniel España), ang bully sa kanilang paaralan. May kanya-kanyang pinagmulan ang tatlong bata. Anak ng isang desaparecido si Ilay, anak ng magsasaka si Ten-ten, at anak na naman ng isang sundalo si Mel.

Sa unang tingin, ang Ganggang ay isang pamilyar na bahagi ng pagkabata sa maraming pamayanan sa bansa. May tuwa sa paghahanap ng gagamba at sa pananabik na makita kung alin ang mananaig. Ngunit isa itong alegorya ng isang lipunang tila nakondisyon nang maniwala na kailangang maglaban-laban ang mamamayan upang mabuhay.

Sa talkback at Q&A session matapos ang screening, ipinaliwanag ni Burgos ang kahulugan ng tunggalian ng mga gagamba. Hindi naman likas sa mga ito ang mag-away sa paraang nakikita sa laro; inilalagay sila ng tao sa sitwasyong kailangan nilang magpatayan. Katulad ng mga mamamayang napipilitang mag-unahan at maglaban sa isang sistemang pinaghaharian ng iilan.

Sentrong usapin ng pelikula ang militarisasyon sa kanayunan. Binabago ng presensya ng mga sundalo ang pang-araw-araw na buhay ng mga residente, kabilang ang mga guro at magsasakang itinuturing na mga miyembro o tagasuporta ng New People’s Army (NPA) dahil lamang sa kanilang mga paninindigan.

Bukod sa karahasan at paglabag sa karapatang pantao na iniuugnay sa estado, ipinakikita rin nito ang epekto ng karahasan sa mga bata at kanilang pamilya.

Mahalagang banggitin na ang ilan sa mga karakter at eksena sa pelikula ay hango sa mga tunay na tao at pangyayari.

Isa rito si Rebelyn, ang gurong karakter sa pelikula na hango kay Rebelyn Pitao, anak ni Leoncio Pitao, na mas kilala bilang Commander Parago ng NPA sa Davao. Noong 2009, dinukot si Rebelyn at natagpuan ang kanyang bangkay kinabukasan. Ayon sa ulat ng Commission on Human Rights, ang biktima ay may mga saksak sa dibdib at iba pang palatandaan ng matinding tortyur. Ang sinapit ni Rebelyn ay isang paalala na ang mga taong hindi naman aktwal na nakikidigma ay maaari pa ring maging target ng estado.

Ang plaka naman ng sasakyang ipinakikita sa unang bahagi ng pelikula ay kapareho ng plaka ng sasakyang ginamit sa pagdukot sa kapatid ng direktor na si Jonas Burgos sa isang mall sa Quezon City noong 2007. Hanggang ngayon, hindi pa natatagpuan si Jonas.

Hango rin sa mga tunay na pangyayari ang eksenang nire-red-tag ng isang opisyal ng militar ang gurong si Rebelyn at ang kaniyang mga kasama bilang mga rebelde …

author: rti_admin
title: The Ahmedabad Reading Controversy and the Freedom to Read
content:
Who gets to decide what we should read? The question arose sharply in Ahmedabad this August, when two books were removed from a school reading list, and a silent reading session was later disrupted.

In August, an Ahmedabad school removed Malala Yousafzai’s I Am Malala and Anne Frank’s The Diary of a Young Girl from its reading list after objections from some parents and protests involving right-wing organisations. Later that month, a silent reading session organised in Vastrapur was reportedly disrupted by a group claiming affiliation with the Vishwa Hindu Parishad and Bajrang Dal. The gathering included students, lawyers, media professionals and others. The reading itself became the object of confrontation.

I Am Malala is the memoir of a girl who survived an assassination attempt after publicly advocating girls’ right to education. The Diary of a Young Girl records the experiences of a Jewish teenager hiding from Nazi persecution before Anne Frank died during the Holocaust. Whatever one thinks of Malala’s political views, or of the ways her story is interpreted, reading her memoir does not require accepting every view she holds. Anne Frank’s diary similarly allows readers to encounter the testimony of a young person caught inside one of history’s greatest crimes.

A book is not a political membership card.

Reading allows a person to encounter an argument without accepting it. A reader can examine its evidence, question its assumptions and reject its conclusions. The point is that judgement becomes possible through encounter.

Education is often described as the transmission of knowledge. But knowledge without the capacity to question it can become another form of conformity.

This question of who may read and what they may encounter carries a specific weight in the Indian context. For much of India’s history, access to formal education was deeply shaped by caste hierarchy. Ambedkar wrote that under the Chaturvarna system, the right to education was assigned to the Brahmins, Kshatriyas and Vaishyas, while Shudras were denied it. He also discussed the denial of education to women. The control of education was therefore connected to the wider system of graded inequality that Ambedkar analysed.

This was one of the structures challenged by Jyotirao and Savitribai Phule. Jyotirao and Savitribai Phule opened a school for girls in Pune in 1848, and Phule later set up schools for the Mahars and Mangs. In his 1882 testimony before the Education Commission, Phule criticised the concentration of education among the higher classes and called for a wider spread of primary and female education. His educational work treated access to knowledge as a social question rather than a privilege confined to a small section of society.

Dr B.R. Ambedkar’s conception of democracy makes this problem especially important. In Annihilation of Caste, he imagined an ideal society with “varied and free points of contact with other modes of association” and described democracy as “a mode of associated living.” For Ambedkar, fraternity was not sameness. It required people to participate in a common social world despite their differences. His writings on the Depressed Classes emerged from a context in which these communities faced restrictions on access to public wells and schools, and were subjected to social segregation and prescribed occupations. The “associated living” he imagined presupposes that those who were once excluded from classrooms are now full participants in the world of ideas.

A democratic society cannot expect citizens to form independent judgements while continually narrowing the range of ideas they are permitted to encounter. The democratic reader needs the freedom to examine an argument before deciding whether it deserves acceptance, rejection or further examination.

John Dewey understood education as inseparable from democratic life. For Dewey, democracy depended on communication, inquiry and shared experience. He saw education as a way of preparing people to participate intelligently in common life.

Not every book belongs in every classroom. Parents can question reading lists, teachers can challenge texts, and schools can make decisions about age, pedagogy and context. Citizens can protest. A democratic society must leave room for disagreement over education. The important distinction is between arguing that a book should not be taught and intimidating people who choose to read it. The first concerns the content and …

author: Sarah Raymundo
title: On liberal opportunism and the “purity” smear
content:
Photo from Naga City Tourism Facebook page

Accusing leftists and activists of demanding a “useless politics of purity” is a classic liberal defense mechanism designed to shift the burden of moral failure onto the critic.

Why did former Vice President and now Naga City Mayor Leni Robredo roll out the pink carpet for the Zionist war machine? When Robredo hosted Israeli Ambassador Dana Kursh for an official courtesy visit, she was not merely performing the routine gestures of local hospitality. She was actively welcoming and legitimizing representatives of the US-Israeli genocidal apparatus. This intervention centers an anti-imperialist analysis to dismantle the liberal apologetics surrounding this act. Rather than an isolated error in judgment, this diplomatic encounter exposes the persistent, foundational tension within the Philippine political landscape: the contradiction between liberal reformism and anti-imperialist national liberation.

Dismissing progressives’ critique of Robredo’s hosting of the Israeli envoy as mere “political purism” is politically and morally impoverished. The underlying mechanism demands a total, systematic critique. To understand why her defenders deploy the “politics of purity” accusation, and why that defense completely falls apart when examining real power dynamics and economic interests, we must lay bare both the liberal class position and the ideological sleight of hand at work.

To make sense of Robredo’s pivot toward imperial hospitality, we must look directly at the liberal class position. Her stance is neither an accidental misstep nor a personal failure of political intelligence but the direct expression of her class character and political alignment. Liberal reformism in the global periphery operates strictly within the legal, institutional, and geopolitical framework dictated by US imperialism.

While Robredo served as a focal point against the overt state terrorism of the Marcos-Duterte dynasties, her opposition was strictly intra-class—a feud over how to manage the neocolonial state, pitting rule-of-law decorum against autocratic violence.

Because her political legitimacy rests upon acceptance by the global capitalist order, her opposition stops at the border of imperial interest. When forced to choose between international solidarity with an anti-imperialist national liberation movement and alignment with the Washington-Tel Aviv axis, liberal reformists invariably side with the imperial core. They cannot critique the drain of value, the extraction of labor, or the military hegemony of US imperialism because their entire political project depends on remaining within that very apparatus.

This structural subservience explains why defenders deploy the “purity politics” weapon whenever that alignment is exposed. Accusing leftists and activists of demanding a “useless politics of purity” is a classic liberal defense mechanism designed to shift the burden of moral failure onto the critic. From a materialist standpoint, this argument relies on three ideological fallacies:

First, it replaces a materialist baseline with ideological absolution. Opposition to active genocide, ethnic cleansing, and imperialist aggression is not a performative or elevated ideological standard; it is the absolute baseline of human solidarity and anti-imperialist struggle. Labeling principled opposition to mass slaughter as “purity” redefines baseline morality as an unreasonable demand, attempting to pass off complicity as pragmatic maturity.

Second, it operates on the logic of liberal idealism, which treats political stances as abstract moral choices made in a vacuum. Political actions reflect concrete class interests. Shielding a public figure from accountability for legitimizing a settler-colonial state serves a specific political function: it conditions the middle forces to accept imperial violence as a routine, acceptable feature of global diplomacy.

Third, it trades scientific alignment for unprincipled unity. Transformative praxis distinguishes between principled unity—built on anti-imperialist struggle and mass interest—and unprincipled unity, which colludes with reaction to preserve electoral coalitions. Demanding that the progressive movement remain silent on international solidarity to protect a liberal politician’s image trades human rights and anti-imperialist consciousness for temporary electoral expediency.

author: chuang
title: “Every War Is a World War”: Interview with a Member of Taiwan Alliance for a Free Palestine
content:
The following is an interview with friends from Taiwan who have formed the umbrella coalition Taiwan Alliance for a Free Palestine (TWAFP). The interview includes an overview of the rifts in the Taiwanese left, and the frustration of TWAFP organizers carving out their place amid divisions between pro-unification and independence, or pro- and anti-American positions, in the contentious and highly polarized politics on the island.


The organizer recounts their efforts to confront Taiwan’s growing ties with Israel and direct support for the genocide in Palestine. They speak with sadness that, even as Taiwan is now the fourth-largest supplier of arms to Israel, surpassing mainland China, most Taiwanese care little for the distant genocide and the struggle in Palestine seems far away. And yet, TWAFP has led successful demonstrations, pulled together a broad coalition of disparate groups in support of Palestine, and conducted research to expose Taiwan’s complicity in the ongoing genocide.


Be sure to read their

report


from 2025, outlining specific pathways of material component support for Israel, including radar, armor, and an array of military hardware.


See also a recent

piece

 submitted to us, outlining Taiwan’s deepening ties with Israel under the DPP government.


–

Chuang


Q: To begin, let’s just set the stage. Over the last few years, the Taiwan Alliance for a Free Palestine (TWAFP) has helped to organize the largest mobilizations against the genocide in Palestine seen in Taiwan. Can you tell us a little about how TWAFP formed and maybe review some of the protests it has organized?


A:

Taiwan Alliance for a Free Palestine (TWAFP)

 was founded in April of 2024. Prior to this, Taiwan had already seen several groups doing Palestine advocacy work arise spontaneously, including Palestine Action Front, Taiwan Palestine Solidarity Network, and Parallel Government. As its name suggests, TWAFP is an “Alliance” that brings together groups that were already involved in initiatives related to Palestine. In addition to the three groups already mentioned, the alliance also includes a migrant worker organization, the

Taiwan International Workers’ Association (TIWA)

; the human rights organization, Taiwan Association for Human Rights; the cultural collective, Taiwan Rave & Punk Solidarity Front for Palestine; the gender issues group, Queer Margins; and the Christian group, Taiwan Olive Branch Peace Collective. From 2024 to today, we have organized one petitioning campaign, issued two open letters, held one candlelight vigil, hosted one book club meeting, staged five protest actions, held three press conferences, and organized three marches. In the future, we plan to engage in a number of other activities, many of which may be smaller in scale.


Q: TWAFP also did some very interesting research on material links between Taiwan and Israel. We can link to the report here, but can you briefly go over the main findings, and maybe go over any new information that you’ve found since that report was released? For example, have there been more details since then?

      


A: In September of 2025, we released our report,

Taiwanese Companies’ Complicity in Israel’s Ongoing Genocide

, which identified specific manufacturers assisting Israel in the production of military weapons, including via the production of components. For example: Gloria Material Technology Corp (GMTC) supplies superalloys and high-grade steel produced through electroslag remelting, while ADLINK Technology supplies embedded computing systems and industrial-grade computers. In another case, Transcom marketed its vertically integrated capabilities—spanning chip design to module production—to enter the Israeli defense supply chain and is now a key, long-term supplier of components for the EL/M-2084 multi-mission radar, which is a core element of the Israeli “Iron Dome” air defense system designed by Israeli defense company Elta.

author: Unknown
title: Camcı: Urban Commune must be established to combat poverty
content:
Deep poverty in Diyarbakır (Amed) is reflected in unemployment, precarious working conditions, food insecurity and difficulties accessing basic necessities. According to 2024 data from the Ministry of Family and Social Services, 196,530 households in the city received social assistance, with the total amount reaching 4.47 billion Turkish lira. These figures reveal that poverty is not merely a matter of individual income loss but a structural problem affecting different aspects of social life.


Field research conducted in the Bağlar and Sur districts of Diyarbakır also reveals the tangible effects of deep poverty on neighbourhoods. Approximately 93 per cent of the women who participated in the research reported reducing their food purchases, while 95 per cent said they had cut spending on clothing. Many families are forced to take on debt to meet their basic needs.


Children living in damp homes affected by water leaks and inadequate heating are reportedly experiencing health problems. The fact that 196,530 households in Diyarbakır received social assistance in 2024 further illustrates the scale of poverty across the city.


Mehmet Şerif Camcı, former chair of the Sarmaşık Association, which was shut down by a Decree-Law (KHK), said that poverty was rooted in the economic policies pursued by the state in Kurdistan over the past century. He stressed that the solution could not be reduced to distributing aid. Camcı called for the establishment of an “Urban Commune” in the city to carry forward the principles and vision of the Sarmaşık Association.


‘State policies are deepening poverty’


Şerif Camcı discussed the reasons why poverty has become increasingly visible in the city, stressing that the problem cannot be understood solely in terms of unemployment and inadequate social support. While acknowledging the global dimensions of poverty, Camcı said that state economic policies were the decisive factor in Kurdistan and Diyarbakır.


Camcı said, “The primary factor deepening poverty in Kurdistan is policies created by human intervention, or more precisely, by the state. Poverty is, of course, a global problem. Another major cause lies in the choices made by capitalist modernity regarding production and distribution. However, what gives poverty its particular character and depth in Kurdistan, and especially in Diyarbakır, is the economic policies that the state has pursued in Kurdistan for the past century.”


‘After Sarmaşık, people were left at the mercy of the state's charity culture’


Camcı said that the closure of the Sarmaşık Association by decree-law had left a significant gap in the city's solidarity networks. He stressed that the association had not merely provided support to people in need but had also developed a model that strengthened social solidarity. Camcı also addressed the social consequences of capitalist relations of production and distribution: “Capitalist relations of production and distribution do not merely produce negative economic consequences. They also erode society's moral foundations, weaken its political reflexes and render people passive and powerless. The most important aspect of the Sarmaşık experience was that it enabled citizens to support one another through solidarity. At the same time, through the model and methods it developed, it helped turn solidarity and a sense of collective responsibility into a shared public consciousness capable of resisting the forces that undermine society.”


Camcı said that the closure of the association had weakened the ability of the city's poor to organise on the basis of solidarity. Criticising existing social assistance mechanisms, he continued: “After Sarmaşık, the urban poor were deprived of their capacity for self-defence. They were pushed back into the traditional relationship between the state and its citizens and left at the mercy of the state's culture of charity. Through its charity-based practices and the handouts it presents as support, the state is effectively telling people: ‘You depend on me. You can only survive through the assistance I provide.’”


‘An Urban Commune should be established based on Sarmaşık's principles’


Camcı also discussed the responsibilities of local authorities, civil society organisations, professional associations and the business community in combating poverty. He stressed that these actors should not confine their efforts to mechanisms that simply distribute aid.

author: Brian Hioe
title: Political Parties Spar Over Taiwan’s Demographic Woes
content:
THE KMT HAS hit out at the DPP’s failure to correct Taiwan’s demographic woes, crticizing the decline in the national population. According to the National Development Council, Taiwan’s population is expected to fall below 20 million by 2045. Taiwan’s population is expected to halve by 2075.

Specifically, the KMT has made a new savings plan it proposed that the DPP rejected, the Taiwan Youth Development and Future Account Act, as proof that the DPP does not care about the issue. The act would have allocated an “Education and Development Account” and “Taiwan Future Account” to each child, the former of which would be able to be used at any time, and the latter of which would be accessible at age 18. 60,000 NT would be provided to each child per year under the proposal. The KMT has also hit out at the inability of the government to construct more social housing.

Nevertheless, one notes that the DPP rejected the Taiwan Youth Development and Future Account Act on the basis that it, in allowing for corporate sponsors, it could increase the gaps in inequality. The DPP has instead proposed a similar proposal that would also allow for 60,000 NT to be allocated to each child annually.

Otherwise, one notes that the DPP plans to increase subsidies for housing, education, and childcare, with particular efforts to spread costs between the government and families in childcare. Likewise, the DPP has stated that it intends to extend the amount of parental leave that can be subsidized to nine months, extend maternity leave to 12 weeks, extend marriage leave to 14 days, and increase the amount of leave that a husband can take to accompany his spouse to prenatal examinations to 14 days.

More generally, the approach would be to increase existing subsidies while extending existing leave programs. Nevertheless, one imagines that the KMT would have more or less adopted the same approach if it were in power–there is little difference between the two major parties when it comes to the political imagination of how to solve Taiwan’s declining birthrate.

Indeed, more generally, both major parties are unwilling to make the larger systematic changes that would allow for such issues to be solved. For example, there continues to be widespread reluctance to open up Taiwanese society to immigrants, with Taiwan only allowing blue-collar migrant workers to come here as individuals, without their families, and also not allowing blue-collar migrant workers to stay in Taiwan beyond twelve or fourteen years.

To this extent, Taiwan’s issues with a declining birthrate often stem from social pressures on newly expectant parents–especially mothers–issues that cannot be solved through simply throwing money at the issue. In this sense, Taiwan’s declining birthrate is likely only to be a political issue used by both sides to hit out at each other, rather than that either side of the political aisle would seriously consider solutions.

author: Kodao Productions
title: Lesson for Sara: Fools destroy nations
content:
By this time, and no thanks to the daily *argle-bargle of the Sara Zimmerman Duterte Carpio camp and its troll army that conditions the minds of their listeners and leaders that truth is expendable and they should only believe what Sara tells them. This attitude harks back to Hannah Arendt’s thesis on totalitarianism, that fascists brainwash people not to believe objective reality and instead eat the **guff of Sara. Arendt, a German philosopher of Jewish extraction, could not persuade her lover, fellow philosopher Martin Heidegger, to denounce Nazism.


Sara Zimmerman Duterte Carpio is a demagogue in the tradition of Nazi demagoguery but her handlers, reputedly corpulent intellectuals and ex-Rasputins to a corrupt, unlamented regime, continue to ***brown nose her and lavish her with praise and other forms of irrationality. They should all be reminded of Winston Churchill’s counsel: “The difference between humans and animals is that animals never allow a fool to lead the pack.” Sara is one such fool for wasting four long years, many of the time overseas, in showing that she’s got what it takes to lead the pack.


Analysts blame not her mercurial style but a deeper problem of not understanding what her role as vice president really is. Her mood swings, her ignorance about issues that affect the country deeply, like Pax Silica and the so-called Luzon Economic Corridor (LEC), her irrational fear of crowds, her paranoia and her fear that the entire world is ganging on her all point to one thing: Her mental state disqualifies her from even becoming illegible to administer the bureaucracy and manage lives and future of 116-million Filipinos. Yet, she had the audacity to assail the Marcos Jr. administration for pushing the 2024 and 2025 national budgets that the Supreme Court (SC) said contained more than P400-billion in unprogrammed appropriations (UA) that the High Court ruled was unconstitutional. This is the same Sara who bragged that she never signed graft-ridden annual budgets. Sara apparently was ignorant of the fact that the vice president doesn’t sign the annual General Appropriations Act (GAA).


The Greeks have a term for it: Peritrope, when the tables are turned and the accuser shoots his arrow back to his head. Sara possibly doesn’t find it cute that she must argue with clean hands, but all her 10 fingers drip with mud. Like Vivek Ramaswamy bashing Amy Acton with a $4-million ad using Acton’s mother to argue that she cannot be trusted. The issue boomeranged as Acton told the truth about her stepfather sexually abusing when she was 12 and her own mother didn’t lift a finger, and her claim was corroborated by her brother. By raking Acton over the coals, Ohio voters busted Ramaswamy for his cruelty and violating the rule about truth in advertising.


This is akin to the expose of Nobel laureate Alice Munro’s coddling of a sex predator who sexually abused her own daughter and arguing that the issue was between her daughter and her husband. Munro should also donate her Nobel medal to Donald Trump, who continues to complain that he should have won the Nobel peace prize for stopping fight fictitious wars. Remember that Sara herself claimed that she was also raped? After getting some ill-deserved headlines from media outlets that take whatever comes out of Sara’s mouth as gospel truth, the claim was never checked by journalists. Was it ever true? The terrible thing is that 90% of all valid rape cases are incestuous.


The work-shy Sara Zimmerman Duterte Carpio has shown she can make a mountain out of a molehill and her frequent attacks on Ferdinand Marcos Jr. are interpreted as attempts to rally people against her own president. Sara doesn’t smell like roses for firing missiles at her superior since her indolence is legendary. The Duterte work culture, from the patriarch Rodrigo to Sara, Pulong and Baste Duterte, means signing documents for two hours and then “patrolling” Davao City until the end of office hours. They are giving the Hell’s Angels competition for their big bike monitoring of their turfs. With their abbreviated working hours, the Dutertes have to delegate their duties and functions to their underlings, including signing business contracts that should be signed by the mayor, congressman, vice president and president.


Lawmakers claimed Sara is better known for her absence from her post and for undertaking regular excursions to any place in the country where there are voters. She enjoyed a special budget …

author: groundxero
title: আইডিবিআই ব্যাঙ্ক: দেশের সম্পদ বিক্রির সরল রেসিপি
content:
দেশের মানুষের করের টাকা দিয়ে তৈরি রাষ্ট্রীয় সম্পদ জলের দরে কর্পোরেট মালিকদের বিক্রির সরকারি নীতির ধারাবাহিকতায় এবার বিক্রি হতে চলছে ইনডাসট্রিয়াল ব্যাঙ্ক অব ইন্ডিয়া (আইডিবিআই ব্যাঙ্ক)।


 


সুমন কল্যাণ মৌলিক


 


দেশের মানুষের করের টাকা দিয়ে তৈরি রাষ্ট্রীয় সম্পদ জলের দরে কর্পোরেট মালিকদের বিক্রির সরকারি নীতির ধারাবাহিকতায় এবার বিক্রি হতে চলছে ইনডাসট্রিয়াল ব্যাঙ্ক অব ইন্ডিয়া (আইডিবিআই ব্যাঙ্ক)। ১৪ অক্টোবর (২০২৬) কেন্দ্রীয় সরকার আইডিবিআই ব্যাঙ্কের ৬০.৭২% শেয়ার কানাডার ফেয়ারফ্যাক্স ফিনানসিয়াল হোল্ডিংসকে বিক্রির নীতিগত সম্মতি দিয়েছে এবং আশা করা হচ্ছে মাস ছয়েকের মধ্যে বিক্রিবাটার দলিল চূড়ান্ত হয়ে যাবে। নব্বই এর দশকে বিশ্বব্যাঙ্ক, আন্তর্জাতিক অর্থভান্ডার, এশিয়ান ডেভলপমেন্ট ব্যাঙ্ক প্রভৃতি আন্তর্জাতিক আর্থিক এজেন্সিগুলির পৌরহিত্যে যে নয়া সংস্কার অর্থনীতিতে চালু হয় তার প্রধান স্তম্ভ ছিল ভারতের বিপুল সম্পদ দেশি বিদেশি কর্পোরেট মালিকদের হাতে তুলে দেওয়া। উপুর্যুপরি সরকার এই কাজে দায়বদ্ধ থেকেছে কিন্তু পরিসংখ্যানের বিচারে বিজেপির নেতৃত্বাধীন এনডিএ সরকার এতে সবিশেষ পারদর্শিতা দেখিয়েছে। বছর দুয়েক আগে কেন্দ্রীয় বাজেটে সরকার পরিষ্কার জানিয়ে দেয় যে সমস্ত ক্ষেত্রেই বেসরকারিকরণ হবে এবং সরকার আর কোন সম্পদই নিজের হাতে রাখবে না। খনিজ সম্পদ, স্টিল, টেলিকমুনিকেশন, আকাশ পরিবহন, বিভিন্ন শিল্প কর্পোরেশন ইতিমধ্যে প্রায় ৯০% বিক্রি হয়ে গেছে। এবার নজর পরেছে সামরিক শিল্প, মহাকাশ ও ওষুধ শিল্পের দিকে। আর্থিক ক্ষেত্রে বিমা শিল্পের গল্প প্রায় শেষ, এবার স্বাভাবিক ভাবে কর্পোরেট হাঙরদের পাখির চোখ রাষ্ট্রায়ত্ত ব্যাঙ্ক এবং ডাকঘর। আগামী দিনে রাষ্ট্রায়ত্ত সম্পদের বিলগ্নীকরণ ও পরবর্তীতে বেসরকারিকরণ এক বড় ক্ষেত্র হতে চলেছে ব্যাঙ্কিং শিল্প। সেই প্রেক্ষাপটে আইডিবিআই ব্যাঙ্ক বিক্রির ঘটনা অত্যন্ত গুরুত্বপূর্ণ।


 


আলোচনার সুবিধার্থে প্রথমে বিক্রিবাটার চুক্তিপত্রটা বুঝে নেওয়া যেতে পারে।বিক্রির আগে ছবিটা ছিল এরকম: আইডিবিআই এর শেয়ারের ৪৯.২৪% ছিল জীবন বিমা নিগমের হাতে এবং ৪৫.৪৮% ছিল ভারত সরকারের। ৫.২৮% ছিল অন্যান্য শেয়ার হোল্ডারদের হাতে। বিক্রির পরে গল্পটা দাঁড়াবে : ফেয়ারফ্যাক্সের হাতে ৬০.৭২ (প্রকৃত অর্থে মালিকানা), এলআইসির হাতে ১৯%, ভারত সরকার ১৫% এবং অন্যান্য যথারীতি ৫.২৮%। দরপত্রের হিসাবটা হল একটা শেয়ারের মূল্য ৮১ টাকা (বেঞ্চমার্ক ছিল ৭৫.৯৯ টাকা), বিক্রি বাবদ আয় ৫২,৮৭৮ কোটি টাকা (৫.৫৬ বিলিয়ন মার্কিন ডলার)।


 


ক্যাবিনেট কমিটি অন ইকনমিক অ্যাফেয়ার্স যে নীতিগত সম্মতি জানাল তা যে পদ্ধতিতে হল তাও একটু বুঝে নেওয়া দরকার। ভারতের প্রাইভেট ব্যাঙ্কগুলোতে বিদেশি বিনিয়োগের অনুমতি নিয়মে আছে। কারা কিনবে, তাদের আর্থিক ক্ষমতা কেমন, শেয়ারহোল্ডারদের ভোটদানের ক্ষমতা কিরকম — সমস্ত বিষয়টা থাকে রিজার্ভ ব্যাঙ্ক অব ইন্ডিয়ার হাতে। নিয়ম হল প্রাইভেট সেক্টর ব্যাঙ্কে স্বয়ংক্রিয় ভাবে (automatic route) প্রত্যক্ষ বিদেশী বিনিয়োগের মাত্রা হল ৪৯% এবং ৭৪% পর্যন্ত বিনিয়োগ করতে হলে ভারত সরকারের অনুমতি বাধ্যতামূলক। সরকারি ব্যাঙ্কের ক্ষেত্রে বিদেশি প্রত্যক্ষ বিনিয়োগ হতে পারে সর্বোচ্চ ২০%, তাও কেন্দ্রীয় সরকারের অনুমতি সাপেক্ষে। আইডিবিআই আগে সরকারি ব্যাঙ্ক হিসাবে থাকলেও ২০১৯ সালে এলআইসির অধিগ্রহণের কারণে তা প্রাইভেট ব্যাঙ্কের তকমা পায়। তাই আইডিবিআই বিক্রির কাঠামোটা সাজানো হয়েছে প্রাইভেট সেক্টরের ব্যাঙ্ক হিসাবে। তবে যেহেতু এই বিনিয়োগ ৭৪% এর সিলিং এর মধ্যে পড়ে তাই অবশ্যই বিক্রির দলিলকে রিজার্ভ ব্যাঙ্ক অব ইন্ডিয়ার শর্তাবলী মেনে হতে হবে। এই পরিপ্রেক্ষিতে একটা প্রশ্ন জরুরি ভাবে উঠছে। তা হল ফেয়ারফ্যাক্সের আরেকটা বড় অঙ্কের মালিকানা রয়েছে ক্যাথলিক সিরিয়ান ব্যাঙ্কে (সিএসবি)। তাহলে তারা আরেকটা ব্যাঙ্কের মালিকানা কিভাবে নেবে! অনেকে মনে করছেন ফেয়ারফ্যাক্স ভবিষ্যতে আইডিবিআই ও সিএসবির মধ্যে মার্জার ঘটাবে।


 


ভারতে বেসরকারিকরণের ধামাকা শুরু হওয়ার পর্বে সরকার দেশের সম্পদ কর্পোরেট গোষ্ঠীগুলোর কাছে বিক্রি করার কারণ হিসাবে প্রধান যে যুক্তিটা খাঁড়া করত তা হল সংস্থাটি রুগ্ন, সেই প্রতিষ্ঠানকে চালানোর অর্থ হল করদাতাদের টাকায় হাতি পোষা ইত্যাদি। যদিও ইতিহাস সাক্ষী যে বিগত তিন দশকে বিক্রি বা বিলগ্নীকরণ, যাই হোক না, কর্পোরেটটা কিনেছে মূলত লাভজনক সংস্থা। এই মুহূর্তে আইডিবিআই দেশের অন্যতম লাভজনক ব্যাঙ্ক, যাকে প্রায় জলের দামে বিক্রি করা হচ্ছে। আইডিবিআই ব্যাঙ্কের ২০২০-২১ আর্থিক বর্ষে নেট লাভের পরিমাণ ছিল ১৩৫৯ কোটি টাকা যা ২০২৫-২৬ সালে হয়েছে ৯,৫১৩ কোটি টাকা। গত ছয় বছরে এদের লাভ ৩০,১০৬ কোটি টাকা। গত অর্থবর্ষে শুধুমাত্র সুদ থেকে ২৮,৯৯৭ কোটি টাকা আয় করছে ব্যাঙ্ক। বর্তমানে সারা দেশে আইডিবিআইয়ের ২১০০ শাখা এবং ৩০০০ এটিএম রয়েছে। সংস্থার ব্যালেন্স শিটে রয়েছে ৪ লক্ষ ১১ হাজার ৬৬১ কোটি টাকা। বর্তমানে প্রায় ৬ লাখ ৭৯৮ কোটি টাকার ব্যবসা করছে আইডিবিআই। ব্যাঙ্কটির নেট অ্যাডভান্সের পরিমাণ ২ লক্ষ ৫৩ হাজার ৬২৬ কোটি টাকা, পাশাপাশি ২০.৬৪ শতাংশ হারে বাড়ছে মুনাফা। ফলে কর্মীপ্রতি লাভের নিরিখে প্রথম স্থানে আছে আইডিবিআই, সেটা কম-বেশি ৪৬ লাখ টাকা। তাই কর্পোরেটরা কোন রুগ্ন ব্যাঙ্ককে কিনছে না, তারা বিনিয়োগ করছে এক চূড়ান্ত লাভজনক আর্থিক প্রতিষ্ঠানে।


 


একথা সকলের জানা যে ১৯৬৯ সালে ইন্দিরা গান্ধী যখন ভারতের প্রধানমন্ত্রী তখন ১৪ টি প্রধান প্রাইভেট ব্যাঙ্ককে …
