author: April Holcombe
title: China’s forgotten miracle makers
content:
History has no parallel for modern China’s economic transformation. To what do we owe the China “miracle”, in which annual GDP growth averaged 9 percent over 40 years, wages up roughly tenfold in 30 years, and more high-speed rail built in ten years than the rest of the world in all time?

In the heyday of globalisation, people said China proved the magic of free markets and free trade. These days, people are more likely to attribute the country’s success to some special Chinese characteristic, such as its state-directed investment or its “Communist” dictatorship. 

These perspectives share in common a wilful or ignorant blindness to capitalism’s real wealth creators. Economic value comes neither from the market’s “invisible hand” nor the state’s “guiding hand”, but plain old everyday hands. The secret to China’s “miracle” is the not-so-miraculous condition of its working class.

Beginning in the 1990s, the greatest ever number of wage labourers was assembled through the collusion of profit-hungry foreign capital with millions of venal bureaucrats and their repressive state machine. Three hundred million people decamped from rural poverty to seek better lives in China’s cities, while urban compatriots in state-owned mines and mills lost their livelihoods through merciless privatisation.

China’s working class is legally stratified into “migrant” and “resident”, subject to the severest dictatorship of their bosses, and deprived of political rights to speak out or unionise. Apply hundreds of billions in Western and Taiwanese investments, lather, rinse, repeat for decades, and voilà! You have the most “miraculous” economic growth in capitalist history. 

China’s migrant workforce

We are used to hearing about how important migrants are to Western economies, but migration—the internal kind from village to city, not country-to-country—has been even more critical to China’s boom. In the 1990s, the government enticed young villagers with the prospect of independence, new experiences and better pay in newly established, deregulated Special Economic Zones with low wages and low taxes.

Lu Qingmin first left her family’s half-acre farm and came to Dongguan, a burgeoning megacity in the southern manufacturing heartland of the Pearl River Delta, in the early 2000s. Bosses preferred migrant women like her, considering them doubly docile. Writer Leslie Chang, in her 2008 book

Factory Girls

, described Lu’s experiences at her first job in a Hong Kong-owned alarm clock factory:

“A day on the assembly line stretched from eight in the morning until midnight—thirteen hours on the job plus two breaks for meals—and workers labored every day for weeks on end. From the moment she entered the factory she wanted to leave.”

The Pearl River Delta opened wide to investment in such sweatshops, and American-style hyper-individualism flowed in with it. Self-help books, life-coaching gurus, pyramid schemes, talent markets, unregulated colleges: each refracted through the false prism of empowerment what migrant workers already felt in their bones:

you are on your own

.

Hukou

: China’s internal visa system

Every migrant who left for the cities took the same thing with them: their rural

hukou

(户口), a residential registration that acts like an internal passport. Originally designed under Mao Zedong in 1958 to prohibit rural-to-urban movement altogether, the

hukou

household registration system was repurposed to create a pliant, defenceless workforce with second-class citizenship wherever it went.

Out-of-town

hukou

holders, also called the “floating population”, now represent just under half of the country’s workforce. Registered to villages far away, they are denied health insurance and pensions by the local government where they actually live. Many cities bar them from buying property, and local schools charge significant sums to teach their children. 

Think of them like the United States’ undocumented immigrants, who can get driver’s licences but not Social Security, who work in practically every key industry, but technically are not supposed to be there at all. Except there are now as many in China as the entire US population.

China does not offer the equivalent of America’s birthright citizenship: children inherit their parents’

hukou

 wherever they are born. Locked out by the prohibitive cost of urban schooling, tens of millions of “left behind” children grow up in the countryside with their grandparents, only seeing their …

author: Tom Sullivan
title: Review: Anti-Zionism: A Jewish History by Benjamin Moser
content:
Anti-Zionism: A Jewish History

 by US writer and Pulitzer Prize winner Benjamin Moser is a useful contribution to uncover the history of opposition to Zionism within modern Judaism. It traces the history of anti-Zionism from the late 19th Century through the lives of several anti-Zionist Jews across the Middle East, Latin America, Africa, Europe and the US.

Moser begins in the late 19th Century in the Russian Empire, where the deep oppression that the Jewish population faced led to a cultural Zionism that, among other things, sought to revive Hebrew. One of its leaders was Aaron Samuel Tamares. But around the same time, there was also a territorial, national, and racial Zionism being developed by figures like Theodor Herzl. Published in 1896, Herzl’s 

Der Judenstaat

 (The State of the Jews) gave a racial definition to Jewish people, as opposed to the then-dominant idea of Jews being a religious community. It also argued that European anti-semitism could never be eradicated and an independent Jewish state was therefore necessary.

In response to Herzl, the cultural Zionism of Tamares and many other rabbis quickly became an explicit anti-Zionism. They were among the first to criticise how Herzl’s Zionism reinforced the existing anti-semitism of the time by defining the Jewish population as a “race” and “foreign elements” in their own countries.

Tamares did not reject Jewish communities in Palestine despite being an anti-Zionist. But he ferociously opposed the establishment of a Jewish state. To him, such a project was inextricably linked to Western imperialism. He asked why the European powers “should make recompense for 

their 

wrongdoings by handing over foreign property, 

Ottoman

land”?’

When the British began that process with the establishment of the British Mandate after World War One, the Zionist movement remained on the fringes within the Jewish population as it had when Herzl published 

Der Judenstaat

. In 1917, for example, Zionist groups in England had no more than four thousand members between them.

Moser describes the early days of the British Mandate through Jacob Israel de Haan. When de Haan emigrated from the Netherlands to Palestine in 1919, he was among the most prominent Dutch Zionists. But after seeing the violence of the Zionist groups against the indigenous population of both the Palestinian Muslims and Orthodox Jews, he quickly became a leading figure of the Agudah, an anti-Zionist, Orthodox Jewish organisation.

De Haan’s articles were some of the first to document the growing Zionist domination of Palestine in the early 1920s. He explained “that no Arab is allowed to live in Tel Aviv. That no Arab is received in a Jewish hotel. That companies in their statutes decide that they can only employ Jews.”

De Haan quickly reached such prominence that 

Ha’aretz

 labelled him and other Agudah members “traitors” and “scum.” Such words helped fuel the violent attacks of Jewish settler groups against Agudah members to the point where, in 1924, a member of the Haganah, the main Zionist militia, assassinated him. The order was given by Yitzhak Ben-Zvi, later to become the second president of Israel. 

Moser then jumps to Egypt, focusing on Sadiq Saad, an Egyptian, anti-Zionist, Jewish leftist. One of Saad’s most important works was 

Palestine in the Claws of Colonialism, 

published in 1947 and detailing the apartheid-style system then already established. One of the book’s contributions was its coverage of the unique experience of the Palestinian peasantry. Unlike almost all other peasantries, when the Palestinians were expelled from their land, they were denied employment by the new owners of the land or in the cities. This came directly from the policies of the Palestine Foundation Fund, the World Zionist Organisation’s fundraising arm, which specifically stated in its loan contracts that the borrower “pledges to hire Jewish workers only.”

The book covers numerous other examples of prominent anti-Zionist Jewish individuals and groups. The chapters on the immediate post-World War Two period are particularly useful in understanding the rapid transformation of both Zionism and those opposed to it. The French New Left, for example, during the 1950s and 1960s suffered through a period of deep confusion that led many prominent figures to support a form of Zionism. Similarly, the chapter on Reform Judaism in the United States, which had opposed Zionism since the late 19th Century, shows how …

author: Paul Gregoire
title: Allega Spender pushes to remove religious exemptions against LGBTIQ students, teachers
content:
The Sex Discrimination and Fair Work Amendment (Equality in Treatment in Religious Schools) Bill 2026, introduced on October 12, seeks to repeal the offending exemptions in federal sex discrimination law as well as removing the related provisions in federal workplace relations law. It also extends protections to associates of those who are captured under the current exemptions.

Section 38 of the Sex Discrimination Act 1984 (SDA) makes it lawful for religious education institutions to discriminate against a teacher, student or contract worker due to their “sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital or relationship status or pregnancy”.

The proposal took centre stage in 2018, as the national religious freedoms debate took off prior to then-Coalition Prime Minister Scott Morrison shooting it down.

Morrison’s push to establish a religious freedoms regime in 2018 uncovered their existence. His years-long religious crusade was defeated after debate on these exemptions.

Labor PM Anthony Albanese promised to progress the reform in 2022, but changed his mind.

Spender, independent MP for Wentworth, is pushing popular reforms, despite far-right commentators claiming it as an attack on religious freedom.

“These exemptions have already been removed in state and territory law, to varying degrees, but there are no national standards,” Spender told NSW Parliament on October 12.

“The Australian Law Reform Commission’s 2024 review found that religious schools could still maintain their ethos without this exemption.

“At its heart, section 38 of the Sex Discrimination Act is repealed in its entirety and replaced with a far narrower provision,” Spender said in her second reading speech on her private member’s bill.

“Protections are also extended to a person’s associates ... This means a child cannot be treated differently just because she has two mums.”

The bill repeals the current provisions affecting students, teachers and contract workers in section 38, replacing it with a provision that allows institutions to preference staff based on faith in two ways — at their initial employment and in the promotion of senior leadership roles such as “principal, vice-principal, religious education teacher, chaplain” or any other comparable role.

The bill inserts section 7AAA into the SDA, which makes it unlawful to discriminate against an associate, such as a spouse or relative, of a person protected under the Act. It removes provisions that permitted discrimination based on sex, sexuality or gender.

It also repeals provisions in the Fair Work Act 2009 that extend discrimination into workplace agreements.

“But preferencing is not a licence to discriminate,” Spender said. “A school can choose a candidate because of their faith. It cannot fire someone because of their sexuality. Many students have wonderful, formative experiences at religious schools. Many LGBTQIA+ students come out to their friends and teachers in these schools and are accepted. But … this is not everyone’s experience.”

The exemptions in section 38 of the SDA relating to sexual orientation and gender identity, were inserted into the Act when a 2013 bill added anti-discrimination provisions into the law that related to sexual orientation, gender identity and intersex characteristics. The exemptions in respect of gay and transgender individuals joined pre-existing ones that permitted discrimination based on sex.

The October 2018 Ruddock review into religious freedoms recommended tightening these exemptions in federal law, which drew attention to and then condemnation of the laws.

While Morrison initially tried to downplay the outcry, he reversed course and promised to repeal the discriminatory measures targeting students. But Morrison, a Pentecostal, attempted to progress three versions of the Religious Freedoms Bill — two in 2019 and one in 2022 — and the removal of any exemptions was forgotten.

Each version of the religious freedoms legislation was increasingly watered down.

Three years of debate on these laws made it clear that his measures sought religious privileges.

The public debate over religious concerns is different to the present, with the conservative push to insert the controversial International Holocaust Remembrance Alliance definition of antisemitism into all levels of government to curb criticism of Israel and its genocide.

author: Elliot Downes
title: NT government closes Darwin’s largest homelessness shelter
content:
Residents of Darwin’s largest homelessness shelter were evicted by the Northern Territory government on 12 October, and relocated to Batchelor, a town 100 kilometres away.

Yilli Short Stay Accommodation (YiSSA), which is run by Yilli Rreung Housing Aboriginal Corporation, was home to hundreds of people, mostly Aboriginal. Many have experienced domestic violence and are living with serious health conditions, including kidney conditions requiring dialysis. 

Residents from communities across the territory would stay at YiSSA while accessing medical care or other services in Darwin. Nearly 400 people were directly affected by the closure of the facility, including 160 children.

YiSSA’s closure will place more pressure on remaining homelessness services in Darwin. Meanwhile, the minority of residents transferred to the smaller facility in Batchelor will not have the same access to support networks, food, healthcare and education. Batchelor is a town with a population of around 500, a small health clinic and no public transport. 

The closure of a key homelessness service is particularly egregious given the Northern Territory has the highest rate of homelessness in the country. According to data released last year by the Australian Institute of Health and Welfare, 

one in every 25 Territorians requires homelessness assistance

, and Aboriginal people make up 89 percent of those accessing homelessness services in the Northern Territory.

As the biggest landlord in the territory, the Northern Territory government is largely to blame for this situation. Territorians on the emergency public housing waiting list can expect to 

wait up to a decade for a roof over their head

. The government is also responsible for the apartheid-like conditions in Aboriginal town camps on the outskirts of places like Darwin and Alice Springs, as well as the overcrowding in remote communities.

The closure of YiSSA was announced by the ruling Country Liberal Party (CLP) in July. Ostensibly, it was due to a failure to secure a deal with Ausco, the owner of the buildings and other infrastructure on the Crown land site. But in reality, it was a political decision. 

After years of renting the demountable buildings, the government offered to buy them for $3 million—the equivalent of just one year’s rent. When this offer was rejected by Ausco, the federal government proposed to cover the cost of the purchase on the condition that Yilli Rreung continue running the service.

The CLP rejected the offer of federal funding, with Chief Minister Lia Finocchiaro calling it a 

“waste of taxpayers’ hard-earned money”

. Yet it has cost 

$16.25 million to establish and fund the Batchelor facility

, run by Mission Australia.

The announcement of YiSSA’s closure sparked a campaign by the activist group, Justice Not Jails (JNJ). It culminated in a 200-strong rally outside of the Australian Homelessness Conference in Darwin just days before residents were to be evicted. 

Anna, an activist with JNJ, told 

Red Flag

 that the decision doesn’t make sense “unless you approach it from an ideological viewpoint. Some of the YiSSA residents have said that [the government] just don’t want Aboriginal people to have a nice, secure place to live.”

The YiSSA closure is symptomatic of a Trumpian government that has targeted Aboriginal people in particular. Since coming to power in 2024, the CLP have lowered the age of criminal responsibility to 10, reintroduced spit hoods in detention, and made it easier for Aboriginal children to be removed from their families and placed into long-term state care.

This has involved a significant expansion in the carceral state, with the prison population 

increasing by 24 percent between 2024 and 2025

, and the Finocchiaro government announcing earlier this year the construction of a new private prison in Darwin. 

The Northern Territory is one of the most incarcerated places in the world, 

second only to El Salvador

, with more than 1 percent of the entire population behind bars. Increasingly, this includes people on remand, who are awaiting trial or sentencing.

According to Anna, the next phase of the campaign will involve putting pressure on the federal Labor government. “There’s been a lot of disagreement between the CLP and Labor about what was actually promised. It’s all really immature and I think disrespectful to the people whose lives are actually being affected,” she told 

Red Flag.

author: Ben Radford
title: US must end its cruel blockade of Cuba
content:
Every year since 1992, the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) has overwhelmingly voted to end the United States government’s cruel and illegal economic blockade of Cuba. One-hundred-and-sixty-five countries voted last year for the resolution on the “Necessity of ending the economic, commercial and financial embargo imposed by the United States of America against Cuba”, with just six against.

This year’s vote, on October 28, takes place as escalating US economic warfare against Cuba is causing a devastating humanitarian crisis. The blockade’s impacts have been characterised as a “silent genocide”, severely restricting Cubans’ access to food, medicine, equipment and fuel, and impacting every aspect of daily life.

The Cuban government submitted its annual report to the UNGA in September, detailing last year’s impacts of the US blockade. Between March last year and February this year, the blockade inflicted more than US$8 billion worth of damages.

The economic cost of just four days of the blockade amounts to the cost of all fuel imports needed to meet Cuba’s demand.

On top of existing strangulation mechanisms, the US government imposed an energy blockade on Cuba in January, claiming that the country posed an “unusual and extraordinary threat” to US national security.

The US announced tariffs on goods from countries that, directly or indirectly, sold or provided oil to Cuba. Following the US’s January 3 attacks on Venezuela, it also blocked all Venezuelan oil shipments to the country.

The energy blockade is the reason for widespread blackouts, as well disruptions to water supply, waste collection and transport.

The fuel shortages are severely impacting hospital operations, including treatments that require a steady energy supply, such as haemodialysis. There are harrowing reports of surgeons having to perform operations by mobile phone lights, due to the blackouts.

The US blockade has affected Cubans’ access to vital treatment and medicine. One example is Cuba’s cancer survival rates, which, while still higher than many low- and middle-income countries, have dropped from 85% to 65%.

Cuba’s infant mortality has risen from 4 out of 1000 live births in 2018 to 9.9 last year — a 148% rise.

Cuban authorities say that the current transport crisis is more acute than during the “Special Period” in the 1990s following the collapse of the Soviet Union, which plunged Cuba into a prolonged economic crisis. Fuel shortages have affected refrigerated transport, preventing more than 30,000 children from receiving vaccines.

In May, the US imposed a regime of secondary sanctions against governments and companies that invest in or trade with Cuba.

For example, the US Office of Foreign Assets Control has imposed fines on US companies for handling cargo shipments bound for Cuba and providing services for people living in the country.

Over the past year, 34 international banking institutions suspended or declined to conduct operations with Cuba, citing risks of secondary sanctions.

Several airlines have ceased operations in Cuba and many international hotel chains also abandoned management agreements for hotels, citing the risks posed by the secondary sanctions regime. These sanctions — along with other US measures — have contributed to the collapse in Cuba’s tourism industry.

“The application of these measures has produced a sophisticated mechanism of asphyxiation directed at the Cuban population, exceeding by far the levels of pressure historically imposed over decades,” the annual report said.

It also notes that the blockade has caused US$3.9 trillion worth of damages since it was imposed. However, it said the impacts go far beyond economic losses, causing suffering, illness and death.

The US blockade of Cuba violates not just international law, but any semblance of humanity.

The US government has made its intention of achieving “regime change” in Cuba by the end of the year very clear; it is openly considering the possibility of military attacks. This has been the US’s policy since Cubans overthrew the US-backed Fulgencio Batista military dictatorship in 1959 and set about implementing a planned economy based on meeting people’s needs.

Since then, the US has undertaken or sponsored terrorist attacks, a military invasion and an economic blockade against the Cuban people, with the explicit aim of bringing about “hunger, desperation and overthrow of government”, as revealed by a 1960 US memorandum.

author: Danica Rachel
title: Operation Paperclip: The Nazis behind the US space program
content:
The Apollo moon landings are some of the most impressive technical feats ever achieved, and, for capitalism’s boosters, definitive evidence of the superiority of Western capitalism over all other social systems. The United States beating the Soviet Union to the finish line in the space race is held up as the ultimate triumph of capitalism over communism. But the path that took humans to the heavens began in the depths of hell: the Mittelbau-Dora concentration camp in Nazi Germany.

Built near the town of Nordhausen in central Germany, Mittelbau-Dora provided its prisoners as slaves to the Mittelwerk. This was a factory built under a mountain for the mass production of the V2 rocket, the world’s first long-range guided ballistic missile. The several thousand civilians killed in London and Antwerp by V2s were not the only victims of these Nazi weapons: at least 20,000 prisoners died as a result of the conditions in Mittelbau-Dora and the Mittelwerk.

Edwin Katzenellenbogen, who was convicted for crimes committed as a doctor at the Buchenwald camp, described Dora as “the Hell of all the concentration camps”. Tens of thousands of prisoners worked in interchanging 12-hour shifts, first to dig the kilometres-long tunnels of the Mittelwerk, then on the dark production lines within.

Sanitation was absent, disease and starvation were rampant, and collective punishment was common. Prisoners were hanged in groups of up to a dozen at a time, and on at least one occasion, bodies were left to dangle over the areas where others were forced to continue working.

Wernher von Braun was an SS officer, scientific director of the V-weapons project, and head of the Mittelbau-Dora planning office. He came from an aristocratic family in the German empire, and was among the first pioneers of advanced rocket science. Through the interwar years, Germany was banned from investing in many kinds of weaponry under the Treaty of Versailles, but rockets were obscure enough to avoid being on the list. During this time, von Braun became a leading designer and inventor of the engines needed to propel explosive missiles over incredible distances.

He joined the Nazi Party in 1937. If you believe his version of events, he joined only to be allowed to continue his scientific work. Regardless of his political loyalty, he was at least comfortable enough with the genocidal policies of the Third Reich to enjoy the slave labour it provided to him from Mittelbau-Dora. He was certainly aware of the reality of the Mittelwerk, having visited the tunnels himself at least ten times.

As the walls closed in on the Third Reich, with US and British forces moving in from the west and Russians from the east, von Braun hid the most important of the design documents for constructing V2s. Alongside Major General Walter Dornberger, head of the German army’s weapons department, von Braun used the hidden documents as leverage to get an amnesty with the Americans, betting that the US wanted the weapons more than they cared about prosecuting war criminals.

He was right. Von Braun, Dornberger and many other German experts in weapons of many terrifying forms—ballistic, chemical, and biological—were brought across the Atlantic under a secret program known as Operation Paperclip. They began work in the US, making weapons for a new, but no less bloodthirsty, empire. Their pasts were whitewashed, with the story being that they were innocent scientists forced by circumstance into working for the Nazi regime.

For his part, Joseph Stalin got the Mittelwerk factory itself, which continued operation for a few years before its machinery was brought back to Russia, along with thousands of German technicians needed to operate it. The USSR also got the equipment and methods to manufacture sarin gas, a chemical weapon so potent that contact with a single droplet causes a painful death.

Sarin was invented by Nazi chemists, among them Otto Ambros, who tested it on Auschwitz prisoners. Ambros was convicted for crimes against humanity in the Nuremberg trials, but that wasn’t a barrier to later working for US chemical companies and the US army. Within a few years of the end of the war, both imperial superpowers were producing large quantities of sarin and other chemical weapons.

The Cold War and the arms race 

The new phase of world imperialism had the globe divided into the West, with the US on top, against the East orbiting the USSR. The prospect of direct hot war between the empires gave …

title: ‘Sosyal demokrasi, en çok da emeğin karşısında sınanır’
content:
Bu mektubu yalnızca bir belediye çalışanının işine iadesini istemek için değil; emeğin onurunu, demokratik hakları ve sosyal demokrasinin tarihsel sorumluluğunu hatırlatmak amacıyla yazıyorum.

Karabağlar Belediyesi'nde 15 yıl sosyolog olarak görev yapan Murat Mengirkaon'un, Temmuz 2026'da imzalanan Toplu İş Sözleşmesi'ne yönelik eleştirilerinin ardından rotasyon gerekçesiyle Temizlik İşleri Müdürlüğü'ne görevlendirildiği; gerçekleştirdiği oturma eylemi ve basın açıklamalarından sonra disiplin soruşturması açılarak 29 Eylül 2026'da işten çıkarıldığı belirtilmektedir.

Bu süreç, işten çıkarma kararıyla çalışanın demokratik itirazları arasında ilişki bulunup bulunmadığı sorusunu doğurmaktadır. Bu sorunun yanıtlanması, yalnızca ilgili çalışana değil, Karabağlar halkına ve sosyal demokrat belediyeciliğin ilkelerine karşı da bir sorumluluktur.

Sosyal demokrasi, itiraz eden işçinin susturulması üzerine kurulamaz.

Sosyal demokrasi, tarihsel olarak emeğin korunması, eşitsizliklerin azaltılması ve çalışanların yönetime katılması mücadelesinden doğmuştur. Eduard Bernstein'ın demokratik reform anlayışından Rosa Luxemburg'un özgürlük vurgusuna uzanan bu geleneğin temelinde, emekçinin hakları ve itirazları olan özgür bir yurttaş olduğu düşüncesi vardır.

Luxemburg'un, "Özgürlük, her zaman farklı düşünenin özgürlüğüdür." sözü, demokratik yönetimin ahlaki ölçütünü ortaya koyar. Demokrasi, yalnızca yönetime katılanların değil, ona karşı çıkanların da haklarını koruyabilmektir.

Bir çalışanın toplu iş sözleşmesini eleştirmesi, sendikal süreçleri sorgulaması veya çalışma koşullarına ilişkin görüşlerini açıklaması, tek başına disiplin yaptırımını haklı kılamaz. Kurumların hukuka uygun disiplin yetkileri bulunmakla birlikte bu yetkiler demokratik hakların cezalandırılmasına dönüşmemelidir.

Türkiye Cumhuriyeti Anayasası'nın 25. ve 26. maddeleri düşünce ve ifade özgürlüğünü, 36. maddesi hak arama hürriyetini, 51. maddesi sendikal örgütlenmeyi, 53. maddesi toplu iş sözleşmesi hakkını güvence altına almaktadır. Türkiye'nin taraf olduğu ILO'nun 87 ve 98 sayılı sözleşmeleri de sendikal özgürlükleri ve toplu pazarlık hakkını korumaktadır.

Bu güvenceler her eylemin koşulsuz hukuka uygun olduğu anlamına gelmez. Ancak işten çıkarma kararının demokratik hakların kullanılmasıyla bağlantılı olup olmadığının titizlikle araştırılmasını gerektirir.

Hukuka uygunluk yönetimin asgari yükümlülüğüdür; adalet ise ahlaki sorumluluğudur.

Türkiye'de emek mücadelesi aynı zamanda demokrasi mücadelesidir. 1961 Anayasası'yla güçlenen sendikal haklar önemli kazanımlar sağlamış; 12 Eylül 1980 darbesi sonrasında bu hakların sınırlandırılması demokratik yaşamda ağır yaralar açmıştır. Günümüzdeki bir personel işlemiyle darbe dönemini özdeşleştirmek doğru değildir. Ancak bu tarihsel deneyim, itirazın susturulmasının demokratik kültürü zayıflattığını göstermektedir.

Sosyal demokrat belediyecilik yalnızca sosyal yardım ve kamusal hizmet üretmek değildir. Kendi çalışanlarına adil davranmak, sendikal özgürlükleri korumak ve eleştiriye açık olmak da bu anlayışın ayrılmaz parçalarıdır.

Murat Mengirkaon'un 15 yıllık hizmeti, yalnızca çalışma süresinden ibaret değildir. Sosyal hizmet alanındaki mesleki birikimi, kurumsal hafızaya ve toplumun kırılgan kesimlerine sunduğu katkılarla birlikte değerlendirilmelidir. Görev yerinin değiştirilmesi ve ardından işten çıkarılması; idari yetkinin yanında hakkaniyet, ölçülülük, mesleki saygınlık ve kamu yararı açısından da incelenmelidir.

Hannah Arendt'in kamusal yaşamda çoğulluk ve farklı görüşlerin birlikte var olmasına ilişkin düşünceleri, eleştirinin demokratik yönetim için taşıdığı önemi hatırlatmaktadır. Güçlü yönetim, eleştiriyi ortadan kaldıran değil, eleştiri karşısında adalet duygusunu koruyabilen yönetimdir.

Sosyal adalet, belediye binasının kapısında sona eremez.

Burada mesele, Murat Mengirkaon'un bütün görüşlerini veya eylemlerini onaylamak değildir. Mesele, bir çalışanın yönetime itiraz ettiği için mesleki geleceğini kaybetmemesi gerektiği ilkesini savunmaktır.

author: Mag
title: „An euren Händen klebt Blut!“: Studentische Proteste gegen tödliche Korruption weiten sich in Serbien zu Streiks gegen die neoliberale Regierung aus
content:
Dossier


„

In Serbien finden derzeit die größten Straßenproteste seit Jahrzehnten statt. Der Anlass: Anfang November stürzte in der nordserbischen Stadt Novi Sad das Vordach des Bahnhofs ein. Bei dem Unglück kamen 15 Menschen ums Leben. Studierende organisieren seit dem Vorfall Proteste und fordern von der Regierung, Verantwortung zu übernehmen und den Fall aufzuklären. Die Demonstrierenden sehen die tief verwurzelte Korruption im Land als Ursache für den Einsturz. (…) Die Proteste weiteten sich über das ganze Land aus. Den Protesten haben sich Oppositionelle, Schüler und Schülerinnen, Professorinnen, Künstler und Bauern angeschlossen. Im Dezember wurde ein weiterer Skandal öffentlich, der das Vertrauen in die Regierung erschütterte: Die Menschenrechtsorganisation Amnesty International berichtete, dass die serbische Polizei und Geheimdienste die Handys von Aktivisten und Journalisten mit einer israelischen Spionagesoftware infiziert haben.

..“ Umfangreicher

Beitrag vom 26.12.2024 im Deutschlandfunk

Noch kurz vor der Wahl in Serbien zeigt die studentisch und zivilgesellschaftlich organisierte Bewegung, dass sie unabhängig vom Wahlverlauf gewonnen hat…

Es stimmt auch, dass Menschen, die noch nie in ihrem Leben politisch involviert, engagiert waren, in den letzen Monaten Schulungen durchlaufen haben, um als Wahlbeobachter*innen an den abgelegensten Orten Serbiens zu sein. Es kursieren schon Videos, wie Betrugsversuche aufgedeckt, verhindert werden

author: CMI Argentina
title: El paro del subte derrotó el ataque de Jorge Macri, Emova y el Poder Judicial porteño al derecho de huelga
content:
Los trabajadores del subte pararon la campaña de “Ley y orden”


El enorme paro de las trabajadoras y los trabajadores del subte derrotó el ataque de Jorge Macri, Emova y el Poder Judicial al derecho a huelga. La medida de fuerza duró cerca de seis horas y se desató luego de la detención completamente arbitraria de dos integrantes de la Comisión Directiva del sindicato y un delegado que fueron apresados por parte de la Policía de la Ciudad de Buenos Aires, cuando realizaban una apertura de molinetes como parte de sus medidas de lucha contra sanciones de parte de Emova contra un trabajador que era obligado a trabajar horas extras.


Detención del metrodelegado Claudio Dellacarbonara.


El paro contundente logró la liberación de los detenidos y dejó un gran ejemplo para toda la clase trabajadora. Es con la lucha y con métodos contundentes que se puede enfrentar y derrotar los ataques patronales y de un gobierno que avanza en instaurar un Estado policial en la Ciudad. Ese es el camino para ponerle límites a los constantes intentos de precarizar las condiciones laborales, despedir o hundir más el salario.


Paro del subterráneo. Bernardino Avila


Esta acción logró derrotar esta intentona de Jorge Macri contra los metrodelegados. En este ejemplo se encuentra el embrión de cómo parar la avanzada de un Estado policial contra trabajadores y sectores populares. Jorge Macri semanalmente hace videos de campaña por “ley y orden” encanando a vendedores ambulantes que solo buscan subsistir, a personas en situación de calle que no tienen dónde vivir, a habitantes de conventillos que son desalojados sin órdenes judiciales con la policía o los ya reiterados operativos “Tormenta Negra” contra los barrios populares.


El paro contundente, la amplia solidaridad son más fuertes que el gobierno, la empresa y la justicia. Un gran ejemplo y un camino a seguir para acabar con el Estado policial de Macri.


La solidaridad activa también jugó un papel el martes. Docentes, estudiantes de la universidad y trabajadores de sectores del sindicalismo combativo acompañaron la pelea con un corte de la avenida Triunvirato, cerca de la Estación Rosas donde resistieron la represión policial.


Por Mario Hernandez


 


Viajes en subte: pasajes caros y mal servicio


El Gobierno de la Ciudad viene vaciando el subte porteño desde hace años. Tarifas cada vez más caras, una red que no se amplía, falta de inversión y contaminación con asbesto conviven con un servicio que pierde pasajeros y con una empresa concesionaria que hace ganancias millonarias.


Los trabajadores que denuncian esta situación y salen a luchar por sus derechos enfrentan sanciones, persecución sindical y hasta detenciones, como ocurrió el martes pasado con los Metrodelegados.


Los datos oficiales permiten dimensionar el deterioro, entre enero y agosto de 2023, el subte transportó unos 152 millones de pasajeros. En el mismo período de 2026 fueron casi 122 millones. Son 30 millones menos de pasajeros en tres años, una caída cercana al 20 %. Los usuarios se ven obligados a buscar otras formas de viajar debido a los tarifazos y el mal servicio.


El Gobierno de Jorge Macri impone pasajes cada vez más caros por un servicio que no mejora. La situación actual es el resultado de años de políticas que priorizan los negocios privados y descargan sobre trabajadores y usuarios las consecuencias de la falta de inversión.


Viajar en subte se volvió cada vez más difícil para los bolsillos populares. El aumento del boleto superó a la inflación y casi duplicó el incremento de los salarios registrados, según los datos recopilados por el Centro de Estudios Laborales y de Investigación Social (CELID). Entre agosto del 2019 y el mismo mes de 2026 la tarifa del subte pasó de $21 a $1.684, casi un 8.000%, mientras los salarios crecieron sólo un 4.100% en el mismo periodo.


El mecanismo de actualización tarifaria aprobado por el Gobierno porteño mantiene aumentos mensuales que combinan un 2 % adicional con la variación del índice de precios al consumidor. De esta manera, el boleto continúa aumentando automáticamente por encima de la inflación, sin que exista una mejora equivalente del servicio para quienes lo utilizan.


La caída de pasajeros es un indicador de este deterioro. La cantidad de viajes registrados durante los primeros ocho meses de 2026 fue casi un 20 % menor que en el mismo período de 2023. Los datos no permiten atribuir toda esa diferencia a los aumentos tarifarios, pero sí es claro que el …

author: CNT Galiza
title: La CNT logra que una empresa de limpieza de A Baña pague el pago único por horas extras que le debía a un trabajador
content:
Leer en

Castellano

Galego


Castellano

La CNT logra que una empresa de limpieza de A Baña pague el pago único por horas extras que le debía a un trabajador.


La sección sindical de la CNT en Compostela ha logrado una nueva victoria en la defensa de los derechos de las trabajadoras de limpieza. Tras la intervención sindical, la empresa LISERINCO SL, con sede en A Baña, abonó el pago extraordinario por horas extras que establece el convenio colectivo provincial para el año 2025 y que se le había denegado a una compañera. El acuerdo se alcanzó en la ceremonia de conciliación celebrada en el SMAC.


La CNT suma así una nueva victoria en la lucha por los derechos de las trabajadoras del sector de la limpieza, uno de los más feminizados y precarios del país. En esta ocasión, la intervención sindical permitió que una compañera empleada por la empresa LISERINCO SL, con sede en el municipio de A Baña, recibiera el pago extraordinario por horas extras que le correspondía y que la empresa le había denegado.


El pago en cuestión está incluido en el Convenio Colectivo Provincial de Limpieza de Edificios y Locales de la provincia de A Coruña, firmado en 2025. Este convenio establece, para el año 2025, un pago extraordinario único, de carácter lineal para todas las categorías, no acumulable y proporcional a la jornada y el tiempo trabajados durante el año. El pago debía efectuarse en un plazo máximo de 20 días a partir de la publicación del convenio en el Boletín Oficial de la Provincia.


La empresa LISERINCO SL, lejos de cumplir con lo establecido en el convenio que le es aplicable, se negó a abonar dicha cantidad al compañero. Ante esta situación, el trabajador acudió a la CNT y presentó la correspondiente moción de conciliación ante la SMAC.


El acto de conciliación, celebrado en los últimos días, concluyó con un acuerdo entre las partes: la empresa se comprometió a abonar el pago extraordinario único que adeudaba al trabajador. Una victoria que, aunque modesta, reviste enorme importancia: demuestra que la organización colectiva funciona incluso en los sectores más atomizados y precarios.


«No se puede permitir que las empresas incumplan el convenio colectivo con el pretexto de que los trabajadores no se quejarán. El salario único es un derecho, no un favor. Y cuando hay alguien que se organiza y defiende, se cumple la ley», denuncia la CNT.


La CNT recuerda que el sector de la limpieza es uno de los más precarios de Galicia, con una plantilla mayoritariamente femenina y salarios miserables. Por ello, el control del cumplimiento del convenio es fundamental.


La CNT hace un llamamiento a todos los trabajadores de la limpieza que se encuentren en una situación similar —impago de salarios extraordinarios, salarios inferiores a lo estipulado, horas extras no remuneradas o cualquier otra violación de sus derechos— para que acudan al sindicato. La organización ofrece asesoramiento y defensa legal, y demuestra una y otra vez que la lucha colectiva es la única herramienta eficaz contra la precariedad y la explotación.


NO ESTÁS SOLO/A. ORGANÍZATE. DEFIENDE TUS DERECHOS.


Si trabajas en el sector de la limpieza y no se respetan tus derechos, acude a la CNT. La lucha colectiva es la única herramienta eficaz contra la precariedad y la explotación.


Galego

author: Radikal Perspektif
title: Yeşil Sendikalizm – Çok Kısa Bir Giriş
content:
Yazan: Jeff Shantz


Çeviren: Gorthim


Çevirilen Asıl Metin


PDF Linki


Kapitalizm altında emeğin sömürülmesi ile toprağın sömürülmesi her zaman ayrılmaz bir şekilde birbirine bağlı olmuştur – biri diğeri olmadan gerçekleşmez. Ortak mülkiyet alanlarının çitlerle çevrilmesinden kaynaklanan şiddet, sömürgecilik yoluyla tüm dünyaya yayılmıştır – bu devam eden eylemler, kapitalist mülkiyet ilişkilerinin temelini oluşturmaktadır. Çitlerle çevrilenlerin mülksüzleştirilmesi, yerinden edilmesi ve sosyal kontrolü, kapitalist mülkiyet ve işgücü piyasalarının hizmetinde gerçekleştirilmektedir.

1

 Toprağın ve yaşamın sürdürülmesi için gerekli araçların şiddet yoluyla kamulaştırılması, kâr amaçlı zorla üretimin temel koşullarıdır. Emek, özerk bir şekilde hayatta kalma koşullarının yok edilmesi yoluyla sömürülebilir hale getirilir.


Toprak ve işgücünün sömürülmesinin birbiriyle bağlantılı niteliği, doğaya en doğrudan zarar veren endüstrilerin aynı zamanda işçiler ve yerli halklar için de en tehlikeli ve ölümcül olanlar olması gerçeğinde çarpıcı bir şekilde ortaya çıkmaktadır. Ormancılık, madencilik, balıkçılık, tarım.


Birinin sömürülmesine son vermek, diğerinin sömürülmesine son vermeden mümkün değildir. Evet, buna Yerli halkların topraklarına geri kavuşması da dahildir. Kâr elde etmek amacıyla toprağın mülkiyetine sahip olmak, doğanın yok edilmesine ve dünyasal yaşamın (elbette insan yaşamı da dahil olmak üzere) yok edilmesine yol açan temel faktördür. İnsanlar, hayatta kalma araçları olan doğa sömürüldüğünde, alınıp satılan bir işgücü haline getirilir.


Yeşil sendikalizmin temel bir görüşü, sermaye tarafından üretim, yeniden üretim ve dağıtım süreçlerinde sömürülen ve işgücü piyasası aracılığıyla hayatta kalmaya zorlanan işçi sınıfının, toprak ve emeğin çifte sömürüsüne son vermek için hayati bir konumda olduğudur. Bunun birkaç temel nedeni vardır.


İşçilerin Potansiyel Gücü


Her şeyden önce, emek süreci içindeki merkezi konumları ve işyerlerindeki yerleri göz önüne alındığında, işçiler zararlı endüstriyel uygulamaları doğrudan durdurabilirler. Bu durum en açık şekilde grevlerde görülür. İşçiler, emeklerini geri çekip vermeyerek endüstriyel süreçleri durdururlar. Bu süreçler kelimenin tam anlamıyla işlevini yitirir. Aynı zamanda, yeniden üretim süreçlerine ilişkin bilgileri sayesinde, işçiler doğaya ikincil zararlar vermeyecek şekilde üretimi durdurabilir veya değiştirebilirler.


İşçiler, kullanıldığında dış aktörlerin dışsal ya da ikincil eylemlerinden daha doğrudan ve anında etki yaratabilecek bir potansiyel güce sahiptir. Örneğin, bir fabrikada ya da şantiyede protesto eylemi düzenleyen çevreciler, orada çalışan işçilerin düzenleyeceği bir protesto eyleminin yaratacağı etkiden daha az etki yaratacaktır. Dolayısıyla, aynı eylem bile, bir grup için diğerine kıyasla, yalnızca üretim ve yeniden üretim süreçleri içindeki yapısal konumları nedeniyle daha fazla güç taşıyabilir.


İşçilerin sağlık ve güvenlik konusundaki endişeleri (işyerindeki kirletici maddelere maruz kalma vb.), ekolojik kaygılarla son derece kişisel bir şekilde kesişmektedir. İşyerlerindeki endüstriyel süreçlerden etkilenen bölgelerde, topluluk ve aileye yönelik endişeleri de aynı şekilde bu kaygılarla örtüşmektedir. Bu durum, aksini savunan katı klişelere rağmen, işçileri güçlü ekolojik müttefikler haline getirebilir.


Taktikler


İşçilerin stratejisi ve taktiklerinin gücü – işçi olarak – yeniden üretim ve dağıtım süreçleri içindeki özel konumlarından kaynaklanır. Genel olarak en güçlü taktik grevdir – toprağı ve emeği tahrip eden işleri yapmayı reddetmektir. Grev, en etkili doğrudan eylemdir; zararın gerçekleşmesini engeller ve sermayenin bu eylemlere devam etmesini zorlaştırır ya da imkansız kılar. Bu, ahlaki bir çağrı, rica ya da talep bile değildir; üçüncü tarafların arabuluculuğuna gerek kalmadan, amaçlanan hedefe doğrudan ulaşan sonuç odaklı bir eylemdir.


Bu elbette, tabandaki örgütlenme düzeyine ve grev kırıcıların devreye sokulmasını engelleme ya da muhafazakar sendika yönetiminin işverenle anlaşmalar yapmasını önleme kapasitesine bağlıdır. Hiçbir taktik saf haliyle uygulanmaz ve örgütlenme her zaman başlı başına bir eylemdir. Ancak bu durumda bile, grev kırıcıların kullanılması sermayeye bir maliyet getirir.


Bir diğer önemli taktik ise

sabotaj

author: Unknown
title: Sevda Karaca: War policies undermine unity and labour struggles - Part Two
content:
Sevda Karaca, Deputy Chair of the Labour Party (EMEP) and MP for Antep, answered ANF's questions about labour struggles and the struggle for peace. 


Part one of this interview can be read

here

.


Do war, conflict and the resulting militarism push poverty, insecurity and workers' demands out of the public agenda? How exactly are labour struggles weakened during periods when security-driven policies intensify?


The past 40 years have shown us that the effects of war are not confined to areas of armed conflict. War permeates every aspect of social life. Workers' demands for higher wages, the right to strike, women's struggle for equality and people's democratic demands can suddenly be pushed into the background by debates over 'national security', 'the survival of the state' or the 'domestic front'. Rather than answering the questions working people raise about its policies, the government attempts to bring them into line by presenting them with another supposed threat.


This mechanism has very concrete consequences. Strikes are postponed on national security grounds. Trade union organising faces repression. Democratic protests are portrayed as security threats. The conflict of interests between workers and their employers is treated as a security threat, with employers' interests presented as though they were the common interests of society as a whole. Moreover, under conditions of war, those who voice objections can easily be accused of failing to care about their country or their nation. It is workers, working people and poorer sections of society who pay the heaviest price for war. People face both economic devastation and the social consequences of war. Yet they are still expected to make sacrifices. Their questions about why their wages are insufficient, where public resources are being spent and why their rights are being restricted are often drowned out by nationalist rhetoric and growing chauvinism.


Opposition to war and the labour struggle are not two separate areas of struggle. Opposing war cannot be separated from defending workers' livelihoods, their right to strike and their freedom to organise. The political climate created by war restricts working people's ability to defend their rights. At the same time, struggles to protect those rights can become a force against the social consequences of war policies. What matters is that opposition to war must not be confined to a separate sphere, disconnected from the everyday demands of working people.


Opposing war is not a separate task from defending workers' livelihoods, their right to strike and their freedom to organise. On the contrary, to understand why these rights are constantly under threat, we must recognise the social role played by war and militarism.


‘Racism and chauvinism prevent people from coming together’


How can we build a movement for social peace by connecting opposition to war with demands for a higher minimum wage, tax justice, trade union rights and women's right to life?


First of all, we must not reduce peace to politicians sitting around a negotiating table, the silencing of guns or the signing of an agreement. These are, of course, important. But those responsible for war have spent decades using propaganda to legitimise it, dividing peoples and forcing the working class into artificial divisions. Social peace cannot be achieved, nor can peace take root throughout society, simply by bringing the opposing forces to the negotiating table.


War is also a major obstacle to bringing class struggles and broader social movements together. The racism, nationalism and chauvinism being fuelled prevent people, women and young people from uniting around common demands. For example, a worker in the defence industry may be subjected to terrible exploitation, yet that exploitation can be dismissed as an issue because their work is presented as service to the nation.


We must also remember that an atmosphere of war and conflict makes it easier to promote false answers to the question of who is responsible for the poverty, insecurity, discrimination and violence people experience every day. The real causes lie in the existing system and its political and economic representatives. Yet the ruling classes can easily point the finger at migrants, women or an oppressed nation instead.


Another decisive aspect of the struggle to establish lasting peace on a social foundation is discussing what kind of lives people will lead, what rights …

author: radical.guide
title: All power to the people is something we build
content:
General Strike U.S. describes a phase where a movement has built something beyond capitalism, is ready to withdraw, is ready to sustain that withdrawal and has material power behind it. We don't disappear after disruption, the speaker says. We govern what we build, a dual and contending power becoming real power. All power to the people is something actually being built and committed to.


From the workshop "Many Struggles, One Fight: Building Autonomous Intercommunal Power, Direct Action Strategies and Revolutionary General Strike Networks" at the 2026 International Workshops.

author: Unknown
title: Food as an Act of Resistance
content:
The Thirty-Second Art Bulletin (October 2026)


The images in this art bulletin are from the exhibition

MST: 40 Years

, an online exhibition of illustrations celebrating four decades of struggle for land and agrarian reform by Brazil’s

Landless Rural Workers’ Movement (MST)

, organised in partnership with Tricontinental: Institute for Social Research and other organisations.


Listen to ‘

A desalambrar

’ (Tear Down the Fences!), written and performed by Uruguayan singer-songwriter Daniel Viglietti and also performed by Chilean singer-songwriter and theatre director Víctor Jara.


‘A desalambrar’ raises a fundamental question: who owns the land, and who has the right to cultivate it? The song’s call for agrarian reform and collective control over the resources that sustain life resonates with the struggle for food sovereignty.


Every 16 October, on World Food Day,

La Via Campesina

 and its member organisations around the world mobilise for the International Day of Action for Peoples’ Food Sovereignty and against Transnational Corporations. Their mobilisation affirms that food systems should serve peoples’ needs and protect nature rather than generate profits. The movement also calls for the defence of peasant seeds – seeds that farming communities have cultivated, selected, saved, and exchanged over generations – and communities’ rights to save, reproduce, exchange, and sell them.


To explore how the struggle for food sovereignty extends from the land to the kitchen, encompassing the preservation of seeds, cultural knowledge, and collective traditions, we interviewed four cooks, chefs, and organisers.

Anita Epulef Panguilef

, a Mapuche cook and seed keeper from Curarrehue in Chile’s Araucanía Region, demonstrates how food sovereignty is practised through everyday relationships with land, water, biodiversity, and community. Norma Listman and Saqib Keval, chefs and co-owners of

Masala y Maíz

 in Mexico City, explore the connections between Mexican, South Asian, and East African culinary traditions, using cooking to recover histories obscured by colonialism and shaped by migration and displacement. Ana Chã, a member of the MST and coordinator of the Elza Soares Cultural Centre in São Paulo, explains how these practices become part of a collective political project in which the struggle for land extends all the way to the table.


Together, their experiences show that defending food sovereignty means defending more than what ends up on our plates. It means defending peoples’ right to decide what is planted, who grows it, which seeds circulate, how food is prepared, whose knowledge is recognised, and how communities gather to eat.


Credit: Ricardo Keferaus.


In Curarrehue, nestled among the mountains, forests, and rivers of southern Chile, Anita Epulef reminds us that food sovereignty is not an abstract concept but an everyday practice that begins long before a pot is placed over the fire. Her daily life involves selecting seeds for planting, preparing a

trafkintu

 (a traditional Mapuche gathering for exchanging seeds and knowledge), checking whether frost has damaged the plants, gathering food from the vegetable garden, observing streams and other waterways, tending to

lawen

 (medicinal plants), reading the clouds, and greeting fellow community members. She describes these practices as a dialogue with

itrofillmogen

, a Mapuche concept encompassing the diversity of life and the relationships among all living beings.


The word ‘Mapuche’ itself means ‘people of the land’. The name expresses more than an identity tied to a particular territory. For Anita, the relationship with the land shapes people’s understanding of nourishment, health, knowledge, and responsibility. ‘If the land becomes sick, the food becomes sick too’, she explains. Caring for the land therefore means caring for life.


Yet this relationship is threatened by the growing concentration of agricultural land in fewer and fewer hands. According to a 2026

report

 jointly published by the Food and Agriculture Organisation of the United Nations (FAO), the International Land Coalition, and the French Agricultural Research Centre for International Development, there are approximately 570 million farms worldwide. About 85% of the world’s farms are smaller than two hectares, yet they account for only 9% of agricultural land. By contrast, farms larger than 1,000 hectares represent just 0.1% of all farms but operate more than half of that land …

title: Posición del colectivx anarquista NOS en las elecciones generales en Brasil en 2026
content:
POSICIÓN DEL COLECTIVX ANARQUISTA NOS EN LAS ELECCIONES GENERALES EN BRASIL EN 2026


A todxs


Este domingo, 25 de octubre de 2026, habrá segunda vuelta de las elecciones de la “democracia” burguesa en el espacio ocupado por la república Federativa de Brasil. Habrá elecciones para gobernador en algunos estados de la federación y para el cargo de presidente de la república. Los candidatos son: el actual presidente Lula da Silva en un intento de reelección; y Flavio Bolsonaro, senador e hijo del psicópata Jair Bolsonaro que gobernó Brasil entre 2019 y 2022.


Por un lado, Lula da Silva, representante de la izquierda institucional y del campo “progresista”. Notorio conciliador de clases y celoso gestor del capital en Brasil, Lula da Silva, su partido PT y su central sindical CUT representan la “democracia” de los ricos, con una política socialdemócrata disfrazada de socialismo donde las élites (financiera, industrial, terratenientes) siguen siendo élites y el pueblo permanece en una posición subalterna, con algunas migajas siendo distribuidas a los más pobres (subsidios en dinero, pequeños aumentos por encima de la inflación para jubilaciones y asalariados de bajos ingresos, ascenso social limitado para hijos de pobres a través del ingreso en universidades, etc.), y convivencia conciliadora más o menos pacífica con los dos bloques que se están formando en el mundo y que caminan hacia la Tercera Guerra Mundial: los Atlantistas (EE. UU., Unión Europea, “israel”) y el Mundo Multipolar (China, Rusia, Irán).


Por otro lado, Flavio Bolsonaro, representante de la extrema derecha y títere del imperialismo yanqui-sionista. Tan celoso como Lula da Silva en la gestión del capital, Flavio se diferencia de él por ser la figura clave en el proyecto del dictador yanqui Donald Trump de imponer gobiernos de extrema derecha en toda Sudamérica. Flavio mantiene una alianza con el dictador argentino Javier Milei y con el carnicero Benjamín Netanyahu, y ya ha advertido que aplicará la misma política económica que Milei en Brasil, que formará una alianza político-económica-militar con el Estado terrorista de “israel”, e incluso invitará a Marco Rubio, Secretario de Estado de Trump, A formar parte de su equipo de gobierno. Una de las principales bases de apoyo de Flavio son las iglesias evangélicas neopentecostales sionistas vinculadas a Estados Unidos y “Israel”.


Flavio es amigo íntimo del banquero Daniel Vorcaro, autor del mayor fraude financiero de la historia de Brasil, quien robó aproximadamente R$ 57.000.000.000,00 (US$ 11.000.000.000,00/EUR 10.000.000.000,00) de fondos de pensiones pertenecientes a empleados de empresas estatales, seguridad social y inversionistas privados. Flavio Bolsonaro recibió R$ 134.000.000,00 (US$ 26.000.000,00/EUR 23.000.000,00) de Vorcaro, supuestamente para la producción de la película Dark Horse, una biografía ficticia del psicópata Jair Bolsonaro. La mayor parte del dinero robado del pueblo fue desviado para el disfrute personal de la familia Bolsonaro.


Flavio tiene vínculos en el submundo del crimen con la cúpula de la organización mafiosa Comando Vermelho y con narcomilicias de extrema derecha.


Flavio actuó, sin cobrar honorarios, como abogado de Bruno Dias Delaroli, cabo de la despreciable PMERJ — Policía Militar del Estado de Río de Janeiro, quien en 2021 mató a la niña Ana Clara Gomes Machado, de 5 años, disparándole dos veces en la cabeza con un fusil de calibre 7,62x51mm NATO, sin motivo aparente alguno. El asesino permanece impune hasta el día de hoy gracias a las maniobras jurídicas de Flavio.


Flavio y su asesora económica, Daniella Marques, han declarado que las políticas criminales de Milei constituyen un “excelente ejemplo”; planean reemplazar a los funcionarios públicos por inteligencia artificial, modificar la Constitución de Brasil sin contar con una asamblea constituyente elegida para tal fin y cancelar las elecciones burguesas de 2030, con el objetivo de que Flavio ejerza un mandato ilegal y dictatorial de ocho años para, supuestamente, “poner a Brasil en su lugar”.


En definitiva, Flavio Bolsonaro es una figura similar a un Ramfis Trujillo o un “Tachito” Somoza: un *playboy* y vividor, hijo de un dictador, elevado a la categoría de político; alguien incluso peor, más perverso y maligno que su propio padre, que pretende transformar Brasil en una dictadura narco-fascista, evangélica, sionista y personalista al servicio de la familia Bolsonaro.


Ante este panorama alarmante …

title: 17 octobre 2026 : Et notre classe releva la tête
content:
La lutte de classe en France s'est accélérée et clarifiée en une séquence en réalité très dense et aux conséquences certainement peu mesurables actuellement. Dans tous les cas, la rencontre qu'il y a eu le 17 entre différentes fractions de la classe en lutte et la force prolétarienne qu'elle permet de poser est précieuse.


1 - Discussion en acte


Après un mois d'une lutte acharnée au sein du mouvement qui a pris dans les lycées en septembre 2026, les jeunes prolos les plus offensifs commençaient à être isolés face à la répression et la dissociation. Dans ce contexte la date du 17 octobre, qui circulait déjà comme un appel au retour des Gilets Jaunes, a sonné comme un appel à la classe : un appel à un grand mouvement fort, massif et déterminé à ne pas se laisser écraser par la répression. Un appel à ce que la classe relève la tête, prenne la rue et exprime sa force.


À cet appel, la classe en lutte a répondu présent. Défiant les tenants de l'ordre, posant une importante offensivité, elle a fait un doigt d'honneur à l'ordre bourgeois et exprimé en acte sa prise de parti pour la radicalité de la lutte. Les plus jeunes prolos doivent être tellement satisfaits de pouvoir trouver là la force de continuer à tenir tête à tout les tenants de l'ordre :

CPE

, flics, patrons, prêtres en tout genre, grands-frères, profs, éducs et parents.


Cette date du 17 a été un moment pour se constituer comme force. C'est un début. Et ça fait du bien. Il s'agissait déjà, pour la classe en mouvement, de se compter, d'éprouver la force dont elle est capable et de poser en acte la question de son orientation dans la période.


2 - Lutte dans la lutte


Il y a eu une lutte dans la lutte ce 17 octobre. Une lutte entre la tendance «

 

manifestation-revendication-réforme

 

» liée à la gauche et une tendance plus autonome, plus offensive, qui porte la proposition de l'attaque directe des institutions de l'État et de la marchandise. Une lutte entre les tendances qui portent le discours de dissociation d'avec les violences et les pillages, et les tendances qui poussent à la radicalisation, l'offensivité et la prise au tas. Cette lutte s'est faite par des discussions, des engueulades, et parfois des coups. Mais très vite il s'est avéré que la tendance réformiste était complètement dépassée, en particulier dans les métropoles de taille moyenne ou grande.


D'un point de vue général, c'est clairement la seconde option qui a gagné la bataille de l'hégémonie, en tout cas ce 17 octobre. Ce n'est pas un acquis pour toujours. L'autre camp de cette lutte dans la lutte, celui de la dissociation, s'organise pour répliquer. La gauche réformiste, partisane de la désescalade, de la négociation, de la respectabilité, de la République et de la démocratie est aujourd'hui dans le parti de l'ordre, préparant la contre-révolution. Elle y porte la solution démocratique et le retour à l'ordre par la réforme institutionnelle et le dialogue social (6

e

 République, nouvelle constitution, élection anticipées, etc.). La disquette habituelle, déjà expérimentée in vivo au Chili de 2019 à 2021 notamment. La gauche endort la révolte en engageant le processus démocratique de la réforme de l'État et en se posant comme l'alternative au fascisme. Mais partout où elle a été portée au pouvoir, elle n'a en réalité fait qu'entretenir le désastre, réprimant tout ce qui refuse son cadre et le déborde dans la lutte, préparant ainsi la victoire écrasante de l'extrême droite dans la foulée.


Mais le destin funeste promis au 21

e

 siècle n'est pas une fatalité. Les jeunes prolos se soulèvent partout dans le monde pour le refuser. L'autonomie, l'offensivité révolutionnaire, la volonté de synchroniser les offensives pour se constituer en force capable de détruire l'ordre existant, sont des positions qui existent dans la société. Elle ne sont pas majoritaires, mais elles ont une place de plus en plus importante dans la jeunesse prolétarienne actuelle. Et au vu du futur cauchemardesque et suffoquant promis par la bourgeoisie à notre classe, ces positions sont appelées à se répandre bien plus. Tout l'enjeu pour notre classe est de parvenir donc à se constituer en une force capable de frapper le monde bourgeois d'une façon si importante que cela lui soit fatal. Et de parvenir dans le même mouvement à poser les bases d'un rapport social où s'en sera terminé de l'exploitation, du fric, de l'État, des armes, des nations et de leurs colonisations permanentes, et de toute la liste des …

author: Unknown
title: İsviçre’de aşırı sağa karşı ortak mücadele ve dayanışma çağrısı
content:
Geçtiğimiz hafta sonu İsviçre’nin Basel kentinde BastA! (Basels starke Alternative – Basel’in Güçlü Alternatifi) Tarafından düzenlenen Siyaset Evi etkinliğinde bir araya gelen toplumsal ve politik muhalefet güçleri Avrupa'da yükselen aşırı sağla mücadelede ortak politika imkânlarını harekete geçirmek konusunda görüş birliğine vardılar. 


“Faşizm, Karşı Güç ve Gelecek” başlığıyla gerçekleştirilen etkinlikte, Avrupa’da aşırı sağın yükselişi, otoriter politikaların yaygınlaşması ve bunlara karşı geliştirilebilecek ortak mücadele stratejileri ele alındı.


Konuşmaların, atölyelerin ve grup tartışmalarının gerçekleştirildiği etkinlikte, sol hareketlerin yalnızca mevcut politikalara karşı çıkmakla yetinmemesi, toplumsal sorunlara somut çözümler üreten ve gündelik yaşamda karşılık bulan dayanışma ağları oluşturması gerektiği üzerinde duruldu.


Bolliger: Sol, somut dayanışma yapıları inşa etmeli


Etkinliğin açılış konuşmasını yapan BastA! Başkanı Oliver Bolliger, artan kiralar, yükselen yaşam maliyetleri, ağır çalışma koşulları ve geleceğe ilişkin belirsizliklerin toplumun geniş kesimlerini doğrudan etkilediğine dikkat çekerek, sol hareketlerin bu sorunlar karşısında yalnızca eleştiri üretmesinin yeterli olmadığını söyledi.


Bolliger temel yönelimini çöyle özetledi:


“Kiralardaki artış, yükselen yaşam maliyetleri, stresli çalışma koşulları ve geleceğe yönelik belirsizlik, insanların günlük yaşamlarını doğrudan etkiliyor. Sol, eleştiriyle sınırlı kalmamalı. İnsanların bu sorunlarla başa çıkmalarına yardımcı olacak somut dayanışma yapıları inşa etmelidir.” 


Atölyelerde ortak mücadele yöntemleri tartışıldı


Etkinlik kapsamında düzenlenen beş atölyede feminist mücadele, iklim adaleti, demokratik konfederalizm, antifaşist sosyal politikalar, mahalle örgütlenmesi ve örgüt içi dayanışma konuları ele alındı.


Katılımcılar, farklı toplumsal mücadelelerin birbirleriyle nasıl ilişkilendirilebileceğini, ortak örgütlenme olanaklarını ve dayanışma ağlarının nasıl güçlendirilebileceğini tartıştı.


İsviçre merkezli ilerici kampanya ve dayanışma örgütü Campax’ın Genel Yöneticisi Itziar Marañón, aşırı sağa karşı mücadelenin yalnızca mevcut hak ve kazanımların korunmasıyla sınırlı kalmaması gerektiğini belirtti.


Marañón, alternatiflerin ortaya konulmasını istedi:


“Mücadelemizi mevcut kazanımları savunmakla sınırlamamalı, şiddet içermeyen ve adil bir yaşam için olumlu alternatifleri görünür kılmalıyız."


Faşizme karşı feminist stratejilerin tartışıldığı atölyede, kadın düşmanı erkeklik anlayışlarının gençler üzerindeki etkileri ve sosyal medyada cinsiyetçilikle mücadele yöntemleri değerlendirildi.


Aşırı sağa karşı mücadelede kullanılan dilin de belirleyici olduğunu vurgulayan Marañón, siyasi söylemin toplumun geniş kesimlerinin anlayabileceği ve kendi yaşam deneyimleriyle ilişkilendirebileceği bir biçimde kurulması gerektiğini söyledi.


İklim adaleti mücadelesi ve ekofaşizme karşı direniş


İklim adaleti üzerine gerçekleştirilen atölyenin sonuçlarını paylaşan Kolektif İklim Adaleti temsilcileri Zoë ve Mirjam, iklim krizi ile aşırı sağın yükselişi arasındaki ilişkiye dikkat çekti.


İklim adaleti mücadelesinin ırkçılığa, ayrımcılığa ve otoriter politikalara karşı mücadeleden ayrı düşünülemeyeceğini belirten Zoë ve Mirjam, ekofaşizme karşı örgütlü ve aktif bir direnişin gerekli olduğunu vurguladı.


Atölyede, büyük teknoloji şirketlerinin çevresel ve toplumsal etkileri de tartışıldı. Bu şirketlerin yüksek enerji tüketiminin yanı sıra gözetim ve denetim mekanizmaları aracılığıyla otoriter eğilimleri güçlendirdiği ifade edildi.


Katılımcılar, ekolojik krize karşı mücadelenin yalnızca çevrenin korunmasıyla sınırlı tutulamayacağını, toplumsal eşitsizlikler ve otoriterleşmeyle birlikte ele alınması gerektiğini belirtti.


Demokratik konfederalizm ve mahallelerde öz örgütlenme


Ronahî Kadın Konseyi adına değerlendirme oturumuna katılan Özen Aytaç, yerel örgütlenmenin, toplumsal katılımın ve mahallelerde kurulan dayanışma ilişkilerinin önemine dikkat çekti.


Suriye ve Rojava’daki demokratik konfederalizm deneyimlerinden örnekler veren Aytaç, özellikle kriz dönemlerinde insanların yaşadıkları mahallelerde örgütlenmesinin ve ortak karar alma mekanizmaları oluşturmasının önemini vurguladı.


Mahalle örgütlenmesinin yalnızca benzer siyasi görüşlere sahip kişileri bir araya getirmekle sınırlı kalmaması gerektiğini belirten Aytaç, gündelik yaşamda kurulan ilişkilerin uzun vadeli ve sürdürülebilir dayanışma ağlarına dönüşebileceğini ifade …

author: Chris Walker
title: Kagan Warns Far Right Supreme Court Rulings Will Undermine American Democracy
content:
The American people view the current political system as “a nightmare,” Kagan said, “and they’re right.”

Truthout is a vital news source and a living history of political struggle. If you think our work is valuable, support us with a donation of any size.

Supreme Court Justice Elena Kagan warned a group of law students at Catholic University on Tuesday that the current iteration of the court — which has a 6-3 majority of far right conservatives — is upending American democracy.

Kagan focused much of her remarks on addressing gerrymandering over the past year by both political parties. The map-changing began when Republicans started redrawing districts in order to get an upper hand over Democrats in the midterms. Democrats responded in kind, redrawing maps in states where they were more likely to see gains to counter the Republicans’ efforts.

(Democrats have also submitted legislation to prevent these “gerrymander wars” in the future by requiring nonpartisan boards to redraw maps going forward, a proposal that Republicans have rejected.)

“Both political parties have been engaged in a race to the bottom in terms of doing these partisan gerrymanders, effectively depriving masses of citizens of their rights to voting equality,” Kagan lamented in her lecture to the law students.

Such gerrymandering pushes political parties “toward the extremes, because the only thing anybody has to worry about anymore is being primaried,” Kagan said.

It is making what I think is unfortunately a too polarized country even more so. In this election, and the next election, we are seeing large states with substantial numbers of people who vote for Republicans and who vote for Democrats, and the states are going to be tried to turn all red or all blue in a way that I think is very destructive to our democracy.

Through these redistricting efforts, many conservative states ended up gerrymandering Black residents out of districts where they were the majority, thus reducing their voices in Congress. The conservative-led Supreme Court upheld that process this year, ruling that enforcement mechanisms for the Voting Rights Act that preserved Black-majority districts were unconstitutional, a finding that Kagan dissented from.

She elaborated on her opposition to that opinion on Tuesday.

“I think part of the reason why the court got it wrong was a lack of the appropriate concern or understanding of the consequences of their decisions. … The court has blinded itself to the very deleterious effects of their rulings on how the political system works and has created a democracy that doesn’t work as well as it should,” Kagan said.

The liberal justice also discussed the Supreme Court’s rulings on campaign finance, which have opened up the floodgates of influence spending by millionaires and billionaires in recent years.

“The people of America look around this political system and think that all this money, chasing all these political candidates, is a nightmare, and they’re right,” Kagan said.

Polling shows that a majority of Americans are indeed upset with the current iteration of the nation’s high court.

In an Economist/YouGov survey conducted at the end of the Supreme Court’s term earlier this year, only 36 percent of voters gave the justices overall approving marks, while 50 percent voiced disapproval of the court. There was a notable partisan edge in favor of liberal bloc members of the court, the poll found, noting that every member of that bloc received net positive ratings, while every conservative justice on the court received negative ratings.

The Supreme Court’s rulings threaten to undermine election safety, too, said Dan Canon, professor at the Louis D. Brandeis School of Law, in an op-ed for Truthout earlier this week.

“What harm might result from the opinions of today’s Court, an institution unmistakably captured by a power-hungry executive? In a nation of this size, facing democratic decay this severe, there is no such thing as a safe prediction,” Canon wrote. “But if you’re the gambling type, the smart money is on a spectacularly violent future for U.S. elections, if not in the upcoming midterms, then likely by 2028.”

“At their best, independent courts channel even the most heated political grievances into nonviolent resolutions,” Canon said. “If an apex court abdicates that role by disenfranchising voters, institutionalizing clientelism, and shielding executive lawlessness, it removes the pressure valves that keep democratic …

title: Αντιφασιστική – αντιρατσιστική συγκέντρωση και πορεία, Σάββατο 24/10, στο Σταθμό Λαρίσης, Αθήνα
content:
ΣΥΛΛΟΓΟΣ ΕΚΠΑΙΔΕΥΤΙΚΩΝ Π.Ε. «Ο ΑΡΙΣΤΟΤΕΛΗΣ»


Αθήνα, 21-10-2026


Θέμα: Ντόπιοι – Μετανάστριες ζούμε, δουλεύουμε μαζί, όλοι μαζί τσακίζουμε φασίστες και Ναζί/ Όλες/Όλοι στη συγκέντρωση και πορεία Σάββατο 24 Οκτωβρίου, 12:00 Στ. Λαρίσης/Στηρίζουμε τη συγκέντρωση την Πέμπτη 22 Οκτώβρη, 6:30μμ, πλ. Βικτωρίας


Τη Δευτέρα 12 Οκτωβρίου στις 21:00 το βράδυ, ομάδα 15-20 φασιστών επιτέθηκε σε βάρος δύο προσφύγων μαθητών έξω από το 6ο Εσπερινό ΓΕΛ Αθηνών – ένα σχολείο όπου φοιτούν παιδιά της εργατικής τάξης, ντόπιοι και μετανάστες που παλεύουν για ένα μεροκάματο. Ο απολογισμός ήταν να νοσηλευτεί ο ένας σε σοβαρή κατάσταση και διασωληνωμένος έπειτα από πισώπλατη μαχαιριά που δέχτηκε, και ο άλλος με τραύματα από ξυλοδαρμό. Η έρευνα της αστυνομίας για το περιστατικό κωλυσιεργεί και προσιδιάζει σε συγκάλυψη, όμοια με τα «στραβά μάτια» που έκανε στις επιθέσεις της Χρυσής Αυγής, ενώ ήδη κυκλοφορούν βίντεο που ταυτοποιούν τους δράστες. Η παραπάνω δολοφονική επίθεση έρχεται να προστεθεί σε μια σειρά φασιστικών χτυπημάτων που έχουν σημειωθεί σε βάρος προσφύγων, μεταναστών και αντιφασιστών αγωνιστών του κινήματος, τόσο στις λαϊκές γειτονιές του Κέντρου (Άγιος Παντελεήμονας, Σεπόλια, Κολωνός, Κυψέλη ,Παγκρατι) όσο και σε εργατικές περιοχές, όπως η πρόσφατη επίθεση με μαχαίρι στην Ελευσίνα.


Τα παραπάνω θυμίζουν έντονα τα πογκρόμ της Χρυσής Αυγής. Η πρόσφατη αποφυλάκιση του φασίστα Κασιδιάρη, η δραστηριοποίηση μελών της Propatria και η επανεμφάνιση του μετώπου νεολαίας της Χρυσής Αυγής μαρτυρούν την οργανωμένη προσπάθεια των φασιστών να ξαναβγούν στους δρόμους. Στόχος τους είναι να λειτουργήσουν ξανά ως το μακρύ χέρι του συστήματος: να στρέψουν τον εξαθλιωμένο κόσμο της δουλειάς ενάντια στους πιο καταπιεσμένους, κρύβοντας τον πραγματικό υπεύθυνο για τη φτώχεια μας. Η ευθύνη της κυβέρνησης είναι τεράστια και εγκληματική. Την ίδια στιγμή που η κυβερνητική πολιτική τσακίζει τις ζωές μας, ο Υπουργός Προστασίας του Πολίτη προαναγγέλλει πογκρόμ και καλεί σε χαφιεδισμό σε βάρος μεταναστών, κλείνοντας το μάτι στα φασιστικά τάγματα εφόδου για να αποπροσανατολίσει την κοινωνική οργή. Μη χάνοντας ευκαιρία, στις γειτονιές της Κυψέλης κυκλοφορεί κάλεσμα από ένα σύλλογο που καλεί τον κόσμο να καταδίδει σε αυτους και την αστυνομία όπου εντοπίζει συγκατοίκηση μεταναστών, προσπαθώντας να κανιβαλίσουν την κοινωνική δυσαρέσκεια.


Κυβέρνηση, αστυνομία, αφεντικά και φασίστες συνεργάζονται για να επιβάλουν τον φόβο. Την ώρα που η καλπάζουσα ακρίβεια στα είδη πρώτης ανάγκης, τα απλησίαστα ενοίκια και η στεγαστική κρίση διώχνουν τις εργατικές οικογένειες και τη νεολαία από τις ίδιες τους τις γειτονιές, η κυβέρνηση και το κεφάλαιο θέλουν τους μετανάστες χωρίς έγγραφα και δικαιώματα. Τους θέλουν απομονωμένους, ώστε να αποτελούν ένα απόλυτα αναλώσιμο και φθηνό εργατικό δυναμικό, έρμαιο στις ορέξεις της εργοδοσίας, συμπιέζοντας τους μισθούς όλων μας. Θέλουν να επιβάλουν παντού «νέες Μανωλάδες» της άγριας εκμετάλλευσης. Χαρακτηριστικό παράδειγμα αποτελεί η σωρεία εργατικών ατυχημάτων (εργατικών δολοφονιών) Αράβων μεταναστών στο μεγάλο κατασκευαστικό κάτεργο του Ελληνικού, εκεί όπου τα κέρδη των κεφαλαιούχων ποτίζονται με το αίμα της τάξης μας.


Οι γειτονιές, τα σχολεία και οι πλατείες μας ανήκουν σε ντόπιους και μετανάστες που ζουν, υποφέρουν από την ίδια ακρίβεια και παλεύουν μαζί. Δεν θα επιτρέψουμε στους φασίστες να γίνουν οι μαντρόσκυλα των αφεντικών και της κυβέρνησης στις γειτονιές μας. Απέναντι στον διαχωρισμό με βάση τη φυλή ή την καταγωγή, εμείς προτάσσουμε την ταξική αλληλεγγύη. Φασίστες, κράτος και κεφάλαιο θα βρίσκουν απέναντί τους την οργανωμένη, κοινή μας δράση για ζωή, στέγαση, δουλειά και αξιοπρέπεια.
