author: Mag
title: Brandbrief von Lehrkräften über Rechtsextremismus an der Schule: Oft verharmlost und kein Einzelfall, nicht nur in Brandenburg
content:
Dossier


„

Nach einem

Brandbrief über rechtsextreme Vorfälle


 an einer Schule in Brandenburg hat der designierte Bildungsminister Steffen Freiberg (SPD) die Lehrkräfte zu Offenheit aufgerufen. (…) Die Forscherin Heike Radvan forderte, die Kultusministerkonferenz (KMK) solle sich stärker mit Rechtsextremismus an Schulen vor allem in Ostdeutschland befassen. Die Amadeu Antonio Stiftung hofft, dass der Brief aufrüttelt. In einem anonymen Brief hatten Lehrkräfte an einer Schule in Burg im Spreewald beklagt, sie seien täglich mit Rechtsextremismus, Sexismus und Homophobie konfrontiert. Dabei geht es um mehr als Hakenkreuze auf Möbeln, rechtsextreme Musik im Unterricht und demokratiefeindliche Parolen in den Schulfluren. Die ausländischen Schüler an der Schule erlebten Ausgrenzung, Mobbing und Gewaltandrohungen. Es herrsche das Gefühl der Machtlosigkeit und der erzwungenen Schweigsamkeit. In dem Brief ist auch von einer „Mauer des Schweigens“ die Rede. Die Lehrkräfte beklagten fehlende Unterstützung von Schulleitungen, Schulämtern und Politik

…“

Meldung vom 01.05.2023 im Migazin


 („Rechtsextremismus an Schulen oft verharmlost“), siehe weitere dazu, nicht nur in Brandenburg und nicht nur SchülerInnen:


Preis für Zivilcourage für die Lehrkräfte von Burg: Was ihr Brandbrief bewirkte – und was nicht


„Für ihren Mut gegen Rechtsextremismus werden die Brandenburger Lehrkräfte Laura Nickel und Max Teske am Sonntag (25. Oktober) in Köln mit dem Karl-Küpper-Preis für Zivilcourage ausgezeichnet. Der mit 10.000 Euro dotierte Preis erinnert an den Kölner Karnevalisten Karl Küpper, der während der NS-Zeit den Nationalsozialismus öffentlich verspottete. Nickel und Teske hatten im Frühjahr 2023 etwas ausgelöst, das weit über ihre Schule hinausging. Ihre Warnung sorgte bundesweit für Aufmerksamkeit, beschäftigte den Brandenburger Landtag und gab Anstöße für politische Veränderungen. Auch an ihrer ehemaligen Schule hat sich einiges getan. Doch drei Jahre später zeigt sich: Die Probleme, vor denen sie warnten, bestehen fort. Begonnen hatte alles an der Grund- und Oberschule „Mina Witkojc“ in Burg im Spreewald. Im April 2023 veröffentlichten Nickel und Teske einen zunächst anonymen Brandbrief. Sie schilderten Hakenkreuze auf Schulmobiliar, Hitlergrüße, rechtsextreme Musik und rassistische Parolen in ihrer Schule. Kinder und Jugendliche mit Migrationsgeschichte wurden nach ihren Angaben bedroht, beleidigt und ausgegrenzt. Auch Sexismus und Homophobie gehörten zu den Problemen. (…) Der Brief sorgte bundesweit für Aufsehen. Für die Verfasser hatte das schwerwiegende Folgen. Nachdem ihre Identität bekannt geworden war, wurden sie öffentlich angefeindet und in sozialen Netzwerken bedroht. Im Ort tauchten Aufkleber mit ihren Gesichtern und beleidigenden Aufforderungen auf. Im Sommer 2023 entschieden sich beide, die Schule zu verlassen. Auch den Rückhalt der Politik empfanden Nickel und Teske als unzureichend. (…) Nach dem öffentlichen Eklat kam zunächst Bewegung in die Schule. Im August 2023 wechselte die Schulleitung. Lehrkräfte erhielten zusätzliche Fortbildungen, externe Fachleute unterstützten die Aufarbeitung der Vorfälle und es wurden Projekte zur Demokratiebildung entwickelt. Die

Regionalen Arbeitsstellen für Bildung, Integration und Demokratie (RAA)


 begleiteten die Schule. Hinzu kamen Projekte, bei denen Schülerinnen und Schüler lernen sollten, rechtsextreme Einstellungen zu erkennen und sich mit demokratischen Werten auseinanderzusetzen. (…) Auch auf politischer Ebene blieb die Debatte nicht folgenlos. Brandenburg verschärfte 2024 sein

Schulgesetz


. Nach dem neu eingeführten Paragrafen 64a müssen Schulen unter anderem antisemitische und rassistische Handlungen sowie bestimmte Formen der Verherrlichung des Nationalsozialismus unverzüglich dem zuständigen Schulamt melden. Sie müssen außerdem über eingeleitete Maßnahmen informieren. Damit wurde der Umgang mit solchen Vorfällen verbindlicher geregelt. Im September 2025 traten zudem überarbeitete Vorgaben unter dem Titel

„Hinsehen – Handeln – Helfen“


 in Kraft. Sie beschreiben genauer, wie Schulen auf Gewalt, Diskriminierung und verfassungsfeindliche Handlungen reagieren müssen. (…) In einem

rbb-Interview vom März 2026


 zog Nickel eine teilweise positive Bilanz. Demokratieprojekte würden stärker nachgefragt, es gebe mehr Fortbildungsangebote. Gleichzeitig müssten Schulen diese Möglichkeiten häufiger nutzen. Dafür brauche es mehr Geld, Personal und zeitliche Entlastung …

author: CNT Valladolid
title: El nuevo local de CNT en Valladolid abre sus puertas
content:
Antifascistas, antirracistas, anticapitalistas, transfeministas e internacionalistas. En medio de una convocatoria de huelga general por la vivienda y contra todos los poderes que viven de desangrar a la clase trabajadora, CNT Valladolid inaugura un nuevo local en calle Merced, 6, de Valladolid, entre las plazas de Santa Cruz y Circular.


Hace más de dos años empezamos un proyecto muy ilusionante. Nuestro local se quedaba pequeño y teníamos que buscar otro. Hicimos un proceso de reflexión colectiva, para tener claras nuestras necesidades presentes y futuras. Una tienda de fontanería se ha convertido en un sindicato como el nuestro, con más salas donde reunirse, un salón amplio en el que convocar actos… Un nuevo espacio en Valladolid a disposición de todas las personas trabajadoras.


A pesar de que quedan retoques, el pasado 17 de octubre nos decidimos a abrir puertas en un acto en el que nos reunimos la afiliacIón con personas afines del presente y del futuro. Contamos con las actuaciones de Jesús Puebla MImo, de Rubén Ruiz, Rosa Vicente y José Luis Alonso, de Chusma y de Juguillos, de Astrolabio, y tuvimos ocasión de mover el esqueleto con las aportaciones de Eva DJ. No faltaron el recorrido por el nuevo local, el picoteo hecho a mano en comida y bebida, y sobre todo las ganas de llenar de vida esta nueva casa para la rebeldía y la defensa frente a empresaurios y politicastros de todos nuestros derechos actuales y los que nos inventemos en el futuro. Para todo ello y más, contad con CNT, vuestra herramienta de lucha, vuestro sindicato de clase, vuestra alternativa sindical.


A continuación hemos puesto en marcha unas jornadas de inauguración de las que tenéis información en inauguracion.cntvalladolid.es


Reproducimos a continuación el manifiesto que refleja esta nueva etapa:


Hoy, sábado, 17 de octubre, inauguramos una nueva etapa en CNT Valladolid.


Estrenamos un espacio más amplio. Un espacio donde pueda entrar más gente, donde podamos encontrarnos, organizarnos y construir juntas una respuesta colectiva a la realidad que vivimos.


Porque este local no es solamente un lugar nuevo. Es un espacio de encuentro para quienes entendemos que nuestros derechos no son concesiones, que la dignidad no se negocia y que nuestra fuerza está en la lucha obrera.


Y cuando decimos clase trabajadora, no hablamos solo de quienes tienen un contrato o un empleo. También hablamos de quienes trabajan sin derechos, de quienes sostienen los cuidados y de quienes encuentran las puertas cerradas al empleo por su identidad o su condición.


Porque si el sistema utiliza esas diferencias para dividirnos y para colocar a unas personas en posiciones de mayor vulnerabilidad, el sindicalismo tiene que hacer justamente lo contrario:

reconocernos como parte de una misma clase y organizarnos juntas.


Por eso abrimos este espacio.


Para que haya más gente, más organización y más lucha.


Porque somos CNT


CNT tiene una historia profundamente ligada a la organización de la clase trabajadora y a la lucha por los derechos laborales y sociales.


Antes que este local, CNT tuvo varios, cada uno con su historia: desahucios, asaltos policiales, atentados… Desde la calle Francisco Zarandona multiplicó por diez su afiliación en tiempos de la segunda republica; desde los pactos de la moncloa, superando multiples dificultades, hemos crecido en varios locales en Valladolid que han ido abriendo cada vez más brecha en la provincia y en la ciudad. Hasta llegar a este en el que nos encontramos


Somos anarcosindicalistas. Entendemos que quienes vivimos de nuestro trabajo tenemos capacidad para defender nuestros derechos colectivamente y para construir otras formas de relacionarnos y organizarnos frente a la explotación.


Tenemos una memoria sindical fuerte y combativa. Pero no queremos convertir esa memoria en una fotografía, ni mirar hacia atrás únicamente para recordar lo que fuimos.

Nuestra memoria nos obliga a mirar hacia delante.


Porque el sistema contra el que se organizaron quienes nos precedieron no ha desaparecido. La explotación adopta nuevas formas. La precariedad se normaliza. Trabajar ya no garantiza unas condiciones de vida dignas. Y quienes acumulan riqueza siguen teniendo capacidad para decidir sobre nuestras vidas.


Por eso estamos aquí.


Porque la lucha sigue


Y esa lucha sigue hoy en múltiples frentes que se complementan.


Una de ellas es la

lucha antifascista

.

title: Émeutes, pillages et état d'urgence
content:
Allons nous enfin quitter l'époque contemporaine ? C'est la question qu'est venue ouvrir avec fracas le soulèvement du 17 octobre. Pour discuter de cette journée, de ce qu'elle enseigne, appelle et peut-être présage, nous allons enchaîner les invitations et les discussions. Pour cette première, nous accueillons Eugénie Mérieau et Samuel Hayat. On discute de ce qui a fait événement et de pourquoi cet événement naît d'une époque, celle-là même que tout le monde veut quitter et pas seulement la GenZ. Comment la police s'est-elle retrouvée à ce point en déroute ? Pourquoi l'état d'urgence n'a-t-il pas encore été décrété ? Sommes-nous à l'aube d'un virage encore plus autoritaire du régime ou de sa dislocation finale ? En quoi le pillage doit-il être défendu contre ceux qui s'en désolidarisent ? author: Ben Hillier
title: ‘Post-truth’ politics is business as usual
content:
Since Donald Trump’s arrival on the scene more than a decade ago, lying in politics has become ever more shameless. It’s the “post-truth politics” era, apparently. Oxford Dictionaries, which crowned “post-truth” the word of the year when Trump first took up residence at the White House, noted that “it describes not just particular assertions, but a general characteristic of our age”. The

Economist

 wrote at the time:

“His brazenness is not punished, but taken as evidence of his willingness to stand up to elite power … [Post-truth politics] picks out the heart of what is new: that truth is not falsified, or contested, but of secondary importance. Feelings, not facts, are what matter in this sort of campaigning.”

Yet if “post-truth” is characterised by emotional appeals and relegating facts to the sidelines, it’s not clear that politics has fundamentally changed at all.

On a 2008 autumn night in Grant Park, Chicago, Democratic president-elect Barack Obama, promoted as an articulate Harvard Law graduate with a firm grasp on reality, addressed an enormous crowd. The backdrop was an emerging economic depression: millions of workers were being sacked, more than 3 million homes had been foreclosed in the previous 24 months, the financial system had collapsed, and tent cities of the newly homeless were springing up on the edges of cities across America.

“The true strength of our nation comes … from the enduring power of our ideals: democracy, liberty, opportunity”, Obama promised. “This is our time … to reclaim the American dream and reaffirm that fundamental truth, that, out of many, we are one.” His optimistic gesture was one of the finest moments for the politics of feeling, the culmination of a campaign run on vague notions of hope, change and the slogan “Yes, we can”—appropriated from the mass struggle of undocumented migrants, millions of whom he would go on to deport as president.

Yet Obama’s oration wasn’t considered “post-truth”, because the sentiments, similarly articulated by most political leaders in the democratic West for the last century, were underpinned by unchallenged liberal certainties: that under capitalism, anyone can “make it”, that improvement is the child of hard work, that all individual interests can be accommodated within the national interest. 

“Dream, believe, achieve.” Vacuous aphorisms of this variety are the bedrock of capitalist politics. They aren’t facts or truths, but expressions of an idealised liberal-democratic world whose promises have never been realised. Yet they endure. So why only now are we said to live in a world of post-truth politics? Probably because the empty pledges of progress and prosperity have given way to messages and tones that reflect an era of social decline and political decay at odds with the vision of the world that liberals remain desperate to believe. 

Marketing the truth

Many have pointed out that the last four decades of rapacious free trade and economic and political crises sowed the seeds of this post-truth age. Soaring inequality, greater economic precariousness, more and more people expected to fend for themselves against the forces of globalised capitalism. So British commentator George Monbiot wrote in the

Guardian

 that “Donald Trump’s election started in England in 1975”, when Margaret Thatcher took over the leadership of the Conservative Party and got everyone reading, and later implementing, the work of Frederick Hayek.

This focus on a purportedly neoliberal economy in producing the “Trumpian moment” (and the broader rise of the far right) misses the universal aspect of this so-called post-truth era. Capitalism is based on theft, and all pro-capitalist politics—far right, conservative, libertarian, liberal, even social democratic—exists to cover up or justify it. Pro-capitalist politics is fundamentally about deceiving people into thinking the system is either fair or natural, when it is neither. 

Nearly 200 years ago, Karl Marx and Frederick Engels first wrote of the stripping away of humanity that came with capitalism’s emergence from the old medieval order:

“The capitalist class, wherever it has got the upper hand, has put an end to all feudal, patriarchal, idyllic relations. It has … left remaining no other nexus between man and man than naked self-interest, than callous ‘cash payment’ … It has resolved personal worth into exchange value, and in place of the numberless indefeasible chartered freedoms, has set up that single …

title: ‘Terror-free Turkey’ rhetoric and security directive mark new university term
content:
The new academic year has begun under the shadow of security-oriented policies, alongside chronic problems such as inadequate student grants, safety concerns in dormitories run by the Credit and Dormitories Institution (KYK), dysfunctional democratic mechanisms and sexism on campuses. The Ministry of Interior's 17-point circular on “Security Measures at Universities”, issued on 9 September 2026, effectively treats campuses as “crime scenes”. Together with the Council of Higher Education's (YÖK) instruction to address the theme of “Terror-free Turkey” in the first lecture, it reflects the government's efforts to tighten its control over universities.


ANF spoke to Sude Şener from Labour Youth, Yasin Incekara from the Revolutionary Youth Union (DGB) and Özcan Berber from Student Activity about the new academic year, the government's security policies at universities and how students plan to organise in the coming period.


‘The Council of Higher Education promotes nationalism under the guise of peace’


 


Sude Şener from Labour Youth said the government and the Council of Higher Education were seeking to reduce the question of peace to a matter of “terrorism” through these measures. Şener said, “We must establish our own perspective in response to the presidential regime's attempts to restrict struggles for rights. Although the government fuels nationalist sentiments, what matters to us is the Kurdish people's struggle for freedom and peace.”


Özcan Berber from Student Activity said the government's recent policies, including its “Terror-free Turkey” initiative, were fundamentally aimed at neutralising social opposition. Berber said the demands of workers, students and the wider public, including growing calls for peace and democracy, were being suppressed through the rhetoric of “counterterrorism”. He said the government's rhetoric served a political agenda extending beyond security concerns, adding that even the most basic gatherings, information stands and awareness-raising activities on campuses were being treated as potential criminal offences.


 


Berber described the policy as follows: “As a continuation of neoliberal policies, they want to divide students, make them focus solely on their individual careers and prevent them from questioning social issues. They want a system in which we cannot trust one another or act collectively. They know that when we come together, we will begin to question this system. By isolating us, they aim to make us remain silent as even our most fundamental rights are taken away.”


Yasin Incekara, a member of the Revolutionary Student Union, said they had witnessed a series of attacks by the capitalist state against social opposition in general and universities in particular. Incekara said, “Organising events at universities under the banner of ‘Terror-free Turkey’ is seen as a means for the capitalist government, the reactionary AKP administration, to continue spreading its ideological and cultural propaganda on campuses. The events announced by the Council of Higher Education today are being presented as part of ‘Terror-free Turkey’. Yet we live in a country where even the most fundamental democratic rights and freedoms of all sections of social opposition are being trampled upon. The Council of Higher Education, which has promoted chauvinism, nationalism and other misguided ideas and attitudes in previous years, now appears to be taking certain steps under the banner of ‘Terror-free Turkey’ with an insincere approach.”


Incekara said the presidential regime viewed the peace process as an opportunity to bring a national liberation movement under its control and, in a sense, confine it within the boundaries of the existing system. He added that the growing repression at universities and attacks against students, which amounted to a veiled threat, clearly demonstrated how insincerely the government was approaching the process and how it was proceeding through deception.


‘They want to create an atmosphere of fear’


Sude Şener described the ministry's 17-point circular as a reflection of security-oriented policies on university campuses, saying that the deployment of police officers and detention vehicles outside universities was intended to marginalise the student movement. Şener said, “They are trying to turn universities into places where people are afraid, as though only a handful of students were raising their demands or taking action. We have never experienced a period …

author: Tam Saavedra
title: The UN CRPD Guidelines on Intersectionality are Here!
content:
The UN CRPD Guidelines on Intersectionality Just Changed the Game for Disability Rights—Here’s What You Need to Know 


Big news for women with disabilities and all feminist disabled advocates, allies, and organizations worldwide!

 


During its 35th Session in August 2026, the

UN Committee on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities

 (UN CRPD)

 officially adopted the historic

Guidelines on Identifying and Addressing Intersectional Discrimination Against Girls, Adolescents, Women, and Older Women with Disabilities

.

 


This milestone represents a monumental step forward for disability rights. For the first time, States have explicit, actionable guidance to support their obligations at the intersection of gender and disability.

 


Read the official CRPD Guidelines here

 


What Are the CRPD Guidelines on Intersectional Discrimination?


The Guidelines serve as an authoritative framework developed by the UN


CRPD Committee to help States better prevent, monitor, and address intersectional discrimination.

 


Throughout years of UN CRPD country review processes, the Committee identified a persistent, critical gap:

the specific rights of women with disabilities and the complex, intersectional discrimination they experience are rarely understood or adequately addressed by governments.

 


As the UN CRPD celebrates its 20th anniversary, these Guidelines were issued to bridge that gap—ensuring the convention is implemented to benefit

all

 women, girls, and gender-diverse people with disabilities across their lifespans.

 


Why Are These Guidelines a Game


–

Changer?

 


International documents rarely explicitly focus on the detailed, lived experiences and rights of women with disabilities. These Guidelines clearly name and elaborate on the systemic barriers

 women and gender-diverse people with disabilities face daily across the globe, including:

 


Sexual & Reproductive Health and Rights (SRHR):

 Addressing and preventing enforced sterilization, forced contraception, lack of accessible healthcare, restrictions on abortion, and lack of perinatal, menstrual, and menopause care.

 


Gender-Based & Disability-Based Violence:

 Exposing institutional violence, digital/online abuse, and the widespread lack of support services for victims.

 


Caregiving Recognition:

 Validating women with disabilities as active caregivers and mothers, rather than only recipients of care.

 


Economic & Educational Exclusion:

 Highlighting barriers in the labor market, economic and exclusion from education during puberty.

 


Crisis & Climate Response:

 Tackling compounded exclusion during environmental disasters, climate emergencies, and humanitarian relief efforts.

 


…just to name a few.

 


7 Key Breakthroughs in the Framing of the Guidelines 

 


What makes this document uniquely transformative is its progressive, structural approach:

 


Explicit Inclusion of Gender Diversity:

 The Guidelines explicitly encompass the rights of transgender, intersex, non-binary, and other gender-diverse people with disabilities and ask for gender diversity – inclusive interpretation of all obligations described.

 


Recognition of Historical Root Causes:

 The Committee explicitly addresses the legacy and ongoing impacts of

colonialism and enslavement

, establishing that States benefiting from these historical systems bear a particular responsibility to remedy their ongoing effects.

 


An Open Catalogue of Diversity:

 The text recognizes that women with disabilities belong to multi-marginalized communities—including Indigenous, Black, Dalit, Adivasi, refugee, asylum-seeking, religious minority, and pastoralist groups or people living in informal settings, among others —while leaving space for all intersecting identities.

 


Structural & Preventive Approach:

 Moving beyond a strictly punitive, reactive model, the Guidelines demand the dismantling of systemic oppression (such as ableism, audism, racism, and patriarchy) through early intervention, education, and public policy reform. 

 


Decriminalization

 is also a disability issue:

The guidelines recognize impacts of criminalization of abortion, homosexuality, gender identity and expression as well as

restricting marriage or consensual relationships as an important intersectional disability rights issue.

 


Holding digital platforms accountable:

author: Dominique Gené - Local Journalism Initiative Reporter
title: Nunavik school board to pilot sex-education program
content:
Kativik Ilisarniliriniq, Nunavik’s school board, will test a sexuality education program in Kuujjuaq and Umiujaq in November.


The pilot program was developed with the Nunavik Regional Board of Health and Social Services and is intended to help children understand personal boundaries and how to stay safe in sexual situations, said Sarah Aloupa, president of Kativik Ilisarniliriniq, in an interview.


“It’s important for parents to take this very seriously. This program is for the students’ well being,” she said.


Aloupa said the initiative responds to a need raised by Nunavik residents and parents. The school board’s council of commissioners heard a presentation from the health board about the proposed program in June.


The program will cover students from kindergarten to Grade 11, with information packages for different age groups.


Aloupa declined to share the teaching material.


The pilot is scheduled to run Nov. 2 to 6 at Jaanimmarik School and Pitakallak School in Kuujjuaq and Nov. 16 to 20 at Kiluutaq School in Umiujaq. The schools were chosen in part because they were ready to take part and have staff with relevant experience, said Jade Duchesneau-Bernier, spokesperson for the school board.


During those weeks, staff will participate in training and parents can review material and ask questions at evening information sessions.


Their feedback will help shape the final program. While the board has not yet clarified how parents can do so, they can opt their children out, Aloupa said.


Information about the sessions is being sent to parents through school letters and posted on Facebook.


Aloupa pointed to sexual abuse cases in the region as part of the broader need for education on the subject.


In February 2025, Nicolas Cyr, a physical education teacher at Jaanimmarik School, was

charged

 with sexual assault of a minor, sexual interference of a minor and assault.


The pilot is intended to help the Nunavik school board and the region’s health board assess the program before considering whether to expand it to the other 18 schools Kativik Ilisarniliriniq operates, Aloupa said.


The organizations have not yet set a timeline for a region-wide rollout.

author: Kelly Pavelich
title: Equality Culture Club: Make Equality Reality Bookstore
content:
Equality Culture Club: Make Equality Reality Bookstore


For the second time this year, Equality Now hosted a bookstore at the

Make Equality Reality

 Gala

, an arts-based celebration that brings together visionary leaders, powerful performances, and global changemakers committed to advancing gender equality, to highlight some of our favourite feminist titles. The books – both fiction and non-fiction and for readers of various ages – remind us of the urgency of our work and fill us with hope that a better world is possible. From us to you, enjoy the following recommendations straight from the Equality Now library.


A Hymn to Life

 by Gisèle Pelicot


In

A Hymn to Life

, Gisèle Pelicot tells her story for the first time, tracing a life built over five decades, the hidden abuse of her marriage’s final decade, and the long path to healing. Part memoir, part act of defiance, it is a moving portrait of survival and courage from a woman who broke her silence, reclaimed her voice, and forced a reckoning.


This year, Equality Now honoured Gisèle with the Equality Now Trailblazer Award, which honours individuals whose actions help transform the systems, institutions, and culture that shape the lives of women and girls.


Be Yourself and Other Bad Advice

 by Meredith Walker


Be Yourself and Other Bad Advice

 is part guidebook and part pep talk. The book is infused with humour and packed with practical tools to help teens and young adults figure out who they are, navigate emotions and life’s big questions, and build real confidence. It’s a perfect book for girls learning how to exist in the world. Featuring a foreword by Amy Poehler and stunning illustrations by Nina Cosford, it’s as lovely to look at as it is to read. Meredith attended this year’s Gala and signed copies of her book for guests.


 


For the Sun After Long Nights

 by Fatemeh Jamalpour and Nilo Tabrizy


For the Sun After Long Nights

 documents the rise of the Woman, Life, Freedom movement in Iran, one of Iran’s largest uprisings in decades, which began following the death of Mahsa Jîna Amini. Fatemeh, a local journalist, documented the movement on the ground as a fellow protestor, despite threats to her life, while Nilo reported from afar. The book represents their interwoven stories and sisterhood.


The Freedom Seeker

 by Ruchira Gupta


The Freedom Seeker

 is a young adult novel about an Indian girl whose parents’ interfaith marriage becomes the target of violence. To remain safe, they decide to flee Northern India. Her father leaves first, seeking refuge in the United States, but when her and her mother’s petition is denied, they are left with no choice but to try to reunite their family on their own. Ruchira’s other title,

I Kick and I Fly

, also appeared in our library. This young adult novel follows Heera, who is sold into the sex trade at the age of fourteen. She eventually has the opportunity to learn martial arts, which transforms her life. 


Like Meredith, we were fortunate to have Ruchira in attendance at this year’s

Make Equality Reality

Gala, where she signed books in the Equality Now library. Ruchira also contributed to our

Equality Culture Club interview series

, sharing why storytelling remains important, especially for a young audience; how her experience as a journalist has shaped her writing style; and what she envisions for a gender-equal future.


Nobody’s Girl

 by Virginia Roberts Giuffre


Nobody’s Girl

 is the memoir that Virginia Roberts Giuffre, Jeffrey Epstein and Ghislaine Maxwell’s most outspoken survivor, completed before her passing in April 2025. In it, she gives an unsparing account of her childhood abuse, her years being trafficked by Epstein and Maxwell to prominent men, her escape at nineteen, and the courage it took to hold her abusers to account and fight for other survivors. 


Equality Now was proud to posthumously present the Courage Award to Virginia Roberts Giuffre, an outspoken Epstein survivor, who spoke out when silence would have been easier. Virginia’s brother and sister-in-law, Sky and Amanda Roberts, accepted the award on her behalf.


Anjali Can!

 by Sheetal Sheth


In

Anjali Can!

, the third book in the Anjali picture book series, Anjali works to prevent her local community centre’s closure and shows the power one individual can have in enacting change. Sheetal joined Meredith, Ruchira, and Jackson Katz in the Gala’s library for a book signing after the program.

author: Chris Walker
title: Acton Says Ramaswamy Exploited Her Estranged Mother for Political Gain
content:
Ohio gubernatorial candidate Amy Acton accused her mother’s then-husband of sexual assault when she was a child.

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

Democratic candidate for Ohio governor Amy Acton has responded to a political ad produced by her Republican opponent Vivek Ramaswamy’s campaign, which features her mother — whom she’s been estranged from for decades — describing Acton as a liar.

The ad is being widely criticized as distasteful because Acton accused her mother and her then-stepfather of abuse and sexual assault when she was just a child.

In the ad, Donna Arthur, Acton’s mother, is shown speaking directly into the camera about her daughter, whom she has not seen since 1978, when Acton was just 12 years old.

“Amy has a serious problem. She is a liar,” Arthur says. “She’s lied her entire life. My daughter needs help.”

The ad doesn’t mention why Arthur believes her daughter is a liar, and it leaves out all relevant information about their estrangement.

Acton alleges that she was the victim of sexual abuse by Arthur’s now-deceased husband when she was between the ages of 10 and 12. Acton has also recalled being unhoused at one point while living with her mother and stepfather.

She later told her father about the abuses, and a grand jury indicted her stepfather. Her mother and stepfather then fled the state to avoid prosecution, Acton has recounted.

The ad did not indicate who paid for or produced it. Though the Ramaswamy campaign had initially avoided taking responsibility for the ad, it has now admitted they made the commercial. What’s more, the campaign intends to spend an additional $4 million to continue airing it.

The campaign defended the ad in a statement.

“We don’t know what happened between Amy and her mother, who first spoke about Amy in 2020, but we know that Amy Acton is a serial fabulist who has some serious problems with the truth that the public needs to be aware of before deciding who to entrust as governor,” the Ramaswamy campaign said.

On Wednesday, Vice President JD Vance came to Ramaswamy’s defense.

“Whether the ad was appropriate or not is not really my concern,” Vance said in response to a reporter’s question, saying he was more focused on the election’s outcome.

“Have the opinion you want to have on that ad,” Vance continued, adding that he was “disgusted” at members of his own party “whining” about the contents of the ad.

Acton has condemned Ramaswamy for the ad in a statement posted on Facebook.

“Between the ages of 10 and 12, I was sexually abused by her husband, while my birth mother did nothing to protect me. … I’ve always known that she was deeply sick and unwell, and it’s sad to see Vivek Ramaswamy exploit her all for his own political gain,” Acton said.

I know what it feels like to be a child who is hungry, frightened, and uncertain of what tomorrow will bring. I know what it means to feel powerless and to depend on the courage and compassion of others to find a way forward. Those experiences shaped my values, my compassion, and my belief that every person deserves to be safe, to be heard, and to have a fair chance at a better life. They are part of what led me to become a doctor, to dedicate my life to public service, and to fight for people who too often feel forgotten or left behind.

Acton’s brother, Phillip Stearns, has also blasted the ad.

“It’s not surprising that Vivek Ramaswamy has stooped to such a despicable low as to attempt to turn the sexual abuse Amy endured at twelve years old from our birth mother’s husband into a political talking point,” Stearns said in a statement, adding that the commercial is a “desperate, disgusting attack” that “reveals exactly who Vivek Ramaswamy is at his core – a pathetic excuse for a man who is willing to hurt anyone as long as it gets him what he wants.”

The race between Acton, a physician and former director of the Ohio Department of Health, and Ramaswamy, an ally of President Donald Trump, is a tight one. According to an average of polling data compiled by FiftyPlusOne, Acton is currently leading the contest, garnering around 49 percent of support in the state, while Ramaswamy receives 44.5 percent.

Truthout is one of only a few platforms for justice-oriented, grassroots journalism. Today, we face an existential threat.

author: Sue Bolton, Sarah Hathway
title: Socialist Alliance: ‘Stop weaponising shocking attack on Helen Haines MP’
content:
Socialist Alliance condemns the terrible attack on Helen Haines MP and we send our best wishes to her and her family.

This shocking incident had been politically weaponised even before the facts were established; the corporate media and some MPs went looking to find someone to blame.

The Zionists and right-wing commentators were quick to blame the pro-Palestine movement, because the alleged perpetrator — along with the majority of people in Australia — was critical of Israel’s genocide in Gaza. It has become stock in trade for mainstream media to brand critics of Israel as “extremist”.

We now know the alleged perpetrator suffered from poor mental health and that their family was friends with the Haines family.

As pressures mount around housing affordability and the rising cost of living, poorly resourced mental health services, especially in regional and rural Victoria, may contribute to anti-social behaviour.

The 2021 Royal Commission into Victoria’s Mental Health System made 65 recommendations and nine interim recommendations. These largely remain unfunded or not implemented, despite the Victorian Labor government promising to do so.

An independent report earlier this year made 270 sub-recommendations — only 54 have been fully implemented.

Right-wing influencers and the manosphere are also playing a role in influencing a layer of more vulnerable people to take on extreme and conspiracist views.

Data from Women for Election shows that online abuse towards those in elected positions is negatively impacting those in office, those running for office and those considering doing so. Just under 90% of women surveyed reported experiencing online abuse or intimidation connected to their political participation.

No one should be threatened or made to feel fear for themselves or their family members.

This attack on Haines is happening in the context of one woman a week being killed by a current or former partner in Australia. Despite advocacy and mass mobilisations to stop violence against women, misogyny is still pervasive.

Abuse and threats of violence towards women are also on the rise.

Pauline Hanson’s One Nation Party has been aggressively whipping up hate and division. Its scapegoating of vulnerable groups, based on ethnicity, religion, immigration status, gender and ability, as the “cause” of societal problems is part of the political context.

The major parties are contributing to this divisiveness, either through policy or rhetoric. This is being exacerbated by the mainstream media’s clickbait.

As a result, it is not just elected representatives who are being targeted with threats and violence; people are being emboldened by divisive politics to target already marginalised groups with racial, gendered or other violence.

There are solutions, but One Nation doesn’t have them. And while the major parties steal One Nations’ immigration policies, they help fuel the tinderbox atmosphere of fear and hate.

The mainstream parties pander to the extremist right, because it helps them divide and rule.

[Sue Bolton is a Socialist Alliance councillor on Merri-Bek City Council and is the Socialist Alliance candidate for Broadmeadows in the Victorian election. Sarah Hathway is a former City of Greater Geelong Councillor and the Socialist Alliance candidate for Lara in the Victorian election.]

 kapsamında düzenleniyor. 


Yani Gerçek’in durumunda olduğu gibi cezaevindeki bir yakına par göndermek de bu suçla ilişkilendiriliyor, ya da cezaevindeki yazarlara da telif ödemesi yapmak bu suçla ilişkilendiliyor. Evet evet. Ocak 2026’da K

or Kitap

’ın yayınevi temsilcisine, tutuklu yazar ve editörler Tonguç Ok ile Necip Baysal’a telif ödemesi yaptığı gerekçesiyle konutu terk etmeme (

ev hapsi

) şeklinde adli kontrol tedbiri uygulandı.


Benzer durumda olan ağır bir hasta mahpus Hatice Yıldız da var. Yıldız, cezaevinde tutuklu bulunan öz kızına ve kızının ihtiyaçlarını karşılayabilmesi için aynı koğuşta kalan arkadaşına PTT (Devlet Posta Kurumu) üzerinden resmi kanallarla para yatırdığı için de suçlanabiliyor. 


Bu arada hem cezaevindeki Yıldız’ın hem de GErçek’in tedavileri yarım kalıyor, bakımları yapılmıyor, kimi zaman tek kalıyorlar. 


Gerçek’in durumunda ise başka bir şaşırtıcı detay daha var, kendisi ile aynı dosyada tutulu olan diğer kişiler hakkında önce adli kontroller kaldırılıyor, ardından 2 Nisan’da hepsi beraat ediyor. Buna rağmen Hülya Gerçek hakkında uygulanan ev hapsi kaldırılmıyor. Bu da insanın aklına Gerçek’e yönelik başka özel bir öfke mi va sorusunu akıllara getiriyor? Neden?


Anayasa’nın 17. maddesi yaşam hakkını ve kişinin maddi ve manevi varlığını koruma hakkını, 56. maddesi ise herkesin sağlık hizmetlerinden yararlanma hakkını güvence altına alıyor. Avrupa İnsan Hakları Sözleşmesi’nin 2. ve 3. maddeleri uyarınca devletin yaşamı koruma ve insanlık dışı ya da onur kırıcı muameleyi önleme yükümlülüğü bulunuyor.


Birleşmiş Milletler Ekonomik, Sosyal ve Kültürel Haklar Sözleşmesi’nin 12. maddesi ise herkesin ulaşılabilir en yüksek sağlık standardına sahip olma hakkını tanıyor. 


En yalın hali ile Anayasa, yasalar ve uluslararası düzenlemelere rağmen Hülya Gerçek hakkında uygulanan adli kontrol tedbirinin devam ettirilmesi; ölçülülük, gereklilik ve orantılılık ilkeleriyle bağdaşmıyor. 


DEM Parti Milletvekili Çiçek Otlu, Adalet Bakanı Akın Gürlek'in yanıtlaması talebi ile 7 Ekim'de Gerçek'le ilgli bir soru önergesi sundu.  "Aynı dosya kapsamında tutuklu bulunan şüpheliler tahliye edildi diğer şüpheliler yönünden uygulanan adli kontrol tedbirleri kaldırıldı. 2 Nisan'da görülen karar duruşmasında dosya kapsamındaki tüm sanıklar hakkında beraat kararı verildi. Buna rağmen Hülya Gerçek hakkında uygulanan ev hapsi tedbirinin sürdürülmesi, hukuki değil keyfi bir uygulama izlenimi yaratmakta, eşitlik ilkesine ve adil yargılanma hakkına aykırılık oluşturuyor" dedi. 


1412 hasta mahpus 


Geçen hafta ise bu kez HDK Eş Sözcüsü / DEM Parti Erzurum Milletvekili ve Anayasa Komisyonu Üyesi Meral Danış Beştaş, Gerçek’in durumunu Meclis gündemine taşıdı. “Ağır veya kronik hastalığı bulunan kişiler hakkında konutu terk etmeme yükümlülüğü kararı verilirken sağlık durumunun, tedavi gereksinimlerinin ve hastaneye erişim imkânlarının değerlendirilmesine ilişkin Bakanlığınızca belirlenmiş bir usul, kriter veya genelge bulunuyor mu?” diye sordu.

author: Ridah Hassan
title: Manosphere making classrooms toxic
content:
“I had male students threatening to rape the female students consistently. They would play ‘rape marry kill’ and used my own name frequently in their ‘game’.”

“Students saying ‘good girl’ to teachers.”

“Less respect for female staff vs male in behaviour—even with the same approaches they instantly listen to males more. More inappropriate jokes—racism, homophobic and sexist jokes with little consequences. Visible [and] audible dismissal/rejection of female staff to their faces when they appear to take classes.” 

These are quotes from a Monash University report which has cast light on the disturbing sexist conditions faced by teachers and students in primary and secondary schools across the country. 

Duty of Care: Teachers’ experiences of sexism, misogyny and sexual harassment in Australian schools

 is based on the testimony of 2,600 educators and reveals the breadth and depth of the crisis. 

A common theme in the report is the lack of respect male students show female teachers. This includes frequent interrupting, ignoring of instructions, mocking and mimicking, speaking disrespectfully and refusing to accept responsibility when challenged about inappropriate behaviour. Physical aggression and intimidation were also reported, along with threats of more serious physical and sexual assault. Male students frequently make “derogatory comments toward females focusing on appearance and worth”, “jokes about gender roles e.g. the kitchen”, “inappropriate sexualised remarks about female bodies, including specifically about peers and/or staff” and “[making] sexual noises in the classroom” while female staff are trying to teach.

This behaviour is contributing to the burn-out of teachers in a profession already facing shortages due to poor pay and unmanageable workloads. One respondent put it clearly: “Being the front line and bearing the brunt of misogyny is exhausting and erodes self-worth”. According to the report, 77 percent of teachers say that sexism and misogyny have a “negative” or “very negative” impact on their wellbeing, and more than 50 percent of female teachers report that they either “occasionally” or “frequently” consider leaving the profession because of it. And the situation is getting worse—both primary and secondary teachers reported that gendered violence on the part of students had increased significantly in the previous twelve months.

Given adult teachers are feeling undermined, threatened and belittled by male students’ behaviour, the impact on teenage girls should be cause for immediate action. According to the report, “Younger students are comfortable using misogynistic language without thought e.g. calling girls in class a ‘slut’ ‘whore’ because they won’t share a highlighter”, and “Women/girls in class are okay with being treated with misogyny as this is seen as ‘normal’ now. They do not retaliate and internalise, making emotional regulation hard”. Another teacher observed: “Female students are scared to speak out and express their opinions in class with males who chastise them. I am noticing students are very hesitant to participate in discussion these days whereas it used to be female students being quite eager to share ideas and answer questions. Female students appear angrier than in the past as well”.

Male students direct sexist and misogynistic language towards their female peers freely, entrenching a toxic gender divide among students. Again, the statistics bear this out, with 80 percent of respondents agreeing that the behaviour is having a negative impact on student wellbeing. In observing and being victim to male students’ sexism—including constantly disrupting learning and making spaces hostile—girls are being socialised to accept dehumanising language and treatment and to make themselves small targets by withdrawing and accommodating to the selfish and anti-social behaviour of boys. 

And though there are undoubtedly some who are willing to challenge their peers’ appalling behaviour, it is an unacceptable environment for female students to be expected to navigate every day, while at the same time trying to do the actual tasks of deciphering Shakespeare or learning calculus. It is well established that students learn best when they feel safe, supported and respected. This is currently not the case for female students at Australian schools. 

Misogyny and the rise of the ‘manosphere’

author: Unknown
title: I can’t find the source now but someone went back and studied MOGAI culture on tumblr in the 2010s…
content:
confession theres a lot of lgbt microlabels and contradictory identities and xenogenders that i 100% do not understand no matter how many explanations i see. but my logic when i encounter someone who flies those flags is “well, i doubt anyone would land on those labels without putting a whole lot of thought into their identity, so thats none of my business” . this attitude has served me well and will continue to serve me well forever i think. good luck with that you crazy kids.

I can’t find the source now but someone went back and studied MOGAI culture on tumblr in the 2010s and found that

Over 50.000 new identities and flags were coined in a few years.

Most described some state of being unsure, undefined or inbetween.

Most were used once or twice and then never again, not even by the people who coined the term and designed the flag.

While that could be seen as a negative thing, former participants generally looked back positively on these single-use microlabels as something that gave them room to explore and removed the pressure of choosing something definitive.

So the lesson here was: sometimes someone uses a microlabel because they’re not done putting thought into their identity, and that’s also a great reason to have a microlabel. Getting the ‘what am I?’ question out of the way by choosing a deliberately vague microlabel can be a way to make space to just exist, to experience queer life without the pressure of labeling it any further. That’s very useful and hella queer.

author: Brooke Migdon
title: Ballot Measures Will Impact LGBTQ+ Rights in 7 States This Election
content:
Voters will decide how trans youth can participate in school sports, access gender-affirming health care, and more.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

Voters in seven states this fall will weigh more than half a dozen ballot initiatives with direct bearings on LGBTQ+ people — disproportionately on transgender youth. They come as LGBTQ+ rights issues feature heavily in campaigns for candidates on either side of the aisle in the final stretch of November’s midterm elections, which will determine party control of Congress and several key governorships.

Nearly half of LGBTQ+-related ballot initiatives this year would restrict trans student-athletes from competing in line with their gender identity, an issue championed overwhelmingly by Republicans and by a rising share of Democrats. Others would ban certain transition-related treatments for minors — another focus of conservative candidates and President Donald Trump’s second administration.

Since 2021, more than half the nation has adopted laws barring trans students from playing on school sports teams matching their gender identity, and 27 states have banned gender-affirming care for trans youth. Nationally, the number of trans students who participate in school sports is unknown, but is believed to be relatively low: The Williams Institute estimates that just over 300,000 13- to 17-year-olds in the United States are trans, and not all of them will play sports.

In Washington state, where voters will decide this fall whether to ban trans student-athletes from teams matching their gender identity, the organization governing high school sports told The 19th that it is aware of about 10 trans middle and high schoolers who play sports out of more than 200,000 students who compete statewide.

Other ballot initiatives appearing before voters this fall include measures to change the state constitution to expand nondiscrimination protections for LGBTQ+ people; formally repeal language against same-sex marriages and modify students’ and parents’ rights in schools.

Here’s where LGBTQ+ rights are on the ballot this November.

Arizona voters will decide this fall whether trans student-athletes may continue to compete on school sports teams that align with their gender identity. A ballot initiative introduced late last year by state Rep. Selina Bliss, a Republican running for reelection, would effectively restore a 2022 state law restricting trans athletes’ participation that a federal appeals court had blocked in 2024.

Kris Mayes, Arizona’s Democratic attorney general, has declined to defend the law in court.

Bliss’ proposal would require public and qualifying private schools to designate K-12 sports teams as exclusively “male,” “female” or “coeducational” based on participating students’ “biological status at birth.” It would also bar trans students from using restrooms, locker rooms and other spaces “integral to athletic engagement” that match their gender identity.

In July, a lawsuit challenging the measure claimed it violated a requirement that Arizona ballot initiatives address only a single subject and was “misleading to the point of fraud.” A state superior court judge later ruled that the initiative could remain on the November 3 ballot.

Colorado voters will decide whether to bar trans student-athletes from competing in line with their gender identity by designating K-12 and collegiate sports teams based on students’ “biological reproductive systems.” The ballot initiative qualified for the general election after Protect Kids Colorado, the organization behind it, collected more than 168,000 signatures statewide.

Voters will also decide whether to ban transition-related surgeries for minors, and whether state or federal funds, Medicaid reimbursements or insurance coverage can be used to help pay for them. Such surgeries are already rare. The measure, also introduced by Protect Kids Colorado, does not directly mention nonsurgical care.

State medical organizations, including the Colorado Academy of Family Physicians and the Colorado Medical Society (CMS), the state’s largest organized group of practitioners, have publicly opposed the healthcare-related initiative. “CMS members hold diverse political views but share a core principle: medical decisions belong in the exam room,” Brigitta Robinson, the organization’s president, said in September.

That initiative also runs counter to “shield laws” …

author: CMI Argentina
title: Neuquén: jurado popular encontró culpable a Roberto Sánchez por el transfemicidio de Azul Semeñenko
content:
Un jurado popular declaró culpable a Roberto Daniel Sánchez por el homicidio de Azul Semeñenko, triplemente agravado por ensañamiento, odio a su identidad de género y mediado por violencia de género. Se trató de un juicio histórico en la provincia de Neuquén, que se desarrolló a lo largo de 12 audiencias y contó con más de 30 testimonios.


Escuchar el reporte de La Revuelta y Periodistas Feministas


Durante las jornadas, compañeras de trabajo de Azul, organizaciones feministas, integrantes de la comunidad LGBTIQ+ y organizaciones sociales acompañaron el proceso. En la última audiencia, estuvieron presentes con un altar en homenaje a Azul, carteles y música.


Tras conocerse el veredicto, su hermano,

Marco Millapán

, destacó el acompañamiento colectivo y la importancia de la decisión judicial.

“La verdad que haber conseguido este veredicto del jurado popular es fruto colectivo de cada uno de los que hoy están presentes y de los que nos han venido acompañando a lo largo de todo este año”

, expresó.


“Logramos lo que todos queríamos, justicia por y para Azul. Esto fue un transfemicidio, esto fue un crimen de odio”

, afirmó.


Por su parte, el fiscal jefe

Agustín García

 señaló que el juicio implicó un importante desafío por la cantidad y complejidad de las pruebas presentadas.

“Fue un juicio en donde había mucha información, muchos testigos, muchos peritos. Había que trabajarlo de tal modo que toda esa prueba fuera bien comprendida por el jurado, en el contexto en que se dan las cosas, acá no se puede aislar hechos individuales sin contextualizarlo”

, explicó.


García también remarcó la relevancia del reconocimiento de las agravantes:

“El primer caso en Neuquén, en donde desde la reforma del año 2012 se juzga a una persona con estas agravantes, era un desafío también para nosotros”

.


El homicidio ocurrió durante la madrugada del 25 de septiembre de 2025 dentro de la vivienda de Sánchez, situada en la ciudad de Neuquén. De acuerdo con la acusación, dentro de la casa Sánchez atacó a Azul con golpes realizados con elementos contundentes y con un arma blanca. La autopsia confirmó que la víctima recibió 25 heridas de arma blanca.


Desde la querella valoraron el veredicto como un alivio para la familia, después de atravesar un largo proceso en busca de justicia.

“Hoy es una brisa también que alivia un poco el fuego en el que se viven las injusticias, como venía viviendo la familia hasta este día”

, expresaron.


Además, remarcaron que la decisión del jurado debe generar una reflexión social:

“Declararon que fue un transfemicidio, pero esto tiene que construir también un aprendizaje a nuestra comunidad. Azul no nos la devuelven, pero Azul tiene que ser la última”

.


Tras la declaración de culpabilidad de Sánchez, se espera que en los próximos días se realice la audiencia de determinación de la pena.

author: TGEU
title: Hungary removes anti-LGBTI provisions, but trans people are still left out
content:
TGEU welcomes the decision of the Hungarian National Assembly on 13 October, 2026 to remove the anti-LGBTI content from the 2021 ‘child protection’ law. This is a necessary step to implement the Court of Justice of the EU (CJEU) judgment in

Commission v Hungary

 (C-769/22).


In its April 2026 judgment, the CJEU found that the law, which stigmatised LGBTI people under the guise of child protection, breached EU law. It also rejected Hungary’s reliance on national identity to justify discriminatory measures. 


Why this matters for trans people


The ruling matters for trans people across the EU, because it confirms that Member States cannot use ‘child protection’ or national identity as an excuse for excluding trans and other LGBTI people from public life and the rights EU law guarantees them. The CJEU has already held in

Mirin

 (C-4/23) that Member States must recognise a legal gender change obtained in another Member State, so the Commission has clear legal grounds to act. The CJEU has also held in

Deldits

 (C-247/23) that a Hungarian refusal to rectify a trans refugee’s gender marker breaches the GDPR, which further strengthens the case for Commission action.


The reality of LGBTI rights in Hungary


However, compliance with EU law and European human rights standards remains incomplete. Hungary’s Fundamental Law (its constitution) continues to enshrine a rigid gender binary just like in

Slovakia

, and Hungary still bans legal gender recognition. Since 2020, trans and intersex people in Hungary have been unable to have their gender legally recognised, with serious consequences for daily life, access to services and personal safety.


Our call to action


TGEU calls on the European Commission to pressure Hungary, as well as Slovakia, to amend their constitutions in order to remove the forced gender binary. Both countries must also establish quick, transparent and accessible legal gender recognition procedures that comply with EU and ECHR (European Court of Human Rights) standards.


Your support makes change possible


We work across Europe and Central Asia to advance trans rights, build strong communities, and drive change through research, advocacy, and community-building.


Your donation helps us continue this vital work — defending trans lives, amplifying trans voices, and advocating for justice every day.

content:

Καλούμε σε συγκέντρωση έξω από το κολαστήριο των γυναικείων φυλακών Κορυδαλλού την Τετάρτη 21/10 στις 18:00


Οι ζωές των κρατουμένων μετράνε


Την τρίτη 20/10 αυτοκτόνησε μια κρατούμενη στις γυναικείες φυλακές Κορυδαλλού, η δεύτερη τους τελευταίους 4 μήνες. Οι διαρκής υποτιμηση των ζώων των κρατουμένων, οι άθλιες συνθήκες διαβίωσης, η έλλειψη ιατροφαρμακευτικής περίθαλψης, το απάνθρωπο βάρος του εγκλεισμού και ο υπερπληθυσμός των κρατουμένων είναι μόνο λίγα από όσα μπορούμε να αναφέρουμε για αυτά τα κολαστήρια. Σε μία συνθήκη που το κράτος επενδύει σε νέες φυλακές, συνεχίζει να θεωρεί τους φυλακισμένους/ες αναλωσιμους/ες αδιαφορώντας για την ανθρώπινη ύπαρξη. Κανενας θάνατος μέσα στις φυλακές δεν θα μείνει αναπάντητος.


Όλοι/ες/α αύριο στην συγκέντρωση έξω από τις φυλακές για να δείξουμε ότι για μας οι ζωές των κρατουμένων έχουν αξία. Δεν συνηθίζουμε τον θάνατο. Μέχρι την καταστροφή και του τελευταίου κελιού.


Δύναμη και αλληλεγγύη στις έγκλειστες.


Καμία μόνη στα χέρια του κράτους


Ταμείο αλληλεγγύης φυλακισμένων και διωκόμενων αγωνιστών/τριών


[Έκτακτο] Κάλεσμα στις γυναικείες φυλακές κορυδαλλού Τετάρτη 21 Οκτώβρη 18:00


Σήμερα, 20 Οκτώβρη, μια ακόμα κρατούμενη αυτοκτονεί στα κελιά της δημοκρατίας και εντοπίζεται από τις συγκρατούμενές της, μεταξύ των οποίων και οι τρεις συντρόφισσες που βρίσκονται στον Κορυδαλλό. Μια ακόμα σκληρή προσθήκη στη μακρά λίστα κρατουμένων που έχασαν τη ζωή τους στις ελληνικές φυλακές. Πρώτο μέλημα της διεύθυνσης στο άκουσμα αυτής της ανατριχιαστικής είδησης, είναι να απειλήσει με πειθαρχικά σε περίπτωση κινητοποιήσεων εντός της φυλακής.


Ενάντια σε αυτή τη βαρβαρότητα και το σύστημα που τη γεννά, τη συντηρεί και την απολαμβάνει, ως ελάχιστη ένδειξη αλληλεγγύης στις κρατούμενες,

καλούμε αύριο συγκέντρωση στον Κορυδαλλό 18:00.


ΜΕΧΡΙ ΤΟ ΓΚΡΕΜΙΣΜΑ ΚΑΙ ΤΗΣ ΤΕΛΕΥΤΑΙΑΣ ΦΥΛΑΚΗΣ


ΜΠΟΥΡΛΟΤΟ ΚΑΙ ΦΩΤΙΑ ΣΕ ΟΛΑ ΤΑ ΚΕΛΙΑ


Ανοιχτή Συνέλευση Αλληλεγγύης στους/ις διωκόμενους/ες για την απαλλοτρίωση τράπεζας στην Κάτω Τιθορέα


[ΕΚΤΑΚΤΟ] Συγκέντρωση στις γυναικείες φυλακές Κορυδαλλού – Τετάρτη 21/10 στις 18:00


Στις 20/10 αυτοκτονεί κρατούμενη στο Κατάστημα Κράτησης Κορυδαλλού ΙΙ. Κρατούμενες συμπεριλαμβανομένων και των 3 συντροφισσών που κρατούνται εκεί, την βρίσκουν κρεμασμένη στο μπάνιο. Η διεύθυνση της φυλακής σε μια προσπάθεια να αποτρέψει τις κινητοποιήσεις απειλεί με πειθαρχικά.


Τέσσερις μόλις μήνες μετά την αυτοκτονία κρατούμενης εντός του Κέντρου Κράτησης Κορυδαλλού ΙΙ, ένας ακόμη θάνατος μπαίνει σε μια τεράστια λίστα από κρατούμενους/ες που έχουν χάσει την ζωή τους μέσα σε κέντρα κράτησης και φυλακές. Το αδηφάγο σύστημα της φυλακής με τα πιόνια που το στηρίζουν, απειλούν, βασανίζουν και καλύπτουν αυτοκτονίες στο όνομα ενός σωφρονισμού που υπάρχει μόνο στα διεστραμένα μυαλά τους. Ψυχολογική επιβάρυνση, στοχοποίηση όσων στέκονται απέναντι στην απαξίωση της ζωής, καταπάτηση της αξιοπρέπειας είναι μόνο μερικά από τα όσα αποπειρώνται τα υπαλληλάκια της καταστολής.


Μπορούν να κρυφτούν πίσω από κάμερες ασφαλείας, τοίχους και στολές όσο θέλουν. Η οργή μας θα τους πνίξει όπως το ποτάμι πνίγει τους αφρούς του. Ας έχει υπόψιν η διευθύντρια των φυλακών ότι οι συντρόφισσες μας δεν είναι μόνες και οποιαδήποτε απειλή δε θα μείνει αναπάντητη.

In this edition of the Equality Culture Club’s interview series, we speak with Meredith Walker, author and co-founder of Smart Girls, an online community created to help girls learn more about themselves and the world around them. Through a series of questions and answers, she addresses her writing style, the advice that can often feel like a trap, feminist media recommendations, and more.

Q: Was there a specific moment or conversation that made you realize Be Yourself and Other Bad Advice needed to exist?

A: Through years of listening to girls in schools and communities, a pattern emerged. Teens and young women told me how stressful it was to feel so much pressure to achieve and to have their lives mapped out before they even knew what they really wanted or were good at.

That pressure isn’t anything new, but social media has added another dimension. Now it’s continuous, hyper-targeted, and carried around with them all day. There’s a constant stream of content telling them what life should look like and all the ways they could be improving themselves.

It became clear to me that girls need more tools for questioning all of those expectations and pressures. They need some help figuring out what they actually think and want. Getting to know yourself and learning to think for yourself are skills. This book is a way to practice them.

Q: What’s a piece of advice that sounds empowering but can actually be a kind of trap?

It was meant as an expansive message that women didn’t have to accept all the old limits on what their lives could look like. But it can easily become another source of pressure. We’ve turned it into: “You should have it all, and what’s wrong with you if you can’t pull it off?” A great career, meaningful relationships, financial success, a comfy home—and somehow hold it all together without much of a social safety net. Good luck!

We can have an interesting, meaningful life, but probably not every version of it, all at the same time. And that’s okay.

Q: If you could put one line from Be Yourself and Other Bad Advice on a poster in every school hallway, what would it be?

A: “No matter where you go, you’ll always bring you with you—so make sure you like who that person is.”

Q: How do you balance humour and vulnerability on the page?

A: I wanted readers to know the book was going to be honest, and I was willing to be honest about myself, too. I struggled my first year of college, made mistakes, had boring jobs….and had the emotional intelligence to once throw an egg at my brother. Not when I was a toddler. When I was 20.

For me, the balance is being vulnerable (and ridiculous) without making the reader the joke. A little humour lets me write honestly about my mistakes and what I learned the hard way without sounding preachy.

Q: For anyone unfamiliar, how would you describe the mission of Smart Girls?

A: Smart Girls was created to help girls know themselves better and become more curious about the world around them.

We offered web shows, interviews, workshops, summer camps, journalism boot camps, and a friendly digital community. The idea underneath all of it was pretty simple: girls are totally interesting, their ideas matter, and the world is worth being curious about.

Q: Can you point to a moment that confirmed you were doing something important?

A: Well, it was pretty rad when we started Smart Girls Ask. We showed up …

title: Ozgul Sakiyê li Metrîsê serdana girtiyên LGBTÎ+ kir: Hevgirtin wan bihêztir dike
content:
Parlementera Stenbolê ya Partiya Wekhevî û Demokrasiyê ya Gelan (DEM Partî) Ozgul Sakiyê li Girtîgeha Metîsê serdana LGBTÎ+yên girtî kir. Operasyonên navborî di 12ê Îlonê de li dijî  rêxistin, aktivîst û cihên LGBTÎ+yan hatibûn kirin. Di wan operasyonan de gelek LGBTÎ+ hatibûn girtin.


Sakiyê têkildarî serdana xwe li ser hesabê xwe yê medyaya civakî daxuyanî daye. Sakiyê diyar kir ku girtiyan ji xizm û heskiriyên xwe re slav şandin.


Li Stenbolê di operasyonên li dijî LGBTÎ+yan de 20 kes hatin girtin


17 Îlon 2026


Sakiyê da zanîn ku mehek li ser girtîbûna wan re derbas bûye û bertek nîşanî ne berdana wan da.


“Tevî ku tu sedemeke tune ye da ku rojekê tenê jî girtî bimînin, di yekem nirxandina girtîbûnê de jî nehatin berdan.”


“Piştgiriya li derve hêzê dide wan”


Sakiyê ragihand ku mercên girtîgehê li gorî rojên destpêkê baş bûne û anî ziman ku ew bi rêvebirê girtîgehê re jî civiyaye û hin daxwazên girtiyan gihandine rêveberiyê.


Sakiyê diyar kir ku LGBTÎ+yên ku wê dîtiye, bi taybetî bal kişandine ser girîngiya piştgiriya li derve:


“Her yek ji wan bi cihêyî anî ziman ku piştgiriya li derve hêzê dide wan.”


Sakiyê destnîşan kir ku divê girtî di demek nêz de serbest bên berdan û daxuyaniya xwe bi banga piştgiriyê bi dawî anî:


“Lêbelê tişta herî girîng ew e ku em ji bo ku ew di zûtirîn demê de azadiya xwe bi dest bixin, têkoşîn û piştgiriyê kêm nekin.”


Polîsan bi ser Kaos GLyê de girt: Polîs ketin komeleyê, rêveber hatin desteserkirin


14 Îlon 2026


Çi bûbû?


Di 12ê Îlonê de di çarçoveya operasyonên “Malbata min di ewlehiyê de ye” polîsan li gelek bajaran bi ser komeleyên LGBTÎ+yan, malên aktivîstan û mekânên cuda de girtin.


Di operasyonan de gelek kes hatin desteserkirin. Di heman demê de malperên înternetê yên rêxistinên LGBTÎ+yan û hesabên medyaya civakî yên aktivîstan hatin astengkirin.


Derbarê neh LGBTÎ+ yên li Stenbolê hatibûn girtin de, di yekem nirxandina girtîbûnê ya mehane de biryara berdewamiya girtîbûna wan hate dayîn.

title: Sincan’dan notlar: LGBTİ+ operasyonu tutukluları ve dayanışmanın politikası
content:
Bugün Sincan Cezaevi’ndeydim. “Ailem Güvende” adı verilen operasyon kapsamında tutuklanan sekiz arkadaşımızı ziyaret ettim: Janset, Umut, Metin, Baran, Tuğba, Nedime, Burçin ve Selin.


Bazılarıyla uzun zamandır tanışıyorum. Bazılarını ise sadece isimlerinden, politik mücadelelerinden biliyorum. Eylül’ün 12-13’ündeki baskın ve gözaltı sürecinde elimden geldiğince yanlarında olmaya çalıştım. Ardından bir süre Ankara dışında olduğum için ziyaretlerine gidemedim. Bugün, tutuklanmalarından sonra ilk kez bir araya geldik.


Cezaevi ziyareti muhalefet milletvekillerinin, bilhassa bizim partinin bir rutini. Son zamanlardaki gelişmeler sanırım CHP ve Yeni Parti’nin de çok daha sık cezaevi yollarına düşmesini getirdi. Ben de üç buçuk yıllık milletvekilliğim boyunca Sincan’a özellikle çok sık gittim. Kobani duruşmalarının sürdüğü dönemde bir ayağım neredeyse hep oradaydı. O davadan tutuklanan arkadaşlarımızı, Gezi tutuklularını, farklı siyasi davalardan içeride bulunanları fırsat buldukça ziyaret etmeyi sürdürüyorum. Bakırköy, Silivri, Diyarbakır, Edirne, Erzincan, Kandıra, Sincan… Gidebildiğim cezaevleri.


Her cezaevi başka bir dünya. Gezi tutuklularının deneyimi başka, Kobani davasından tutuklananlarınki başka, LGBTİ+’larınki bambaşka. Bu dünyaları birbirine benzetmek, aralarındaki farkları silmek olur. Ama her birinde insanın özgürlüğüyle, onuruyla, bedeniyle ve hayatını kurma hakkıyla ilgili ortak bir mesele var.


Cezaevleri, dışarıdaki hayatın bir süreliğine paranteze alındığı yerler değil yalnızca. Aynı zamanda dışarıdaki eşitsizliklerin, ayrımcılıkların ve iktidar ilişkilerinin içeride başka biçimlerde yeniden üretildiği mekânlar. Üstelik kapılar kapandığında, içeride yaşananların dışarıda duyulması da giderek zorlaşıyor.


Bu nedenle siyasetçilerin, milletvekillerinin ve hak savunucularının cezaevlerini sessiz bırakmaması gerekiyor. Avukatların ve ailelerin kurduğu dayanışma elbette vazgeçilmez. Fakat dışarıdan kurulan bağların da sürmesi, içeride yaşananların gündeme taşınması, insanların yalnızca dosyalarından ibaret olmadıklarının hatırlanması gerekiyor. Siyasetçilerin bir gözünün ve bir kulağının orada olması gerekiyor. Bir ayağının orada olması gerekiyor.


Bugün sekiz kişiyle görüştüm. Sabahtan akşam mesai bitinceye dek. İçeri girerken bıraktığım Ankara, çıktığımda puslu neredeyse kar havası diyeceğim bir havaya ve yağmura teslim olmuştu. Belki de ne kadar isterlerdi o havada dışarıda olmayı, yağmurda ıslanmayı, hatta üşümeyi... Şehre bir buçuk saatte dönebildik. Sekiz ayrı hayat, sekiz ayrı hikâye. Zaman zaman güldük, zaman zaman ağır şeyler konuştuk. Her birinin kendi koşulları, kendi ruh hâli, kendi direnme biçimi var. Ama ziyaretlerin sonunda aklımda kalan, yalnızca kendilerine yapılanları anlatmaları değildi. Kendi bildik hayatları tümden ellerinden alındığında bile başkalarının hayatlarına bakmaya devam etmeleriydi.


Belki de bugün en çok bunu düşündüm.


Janset’in söylediği bir şey var. Bunları öğrenmemiz için onları ziyarete gitmemiz gerekmiyor.


Haklıydı. Hak ihlallerini, ayrımcılığı, yoksulluğu ve cezaevlerinin koşullarını öğrenmek için bunları yaşayan insanların bunu anlatmasını beklememeliyiz. Birilerinin yaşadıklarını bize anlatmak zorunda kalmadığı bir politik duyarlılık geliştirebilmeliyiz. Ne var ki çoğu zaman, bildiğimizi sandığımız şeylerin gerçek anlamını, karşımızda bir insan oturduğunda, onun hikâyesini dinlediğimizde kavrıyoruz.


İlk Janset’le görüştüm


Janset’i Ankara’daki çeşitli panellerden, toplantılardan tanıyorum. Aramızda bir dayanışma hukuku olduğunu sanıyorum. Bana bir dostum, arkadaşımmış gibi geliyor. Söylediklerinde kişisel bir sitemden çok, son derece açık bir politik itiraz vardı. Siyasetçilerin LGBTİ+’larla dayanışma konusundaki çekingenliğine dikkat çekti. Sözü dolandırmadan söyledi: Siyasetçi linci göze alacak. Cesareti yoksa da "mış gibi", dayanışıyormuş gibi yapmayacak.


Bu sözün üzerinde durmak gerek.


Siyaset, herkesin zaten rahatlıkla söyleyebildiği şeyleri tekrar etmekten ibaret değil. Başkalarının dile getirmekte zorlandığı sözleri de dile getirmek gibi bir sorumluluğunuz var. Bunun bir bedeli olabilir. Hedef gösterilebilirsiniz, linç edilebilirsiniz, hiç hak etmediğiniz saldırılara maruz kalabilirsiniz. Ama siyasetçinin meselesi, kendisini bu ihtimallerden korumak olamaz.


Ben de lincin zaten hep orada tetikte beklediğini söyledim. Kadın voleybolculara destek amacıyla attığım bir tweetin günlerce süren bir linç kampanyasına dönüşebildiğini anlattım. Yıllar …

"Estrella: Bittersweet Freedom for a 'Bad Mexican'"

We’re joined by Latino USA host Maria Hinojosa as she shares the story of Estrella Diamantina González, an undocumented transgender woman and trafficking survivor from Mexico caught up in the United States’ criminal and immigration systems. This summer, after serving a nine-year sentence in a Texas men’s prison, Diamantina González was released, but she wasn’t free. She was immediately transferred to an immigration detention facility and then deported. Hinojosa, who has been reporting on Diamantina González’s ordeal for the last decade, followed her to Mexico in the new audio documentary “Estrella: Bittersweet Freedom for a 'Bad Mexican.'”

Maria HinojosaPulitzer Prize-winning journalist, founder of Futuro Media and host of Latino USA.

"Estrella: Bittersweet Freedom for a 'Bad Mexican'"

AMY GOODMAN: This is Democracy Now!, democracynow.org, The War and Peace Report. I’m Amy Goodman.

Soon after President Trump’s inauguration, in February of 2017, one of the first people arrested by immigration agents inside a courtroom was Estrella Diamantina González, a trans woman from Mexico. She was there to get an order of protection against an abusive boyfriend, but she never got the chance. Estrella spent most of the next decade caught up in the U.S. criminal and immigration systems. This summer, after serving a nine-year sentence in a Texas men’s prison, Estrella was deported to Mexico.

Journalist Maria Hinojosa was the first journalist to interview her after that courtroom arrest, and she’s been speaking to her ever since, for about a decade. Maria Hinojosa is the Pulitzer Prize-winning host of Latino USA. A new audio documentary is out today about Estrella, her life, her deportation and the evolving relationship with Maria. It’s called Estrella: Bittersweet Freedom for a “Bad Mexican.” This is a clip from a video that accompanies the documentary. It begins with Estrella stepping out of a bus and seeing Maria Hinojosa, who is waiting for her in Mexico City.

author: Maríangeles Guerrero
title: "Creemos en la potencia política de los feminismos para sembrar semillas de esperanza"
content:
Por Mariángeles Guerrero


Desde Córdoba


De todas las provincias, del campo y de la ciudad, llegan mujeres, lesbianas, travestis, trans. Viajan hace 40 años para encontrarse. Para compartir con otras lo que viven cotidianamente en sus territorios, para aprender de otras experiencias, para contar las propias. Este año, el

39° Encuentro Plurinacional de Mujeres, Lesbianas, Travestis, Trans, Bisexuales, Intersexuales y No Binaries

 se realizó el fin de semana pasado en Córdoba capital. Los temas a debatir se organizaron por ejes. En el Eje Soberanía, la soberanía alimentaria tuvo su propio taller. Carina Vallejo, de la Unión de Trabajadoras y Trabajadores de la Tierra (UTT) de Santiago del Estero rescata “la fuerza de poner en común nuestras realidades y darte cuenta de que no estás sola”.


Y añade: ”Poder encontrarnos, escucharnos y ver que las problemáticas del agua, la tierra y el modelo de producción nos atraviesan a todas por igual en distintos puntos del país nos fortalece muchísimo. Nos permite

salir del aislamiento del interior

 y llevar nuestras voces comunitarias a debates colectivos y asambleas de mujeres”.


Dhanna Moyano es travesti, productora caprina en Luján de Cuyo (Mendoza), integrante del Movimiento Nacional Campesino Indígena-Somos Tierra (MNCI-ST) y representante de Argentina en la Coordinadora Latinoamericana de Organizaciones del Campo (CLOC) - Vía Campesina. Fue una de las participantes del Encuentro y señala que la masividad que tuvo es una muestra del enojo que hay hacia el Gobierno. “

Hemos tenido travesticidios, femicidios, ventas de nuestras tierras

. Hoy estamos defendiendo la soberanía alimentaria porque es preocupante para nuestros cuerpos y cuerpas en todo el país. Este 15 de octubre tenemos que salir a defender que no nos vendan las tierras, porque venderlas es despojar a las familias campesinas, a las comunidades indígenas y al colectivo de la diversidad que está retomando ese camino”, denuncia.


Y agrega: “Nos abrazamos, lloramos, porque estamos mal en todo el país pero también estamos dando una gran lucha por un país soberano, libre y con igualdad de derechos para todos y para todas”.


Subraya que las diversidades sexuales son parte de la lucha campesina porque es un proyecto de vida concreto para ellas. “El Estado dice que las travestis nos morimos entre los 35 y 40 años por la calidad de vida que llevamos. Volver al campo implica que esa calidad de vida aumenta, porque es una vida más sana, más saludable”, explica.


Ante el desmantelamiento de las políticas para la agricultura familiar y las políticas de género,

la presencia de la realidad campesina en los debates feministas se vuelve urgente

. En este Encuentro, por primera vez la UTT, el MNCI-ST y el Movimiento Nacional Campesino Indígena marcharon en una misma columna, representando a las organizaciones campesinas.


Carolina Llorens, del MNCI-ST y del Movimiento Campesino de Córdoba (MCC) remarca “la potencia política que tenemos los feminismos de articular luchas ante un horizonte tan fragmentado y sembrar semillas de esperanza y de organización”. Y apunta que ese es el rol que tienen los feminismos campesinos, indígenas y populares. Y que los encuentros son un espacio potenciador de esa presencia política, del protagonismo de las mujeres y las diversidades.


Graciela Salto vive a 60 kilómetros de la localidad de Quimilí (departamento Moreno, al este de Santiago del Estero). Es la primera vez que participa de un Encuentro. “Aquí se dice la verdad, uno no viene con invento, dice lo que conoce. En la vida del campo es muy importante la tierra. Y si la defendemos, es para algo bueno, para algo sano. Es para la familia, para nuestros abuelos, para nuestros hijos”, valora.


Salto participó del Encuentro con la bandera del MNCI en la espalda, junto a su hija y otras compañeras que viajaron con ella. Cuenta que el mensaje que fue a compartir con compañeras de otras provincias es lo que sucede en su territorio: las fumigaciones con agrotóxicos y los desalojos. “No podemos criar animales porque te los envenenan, no podemos poner una fruta o una verdura por el tema del veneno. Y si nos desalojan, ¿adónde vamos a ir? No queremos irnos, somos nacidos y criados en el campo”.


Al encuentro llevó su bandera y la realidad del lugar donde vive. Y vuelve a su casa, dice, “con muchos recuerdos de todo lo que se habló y de las compañeras que conocí”.

author: Simón Rodríguez
title: Dominican Republic Cozies Up to Israel Amid Right Wing Surge in Latin America
content:
The government recently adopted the IHRA definition of antisemitism while escalating its ethnic cleansing of Haitians.

Truthout is a vital news source and a living history of political struggle. If you think our work is valuable, support us with a donation of any size.

On August 24, the Dominican government adopted the International Holocaust Remembrance Alliance (IHRA) working definition of antisemitism, infamous for equating opposition to Israeli apartheid and Zionist colonialism with antisemitism. President Luis Abinader made the announcement in Santo Domingo, while speaking at an event organized by the U.S. Zionist organization Combat Antisemitism Movement. Subsequently, a statement from the Dominican Foreign Ministry justified the decision by invoking a supposed official policy against hate and discrimination dating back to 1938 when, according to the text, “the Dominican State was the only one to offer asylum in Sosúa to a significant number of Jewish refugees fleeing the war crimes perpetrated by the Nazi regime”.

In 1938, the racist and genocidal Trujillo dictatorship was in power. Just as the Israeli regime pushes for the redefinition of antisemitism to shield itself, in Orwellian fashion, Abinader is rewriting the past to accommodate the neo-Trujilloist present.

It is not surprising that the Dominican government, led by Abinader, would uphold the Trujilloist legacy.
