author: By L. Cam Anderson, Contributor
title: How The Proud Boys Lost Their Name
content:
West Palm Beach, FL – On Sept. 26, the film “American Martyrs” premiered at the Kravis Center’s Cohen Pavilion in West Palm Beach, Florida. 


The subject of the film, presented by the far-right media outlet Gateway Pundit, was the Proud Boys – specifically the “seditious five,” whom a federal jury found guilty of seditious conspiracy to stop the presidential transfer of power for their role in the Jan. 6, 2021 storming of the U.S. Capitol.


The official poster for the film, promoted by Enrique Tarrio and Gateway Pundit on X ahead of its premiere. Note that Zachary Rehl, first on the left in the lineup, is AI-generated.


The five Proud Boys presenting the film were chairman Henry “Enrique” Tarrio, Ethan Nordean, Joe Biggs, Zachary Rehl and Dominic Pezzola. In reality, the actual fifth member of the “seditious five” is Jeremy Bertino, not Pezzola, who pleaded guilty and testified against the others during their trial. 


In August 2025, Bertino appeared on an episode of Tarrio’s Substack podcast titled “Kiss of Judas,” where the “government star witness” allowed the permanently sunglasses-clad chairman to humiliate him for the twelve people who liked the post. Despite this entreaty to re-enter the flock, Bertino did not make the cut as an “American martyr.”


Besides Tarrio, who received a full pardon, the others had the sentences commuted by executive order during President Donald Trump’s first day back in office on Jan. 20, 2025. 


The film premiere, held less than four miles from Trump’s Mar-a-Lago Club, was graced by numerous right-wing characters, including leading “Stop the Steal” figure and former New York City Mayor Rudy Giuliani,

QAnon digital warrior

 and former U.S. Army general Michael Flynn and convicted fraudster George Santos.


Led by right-wing media figure Lara Logan, the event opened at 7 p.m. with an open bar that overlapped with a 10-minute window set aside for “prayer, national anthem and pledge.”


After the 80-minute film concluded, the Gateway Pundit presented Tarrio with a Gateway Pundit-branded award created specifically for the occasion recognizing him “as an American Martyr and Hero.”


“It’s not an Emmy,” Tarrio wrote on X two days later. “But it’s so much better.”


[Source: Enrique Tarrio on X]


Despite the obvious connections to the Proud Boys organization, the premiere lacked any of the recognizable branding belonging to what it depicted as a persecuted “drinking fraternity.”


Even on Tarrio’s person, the golden cock and abbreviated name have given way to the branding for his streaming outfit, “War Boys,” which has gained a whopping 700 followers on Rumble since the channel was created in April last year.


And on Tarrio’s merch website – where the Afro-Cuban now in his 40s markets just about any idea as apparel, including a t-shirt reading “Enrique Tarrio Eats Cream Pies” with an AI illustration of Tarrio licking an over-sized cream pie – reveals a distinct absence of Proud Boys related merchandise.


[Source: Enrique Tarrio on X]


Tarrio’s ability to capitalize on Proud Boys merchandising, which once characterized his merch store, hit a setback last year when a D.C. Superior Court judge awarded the brand to a historically-Black church following a years-long legal battle set in the wake of the 2020 Presidential election.


At the beginning of 2025, the Metropolitan African Methodist Episcopal (MAME) church was the only place one could purchase official Proud Boys merchandise, re-branded to signify Black pride, with proceeds going toward the church’s community justice fund.


In April 2025, the church’s hold on the brand was tested on the Hudson Valley Proud Boys, who were sued in the Southern District Court of New York for their continued usage of the Proud Boys branding and merchandising.


The court reached a default judgment against the Hudson Valley Proud Boys, a chapter associated with Tarrio, earlier this year on April 8, awarding MAME $75,000 for trademark infringement and nearly $200,000 in attorney’s fees.


The judgment against the Hudson Valley Proud Boys is only a small part of the church’s pursuit to be fully compensated in the amount awarded by the court, which continues to be a major struggle to this day and sees all related parties continue to be wrapped up in the ongoing court battle.

title: Irkçı Le Pen'den Türkiye'ye AB desteğini kesme çağrısı
content:
Fransa’da ırkçı Ulusal Birlik Partisi’nin lideri Marine Le Pen, 15 Ekim’de Brüksel’de düzenlenen Avrupa Birliği liderler zirvesi öncesinde yaptığı açıklamada, Türkiye’ye yönelik AB politikalarının sona erdirilmesini istedi.

Euronews’ün haberine göre Le Pen, Türkiye’ye sağlanan mali desteğin yanı sıra üyelik öncesi politikaların ve kalkınma programlarının da bitirilmesi gerektiğini savundu.

Le Pen, “Üyelik öncesi politikalar, Türkiye’ye destek ve kalkınma programları sona ermeli” ifadelerini kullandı.

Le Pen, açıklamasında Avrupa Komisyonu’nun mevcut yetkilerini de hedef aldı. Komisyonun yetki alanını aştığını öne süren ırkçı lider, kurumun rolünün üye ülkelere hizmet veren bir sekretaryayla sınırlandırılması gerektiğini savundu.

Sağlık ve iç güvenlik gibi alanlarda Komisyonun kendi yetki sınırlarının dışına çıktığını ileri süren Le Pen, Avrupa Birliği’nin ortak karar mekanizmalarının ulusal egemenlikleri zayıflattığını iddia etti.

Avrupa’nın ulusal egemenliklerini koruması, sınır güvenliğini sağlaması ve bağımsız hareket edebilmesi gerektiğini söyleyen Le Pen, mevcut AB politikalarının bu hedefleri karşılamadığını ileri sürdü.

Fransa’nın AB kurumlarının diplomasi, askeri konular ve istihbarat alanlarında daha fazla yetki üstlenmesini kabul etmeyeceğini belirten Le Pen’in açıklamaları, Avrupa Birliği’nin yetki alanı ve Türkiye ile ilişkiler konusunda aşırı sağın yaklaşımını bir kez daha gündeme taşıdı.

Le Pen’in çağrısı, Türkiye’nin AB üyelik süreci ve Birlik tarafından sağlanan mali desteklerin geleceğine ilişkin siyasi tartışmaların sürdüğü bir dönemde geldi.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: Binoy Kampmark
title: Sportswashing the Racing Circuit: Rwanda and Formula One
content:
Tyrants and demagogues love sports and the governing bodies that preside over them. Despite strictures, injunctions and warnings about dealing with unsavoury regimes, a sporting body or organisation can always be relied on to ignore the fine print of their charters and make a dash for the revenue till. While the candidates for such a list are long – the International Olympic Committee and the world footballing body FIFA figure with amoral sprightliness in that regard – Formula One (F1) has shown itself to be most promiscuous.

In its October 13 statement, FI glows with the announcement that motor racing will “return to Africa for the first time since 1993.” Then, the apartheid government of South Africa, one nearing expiration, still offered their good services to F1 to run the tournament as part of a controversial tradition. (The South African Grand Prix had been something of a fixture since the 1960s, barring the interrupting hiccup in the latter 1980s.) In a ten-year agreement with the Rwandan government, the Formula 1 African Grand Prix will become a part of the racing calendar in the early 2030s, beginning its first race at the still to be completed Bugesera circuit. “The new track will be developed to FIA Grade 1 standards as part of a wider sports, tourism, infrastructure, and commercial development project led by the Rwanda Development Board.”

The language of the announcement resembles the best traditions of sporting colonialism on the hunt for willing consumers. “Africa represents one of the most exciting growth opportunities for the sport, with more than 100 million fans already following F1 across the continent, and almost 60% of fans in key Sub-Saharan African Markets under the age of 35.” The project is celebrated as beneficial with its promise of creating “a legacy of supporting tourism, attracting investment, developing local talent and creating new opportunities for communities and businesses.”

F1 also praises Rwanda for its appeal “as one of Africa’s leading destinations for international events, successfully hosting major sport and global gatherings”. These include, amongst others, the UCI Road World Championships, the ICC Women’s Challenge Trophy, the 2023 FIFA Congress and the Basketball Africa League.

The Rwandan President, Paul Kagame, heaped praise on the project. As is a tendency befalling many African leaders, the decision of one country is treated as having been made for the benefit of an entire, neglected continent. “Today belongs to Africa. For more than three decades, the world’s premier motorsport championship has raced without this continent, and that changes with this agreement.”

What, then is there not to like? The answer: much and more besides. For one thing, the motorsport body, despite stipulating the need to respect “internationally recognised human rights in its operations globally” in its own charter, has decided to overlook the distinct unpleasantness of the Kagame regime, one not above using arbitrary detention, torture and stomping on free speech. In its 2026 accounting of the country’s human rights record, Human Rights Watch (HRW) notes continued attacks on freedom of expression and association, including the arrest of Victore Ingabire in June of the unregistered opposition party Development and Liberty for All (DALFA-Umurinzi). Among the charges she faces are forming a criminal group and planning activities with the purpose of inciting public disorder. HRW also notes a lack of progress in investigating the “suspicious deaths of disappearance of critics, journalists, and opposition activists.” Kigali’s spotty record on protecting refugee and migrant rights is reiterated. In terms of foreign policies, a stern eye is trained on the ongoing support for the notorious M23 armed group in eastern Congo, responsible for “mass summary executions, arbitrary detention, torture, forced labor, forced recruitment including child recruitment, forced deportations, sexual violence, and intimidation of journalists and activists.”

In June, the Democratic Republic of Congo filed a case against Rwanda in the International Court of Justice concerning “abuses attributable to Rwanda over a period extending from 1996 to the present day”. author: Ash Sarkar
title: A Motion, a Meltdown, and an Andy Burnham-Shaped Opportunity
content:
They’re calling it the E motion heard around the world, as the fallout continues from the Green party’s ‘Zionism is Racism’ policy, passed at its conference earlier this month.


The motion has dominated the headlines since making it onto the agenda for autumn conference, eclipsing what the leadership had hoped would be the party’s trademark rent controls policy. It kicked off a briefing war, led by GPEW stalwart and second referendum-enthusiast Caroline Lucas. It also prompted 

pointed queries

 from the Equalities and Human Rights Commission.


And now, unwilling to let a good crisis pass him by, prime minister Andy Burnham has piled in, 

ruling out any future coalition

 with the Greens while the policy remains in place. Supporters of the motion may greet this news as a strategic win – distance from Labour cements the Greens’ status as an insurgent, anti-establishment force. But there are rumblings of discontent amongst parts of the Green party of England and Wales.


It’s no secret that Zack Polanski (while publicly supportive of the argument that Israel’s displacement of, and genocide against, the Palestinians is the result of racist ideology) needed this motion like he needed a hole in the head. He was careful to neither unequivocally back nor deride the motion, and warned that it may “create a distraction” by putting Green members and pro-Palestine activists in a position of being attacked.


Whatever the virtues of the motion were, and still might be, Polanski was proved right on this latter point. The days leading up to his unsuccessful attempt to become the MP for Holborn and St Pancras were a storm of negative media coverage, in which he was forced to defend his party against accusations of being a threat to Jewish people. It would be wrong to characterise the byelection loss as a direct result of the ‘Zionism is Racism’ motion. But it didn’t exactly help his efforts to get elected either.


What followed were the first stirrings of Green infighting. For those steeped in the factional bloodletting of Labour party politics, this is all fairly tame stuff: Lucas, the night of the count, 

failing to shut down talk

 of Polanski stepping down, Ellie Chowns 

calling on her leader to “step up”

. But while the Greens might put the ‘civil’ in civil war, this level of publicly-litigated internal division is new for the party.


What’s more, local Green parties and councils have had to manage the reactions of a significant number of Jewish residents and organisations. Haringey council, led by the Greens, found its attempts at overture 

knocked back

 by one local synagogue. “We take it from both the tone and the content of your email that you are deeply embarrassed with the decision taken by your party,” wrote Highgate United Synagogue. “[Your] embarrassment is not enough. If you really want us to feel you do not agree with the racist and genocidal implications of your party’s policy, the least we can expect is for you to publicly resile yourself from that policy and commit yourself and your party colleagues to reverse that policy.”


Enter one Andrew Burnham. Though the early months of his premiership have been marked by his attempts to mend fences with voters alienated from Labour by the party’s moral turpitude on Palestine, the temptation to kick his progressive rivals while they’re down was seemingly too much to resist.


Condemning the motion in the House of Commons at this week’s PMQs, 

Burnham thundered

: “It is wrong, it is antisemitic, and this side of the House will have nothing to do with it.” Polanski, in a statement, hit back, pointing out that he’s the only Jewish leader of a political party and himself a victim of antisemitism – while the prime minister “arms a genocide and locks pensioners up for opposing it”.


Westminster grandstanding has since filtered down to local governance. Yesterday, Labour issued an ultimatum, saying it would scrap any power-sharing deals with Greens in local authorities unless local Green electeds reject the ‘Zionism is Racism’ motion passed by members at conference. According to the New Statesman, such agreements prop up 

more than a dozen local authorities

, including in Bristol. Nice gauntlet you’ve got there, shame if anyone threw it.


Perhaps Alanis Morissette might have something to say about a devolution-loving prime minister imposing the will of the Westminster government on local authorities the minute he thinks it’s advantageous to do so. It’s worth …

author: Jessica Corbett
title: Trump’s Justice Department Ditches Civil Rights and School Desegregation Cases
content:
“Walking away from them doesn’t mean the discrimination has been addressed,” points out a former agency official.

Truthout is an indispensable resource for activists, movement leaders and workers everywhere. Please make this work possible with a quick donation.

A pair of papers published Thursday by the legal group Democracy Forward detail how, under President Donald Trump, the Department of Justice has dumped dozens of cases focused on school desegregation and the civil rights of people of color, all while weaponizing the DOJ to serve “the most dangerous criminal in US history” and his allies.

The cases were previously taken up by the DOJ’s Civil Rights Division, currently led by Harmeet Dhillon, whose confirmation was controversial — like those of Trump’s first attorney general for this term, Pam Bondi, whom he fired in April and replaced with his former personal lawyer, Todd Blanche.

The new analyses of the cases — “Walking Away: DOJ’s Abandonment of Civil Rights Cases for People of Color” and “Filling in The Gaps: Tracking The 50+ School Desegregation Cases DOJ Says It Is Ending” — were developed by Democracy Forward’s oversight and accountability project Red Line for Civil Rights.

“People and communities rely on DOJ to pursue vital cases to address threats to civil rights under our nation’s laws. The Red Line for Civil Rights reports don’t just highlight the cases that have been abandoned, but also make clear the harm that DOJ’s abandonment of its mission retreat has caused,” said Democracy Forward president and CEO Skye Perryman.

The project found at least 36 abandoned cases and probes addressing discrimination against Black, Latino, and Native American people, from Voting Rights Act lawsuits and redlining settlements with banks to firefighter and police hiring issues.

There was United States v. Cobb County, Georgia, in which the DOJ alleged that credit checks and a written exam illegally screened out Black firefighter applicants, and United States v. Patriot Bank, a 2024 consent order over redlining of Black and Hispanic neighborhoods in Memphis, Tennessee.

In United States v. SouthEast Bank, the department argued that a student loan refinancing product discriminated against Alaska Native, American Indian, and Black applicants, and in United States v. City of Minneapolis, the DOJ concluded that police discriminated against Black and Native American in Minnesotans.

“The shameful withdrawal of DOJ resources from these cases and investigations highlights how this administration is abandoning communities across the country,” said Megan Marks, a former leader in the department who is now the project’s deputy director and managing editor. “Walking away from them doesn’t mean the discrimination has been addressed. It just means DOJ is no longer watching.”

In its second analysis, the project identified 56 school districts in 12 states where the department has moved to ditch or end a desegregation case, or did not oppose ending one — from Athens City, Alabama and Chesterfield County, South Carolina to South Bend, Indiana and Waterbury, Connecticut.

“The Supreme Court held in its landmark 1954 case, Brown v. Board of Education, that segregating public school students by race violates the 14th Amendment’s guarantee of equal protection,” the report notes. “Since Brown, DOJ has monitored and enforced desegregation orders, reviewing evidence and often working collaboratively with school districts and, in some cases, private plaintiffs to support progress.”

“This work was central to the Civil Rights Division’s history. The Civil Rights Act of 1964 authorized DOJ to file its own school desegregation lawsuits against public schools or institutions of higher education and to join cases that families had already brought,” the paper explains. “These school desegregation cases are how the promise of Brown reaches individual classrooms. Behind each of these cases are children, families, and a community that fought, sometimes at great personal risk, for the right to an equal education.”

Shaheena Simons previously oversaw the Justice Department’s desegregation docket but is now a senior adviser at the Lawyers’ Committee for Civil Rights Under Law. In response to the report, she said that the “DOJ’s haste to end these cases without deliberation or transparency is a betrayal of Black students who continue to face segregation and inequality in our schools.”

“This retreat is part of a much bigger picture,” Simons …

title: Liberté pour Jülide, Non à son extradition !
content:
Depuis le 4 août, Jülide Yazıcı, notre camarade communiste, militante, autrice pour la revue turque Teori ve Politika et réfugiée politique en France depuis 10 ans, est détenue en Albanie à la suite d'une demande d'extradition émise par les autorités turques par le biais d'une utilisation abusive des notices rouges d'

INTERPOL

.


Depuis plus de dix ans, Jülide milite pour des causes justes en Turquie et en Europe. 


En France, et plus précisément à Tours, Jülide participe à différents cadres militants : le collectif Solidarité Palestine 37, les ateliers populaires anti-impérialiste et l'Union pour la Reconstruction Communiste.


En Turquie, Jülide fait l'objet de poursuites dans un contexte de répression du mouvement kurde et de ses soutiens. Les faits qui lui sont reprochés sont qualifiés de «

 

soutien logistique

 

» au

PKK

 par les autorités turques, qui les inscrivent dans le cadre de la lutte antiterroriste. Nous dénonçons le recours routinier à cette qualification pour criminaliser les engagements politiques et réprimer les solidarités avec le peuple kurde. Nous exprimons notre entière solidarité avec Jülide.


Après deux mois d'incertitude, la décision en première instance a été prise ce mercredi 21 octobre : l'Albanie acte l'extradition de Jülide vers la Turquie. Cette décision de première instance n'est pas définitive dans la mesure où Jülide va faire appel, faire valoir ses droits les plus fondamentaux. Néanmoins, cette décision profondément politique a été prise dans un contexte où le juge prétendait refuser toute considération politique. Ce dernier arguant à l'avocat de Jülide que son argumentaire basé sur le droit d'asile européen n'était pas à appliquer en Albanie, État qui prétend adhérer à l'Union Européenne, État signataire de la convention de Genève de 1951 sur le droit d'asile. 


Malgré ces dispositions juridiques, la justice albanaise a acté, en première instance, l'extradition de notre camarade. 


Nous ne pouvons pas accepter les faits tels qu'ils nous sont présentés. Invoquant son refus de traiter politiquement l'affaire, le juge a pourtant émis une décision profondément politique : il a admis lui-même «

 

s'en remettre au ministère de la justice albanais

Nous lutterons et nous obtiendrons sa libération

author: David Swanson
title: Leaving Borders Behind Us
content:
By David Swanson, World BEYOND War, October 24, 2026


Remarks at

#NoWar2026


Welcome to #NoWar2026 Beyond Borders. Welcome to people from the other sides of countless borders from where I am — borders often effortlessly and thoughtlessly crossed by live images and audio of us, yet sometimes absurdly turned into barriers to some of our physical bodies — turned into such absurdities at enormous financial and environmental and cultural costs. Might there be another way, slightly or radically different from the current way? This will be our topic for these three days.


Thank you to the sponsors and endorsers of #NoWar2026. Our sponsors at the level of War Abolishers are Dr. Michael D. Knox and the U.S. Peace Memorial Foundation. At the level of peace champion is War Prevention Initiative. At the level of Peacemakers, our sponsors are Ann Wright, World Service Authority, Conscience Canada, Just Peace Advocates, and Women’s International League for Peace and Freedom – U.S. Congratulations to that last one for being the recipient this year of the U.S. Peace Prize from the aforementioned U.S. Peace Memorial Foundation. At the level of Supporters, our sponsor is Josette Wier. Our endorsers are far too numerous to name, but you can find them at worldbeyondwar.org/nowar2026.


Thank you to our staff who have all had a role in putting this conference together, and especially to Greta Zarro, its primary organizer.


Thank you to our board and advisory board and chapter organizers and online course facilitators and affiliate organizations and all of you who take part in these annual gatherings and support our work throughout the year.


One of my favorite things about our annual conferences is how many different corners of the world people attend from. It makes it very difficult for anyone to say the sorts of things that peace activists often say, at least where I live, things like “We just threatened to obliterate Iran” or “We just sent troops to Panama.” Of course no peace activists ever, ever actually do such things. But they speak as if they are the military or the ruler of a nation. That’s hard to do when we, the people taking part in an event like this, are from dozens of different nations.


From early on in the existence of World BEYOND War we have sold and encouraged the wearing of sky blue scarves symbolizing the sky we all share. The idea for them came from peace activists in Afghanistan who created what they called

the Border-free Blue Scarves project

.


When we created World BEYOND War 12 years ago it was to create what World BEYOND War is, an organization not based in any nation, but with Board, Advisory Board, Staff, and participants from any corner of the planet possible. From Day 1 we had no use for borders. We’re not just based beyond borders but loyal beyond borders. We don’t support or oppose any particular government. We oppose all warmaking and all weapons making by any governments that do those things, including the ones that do them a lot and the ones that do them a little.


We also created World BEYOND War to be something else that it is, a movement aimed at no particular war or tactic or weapon, but at the entire institution of organized mass killing. We’re not here to examine the war business and decide where it needs tweaking. We’re not upset that an overpriced weapon doesn’t work. We’d love for them all to not work. We can’t provide you with a list of the bad wars and a list of the good wars any more than we can list for you the good cases of any other atrocity. So we’re inclined toward rejecting misleading examples used to justify enormous industries. A claim to have found a just and proper militarized national border is unlikely to win us over to walling off all countries, and more likely to lead us to ask for more information.


In looking at the full picture of war, we see the transformation of borders into war zones as one part of the war problem.


And we point out that in many cases its no transformation, as the borders are products of wars. Our past annual conferences have also looked at particular aspects of war’s destruction. #NoWar2017 looked at what war does to the natural environment, #NoWar2018 at what war does to the rule of law, #NoWar2021 at the business of holding weapons fairs and of preventing them, #NoWar2023 at unarmed defense as an alternative to war, #NoWar2024 at the empires of bases war creates, and #NoWar2025 at abolition — at the project of eliminating something …

title: Comunicado - Brigadas Apoyo Mutuo
content:
CEUTA 23 OCTUBRE 2026


 


Denunciamos la campaña de criminalización en Ceuta tras la entrada por la fuerza de la Guardia Civil en nuestro espacio para registrarlo y la detención de dos de nuestras compañeras.


Ayer 22 de octubre de 2026, se llevó a cabo una operación represiva del estado contra las Brigadas de Apoyo Mutuo, para criminalizar nuestra labor humanitaria y de documentación y denuncia de las vulneraciones de derechos de las personas migrantes en Ceuta.


Después de meses de violencia física y psicológica contra las personas migrantes, este ataque, en este caso dirigido hacia las personas que colaboramos allí y nuestro espacio, supone un paso más en los esfuerzos del gobierno español para expulsar del territorio, por cualquier medio posible, a todas aquellas personas a las que se les niega la libertad de movimiento.


Desde Brigadas de Apoyo Mutuo se quiere dejar claro lo siguiente:


Las personas que participan en este colectivo realizan labores básicas en una situación de crisis humanitaria: reparto de alimentos y primeros auxilios básicos.


Nuestra intervención responde a una situación de vulneración de los derechos humanos por parte del estado y sus instituciones.


Negamos rotundamente que se hayan distribuido en ningún momento esprays pimienta, drogas o cualquier otro objeto de tenencia ilícita de los cuales hacen eco los medios de comunicación. Ante esto, pedimos cautela y criterio a la hora de compartir y difundir dichas acusaciones sin fundamento, que en más de una ocasión ha llevado a la propagación de bulos.


Asimismo, denunciamos la vulneración del derecho a la presunción de inocencia de nuestras compañeras por parte de los medios de comunicación.


Durante estos meses hemos visto cómo se ha negado el registro de menores en situación de calle, cómo se impiden las entregas de ayuda humanitaria, la quema de refugios en la Playa del Trampolín con total impunidad, segregación racial en supermercados, la práctica de la tortura hacia las personas migrantes de los cuales muchos menores y personas del colectivo LGTBIQ+, entre otros muchos ejemplos en un contexto de violencia y agresiones sistemáticas.


Este hecho supone un paso más dentro de una estrategia de intimidación y represión para evitar el apoyo mutuo y la solidaridad frente a un sistema de prácticas racistas y deshumanizantes.


Comunicamos hoy viernes 23 de octubre, la liberación de nuestras compañeras bajo medidas cautelares, a quienes acabamos de recoger en las puertas de los juzgados tras su audiencia.


El aparato estatal que las detuvo quiere una vez más reprimir la solidaridad. La represión no acaba en el momento en que se sale del calabozo. Queremos que esto no apague la llama, sino que la haga prender con más fuerza.


Esto es un llamado a que brote la solidaridad de otros territorios, con las personas en movimiento que continúan en Ceuta pese al hostigamiento y la brutalidad policial y militar, y con las personas que deciden venir autónomamente y hacer posible ese apoyo mutuo


 


ABAJO LAS FRONTERAS Y ABAJO TODOS LOS MUROS

author: Saif Eddine Ghobr
title: Why does Tunisia become African only when Europe needs it to be?
content:
Tunisia is an African country that has spent much of its modern political imagination looking north. That sounds like a question of identity. In reality, it is a question of power — and more precisely, a practice of domination through classification.

For decades, Tunisia has imagined its economic future through the Mediterranean: European markets, French education, tourism, and European investment. Africa has often appeared somewhere beyond the Sahara, associated with instability, migration, and security.

Europe, however, possesses its own geography of Tunisia — one that shifts depending on what Europe needs from it. When Brussels discusses trade, investment, and political cooperation, Tunisia is a Mediterranean neighbor. When Europe discusses migration, border control, Libya, or the Sahel, Tunisia becomes something else: an African frontier state.

This is not a mere contradiction. This is a deliberate mechanism of geopolitical subordination through classification. Europe does not need Tunisia to be culturally European; it needs Tunisia to be strategically African when African space becomes relevant to European security.

The economic relationship makes this asymmetry impossible to ignore, revealing a genuine policy cage. The European Commission identifies the EU as Tunisia’s largest trading partner. In 2025, the EU accounted for 59.5% of Tunisia’s total trade. Some 73.2% of Tunisian exports went to the EU, while 49.6% of imports came from the European market. The EU is also Tunisia’s largest foreign investor, holding 85% of the country’s foreign direct investment stock.

These figures do not merely describe a successful trading relationship; they reveal an extraordinary concentration of Tunisia’s external economic relations in Europe. When three-quarters of a country’s exports depend on one economic space, that relationship ceases to be mere commerce and becomes an instrument of control, shaping industrial priorities, investment decisions, and the political imagination of what is economically possible.

Europe consequently becomes not simply Tunisia’s largest market, but its economic horizon — where economic dependence transforms into geographical dependence. Africa becomes secondary, not because it is irrelevant, but because Tunisia has spent decades learning to imagine prosperity through a northern market. As Kwame Nkrumah warned in 1965, the most insidious form of domination is control through financial and structural instruments, not direct conquest.

The contradiction becomes sharper when migration enters the picture, exposing the biopolitics of European border management. The EU’s relationship with Tunisia increasingly includes border management, migration control, and the fight against migrant smuggling. European support has included equipment, training, and operational assistance to Tunisian security and coast guard structures.

From Brussels’ perspective, this is cooperation. From a geopolitical standpoint, it is the externalization of Europe’s borders. Europe is not merely helping Tunisia secure its own territory; it is moving part of Europe’s migration-control architecture southward, closer to the routes through which migrants attempt to reach European territory. This is the essence of extraterritorial sovereignty as described by Giorgio Agamben in 2005: the European state exercises its power over human bodies beyond its borders.

This changes the meaning of Tunisia’s geography. Tunisia is no longer simply a neighbor across the Mediterranean; it becomes part of a European security perimeter without becoming part of Europe itself. Tunisia consequently occupies a peculiar geopolitical position: its economic relationship with Europe is framed as partnership, while its position on migration is treated as strategic infrastructure. The Mediterranean neighbor becomes the African frontier.

Yet another geography is beginning to emerge — one that challenges the idea of Tunisia as merely Europe’s southern security buffer. In June 2026, AfCFTA Secretary-General Wamkele Mene visited Tunisia. The visit concluded with an agreed action plan aimed at deepening Tunisia’s trade across Africa.

This matters because it offers Tunisia a role fundamentally different from that assigned to it by the European migration agenda. The African Continental Free Trade Area offers Tunisia the possibility of becoming an economic actor within Africa, rather than a buffer between Europe and Africa. The African Development Bank is …

author: Mahmoud Bashir
title: Israeli forces arrest cancer patient, daughter returning to Gaza
content:
Israeli forces arrested two Palestinians on Tuesday evening as they were returning home to the Gaza Strip after traveling to Egypt for medical treatment, according to a statement from their family and one of their relatives who spoke to Mada Masr.


The two arrested, a cancer patient and her daughter, were among patients who were traveling both in and out of Gaza via the Rafah border crossing, which was reopened on Tuesday for the first time following its extended three-week closure by Occupation

forces

.

 


Twenty-nine patients, along with 42 companions,

left

 the Gaza Strip on Tuesday to receive treatment in Egyptian hospitals. Among them were critical cases, chronic disease patients and those with serious injuries.

A group of 75 Palestinians returning to Gaza after receiving medical treatment abroad arrived via Rafah the same day to

the Nasser Medical Complex in Khan Younis.


The Rafah crossing, which was closed for almost two years after Israel

occupied

 the crossing area in 2024, was

reopened

 in February to provide passage to the sick and injured exiting Gaza for medical treatment, those returning from Egypt after completing treatment courses abroad, as well as for Palestinians who were

stranded

 outside the strip and unable to return home amid Israel’s genocidal war.


Before they are allowed to return home, returnees must pass through extensive security checks administered by Israeli forces manning the Karam Abu Salem checkpoint. So far, a number of returnees have been subject to arrest at the site.


Amal Ghazy al-Rify and her daughter Yasmin Rifaat al-Rify were returning to Gaza on Tuesday after around two years of medical treatment in Egypt, according to

Haitham al-Rify, a relative of the two women who lives in Gaza.

 Rify told Mada Masr that Amal is an elderly woman who was receiving treatment for her cancer, and that her daughter had traveled with her as a companion.


They decided to return without completing the medical course as Amal’s health and psychological condition had begun to deteriorate, he said, recalling that she had expressed her desire to return to Gaza despite her illness. “Before she set off on her way back, she said ‘I feel like I’m going to die, and I want to return to die in my country,” he recalled.


Describing Amal’s condition as critical, Rify said that she and her daughter had registered their data at the Palestinian Embassy in Cairo in order to return home, and that they had received prior approval for their travel. 


He condemned their arrest at the Karam Abu Salem checkpoint, stressing that neither is involved in any political or military activities. 


He told Mada Masr that the family was not informed by any entity about the circumstances of their arrest or their place of detention, adding that they have reached out to the International Committee of the Red Cross for further information but are yet to receive further details.


The family

appealed

 in a statement on Wednesday to responsible parties, human rights and humanitarian organizations to intervene urgently to

uncover the fate of Amal and Yasmine, to ensure their safety and work toward their release.

 


The two women left Gaza “seeking treatment and hoping for recovery and returned to find themselves facing detention instead of enjoying safety and stability after a tough medical trip,” according to the family’s statement, which added that medical “treatment is a right, dignity is a right and freedom is a right that cannot be infringed upon without a legal justification.”


The pair are not the first to be arrested during their return journey back. Before the extended closure of the crossing through October, Occupation forces arrested a young man named Mohamed Jihad al-Shourbajy at the border, prompting the Palestinian Center for the Defense of Prisoners to warn that the crossing was becoming a “trap” for Palestinians returning to their families. 


At the time, the center

questioned

 the role of the European mission stationed at the crossing and its responsibility for ensuring the safety of citizens transiting through it.

 


Amal and Yasmin have not been allowed to contact their lawyers, the center stated on Thursday, expressing concern about their safety and conditions in custody. It added that their arrest brings the total number of Palestinians arrested at the crossing to seven, stressing that the border has come to represent a risk to travelers and again questioning the role of the …

title: Iran builds wall along border between South Kurdistan and Rojhilat
content:
According to RojNews, Iranian forces have built a 10-kilometer-long concrete wall stretching from the Seyranben Border Crossing on the border between Bashur (South Kurdistan) and Rojhilat (East Kurdistan) to an area behind the villages of Teymiz and Şêweguwêzan. Observation towers have also been constructed along the wall.


It was further reported that trenches measuring 3 meters wide and 4 meters deep have been dug along the borderline extending from the wall to the village of Mîşyawe, and that strict security measures have been imposed along the border.


 


Iran had previously sought to sever connections between Bashur and Rojhilat by laying barbed wire and landmines along the border. These efforts are now reportedly continuing through the construction of walls and trenches along the border between the two regions.


The construction of the wall and trenches is particularly noteworthy because it is taking place at a time when Iraqi Border Guard forces have been deployed along the borders and forces at border checkpoints belonging to both countries are engaged in dialogue.


Despite Iraqi and Iranian officials repeatedly emphasizing security coordination between Iran, Iraq, and the Kurdistan Region, the Iranian and Iraqi governments have chosen to remain silent about the reasons behind the construction of the wall and the digging of the trenches.

title: Συνάντηση: Η προσφυγιά δεν είναι έγκλημα & η αλληλεγγύη μας αδιαπραγμάτευτη, Τετάρτη 21/10, στις 19.00, στη Θάλασσα Αλληλεγγύης, Ηράκλειο
content:
Κάλεσμα από τη

Θάλασσα Αλληλεγγύης

:


ΑΝΟΙΧΤΟ ΚΑΛΕΣΜΑ ΣΕ ΣΥΝΑΝΤΗΣΗ:


 Παρακολουθούμε με ανησυχία το τελευταίο διάστημα τον ραγδαία, γεωμετρικά αυξανόμενο αριθμό αφίξεων προσφύγων στα νότια της Κρήτης – ανθρώπων που αναζητούν ασφάλεια και καλύτερες συνθήκες ζωής στην Ευρώπη – κυρίως από χώρες της Αφρικής και της Ασίας. Καθώς παρατηρούμε να ποινικοποιείται το δικαίωμα της μετακίνησης και του αδιαμφισβήτητου της ύπαρξης με αυξανόμενη σκληρότητα και εκδικητικότητα, κρίνουμε αναγκαία την στήριξη όλων των κατατρεγμένων συνανθρώπων μας με την παρουσία μας ως ομάδα αλληλεγγύης.


Οι φυλακές και τα κρατητήρια γεμίζουν ασφυκτικά, και οι ανάγκες των ανθρώπων αυτών παραμελούνται με προκλητική κρατική και θεσμική αδιαφορία, και εγκληματικές πολιτικές που παραβιάζουν κατάφωρα τα ανθρώπινα δικαιώματα. Οι πρόσφατες συνεχιζόμενες εξεγέρσεις στο κολαστήριο της Σιντίκης απότυπωνουν πολύ ξεκάθαρα τις άθλιες συνθήκες κράτησης και την απάνθρωπη μεταχείριση προσφύγων και μεταναστών. Παρόμοιες είναι οι συνθήκες σε όλες τις φυλακές και κέντρα κράτησης στη χώρα, η Σιντίκη δεν είναι εξαίρεση.


 Στα πλαίσια του πολυεπίπεδου αγώνα για δικαιοσύνη και την υπεράσπιση της ανθρώπινης ζωής, εντός και εκτός δικαστικών αιθουσών, η ομάδα βοήθειας της Θάλασσας Αλληλεγγύης δείχνει άμεση και έμπρακτη αλληλεγγύη στα προσωρινά κρατούμενα, στα φυλακισμένα άτομα, καθώς και σε οικογένειες μεταναστ@ν που ζουν στο Ηράκλειο, ενισχύοντας με ήδη πρώτης ανάγκης, τρόφιμα και ήδη ρουχισμού.


 Παράλληλα, σταθερή είναι η παρουσία αλληλέγγυων ατόμων της ομάδας στα δικαστήρια, με σκοπό την παρακολούθηση των διαδικασιών των δικών, και τη στήριξη προς τους πρόσφυγες που στοχοποιούνται και δικάζονται με την ξενοφοβικά εμπνευσμένη “κατηγορία” της διακίνησης και διευκόλυνσης, ενώ καλούνται να ανακριθούν και να δικαστούν τις περισσότερες φορές χωρίς καν παρουσία διερμηνέα!


 Λόγω των δυσμενών συνθηκών που εξελίσσονται στην πόλη μας εξαιτίας της απερισκεψίας, της εκμετάλλευσης και της αδιαφορίας της κυβέρνησης – και ιδιαίτερα στο Ηράκλειο με τα αυξανόμενα κύματα προσφύγων – οι ανάγκες για στήριξη ολοένα μεγαλώνουν.


 Καλούμε λοιπόν όλα τα αλληλέγγυα άτομα που θέλουν να πληροφορηθούν, να στηρίξουν και να συμμετέχουν στις δράσεις της ομάδας βοήθειας.


Για αυτό το σκοπό απευθύνουμε ένα πρώτο ανοιχτό καλεσμα σε συνάντηση – συζήτηση στον (ως τώρα) χώρο της Θάλασσας Αλληλεγγύης στην 1770, Νο 34, την


ΤΕΤΑΡΤΗ 21 ΟΚΤΩΒΡΙΟΥ στις 7 το απόγευμα.

author: Antisystemic
title: Διδάγματα απ’ το Βasketgate
content:
Διδάγματα απ’ το Βasketgate


Γιατί μας ενδιαφέρει τι γίνεται στον αθλητισμό; Στο κάτω, κάτω οι διαιτητές που μαθεύτηκε ότι λαδώνονταν μετά τις πρόσφατες αποκαλύψεις του “Basketgate”, ούτε φόνο διέπραξαν, ούτε καταχράστηκαν δημόσιο χρήμα, ούτε άφησαν στο δρόμο χιλιάδες οικογένειες, όπως το πρότυπο έλληνα επιχειρηματία, ο ιδιοκτήτης της Pizza Fan. Εκ πρώτης όψεως, το αδίκημα τους εμφανίζεται δευτρεύον και αμελητέο, χωρίς απτές συνέπειες στην υλική κοινωνική πραγματικότητα. Παρ’ όλα αυτά, τα πράγματα δεν είναι ακριβώς έτσι. Αρχικά, ο αθλητισμός υποτίθεται ότι αποτελεί τον καθρέπτη της κοινωνίας. Διαποτίζεται από τις ίδιες αρχές λειτουργίας κι επικαθορίζεται από τις ίδιες πολιτικές και οικονομικές δομές που καθορίζουν τη λειτουργία της κοινωνίας συνολικά και σε μεγάλο βαθμό, αντανακλά τις υφιστάμενες κοινωνικές διακρίσεις. Για παράδειγμα, στα κράτη που λειτουργούν ως υποδείγματα ανεπτυγμένων καπιταλιστικών οικονομιών, τα ποδοσφαιρικά τους πρωταθλήματα θεωρούνται a priori “πρώτης ταχύτητας”, με τον ανταγωνισμό ανάμεσα στις ομάδες-εταιρείες να διεξάγεται επί ίσοις όροις και με υποτιθέμενη απόλυτη διαφάνεια.


Από αυτή την άποψη λοιπόν, η ανάδειξη της σαπίλας που επικρατεί στο ελλαδικό μπάσκετ, υπονομεύει το κυβερνητικό αφήγημα για το “success story” του καπιταλισμού στην Ελλάδα. Υπενθυμίζει ότι κάτω απ’ τη γυαλιστερή επιφάνεια, ο υπόκοσμος της ελληνικής λούμπεν μεγαλοαστικής τάξης ζει και βασιλεύει. Δεν έχει καμία σημασία ότι η εξιδανικευμένη εικόνα για τα ισχυρά πρωταθλήματα της Ευρώπης δεν είναι παρά μια ιδεολογική αναπαράσταση, που συγκαλύπτει ένα τεράστιο πλυντήριο για το ξέπλυμα του χρήματος το οποίο έχει συσσωρεύσει το διεθνοποιημένο κεφάλαιο από τις έκνομες δραστηριότητες του (π.χ. Αγγλία). Ή μια φινετσάτη καπιταλιστική βιτρίνα, τη στιγμή που οι παράνομες συναλλαγές της μαφίας οργιάζουν στο παρασκήνιο (π.χ. Ιταλία). Εκείνο που έχει σημασία είναι η διατήρηση της ψευδαίσθησης με κάθε τίμημα. Στην περίπτωση του Basketgate, ο Λιόλιος, η Τσαρούχα και το παρεάκι τους, έκαναν θρύψαλα αυτή την ψευδαίσθηση.


Κατά δεύτερο λόγο, εκτός από θέαμα, ο επαγγελματικός αθλητισμός είναι κι ένας κρίσιμος μηχανισμός κοινωνικοποίησης για τις νέες γενιές, οι οποίες εισέρχονται τώρα στην κοινωνία και μαθαίνουν πώς να την ερμηνεύουν και να την κατανοούν. Ή μάλλον επειδή είναι τόσο θεαματικός και παράγει τόσο έντονα συναισθήματα, ο αθλητισμός καταφέρνει να διεισδύσει σε υποστρώματα του φαντασιακού, τα οποία θα μένουν πάντοτε απρόσβλητα στην επίδραση των επίσημων ιδεολογικών μηχανισμών του Κράτους (π.χ. σχολείο). Στις ΗΠΑ, η ιδεολογική αυτή “βιομηχανία ονείρων” είναι πιο ανεπτυγμένη και τελειοποιημένη, σε ότι αφορά την μορφή με την οποία παρουσιάζεται και πλασάρεται. Βρίσκουμε εδώ να υποβόσκει το αφήγημα του ηγέτη-ήρωα που παίρνει την ομάδα από το χέρι και τη σπρώχνει προς το μεγαλείο. Τις φυσικές διαφορές που αναπαράγονται στην κατανομή άνισων ρόλων μέσα στο σύνολο-ομάδα, αλλά και τις ριζικά άνισες απολαβές που αντιστοιχούν “πολύ λογικά” σε αυτούς τους άνισους ρόλους. Επίσης, άλλο ένα ιδεολογικό νήμα που διατρέχει σχεδόν αθέατο αυτή την ιδεολογική αναπαράσταση των ομαδικών σπορ, είναι η λογική της ατομικής αυτοπραγμάτωσης και ο μύθος της κοινωνικής και ταξικής ανόδου μέσω της “σκληρής δουλείας”. Τα παιδιά του Λιόλου ξεφτιλίζουν αυτά τα κίβδηλα   πρότυπα, τα μετατρέπουν στο αντίθετο τους. Υπενθυμίζουν ότι όσο κι αν δουλέψει κάποιος, υπάρχει πολύ μεγάλη πιθανότητα να μείνεις κοινωνικά εκεί που είσαι, ή να βουλιάξεις ακόμη πιο κάτω. Ακόμα αποδεικνύουν με τον πιο εξόφθαλμο τρόπο ότι υπάρχουν κι εναλλακτικές λύσεις για να “ανέβεις”, ή να παραμείνεις ψηλά, που δεν εξαρτώνται απαραίτητα από εσένα και τις δικές σου “επιλογές”, αλλά από ένα σάπιο κατεστημένο που διαφεντεύει και ρυθμίζει τα πάντα.


Φυσικά, διαλεκτικά σκεπτόμενοι θα πρέπει να παρατηρήσουμε ότι κάθε συμβάν ενσαρκώνει και το αντίθετο του. Στην εικόνα σήψης και παρακμής του μπασκετικού παρακράτους που είχε στήσει ο πρόεδρος της ομοσπονδίας μπάσκετ, έρχεται να αντιπαρατεθεί το κράτος-πατερούλης, που θα ρίξει άπλετο φως και θα επαναφέρει το σύστημα στις εργοστασιακές ρυθμίσεις του. Το αφήγημα εδώ είναι ότι για τις παρεκτροπές των πιο “άπληστων” καπιταλιστών, εκείνων που δεν είναι διατεθειμένοι να παίξουν στα ίσα το παιχνίδι και καταφεύγουν στον αθέμιτο ανταγωνσιμό, υπάρχει πάντοτε το αντίβαρο του Κράτους που επιβλέπει άγρυπνο και μεριμνά για την τήρηση των νόμων. Λίγη σημασία έχει ότι μετά την “κάθαρση” που θα ακολουθήσει την πτώση του Λιόλιου και της συμμορίας του, κάποιος άλλος από …

author: Unknown
title: Beyond Polarity: For a Marxist Theory of the World Order
content:
Collage by Tricontinental: Institute for Social Research drawing from a Dymaxion map projection and Islamic, Mesoamerican, Ethiopian, and Chinese maps made between the twelfth and seventeenth centuries.


Images sourced from: Muhammad al-Idrisi, Tabula Rogeriana, 1154, 1929 reconstruction and transliteration by Konrad Miller via Wikimedia Commons; Matteo Ricci and Li Zhizao, Kunyu Wanguo Quantu (坤輿萬國全圖), 1602, Library of Congress Geography and Map Division via Wikimedia Commons; Códice Xólotl, Lámina 1, Tetzcoco, Mexico, c. 1541 via Wikimedia Commons; Tigrayan circular map from the Māshafā Aksum (Book of Aksum), pre-eighteenth century, Bibliothèque nationale de France, Collection Antoine d’Abbadie, via Wikimedia Commons; and Justinkunimune,

Blank World Map, Dymaxion Projection

, 2023, Wikimedia Commons, CC0 1.0.


The maps in this dossier trace how the hegemonic world order has organised and represented the world, from colonialism, the post-World War II international order, and Cold War bipolarity to internationalised capital, the North–South divide, and US unipolarity. More than representations, they distil concepts imperial and colonial powers have used to exercise power. Every dot of ink is a choice: what sits at the centre, which countries appear at the top, and which distortions are considered acceptable. The cover gathers cartographic traditions with different centres, orientations, and cosmologies, asking how, beyond poles and blocs, we might understand the unequal social relations that constitute the world order itself.


The Mercator projection was developed in 1569 for European navigation during the colonial period. During imperial expansion, it became the standard map projection, still used today.

This map, which shows the spheres of influence of the ‘great powers’ and their ‘possessions’, was created by H.E.C. Robinson in 1908. Sourced from the National Library of Australia via Wikimedia Commons.


The language of ‘unipolarity’ and ‘multipolarity’ – whether global power is concentrated in one dominant state or distributed among several major states – has become almost unavoidable in political debates. US and allied policymakers have often described the post-Cold War international system as a ‘liberal international order’ increasingly threatened by ‘revisionist powers’ such as China and Russia. Many governments and movements in the Global South, by contrast, welcome what they see as the emergence of a multipolar world in which Washington can no longer dictate the terms of international life. This aspiration is understandable. Any weakening of the United States’ capacity to impose blockades and unilateral sanctions, organise coups, and wage wars can open political space for sovereign development and for class struggles to advance.


‘Multipolarity’ may function as a slogan of resistance to US primacy and offer a rough description of how certain forms of state power are distributed. Its political appeal, however, should not be confused with explanatory power. The number of powerful states tells us little about the social relations that produce their power, the class interests organised within them, or the imperialist hierarchies that connect them. Multipolarity does not, by itself, provide a Marxist account of the world; when treated as such, it can mislead us into believing that a wider distribution of state power is inherently progressive.

1


Venezuela’s former President Hugo Chávez, who had every reason to welcome a world of many centres, was dissatisfied enough with the term ‘multipolarity’ to coin ‘pluripolarity’ against it – insisting that what mattered was not the number of centres but whether popular subjects were the agents of transformation.

2

 The need to specify this political content was itself revealing: the number of poles alone tells us nothing about the class forces or popular subjects shaping the resulting order.


A Marxist analysis must therefore replace the arithmetic of poles with the analysis of a chain: an unevenly developed system of social formations, each internally constituted by class struggle and externally bound to the others by relations of exploitation and dependence. The question is not how many poles there are but how the chain is held together and where it is most susceptible to being broken.


The problem, then, lies in the image of the pole itself. It asks us to picture the international system as a set of sovereign states treated as its decisive units, each …

title: Adana'da basın meslek örgütlerinden çağrı: “Gazetecilik siyasi iradenin, sermayenin sesi olamaz”
content:
Adana’da Türkiye Gazeteciler Sendikası (TGS), Çukurova Gazeteciler Cemiyeti (ÇGC) ve Anadolu Spor Gazetecileri Derneğinin (ASGD) çağrısıyla basın açıklaması gerçekleştirildi. Seyhan ilçesi Reşatbey Mahallesi’ndeki Sanatçılar Parkı Basın Anıtı önünde düzenlenen açıklamaya çok sayıda siyasi parti, sendika, meslek örgütü ve demokratik kitle örgütü katıldı.

TELE1’e kayyım atanmasının birinci yılında yapılan açıklamayı TGS Adana Şube Başkanı Salim Büyükkaya okudu. Basın özgürlüğünün yalnızca gazetecilerin değil, bütün toplumun sorunu olduğunu vurgulayan Büyükkaya, “Artık yeter! Nefes alamıyoruz!” dedi.

Gazeteciliğin suç, haberin tehdit, gerçeğin ise sakıncalı sayıldığı bir düzene sessiz kalmayacaklarını belirten Büyükkaya, gazetecilerin yanı sıra itiraz eden herkesin sansür, baskı ve cezalandırmayla karşı karşıya bırakıldığını söyledi. Televizyon kanallarına kayyım atandığını, haber sitelerine erişim engelleri getirildiğini, gazetecilerin tutuklandığını ve sosyal medya hesaplarının kapatıldığını belirten Büyükkaya, gazetecilerin ağır çalışma koşulları ve güvencesizlik altında mesleklerini sürdürmeye çalıştığına dikkat çekti.

Hemen her gün bir basın kuruluşunun ya da gazetecinin hedef haline getirildiğini söyleyen Büyükkaya, “Bir basın kuruluşunun ya da habercinin hedef haline getirildiği, yaptığı ya da yapmadığı haber nedeniyle gazetecilerin tutuklandığı, sosyal medya hesaplarının kapatıldığı, gazetecinin açlıkla boğuştuğu bir ülkede demokrasiden de söz edilemez” dedi.

Gazeteciliğin kamusal sorumluluğuna işaret eden Büyükkaya, işçilerin hak gasplarının, emekçilerin direnişlerinin, kadınlara yönelik şiddetin, gençlerin geleceksizliğinin, yoksulluğun ve kamu kaynaklarının sermayeye aktarılmasının haberleştirilmesinin gazeteciliğin temel görevleri arasında olduğunu ifade etti. Büyükkaya, gazetecinin iktidarın bilinmesini istemediği gerçekleri gizlemekle değil, halkın bilmesi gerekenleri açığa çıkarmakla yükümlü olduğunu söyledi.

Gazeteciliğin siyasi iktidarın ya da sermayenin çıkarlarına hizmet edemeyeceğini vurgulayan Büyükkaya, siyasi iktidara yakınlığın mesleki güvencenin teminatı sayılmasına tepki gösterdi. Evrensel gazetecilik ilkeleri yerine günün siyasi çıkarlarına göre hareket eden anlayışın gazetecilik olmadığını belirten Büyükkaya, bunun iktidar ilişkilerinin yeniden üretilmesi anlamına geldiğini söyledi.

Gazetecilerin iktidarın hoşuna gitmeyen sorular sordukları, kamu kaynaklarının nasıl harcandığını araştırdıkları, yolsuzluk iddialarını haberleştirdikleri ve ezilenlerin sesini duyurdukları için hedef alındığını dile getiren Büyükkaya; gazetecilerin gözaltı, tutuklama ve ev hapsi gibi uygulamalarla karşı karşıya bırakıldığını, bazılarının ise işini ve mesleğini sürdürme olanağını kaybettiğini ifade etti.

Sansürün yarattığı güvencesizliğin gazetecileri otosansüre zorladığını belirten Büyükkaya, gazetecilere yönelik baskıların aynı zamanda toplumun gerçeklere ulaşma hakkına yönelik bir saldırı olduğunu söyledi. Büyükkaya, “Gazetecinin kalemi kırılırsa toplum da karanlığa mahkûm edilir. İstenen de budur. Gazeteci yazmasın, toplum gerçekleri öğrenmesin” diye konuştu.

Son yıllarda medya kuruluşlarına yönelik kayyım uygulamaları ve erişim engelleri de gündeme getirildi. Büyükkaya, Flash Haber TV, Ekotürk TV, Habertürk grubu, TELE1 ve Halk TV üzerinden kayyım uygulamalarına ilişkin eleştirilerini dile getirirken, JINNEWS, Mezopotamya Haber Ajansı ve Kaos GL gibi haber kuruluşlarının internet sitelerine getirilen erişim engellerine dikkat çekti.

Evrensel, Kısa Dalga, SolHaber, Yeni Yaşam ve Bianet gibi yayın organlarının sosyal medya hesaplarına yönelik engellemeleri de eleştiren Büyükkaya, çok sayıda gazeteci ile Medya ve Hukuk Çalışmaları Derneği (MLSA) ve İfade Özgürlüğü Derneği (İFÖD) gibi kuruluşların hesaplarının da erişim engelleriyle karşılaştığını söyledi.

author: CMI Argentina
title: Europa: una generación parece decir basta
content:
Una oleada de protestas generalizadas recorre el viejo continente teniendo como trasfondo una situación económica europea cuyas perspectivas son de un bajo crecimiento, a lo que hay que agregarle la persistencia de las guerras y sus consecuencias económico-sociales. ¿Será el inicio de un nuevo ciclo de la luchas de clases en la región?


Protestas en París. Foto: Martin Barzilai


Como otras veces en la historia la situación despuntó en Francia, hace casi un mes atrás, protagonizada por el movimiento estudiantil, fue evolucionando y creciendo frente a la falta de respuestas del gobierno y la radicalización de la represión, casi en simultáneo las protestas se extendieron a Bélgica, Portugal, España Italia, Albania, tomando cuerpo en unas 28 ciudades europeas, llegando hasta la India.


Las protestas fueron reprimidas por los cuerpos represivos de los estados, lo que derivó en enfrentamientos, incendio de autos y edificios, miles de manifestantes que desbordaban calles y avenidas y cientos de heridos y detenidos. Ni corto ni perezoso el presidente Donald Trump culpó a la inmigración y afirmó que Europa debía “cerrar sus fronteras”, mientras que el premier israelí Benjamín Netanyahu señaló que Francia sucumbió a “la invasión del islam extremista”. Sin embargo varios analistas internacionales concluyeron que los inmigrantes no han tenido un papel destacado en estas manifestaciones. Mientras que el presidente de Francia, Emmanuel Macron, impuso el toque de queda en varias ciudades y la Presidenta del Consejo de Ministros de Italia, Georgia Meloni, convocó al ejército y amenazó con aumentar las penalidades.

Reminiscencias del ‘68


En cierto sentido la simultaneidad de estas protestas semeja a la deriva de los movimientos de 1968 que, nacidos en Checoeslovaquia y Polonia pasaron rápidamente a Italia y llegaron a Francia, en lo que se conoció como el Mayo Francés, aunque su influencia traspasó las fronteras de esos Estados. En aquellos años del siglo pasado Europa era todavía una potencia mundial, con un buen nivel de vida de sus ciudadanos producto del Estado del Bienestar y la idea generalizada de que era posible un futuro mejor. La rebelión tenía que ver con la democratización de las aulas, con cuestionamientos a la sociedad de consumo, contra el imperialismo y el estalinismo, contra el propio sistema del capital. Fue el mayor desafío al sistema desde la Revolución de 1917.


Una Europa en Crisis


La actual oleada de protestas generalizadas se desenvuelve en una Europa en crisis, tanto política como económica, que arrastra una extensa etapa de bajo crecimiento. El capítulo europeo del reciente informe del FMI “Perspectivas Económicas Mundiales” (Bangkok, Tailandia octubre 2026), proyecta un crecimiento de apenas 1.1% del PBI este año y 1.2 el próximo para toda la eurozona, mientras que la región muestras fuertes vulnerabilidades fiscales y una deuda pública regional cercana al 90% del PBI. Es esa desaceleración que llevó a una mayor desigualdad social, también entre países, mientras que la inflación (3.6% en septiembre pasado) impulsada por los mayores costos de la energía se tradujo en descontento generalizado por la carestía de la vida y la falta de acceso a derechos básicos, como la vivienda.


El protagonista principal es la juventud estudiantil, pero no solo por ella, también sectores de la clase obrera y fracciones de clase atravesadas por la crisis. Miradas de conjunto los manifestantes se expresan por el derecho a la vivienda, contra las políticas de austeridad que desfinancian los servicios públicos (especialmente salud y educación), contra la inflación (que impulsa la carestía de la vida) y los bajos salarios, por el aumento del gasto militar y por los temores a que toda Europa se involucre en la guerra. Con algunas excepciones, la oleada se caracteriza por no tener líderes definidos ni presencia de partidos u organizaciones políticas (las redes sociales volvieron a jugar un papel decisivo), también por la violencia desatada por las fuerzas represivas y la reacción de los manifestantes. Lo que ha puesto en discusión en todas partes (también en nuestro país) la legitimidad de la violencia de masas frente a la …

author: ACG
title: CITIZENSHIP LAWS IN IRELAND
content:
The coalition government in the south of Ireland is proposing to change the rules surrounding citizenship. At the moment it takes 5 years to become a naturalised citizen. The intention of Minister for Justice, Home Affairs and Migration James O’Callaghan, is that it will require 8 years. In addition, you can’t have had welfare payments in the last 2 years of that period. Plus you need to show you have a certain level of ability in Irish or English. Let’s look at what is driving these revisions.


The change seems to come out of nowhere. One of  O’Callaghan’s explicitly declared reasons for the modification of the law is a technical one. He says that Ireland is an outlier in European Union (EU) terms and should be brought into line with EU norms. He cited Germany as an example of a country that requires an 8 year wait. The trouble is, this is just factually not true. Germany actually reduced its requirements from 8 to 5 years in 2024 (https://www.bmi.bund.de/SharedDocs/kurzmeldungen/EN/2024/06/mod-staatsangehoerigkeitsrecht.html).


 In reality, there are a variety of conditions across the EU. Twelve of the 27 member states have a standard residence requirement of five years for naturalisation, according to a report published in 2025 by the Robert Schuman Centre for Advanced Studies (https://globalcit.eu/new-globalcit-study-compares-conditions-for-citizenship-acquisition-by-immigrants-and-their-descendants/).


Another argument employed was that the changes “…seek to ensure that citizenship reflects a demonstrated, durable connection to Ireland, knowledge of the state and its institutions, and a sustained commitment to participation in Irish society” (Dublin People, 7/10/26). Even if you accepted the desirability of these qualities, how can such vague and subjective things be adequately measured? We are expected to believe that 5 years would not prove a durable connection or a commitment to participation in “Irish society” but 8 years has magically achieved that? It is really just an arbitrary number.


There is clearly more at work behind the scenes. One possible reason for the adjustment is the current Taoiseach/Leader of the Government Michael Martin is seen as vulnerable on his Right flank and O’Callaghan senses an opportunity to look tough as part of a future bid to depose him. So in that aspect, socially vulnerable sectors of society are being used as pawns in an elite power game.


Besides the personally ambitious dimension, there’s also the ideological one of using immigrants as a red herring or scapegoat for failures of the system. By putting pressure on relative newcomers, longer term residents and those born on the island are expected to divert attention towards those supposedly less worthy than themselves. It’s not big business, landlords and their friends in government who are to blame for the housing crisis, energy prices or the general cost of living. It’s Maria the cleaner and Pedro the kitchen hand who have been in Ireland ‘too long’ and need to be discouraged from staying. In other words, classic divide-and-rule.


The new amendments clearly have a class element to them. Imagine you have saved some money and decide to embark on a long journey to start a new life. You secure a job undertaking physical labour, probably one not many of the locals want to do. You work hard for 5 or 6 years. Then you have an accident or develop a disability. Or maybe you lose the job because a tanker is bottle-necked in a canal overseas or a madman running a rogue state starts a war against a small oil rich nation causing delays in supply lines, an increase in prices and lay offs. Or perhaps AI and the development of robots means employers are less reliant on human labour. Any number of reasons beyond your control could cause you difficulty. You’ve paid taxes. You apply for welfare support. Great, don’t expect citizenship now. It’s your own fault, you foreign parasite.


A common phenomenon is one where as an immigrant you take a job that makes it difficult for you socially. Its not uncommon to have a graveyard shift working alone or with fellow immigrants. Likewise you might have to live with people from a similar background. That’s either due to discrimination or lack of finances to take up other options. In reality, due to the cost of living you may actually have to take-on another job as well, just to get ahead. Somehow in such a schedule you have to find time for sleep and to become highly articulate in another …

title: La nuova rivoluzione industriale: Maschinerie, General Intellect e Intelligenza Artificiale
content:
Riprendiamo questo importante contributo di nlp apparso su

Codice Rosso

. Buona Lettura!


I poderosi mutamenti che attraversano oggi la sfera della produzione e l’intero tessuto della società presentano una portata drammatica, paragonabile per

profondità storica

 soltanto alla prima rivoluzione industriale della  fine del Settecento. E una

rivoluzione industriale

 non è un semplice avvicendamento di macchinari, ma costituisce – per usare la celebre categoria antropologica di Marcel Mauss – un “fatto sociale totale” che sconvolge simultaneamente le basi materiali, giuridiche, spaziali e psichiche attraverso le quali una società si riproduce. Come l’avvento della macchina a vapore e del telaio meccanico recintò i beni comuni, produsse lo sradicamento violento di interi ceti sociali e produttivi, ridisegnò radicalmente il piano urbanistico facendo sorgere dal nulla le metropoli operaie e piegò i corpi a una disciplina di fabbrica senza precedenti,

così l’irruzione dell’Intelligenza Artificiale generativa e agentica

 sta ristrutturando la morfologia del mondo contemporaneo.


Anche oggi assistiamo allo smantellamento di intere stratificazioni professionali e intellettuali, accompagnato da una profonda mutazione urbanistica e territoriale: la geografia dei territori viene ridisegnata dall’espansione di giganteschi

data center 

 idrovori ed energivori, dalla proliferazione di

hub

 logistici automatizzati, dallo svuotamento o dalla gentrificazione dei centri storici indotti dal lavoro cognitivo da remoto e dalla messa a valore di ogni

centimetro dello spazio urbano

 attraverso piattaforme di consegna e sorveglianza predittiva. Tutto ciò si salda alla crescita di inedite masse di sapere che, superando di gran lunga i muri dell’officina tradizionale, governano l’accelerazione dei comportamenti, i tempi di vita e le abitudini cognitive sull’intera

scala biopolitica

.


Per comprendere l’origine di questo terremoto al di là delle narrazioni apologetiche o catastrofiste, occorre tornare al capitolo tredicesimo del primo libro del

Capitale

, dove Karl Marx traccia la distinzione ontologica tra lo strumento (

Werkzeug

) e la macchina (

Maschinerie

). Marx ricorda che la rivoluzione industriale si compie quando lo strumento viene strappato dalla mano del lavoratore e inserito in un meccanismo automatico:


“

La macchina capitalistica si appropria dello strumento del lavoratore, sostituendo quest’ultimo con un meccanismo che compie con i suoi strumenti la stessa operazione che prima l’operaio eseguiva con strumenti analoghi.

”


Applicando questa lente all’evoluzione digitale, emerge una convergenza strutturale impressionante. Gli algoritmi di prima generazione e i software tradizionali agivano ancora come “strumenti avanzati”: il programmatore o l’analista manteneva il controllo euristico della procedura, scrivendo le regole riga per riga. Con il

Machine Learning

 e i

Large Language Models

 contemporanei si compie invece il passaggio alla 

Maschinerie

 cognitiva. L’abilità concettuale viene trasferita dall’operatore umano al dispositivo: il lavoratore cognitivo non programma più le regole, ma fornisce alla macchina un ammasso colossale di dati e un obiettivo, lasciando che l’algoritmo estragga, organizzi e applichi autonomamente le regole di inferenza.


Mentre la 

Maschinerie

 classica ha oggettivato e sostituito la forza muscolare e la destrezza manuale dell’operaio, la

Maschinerie

 algoritmica investe direttamente il giudizio, le forme simboliche e l’intera produzione linguistico-cognitiva. Attraverso lo

scraping

 massivo del web, i modelli generativi operano una vera e propria offerta pubblica di acquisto (OPA) sul linguaggio umano: metabolizzano la cooperazione comunicativa della società e traducono trilioni di relazioni semantiche in vettori matematici cristallizzati nei “pesi” neurali. Il cervello collettivo rischia di venire così espropriato, recintato e trasformato in capitale fisso digitale controllato da pochissimi oligopoli transnazionali.


1. L’ecologia ibrida dell’IA: sistemi complessi, ANT ed eccedenza ingovernabile


L’errore teorico più diffuso consiste nel considerare questa nuova

Maschinerie

 come un sistema chiuso, lineare e onnipotente, capace di realizzare una sussunzione reale definitiva da cui sarebbe impossibile evadere. Al contrario, il salto di paradigma dell’IA non risiede nella ripetizione meccanica tipica della vecchia automazione fordista, ma nella sua natura …

author: Unknown
title: Федерация Анархо-Коммунистов Болгарии - Платформа Федерации Анархо-Коммунистов Болгарии 1945 года
content:
Автор

: Федерация Анархо-Коммунистов Болгарии

Название

: Платформа Федерации Анархо-Коммунистов Болгарии 1945 года

Дата

: 10 марта 1945

Источник

: https://www.anarchy.bg/articles/platformata-na-fakb-ot-1945-g/


10 марта 1945 года в Княжево под Софией созвана национальная конференция ФАКБ, которая должна была принять проект программы организации. Подготовка и сама конференция проходили нелегально, но её открытие объявлено публично. Прошло ровно шесть месяцев после переворота 9 сентября. Болгарские анархисты — активные участники антифашистского сопротивления — возвращаются из тюрем и концлагерей, из эмиграции, из нелегального положения. Уцелевшие после репрессий разбросаны по городам и сёлам. Ещё к середине сентября они устанавливают связи между собой. В более крупных центрах созываются встречи, а к концу месяца — местные конференции (в Радомире, Казанлыке, Пловдиве, Килифарево и других местах), на которых все участники выражают нетерпение, готовность, волю к активной деятельности. Определена дата общенациональной конференции по восстановлению ФАКБ (Федерации анархо-коммунистов Болгарии), а также по объединению с ФАСБ (анархо-синдикалистами). В Софии начинает выходить газета «Работническа мисъл» («Рабочая мысль»).


Уже на втором выступлении на конференцию врывается вооружённая милиция. Все делегаты под конвоем доставлены в милицейский участок в Княжево. Они остаются там, пока не приезжают тюремные машины, которые выгружают их в Доме слепых, недавно превращённом во временную следственную тюрьму. Это начало большевистских преследований против безвластнического движения в Болгарии, которое продолжится и в последующие десятилетия.


«Партии ясно, что если мы дадим вам свободу агитации и пропаганды, вы станете силой, с которой мы никогда не сможем справиться. Это определяет отношение к вам», — откровенно делится перед лагерниками-анархистами Руси Христозов, крупнейший милицейский начальник в Болгарии того времени.


На партийном пленуме Цола Драгойчева заявляет: «Если мы дадим анархистам свободу организации, пропаганды и печати, все наши революционные кадры уйдут к ним».


Всё же товарищам удаётся опубликовать Платформу ФАКБ в «Работническа мисъл» в 1945 году. Её содержание отнюдь не только исторический документ. Это свидетельство как о времени, так и о нестареющих идеях анархизма. Более того — и поэтому мы её публикуем — она является хорошей основой для дискуссии о том, что изменилось, а что нет за прошедшие 70 лет.


***


ОСНОВЫ


 Мы отвергаем нынешнюю социальную систему государственности, капитализма и централизма, потому что она основана на власти, которая противоречит народным инициативам и свободе. Всякая власть означает политические, экономические или духовные привилегии. В экономическом отношении она представлена частной собственностью, в политическом — государством, а в духовном — религией.


 Эти три формы власти взаимосвязаны — если какая-либо из них сохранится, она восстановит и остальные. Поэтому мы отвергаем сам принцип власти. Мы сторонники упразднения частной собственности, государства и религии и выступаем за полную ликвидацию всех форм и институтов принуждения и насилия.


 Мы отвергаем всякое учение и всякое социальное, политическое и экономическое движение, целью которого является поддержание государства, частной собственности и церкви, принуждения и насилия в общественных отношениях.


 Мы отвергаем фашизм, который является исторической попыткой восстановления абсолютизма, самодержавия и могущества политической формы власти с целью защиты экономического и духовного господства привилегированных классов.


 Мы отвергаем политическую демократию, потому что она не предусматривает упразднения принципа власти, ведёт к дезориентации масс, втягивая их обманом и иллюзиями в битвы против их собственных интересов, и развращает их через осуществление власти и поддержание стремления к господству.


 Кроме того, политическая демократия совершенно неспособна решить великие социальные проблемы. Она поддерживает хаос, противоречия и преступления, проистекающие из социальных основ централизованного государства и капитализма.


 Мы отрицаем государственный социализм, потому что он ведёт к государственному капитализму: к самой чудовищной форме экономической эксплуатации и угнетения и к полному упразднению общественных и индивидуальных свобод.


 Мы за анархо-коммунизм, или свободный коммунизм, который заменит частную собственность полной социализацией земли, фабрик, шахт, всех средств производства и продукции …

title: Презентация книги Марии Рахманиновой «Контуры автономии. Черновики к анархистской феноменологии субъекта»
content:
Тбилисский книжный магазин Odradek приглашает на презентацию новой книги Марии Рахманиновой.

28.10 20:00 Odradek Bookstore Dzmebi Zubalashvili, 40

На презентации выступит сама Мария, а также автор одного из предисловий к книге Дмитрий Поляков. Все остальные также приглашаются к дискуссии после вступительных слов — как те, кто уже успел ознакомиться с текстом, так и те, кто познакомится с его содержанием через доклады-сообщения выступающих.

Книга Рахманиновой приглашает к вдумчивому и внимательному вглядыванию в вопрос о том, что есть общее и что есть особенное, обращаясь к классикам анархистской мысли и к наиболее видным и скрытым в тени западным философам современности, чьё внимание также касается этого вопроса.

«Предлагаемые „черновики“ — если не первое, то определённо редкое в русскоязычном пространстве философско-антропологическое высказывание о субъекте, скрупулёзно увязывающее анархизм с научным дискурсом XXI века. Выходя в свет, этот текст выводит с собой из тени и либертарную мысль о личности, то и дело вытесняемую „здравым смыслом“ Левиафана. И в этой очередной реактивации анархистских установок, безусловно, есть нечто обнадёживающее — как минимум, их не изживающая себя актуальность». Дмитрий Поляков.

Книжный магазин Odradek напоминает, что книгу уже можно приобрести и совсем скоро — в других независимых книжных Тбилиси. По поводу доставки и появления книг в других городах и странах Odradek обещает своевременно оповестить.

title: 31.10.2026 – Gathering in memory of Kyriakos Xymitiris and all fallen comrades
content:
[eng,de,ελ]


Remember together – Fight together


Saturday 31 of October 2026, we want to invite people to come together and commemorate. We invite everybody to contribute with speeches and everything that is wanted to be shared. There will be food, music and an open mic.


Saturday 31st of October – 17:00 – Marielle-Franco-Platz in front of New Yorck (Bethanien)


KYRIAKOS XYMITIRIS ALWAYS PRESENT IN THE STREETS OF FIRE


Two years after our beloved friend and comrade Kyriakos Xymitiris lost his life on the 31st of October 2024 while he was handling explosives, we continue to keep the revolutionary memory of him and all our fallen comrades alive. Since the moment we learned the news that broke a lot of hearts, many people in Europe and other places all around the world organized actions and events defending his presence in the struggles and his political ideas. Also in the city of Berlin, Kyriakos was part of the struggle against gentrification patriarchy, borders, fascism and in solidarity with workers and prisoners.


His determination led him to take another step in the fight for a liberated world. A struggle that unites us all despite our differences. We understand that resistance has not a single way, but thousands that can break the chains of an oppressive system: from direct action to mutual aid, from the self-organization of everyday life, to words that ignite consciousness. Every rebellious gesture contributes to the struggles. Nevertheless, we value the courage of those that in a moment of constant retreat, and seeing the risks that the armed struggle carries with it, want to contribute to the fight by other means. For this reason, we also see the responsibility to defend his last decision. A decision that took his life and left the struggle and so many without this wonderful person, comrade and friend.


In the same way that we commemorate Kyriakos, we want to remember all the fallen comrades that we lost in the past years. Even though they died in different circumstances, their history and participation in the struggles fuel our passion for freedom. Sharing personal and political moments is a part of honoring their memory and ideas. And having them in our mind and heart in every action. Because revolutionary memory is more than remembering the past. It is a way not to forget that the fight continues. What they sowed with love are the seeds of rage that permeate every step we take against this system of misery. A capitalist, racist and patriarchal system that one day will be destroyed. And with the same tears in our eyes, we will celebrate that one day we said “we are right, we will win”.


It is us who must preserve their memory, remember their explosive action and their sharp determination. It is us who must transform common grief into anger and militant organisation. It is us who must give something, for those who gave everything.


Marianna Manoura and Dimitra Zarafeta


October 2025 – Month in Memory of Kyriakos Xymitiris

Gemeinsam Erinnern – Gemeinsam Kämpfen


Gedenken an Kyriakos Xymitiris und alle gefallenen Gefährt*innen


Am Samstag, dem 31. Oktober 2026, möchten wir alle einladen, zusammenzukommen und zu gedenken. Wir laden alle ein, mit Reden und allem, was geteilt werden soll, einen Beitrag zu leisten. Es gibt Essen, Musik und ein Open Mic.

Zwei Jahre, nachdem unser geliebter Freund und Gefährte Kyriakos Xymitiris am 31. Auch in Berlin war Kyriakos Teil des Kampfes gegen Gentrifizierung, Patriarchat, Grenzen und Faschismus sowie in Solidarität mit Arbeiter*innen und Gefangenen.
