author: ROAPE
title: Eusi Kwayana (1925-2026)
content:
Eusi Kwayana was born Sydney King, as he was known initially for his first, more than two decades in public life. In 1968 he took on his African name which in Swahili means ‘Black man of Guyana.’


Eusi Kwayana was a founding father of post-colonial independence Guyana and Caribbean politics and was associated with the triumvirate of personalities that shaped them: Cheddi Jagan, Forbes Burnham, and Walter Rodney. He came to write the anthems of the three parties they led. Yet his own contributions to the Black and global radical traditions are still being recognized and recorded. This will be challenging in an environment where he receives national and regional honors for being a mere educator, writer, and cultural activist. It’s undeniable; he was a revolutionary.


What does it mean that Eusi Kwayana was a revolutionary? He was a campaigner against white supremacy, empire, capitalism, patriarchy, and ecological destruction. More than that, where he led breakthroughs against colonialism that denied Guyana, the Caribbean, and the Global South self-government, at the post-colonial independence moment he continued to confront the African and Caribbean political class, whether aristocratic or progressive. As historian and political activist, he always wished for everyday people to directly hold the reins of society. Of course, it was a matter of positioning ourselves to bring this about. His strategies of what to do and how to do it, must be revisited.


Detained When Guyana was Occupied by Anglo-American Imperialism


Eusi was detained when the Cheddi Jagan-led People’s Progressive Party (PPP) was overthrown by Anglo-American empire after winning election to Guyana’s colonial legislature in 1953. The country was occupied for 133 days. Before the Cuban Revolution of 1959, the PPP of Guyana was seen as a major threat to US and British hegemony during the Cold War in the Western hemisphere.


Eusi, with Rory Westmaas and Martin Carter, were perceived as the ‘ultra-left’ of the PPP.  In 1956, the split with Cheddi Jagan came, not over disagreements about commitments to a multi-racial party or movement. Rather, when Eusi and others advanced and defended the inclusion of Guyana in the movement for West Indian Federation. It was a permanent concern.


Multi-Racial Unity, Black Autonomy, and Caribbean Federation


This was part of an unfolding process of awareness. Cheddi Jagan was a socialist cosmopolitan when he faced the wider public. But he was also an ethnic leader of the Indo-Guyanese. Eusi concluded that it was no creative conflict to be an advocate for Afro-Guyanese as well. And it was important to address his Afro-Guyanese constituency

within the hearing

 of the Indo-Guyanese.


In 1959, Eusi became friendly with CLR James and Selma James in Trinidad at the height of the movement for colonial freedom led by Eric Williams’s People’s National Movement (PNM). He learned some important things about political journalism and activism in dialogue with CLR as he was editing

The Nation,

and Eusi was responsible for the People’s National Congress’s (PNC)

The New Nation

in Guyana.


Making Guyana a Global Refuge


In 1961, Eusi founded African Society for Racial Equality (ASRE) with the scientist H.H. Nicholson, known as ‘Vigilance’, and in 1964, co-founded African Society for Cultural Relations with Independent Africa (ASCRIA). With his wife

Tchaiko Kwayana

, an African American from Georgia in the US, who made her own mark as a teacher in New York and California, and her own sojourns to Nigeria, Ghana, and Latin America, Eusi pioneered the African cultural revolution in the Western Hemisphere, and was a transmission belt for African Americans and continental Africans finding a refuge from white supremacy and empire in Guyana as they pursued self-reliance and cooperative living. He was instrumental in making powerful ties between Ghana and Guyana.


It was Eusi that in 1966 gave Forbes Burnham the idea for Guyana being known as the ‘cooperative republic’ at official independence. In the early 1970s, Eusi was a supporter of the most dedicated cooperatives in the hinterland, such as the one at Marudi led by Joe Maxwell. The most dynamic cooperatives would be repressed by the state before the famous Jonestown fiasco.


An Original Educator of the African World


Eusi’s travels in Africa in 1964-65 and 1969 brought him to Nigeria, Mali, Sierra Leone, Liberia, Kenya, Tanzania, Zambia, Ghana, and Guinea-Conakry.  As a leader …

author: Yohannes Woldemariam
title: From Haile Selassie to Abiy Ahmed: the Human Cost of Imperial Nostalgia
content:
The irony is difficult to escape. Haile Selassie became a symbol of resistance to foreign aggression while denying Eritreans the right to self-determination. Abiy Ahmed was rewarded for accepting Eritrea’s internationally recognized border, yet within a few years his government began advancing claims to sovereign access to the Red Sea. The very territorial settlement that helped earn him the Nobel Peace Prize now stands in tension with his maritime ambitions.

Both men benefited enormously from international recognition. Their reputations gave them prestige and influence, but those reputations have too often overshadowed the suffering of the people under their rule. Haile Selassie’s imperial government suppressed resistance in Tigray and annexed Eritrea. Under Abiy Ahmed, Ethiopia has endured devastating wars, while his government’s Red Sea rhetoric has renewed Eritrean fears of territorial aggression.

I have written about the dangers of romanticizing Ethiopia’s imperial past, most recently in Imperial Nostalgia: History, Sovereignty, and the Unfinished Work of Decolonization in the Horn of Africa. What concerns me today is that this nostalgia is no longer confined to history books or monuments. It has returned to contemporary politics, and the consequences could be catastrophic for another generation of Ethiopians and Eritreans.

Haile Selassie’s reputation rests heavily on his resistance to Italian fascism. His appearance before the League of Nations in 1936 became one of the defining moments of his international career. But the familiar account gives the emperor far more prominence than the people who actually fought the occupation.

Haile Selassie left Ethiopia in 1936 and spent the following years in Britain. Meanwhile, Ethiopian patriots remained behind, fighting a brutal occupation. They lived in the mountains, organized resistance, endured enormous hardship and risked their lives. The emperor became the international face of their struggle, but he was not the one carrying its daily burden.

Consider Belay Zeleke, one of the patriots who fought the Italians. After the emperor returned to power, Belay came into conflict with the imperial government. In January 1945, he was executed alongside his brother and other associates. Think about the irony. A man who had fought foreign occupation was hanged under the authority of an emperor celebrated around the world for resisting that same occupation.

The emperor’s record in Tigray reveals another contradiction. In 1943, when people in Tigray rose against imperial authority during the first Woyane uprising, Haile Selassie turned to Britain for military assistance. British Royal Air Force aircraft bombed Mekelle and other locations. As Human Rights Watch documented, British air power helped suppress resistance to the imperial government.

Here was an emperor celebrated for standing against European aggression using European aircraft against people resisting his own rule. How does that fit the image of a champion of freedom?

Haile Selassie’s reputation as a Pan-Africanist also deserves scrutiny. His role in establishing the Organization of African Unity in Addis Ababa in 1963 was important. But diplomatic achievement should not be confused with a consistent commitment to African freedom.

Haile Selassie and his foreign minister, Ketema Yifru, worked to establish Ethiopia as a center of African diplomacy. Hosting the OAU gave the emperor enormous prestige. Yet the same government was denying Eritreans the right to determine their future.

Eritrea’s federal autonomy had been systematically dismantled before Haile Selassie annexed the territory in 1962. While the emperor was celebrated as a defender of African independence, Eritreans were beginning a liberation struggle that would last thirty years.

The OAU largely treated Eritrea as an internal Ethiopian matter. Its silence is especially striking when compared with Western Sahara. The organization admitted the Sahrawi Arab Democratic Republic despite Morocco’s fierce opposition. It was prepared to confront one African government over self-determination but failed to extend comparable recognition to Eritreans struggling against Ethiopian rule.

The romanticization of Haile Selassie reached extraordinary heights through the Rastafari movement. Emerging from racial oppression in Jamaica, the movement invested in the Ethiopian emperor with immense spiritual and political significance. For some Rastafarians, he became a …

author: Monthly Review Press
title: The latest on Gabriel Rockhill’s “Who Paid the Pipers of Western Marxism?”
content:
Controversy, controversy…it’s no surprise that this book is selling very well. See more on this from

Bisharat Abbasi

, in his post: “

In Defence Of Gabriel Rockhill’s

Who Paid the Pipers of Western Marxism: Anti-Imperialist Marxism Versus The Imperial Theory Industry

.

“


DIGEST: Reviews, interviews, appearances


Marx Memorial Library

in London hosted a dual book launch for

Requiem for French Theory

 and

Who Paid the Pipers of Western Marxism?

with Gabriel Rockhill, Aymeric Monville, and Jennifer Ponce de León, who engaged in a discussion regarding the effects of imperialism on the production and dissemination of knowledge. Far from simply engaging in a critique of the faux radicalism of the prominent discourses within the imperial theory industry, the discussion was grounded in a reasoned defense of the vibrant international tradition of anti-imperialist Marxism. Topics included the imperial promotion of Western Marxism and postmodern French Theory, the international war of ideas, the failed efforts to discredit anti-imperialist Marxism, culturalism and identity politics vs. a materialist analysis of the colonial question, fascism past and present, the dialectics of actually existing socialism, and the current state of global class struggle in theory and practice.

Watch here

or below


The Left Chapter

, reviewed by Leo Schwarz:


“Shortly before his death, Herbert Marcuse wrote an essay on Rudolf Bahro’s book

The Alternative in Eastern Europe

. In the essay, Marcuse hailed Bahro’s ‘critique of actually existing socialism’ as ‘the most important contribution to Marxist theory and practice in decades.’ This statement was part of a coordinated campaign for the book and for Bahro that swept through the major media outlets of the Western world between 1977 and 1979–80. As we now know (or can know), a striking number of the key figures in this campaign maintained connections in the postwar decades to the Central Intelligence Agency or to various institutions and organizations that were either controlled, funded, or considered ‘friendly’ by the CIA or the U.S. State Department. In the first volume of his three-volume reconstruction of the ‘intellectual world war’ against actually existing socialism, Gabriel Rockhill examines the history and specific function of these networks of the ‘imperial theory industry’ that emerged after 1945, with his interest focused primarily on the Frankfurt School and the academic “Marxisms” of the Western world, which are usually categorized as ‘Western Marxism’…..”

 Read more….


Kaanan

,

 reviewed by Adel Samara


“…I was among those who criticized the Soviet system in its post-Stalin decades, and the lesson learned was that the greatest losers were the peripheral countries, especially the Arab nation, since the Soviets had long acted as a force restraining the imperialist beast. More importantly, this collapse was, in historical-materialist terms, a setback—an exception—because history fundamentally advances upward. Though our wounds were deep, the class enemy emerged victorious but also wounded, most notably by becoming the sole superpower, exposing its flaws and unleashing its brutality. In this brief context, I attempt to summarize Gabriel Rockhill’s book—a painstaking and rigorously documented scholarly work. Yet its timing is no less important than the work itself, for it constitutes a bold revolutionary confrontation that demonstrates the author’s profound communist commitment in an era when loyalty to communism has become rare and the fungi of internalized defeat have spread everywhere, filling the burrows with fleeing rats….”

Read more at

Kaanan.online

belle epoque

author: Tom Bramble
title: US imperialism in the 21st century
content:
At the start of this century, US imperialism was at its peak. It had been a decade since its chief adversary, the Soviet Union, had crumbled; the country was now the unchallenged global superpower. Washington was bringing countries into the North Atlantic Treaty Organization that had been the USSR’s satellites in Europe, and it could rely on its allies to extend US influence into every corner of the world.

The US dominated the World Bank and the International Monetary Fund and was the most powerful nation in the United Nations. Its economy was booming, and the federal government ran surpluses. US multinationals found new markets and investment outlets worldwide. It was the heyday of “globalisation”. The US ruling class boasted that the country was a beacon to the world. As Democratic candidate Al Gore put it in one of the presidential debates in 2000:

“It is a great tribute to our founders that 224 years later this nation is now looked to by the peoples on every other continent and the peoples from every part of this Earth as a kind of model for what their future could be … The power of example is America’s greatest power in the world.”

Twenty-five years later, US rulers are not so assured. The country has suffered a series of crises, and the global balance of power has shifted. The US remains the world’s leading power, but it is wracked by dysfunction on a series of fronts. Its allies are increasingly estranged. Wars in the Middle East have exposed its diminished military power. Its tech sector and banks still lead, but its industrial base is now much weaker. Its political system is seen not as a model for what to do, but what to avoid. 

The decay of US power can be understood as the result of four interrelated phenomena: an imperial crisis in the Middle East, an economic crisis that crashed the world, the challenge from China and a political crisis that reflects and exacerbates these three trends.

The imperial crisis

The 9/11 attack on the World Trade Center in 2001 was a devastating blow to America’s sense of invulnerability. But US strategists also recognised the attack as an opportunity to advance US power—justification for a new round of wars that would intimidate the country’s rivals and allies alike and overcome the Vietnam-era legacy of widespread domestic opposition to far-flung and lengthy land wars. 

The idea of an aggressive revival of US military interventionism had been germinating in the ranks of the Republican Party for some years in its “neoconservative” wing. The leading think tank was the Project for a New American Century, founded by William Kristol and Robert Kagan. Its supporters and associates included Dick Cheney, Donald Rumsfeld, Paul Wolfowitz and John Bolton, all of whom held senior positions in the George W. Bush administration, which had won the 2000 election. 

The October 2001 invasion of Afghanistan was the first step in this wider project. Bush’s cabinet believed that the US would topple the ruling Taliban in Kabul and then lead a triumphal march through the capitals of its defeated enemies. Iraq, Iran and Syria were the main targets and, further afield, North Korea. Regime change was the objective.

In the short term, the invasion of Afghanistan was a stunning success. The Taliban were overthrown within two months. Domestic support for the war was overwhelming. It seemed US imperialism was back. Next was Iraq. The Bush administration justified its invasion by associating the country’s president, Saddam Hussein, with the 9/11 attacks and claiming that he had built an arsenal of weapons of mass destruction to threaten the West. On 19 March 2003, the US and its allies invaded Iraq. Within three weeks, US forces had taken Baghdad, and on 1 May Bush appeared on the deck of the

USS Abraham Lincoln

 to declare “mission accomplished”. 

Yet things turned bad for the US in both countries. In Iraq, local resistance to the occupation soon emerged. By the following year, it was raging. The US responded by flattening whole neighbourhoods, deploying white phosphorus and uranium-tipped weapons. Regular sweeps of suspected resistance activists terrified neighbourhoods and filled the jails. The US destroyed civilian infrastructure providing clean water, power and health care. And it sacked more than 100,000 government employees, creating mass unemployment and impoverishing millions. The death toll rose steadily. A study by the

Lancet

 journal in 2006 estimated 655,000 excess deaths in …

Wenn wir uns die Strasse nehmen wollen, dann nehmen wir sie uns! Weil der Genozid in Gaza noch immer anhält, die Schweiz noch immer imperialistische Komplizin ist und weil der Widerstand gegen Imperialismus, Genozid und gegen ihren Krieg weiterhin als extremistisch geframed und kriminalisert wird.


Die antiimperialistische und antikapitalistische Velodemo startete beim Eigerplatz. Um 15:00 fuhren wir los und widersetzten uns der grossen Polizeipräsenz. Wir nahmen uns die Strassen und den Kreisel beim Eigerplatz und schon von Anfang an solidarisierten sich auch Menschen in Autos mit den Inhalten der Demo! Daraufhin fuhren wir auf die US-Botschaft zu, welche symbolisch für Trump und die US-imperialistische Tyrannei im Allgemeinen steht. Wenig überraschend wurden die umliegenden Strassen bereits von Robocops und Kastenwägen abgeriegelt. Wir führten unsere Smash-US-Imperialism Aktion deswegen mitten auf dem Bubenbergplatz durch.


Wir blockierten mit unseren Velos alle Strassen dieser grossen Kreuzung, und fesselten eine lebensgrosse Trump Figur an eine Säule.


Schliesslich luden wir Demonstrierende wie Passant*innen ein, Trump mit gefüllten Robidogsäckli, zu bewerfen bis er noch beschissener aussah als sonst schon!


Etwas später hörten wir eine Rede eines kurdischen Genossens, der für die kurdische Befreiung gekämpft hat.

author: Unknown
title: TOKİ Tuzla Konutları önünde eylem: “Evlerimizi istiyoruz, adaletli ödeme koşulları bekliyoruz”
content:
Tuzla Aydınlı 632 Konut projesinin hak sahipleri konutların önünde bir açıklama yaparak teslimatın gecikmesini protesto etti. Eylemde yapılan açıklamada "İmar ve mahkeme süreçleri nedeniyle yaşanan belirsizlikler, teslim tarihinin açıklanmaması ve artan ekonomik yükler mağduriyetimizi her geçen gün büyütüyor. Bizler ayrıcalık değil, hakkımız olan evlerimize kavuşmayı ve adil ödeme koşulları istiyoruz." denildi.

İskan sorununun da çözülmesinin istendiği açıklamada şu görüşler dile getirildi:

"Konutlarımızın neden teslim edilmediği, imar ve mahkeme süreçlerinin projeye etkisi ve iskân işlemlerinin hangi aşamada olduğu açıkça anlatılmalıdır. İskân ve teslimat için hangi işlemlerin beklendiği belirtilmeli, gerekli süreçler hızlandırılarak hak sahiplerine yazılı ve somut bir teslim takvimi açıklanmalıdır. Kurumlar arasındaki hukuki ve idari sorunların bedelini vatandaş ödememelidir”.”

Hak sahiplerinin artan kira ve geçim derdiyle mücadele ettiği belirtilen açıklamada, “Konutlarımız için uygulanacağı belirtilen yüzde 10 KDV, üzerimizde ciddi bir ekonomik yük oluşturacaktır. Talebimiz: Konutlarımızda uygulanacak KDV oranının yüzde 10 yerine yüzde 1 olmasıdır. Yetkili kurumları, bu konuda gerekli düzenlemelerin yapılması ve girişimlerin başlatılması için göreve çağırıyoruz. Kalan borç bakiyelerimize altı ayda bir memur maaş artış oranına göre yapılan zamlar, ödeme yükümüzü ağırlaştırmaktadır. Henüz evlerimize kavuşamamışken borçlarımızın öngörülmesi güç oranlarla artması, geleceğimizi planlamamızı zorlaştırmaktadır. Talebimiz: Altı aylık borç artışlarının memur maaş artış oranı yerine TÜFE (Tüketici Fiyat Endeksi) esas alınarak hesaplanmasıdır. Ödeme koşullarının vatandaşın gelirini ve ödeme gücünü gözeten, adil ve öngörülebilir bir sisteme dönüştürülmesini istiyoruz. Borcumuzu ödemekten kaçmıyoruz; borcumuzu ödeyebileceğimiz adil koşullar talep ediyoruz” ifadeleri kullanıldı.

Konutların teslimine ilişkin eyleme katılan bir hak sahibi ise, “Tamamen bitmiş dairelerin yani bugün bir temizlikçi sokun temizliğini ve içine oturun şeklindeki olan dairelerin, A, B, C kurumlarıyla kendi aralarında üstelik hiçbir şekilde sorumluluk kabul etmeyip böyle bitmiş dairelerin durması insanların canını acıtıyor. Bitmiş dairenin içine dahi giremiyorsunuz. Böyle bir ciddi bir güvenlik önlemi söz konusu” diye konuştu.

Projeye başlandığında 3+1 bir daire için 3 milyon 999 bin TL olarak bir sözleşmeye imza attıklarını söyleyen başka bir hak sahibi ise, “Şu an borcumuz 5 milyon üzerinde. İlk ödediğimiz paralar yanlış mı yoksa 13-14 bin liralık rakamlardı şimdi 20 bin lira. Bir kirayı ancak ödeyebilecek insanlar var. TOKİ de bize bir kira daha ama dairemize kavuşamıyoruz… Ben 45 yıllık bir binada oturuyorum. Deprem bölgesindeyiz. Neden ben evime oturamıyorum? Bunun açıklaması da yok. CİMER’e, belediyelere, bir vatandaş sosyal olarak nerede hakkını arayabilirse bütün mercilerde başvurularımızı yaptık. Belirsizlik devam ediyor” dedi.

En geç eylül ayında teslim edileceğine dair duyumlar edindiklerini söyleyen başka bir hak sahibi de, “Ben oğlumu eylülde bitecek diye Tuzla’da okula yazdırdım ve şu an bir ay oldu okula başlayalı. Artık gitmeyeceğim diye tutturdu. Maltepe'den geliyor. Buraya taşınacağız diye buraya aldırdık kaydını ama şu anda da çok mağduruz gerçekten. bir an önce teslim olmasını istiyoruz. Bir de ödemeleri önceden başlattıkları için hem kira hem TOKİ taksiti gerçekten bizi çok zorluyor” ifadelerini kullandı.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: anred
title: RÍO NEGRO: Lof Cona Torres alerta sobre ataques y amenaza de desalojo
content:
La familia de Luis Cona fue inducida a entregar sus tierras como un supuesto “préstamo”, mientras incendiaron su vivienda y la obligaron a trasladarse a Ingeniero Jacobacci. En una situación de extrema vulnerabilidad, tras la muerte de su compañera y con varios hijos a cargo, el empresario Alfredo Abi Saad habría aprovechado esas circunstancias para avanzar sobre el territorio. En el 2004, las familias recuperaron las tierras, presentaron las denuncias y volvieron a  habitar los campos donde vivieron sus antepasados. Hoy, la comunidad enfrenta una nueva amenaza de desalojo y denuncia ingresos y ataques en sus tierras ancestrales. Por ANRed


La comunidad mapuche Lof Cona Torres, ubicada en el paraje Colitoro, Río Negro, denunció nuevos hechos de hostigamiento en medio de una disputa judicial por su territorio. Según el comunicado difundido el 21 de octubre, el lunes 19 encontraron cortado el alambrado de entrada y rastros de vehículos de rodado ancho y de borcegos. Las condiciones del terreno, afectado por las lluvias, les impidieron llegar hasta sus viviendas para comprobar si faltaban pertenencias.


El conflicto tiene una larga historia. La comunidad recuperó su territorio en 2002, con el acompañamiento del Consejo Asesor Indígena (CAI), para regresar al lugar del que habían sido despojados sus antepasados. Sin embargo, la disputa por la propiedad se remonta a 2007 y tiene como contraparte a Alfredo Abi Saad, quien reclama esas tierras.


De acuerdo con los antecedentes denunciados por la comunidad, la entrega de las tierras se produjo bajo la figura de un supuesto préstamo, en un contexto en el que Luis Cona atravesaba una situación de extrema vulnerabilidad. Tras perder a su compañera y quedar a cargo de varios hijos, con escasos recursos para sostener a su familia, habría sido presionado o manipulado para ceder el territorio. En ese mismo proceso, la familia sufrió el incendio de su vivienda y debió trasladarse a Ingeniero Jacobacci.


La historia remite a una práctica denunciada históricamente por comunidades indígenas: aprovechar situaciones de pobreza, desamparo y desigualdad para obtener tierras mediante acuerdos que no siempre fueron libres ni se produjeron en condiciones equitativas. La falta de acceso a asesoramiento jurídico, la precariedad económica y la discriminación estructural colocaron a numerosas familias indígenas en una posición de debilidad frente a particulares con mayor poder económico. En el caso del Lof Cona Torres, la comunidad sostiene que aquella situación forma parte de los antecedentes del despojo que hoy vuelve a poner en riesgo su permanencia territorial.


¿Tierras para los ricos o tierras para el pueblo? Los Cona y la recuperación de Colitoro


La amenaza actual se apoya en una orden judicial de desalojo bajo la figura de “desalojo sumarísimo”. La comunidad señala que el conflicto había quedado suspendido por la Ley 26.160 de Emergencia Territorial Indígena, pero que, tras la derogación de esa norma por el Gobierno nacional, el proceso volvió a avanzar.


El Lof también cuestionó al Instituto Nacional de Asuntos Indígenas (INAI), al que reclama la entrega de la carpeta de relevamiento territorial. Según denunciaron, el trabajo habría sido concluido hace 15 años, pero continúan sin recibir la documentación pese a los reiterados pedidos formales.


En el territorio, la familia reconstruyó su vida comunitaria, sostuvo sus actividades productivas y preservó su espacio ceremonial, donde realiza sus prácticas espirituales. Por eso, advierte que un eventual desalojo no significaría únicamente perder viviendas y tierras, sino también sufrir un nuevo despojo de su historia, su identidad y su vínculo ancestral con el lugar.


La comunidad responsabilizó a quienes pudieran estar detrás de los recientes ingresos y las agresiones por cualquier situación de violencia que afecte a sus integrantes. También advirtió que su caso no es aislado y lo vinculó con las amenazas de desalojo y la persecución que enfrentan otras comunidades mapuche y mapuche-tehuelche en Río Negro, Chubut, Neuquén y Mendoza.


Frente a la amenaza, el Lof Cona Torres reafirmó su decisión de defender el territorio y permanecer en él. “Solo queremos ser libres de vivir para transitar por y en nuestro lugar ancestral”, expresaron.


“No permitiremos otro despojo más”, advirtieron.

author: Nehaa Bimal
title: Housing, homelessness in focus in Ottawa’s Rideau-Vanier race
content:
Six candidates are vying to represent Ottawa’s Rideau-Vanier ward ahead of next week’s municipal election, with housing, homelessness and support for the Inuit community among campaign issues.


Ottawans are set to elect ward councillors Monday to a four-year term. Rideau-Vanier includes Vanier, sometimes called “Little Nunavut,” home to an urban Inuit community.


Statistics Canada counted 1,270 Inuit in Ottawa in the 2021 census.


Lyra Evans, Julie Fiala Chartrand, Brian Paquette and Michael Karl Sewanaku spoke with Nunatsiaq News about issues that could impact Inuit residents in the ward.


Evans, a former Ottawa-Carleton District School Board trustee and chair, said residents have raised concerns about homelessness, addiction, poverty and food insecurity.


“Pushing people out of a park and destroying all their belongings doesn’t stop them from being homeless,” Evans said, criticizing the city’s approach to encampments.


For more than 30 years, the Rideau-Sussex pedestrian underpass has served as a gathering place for unhoused Inuit. Police patrols, tickets and removals over the summer have

scattered

 people throughout the city.

Evans, who experienced homelessness as a teenager, said Ottawa needs more supportive housing.


“I was fortunate enough to get the resources and support from the system to move from homelessness into a transitional housing program,” Evans said. “But those resources and that support should exist for everyone.”


Chartrand, an artist and community organizer, said she has friends in the Ottawa Inuit Circle, a mutual aid group, and has advocated for it when she was co-chair of a safety committee with the Vanier Community Association.


Her great-uncle, Cst. Albert “Frenchie” Chartrand, was an RCMP officer who spent years in the Arctic, spoke Inuktitut and had family ties to Gjoa Haven.


She has proposed a permanent intercultural gathering space in Rideau-Vanier guided by Inuit Qaujimajatuqangit, or Inuit cultural values. She said she also hopes to address safety concerns about aggressive dogs and the sexual exploitation of Inuit women, if elected.  


Paquette, an entrepreneur, martial arts instructor and youth worker, said he has not directly approached Inuit organizations during the campaign. He said he wants to support residents facing homelessness, addiction or mental-health crises.


Paquette said he would donate at least 20 per cent of his councillor’s salary annually to food banks and homeless shelters. He also proposed more proactive overnight police patrols.


Sewanaku, who holds law and medical degrees and is training as a family medicine resident,

argued the city should not displace people without offering alternatives or addressing why they are homeless.


His platform proposes a housing first approach and a public report on the costs of homelessness.


While he has not spoken with Inuit organizations and residents as much as he should have during the campaign, he said he was open to hearing their concerns.


Incumbent Coun. Stéphanie Plante did not respond to an interview request.


During her term, she supported

renaming

 Sandy Hill Park to Annie Pootoogook Park after the Inuk artist and Emond Park in Vanier to Mary Papatsie Park to honour an Inuk woman whose remains were found in Ottawa in 2022.


Eric Smith’s nomination information did not include contact details.

title: Navigieren auf einer neuen Welle von Unruhen
content:
Jetzt ist es wieder soweit, europäische Regierungen zucken zusammen vor Tausenden Randalierer*innen die in den Metropolen auf die Straße gehen, ohne das sie von den Polizeikräften in Schach zu halten sind. Macron tönt, nicht zum ersten Mal in seiner Amtszeit:


„Wer zerstört hat, muss dafür bezahlen. Wer geplündert hat, muss den Schaden ersetzen. Wer versucht hat, die Republik zu stürzen, wird dafür zur Rechenschaft gezogen.“


Die Papageien der Medien schäumen vor Wut, wie immer wenn die Ohnmacht die Seiten wechselt, und auch die freiwilligen Putzkräfte, die im Sommer 2017 beim G20 in Hamburg mit Bürsten die Bordsteine des Schanzenviertels von Krawallspuren beseitigten sind am Start. Jetzt kratzen sie in Paris geschmolzene Leihräder aus dem Asphalt oder sortieren Mülltonnen in Mailand.


Aber wo sind wir? Überrascht von diesen Wutexplosionen, zu deren entstehen wir wie so oft, nicht viel beitragen konnten. Um nicht den Überblick zu verlieren, eine unvollständige Zusammenfassung der letzten Events,


Brüssel


Am 9. Oktober folgten 30.000 Menschen den Aufrufen von Gewerkschaften gegen die antisozialen Maßnahmen der Regierung. Schüler*innen und Student*innen blockierten Bildungseinrichtungen. Von morgens bis abends kam es im Zentrum, im Bereich der Bahnhöfe zu Zusammenstößen mit den Bullen. Unterbrechung des Konsums, statt die wie eine Pest verbreiteten E-Scooter für eine leicht zu trackende Fortbewegung zu nutzen, werden sie heute von Jugendlichen massenhaft ins Feuer geworfen. Die Spannungen hatten sich schon an den Vortagen und auch in anderen Städten angekündigt.


Am 17. Oktober weitere Krawalle in Brüssel und Lüttich, 195 Festnahmen bei einer Demo gegen die Sparmaßnahmen im frankophonen Bildungswesen, gegen die Polizei und gegen die aktuelle belgische Regierung.


Paris


Nachdem letztes Jahr eine Alles Blockieren Bewegung im September an vielen Orten eskaliert war, wurde deren vermeintliches Ende mit einer lahmen Stimmung eines müden Generalstreiks Anfang Oktober 2025 besiegelt. Um plötzlich mit den diesjährigen Bildungsprotesten und Schulblockaden in eine neue Runde zu gehen. Seit Wochen tut die CRS das, was sie immer macht, sie schießen Demonstrant*innen mit Flash-balls die Augen raus und sprengen Jugendlichen mit Granaten die Hände weg. Aber offenbar war am 17. Oktober die Wut größer als die Angst und Frankreichweit wurden Bullen angegriffen, Geschäfte geplündert, Symbole des Staats zerstört. Trotz jahrzehntelanger Erfahrung mit Aufstandsbekämpfung, gelingt es Politik und Verwaltung bisher nicht, die Allianzen von Schüler*innen, Überresten der Gelb Westen, Banlieue Bewohner*innen, Linken und anderweitig Angepissten zu spalten. Macron, der seine Truppen von Kanaky bis Erbil kämpfen lässt und momentan besonders die Golf Monarchien verteidigen will, kündigt Verhaftungswellen und Ausgangssperren an.


Barcelona


Lange blieb es ruhig in Barcelona aber am 5. Oktober kam es wegen der Wohnungsproblematik zu Riots im Zentrum. 100.000 Menschen beteiligten sich an einer Demo, zu der die Sindicat de Llogateres tenants‘ union aufgerufen hatte, danach Unruhen im Bereich Plaça Catalunya und La Rambla. Bullen setzten wie immer Gummigeschosse ein, 30 Mossos wurden verletzt, Stadtmobiliar lieferte an 28 Stellen das Barrikadenmaterial. Die Sprecherin des Sindicat erklärte als Ziel, das Land zu paralyzieren. Die Regierung hat nach dem Tod von Maricarmen Abascal aufgrund der Zwangsräumung und ihrem Scheitern in der Wohnungspolitik Neuwahlen für den 29. November angekündigt. Anarchist*innen verteilen ein Flugblatt während der disturbios:


„Möge die Wut über alle hinwegfegen. Politische Parteien, Gewerkschaften, Parlamente, alle Organisationen links von der PSOE, Polizei, Richter, Journalisten, Faschisten, jeder einzelne von ihnen ist Teil desselben Apparats zur Kontrolle und Bewältigung unseres Elends. … Unser einziges Ziel ist es, Bündnisse im Kampf und auf der Straße zwischen Gleichen zu knüpfen, unsere Klassenfeinde zu identifizieren und sie mit allen Mitteln anzugreifen.“

author: James Crump
title: Berlin’s Plan to Take Back Homes Will Cost Europe’s Biggest Landlord £7bn
content:
Europe’s largest residential landlord is set to lose €8.4bn (£7bn) as a result of plans by leftwing political party Die Linke to bring more than 140,000 Berlin flats into public ownership.


The real estate company Vonovia, which owns roughly 130,000 apartments in the city and

528,000

 across Europe, would be the most affected by the plans, with 120,000 of its apartments set to be put into public ownership. Real-estate giant Heimstaden would also be hit hard with a projected loss of $1.5bn (£1.26bn), according to the

Financial Times.


Die Linke, which won Berlin’s state elections in September, has agreed to talks with the city’s Greens and Social Democrats as part of plans to transfer ownership of flats from companies that own more than 10,000 apartments, with the legislation scheduled to be brought forward in 2028.


Any apartments owned above that 10,000 threshold would have to be transferred into public ownership as part of the policy, with Die Linke proposing an average compensation of around €100,000 per apartment – around 40% below the market value.


Vonovia’s 130,000 Berlin properties have an average market value of $130,000, meaning the company would lose a projected $8.4bn if the legislation becomes law. The company’s chief executive Luka Mucic has labelled the plans as “unconstitutional”, adding that the country needs “reliability, legal certainty and a stable investment environment.”


Housing was a

key factor

in September’s Berlin elections and has been growing in importance over the last half-decade, with 10% of the city’s residents currently living in

housing poverty

and 160,000 reported to have

left the

 capital in 2025. In 2021, Berlin’s residents voted in favour of the city’s government seizing privately-owned flats from large corporate landlords, although that vote was not legally binding.


In order to govern in Berlin, Die Linke has had to form a three-way coalition with the progressive Greens and centre-left Social Democrats, leading to potential political concessions from the leftwing party. The Greens came fourth in September’s election on a commitment to push the property law through, but the Social Democrats’ leader publicly

opposed the policy

 en route to a fifth place finish.


Support for Israel is also a sticking point between the three coalition parties, with the Greens and Social Democrats insisting that “Israel’s right to exist” be non-negotiable if they are to govern together. The parties rejected general boycotts against Israel and did not state whether Palestine has a

right to exist

 in a joint document announcing the talks.

author: Marianne Dhenin
title: Tenants Unions Anticipate Housing Policy Gains After Progressives Win in RI
content:
Reclaim Rhode Island demonstrates the power of tenant organizing to effect change in local politics.

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

The housing crisis emerged as a central issue last month in Providence, Rhode Island, as Democratic socialist David Morales unseated incumbent Brett Smiley in the Democratic primary for mayor and a slate of progressives won their city council races in primaries throughout the Ocean State’s largest city.

In April, Smiley vetoed a rent stabilization ordinance passed the day before, and a month later the city council came up one vote short of overriding his veto.

“The campaign for rent stabilization and Brett Smiley’s veto of it laid the whole framework and groundwork for both David Morales’s race and the council slate,” said Daniel Denvir, co-chair at Reclaim Rhode Island, a member-led housing justice and progressive organizing group that is driving the growth of the Rhode Island Tenants Union. “It was a race around rent stabilization and with a clear mandate to pursue social housing — and we won every single contested race in the city. Now, Providence will be really an unparalleled site for innovative progressive solutions to the housing crisis.”

Reclaim grew out of connections organizers made working on the 2020 Bernie Sanders campaign in Rhode Island and has had some major successes organizing tenant unions across Providence County and in fighting to ban practices that drive rent hikes and profit for landlords, like algorithmic rent setting. One of its biggest wins in the tenant organizing sphere came this June when residents at Charles Place launched their union with supermajority support, becoming the largest chapter of the Rhode Island Tenants Union. The 200-unit apartment block is home to Section 8 tenants, many of whom are aging or disabled. The union has forced the building’s landlord to the table to negotiate an agreement expected to fix persistent problems, including broken air conditioners, an unreliable elevator, and absent management.

After the rent stabilization ordinance in Providence was quashed and an earlier Reclaim-backed effort to protect tenants from unreasonable evictions by codifying just-cause eviction at the state level failed, the organization shifted some of its efforts to organizing around progressive candidates who could help overcome institutional barriers to its just housing agenda in the legislature.

The City of Providence is among the nation’s least affordable for renters. Last year, the city council’s housing crisis task force found that almost half of the city’s renters are spending beyond their means on housing.

“It’s a working-class city, it’s a diverse city, it’s a young city, it’s an artistic and bohemian city, and the unaffordability of housing threatens all of those things that make Providence special,” Denvir told Truthout. “That’s an objective social and economic reality, [and] the role of political organizations like Reclaim Rhode Island is to organize the objective crisis into a collective political response that brings people together to exercise collective power to solve that crisis.”

With progressives expected to hold a majority, if not a supermajority, on Providence City Council after the general election, local organizers are looking forward to implementing the solutions they fought for on the campaign trail.

While candidates were campaigning ahead of Providence’s September 9 primaries, Reclaim fielded about 200 volunteers who knocked on thousands of doors on joint canvasses for Morales and progressive city council candidates. “We won this on the doors,” said Miguel Martínez Youngs, who defeated incumbent John Goncalves by 68 votes in the Democratic primary in Ward 1. Youngs will run unopposed in the general election on November 3.

Ward 1 includes downtown Providence and historic neighborhoods where residents have faced waves of gentrification and displacement. It also includes College Hill, home to Brown University and one of the city’s most affluent neighborhoods. Goncalves has represented the district since 2020 and bills himself as a progressive. But he was also a deciding factor that saw Smiley’s veto of the rent stabilization ordinance stand when he opted not to show up for the vote to override it. “I got good on the campaign trail saying, ‘It wasn’t a no vote, it was a no show — which is worse,’” …

title: Fırat: Cem Foundation seeks to appoint trustee to Kıraç Cemevi
content:
A vigil launched in protest against the eviction order to transfer Kıraç Cemevi, which was built through the collective efforts of local people in Esenyurt and has served the community for nearly 20 years, to the Cem Foundation has achieved its first result. The eviction has been postponed for one month. Those demanding the complete cancellation of the transfer decision are determined to continue their vigil outside the cemevi until their demand is met. Celal Fırat, Istanbul MP for the Peoples' Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party), spoke to ANF and said, “The Cem Foundation, which operates according to the government's mentality, is seeking the support of the government-appointed trustee who took control of Esenyurt Municipality to effectively impose a trustee on Kıraç Cemevi as well.”


‘The walls of this cemevi were built through the people's labour!’


Celal Fırat, MP for the DEM Party, brought the decision to transfer Kıraç Cemevi to the Cem Foundation on the grounds that it stands on Treasury-owned land before parliament and met with the Interior Minister to seek its cancellation. Fırat stressed that the cemevi had been built over the years through the collective efforts of the Alevi community.


Fırat explained that Alevis from Yozgat and Ordu, as well as Turkmen and Çepni Alevis, live in the area surrounding Kıraç Cemevi. He said, “Around 20 years ago, Turkmen Alevis from Yozgat and Ordu, together with our Çepni community members, came together in Kıraç, Esenyurt, and established a place of worship using their own resources. Some contributed their labour, others their earnings, and some donated an entire day's wages. The walls of that cemevi contain more than stone and concrete. They hold the memory of a neighbourhood, the sweat of its people, the prayers of mothers, the breath of pirs and the collective labour of generations. In the 1990s, when Alevi institutions had limited opportunities to obtain legal status and organise, many cemevis began operating under foundations recognised as serving the public interest. Kıraç Cemevi also began providing services under the Cem Foundation during this period. However, this did not change the fact that Kıraç Cemevi is a place of worship built and managed through the collective efforts of local people, where cem ceremonies have been held, lokma offerings shared and funeral services carried out for years. The Kıraç Cemevi Cultural Association, made up of local residents, has been responsible for running the cemevi for years. There had been no problems until now. However, problems have continued for the past year because the Cem Foundation has attempted to remove the existing local management and replace it with its own appointees, relying on the authority to make appointments granted by its statutes. Alevis are standing up against this imposition by the Cem Foundation, which refuses to recognise the will of the people. The community does not accept this system of appointed management.”


‘The Cem Foundation sought control of the cemevi from the trustee who seized Esenyurt Municipality’


Fırat pointed out that the Cem Foundation had claimed the land on which Kıraç Cemevi stands belongs to the Treasury and had requested its allocation from the Ministry of Environment and Urbanisation and Esenyurt Municipality, which is under the control of a government-appointed trustee.


Fırat said that the dispute had led to legal proceedings between the parties. Although the Kıraç Cem Cultural Association filed a lawsuit seeking to suspend the eviction decision issued by Esenyurt Municipality, Istanbul's 3rd Administrative Court rejected the request for a stay of execution. He explained that Esenyurt Municipality's Municipal Police Directorate served an eviction notice on the Kıraç Cem Cultural Association on 6 October 2026, ordering it to vacate the cemevi. Fırat said, “Citing the decision of Istanbul's 3rd Administrative Court dated 10 September 2026, which rejected the request for a stay of execution, Esenyurt Municipality's Municipal Police Directorate claimed that the Kıraç Cem Cultural Association was occupying the premises unlawfully. The directorate notified the association that it must vacate the building and hand over the keys to the Istanbul Provincial Directorate of Environment, Urbanisation and Climate Change under the Istanbul Governor's Office. The Municipal Police Directorate gave the association 15 days from the date of notification to vacate the premises and …

title: Dilan Karaman’ın yarım kalan 25 Kasım yürüyüşü
content:
Geçen yıl Kasım günlerini hatırlar mısınız? Daha doğrusu Dilan Karaman’ı hatırlar mısınız? Önce, “hayatını kaybetti” diye duyuldu, sonra “intihar”, ardından “intihara sürükleme” ve bir dolu soru işareti, bilinmezlik, sorumlular, sorumsuzluklar, suçlamalar, yazılan raporlar, yazılmayan raporlar, soruşturmalar, tanıklar…


Yüzlerce insan Dilan için adalet istedi, sorumlular açığa çıksın dedi, talepler sıralandı…


Bugün, 25 Ekim’de ise bütün bunların ötesinde bir şey oldu. Dilan’ın ablası

Gönül Karaman

, “

Dünyanın En Güzel Dilan’ı / Dîlana Herî Xweşik a Cîhanê”

isimli bir derleme kitap hazırladı. Güldünya Yayınları etiketiyle okurla buluşan kitapta yoldaşının anlattığı Dilan’ı da okuyorsunuz, ailesinin hafızasında yaşayan Dilan’ı da. Fotoğraflarıyla, anılarıyla, geride bıraktığı izlerle…


Kitabın tanıtımı bugün Avcılar’daki Barış Manço Kültür Merkezi’nde yapıldı. Halkların Demokratik Kongresi (HDK) Eş Sözcüsü Meral Danış Beştaş, insan hakları savunucusu ve avukat Eren Keskin, Nimet Tanrıkulu, Kürt kadın siyasetçiler, arkadaşları ve ailesi Dilan’ı anmak için bir araya geldi.


Etkinlikte Dilan’ın yaşamından kesitler içeren kısa videolar da gösterildi. Onun ne kadar çalışkan olduğundan, yorulmak bilmediğinden, gülüşünden, yoldaşlarıyla kurduğu bağdan söz edildi.


Dilan’ı tanımayan biri olarak, anlatılanların çok daha ötesinde bir insan olduğunu hissettim. “Her ölüm erkendir” derler. Bu kez yalnızca bir ölümün erkenciliğini değil, ölümün ardından sorularla baş başa bırakılmanın, adalet arayışının ve bütün bunların içinde yalnız kalmanın ağırlığını da hissettim.


Peşimizi bırakmayan hisler


Ölenlerin ardından söylenen sözlerden biri de “Kel ölür, sırma saçlı olur”dur. İnsanlar öldükten sonra güzelleştirilir, eksikleri unutulur, anıları parlatılır. Ama Dilan için anlatılanlarda başka bir şey vardı. Onun yalnızca ölümünden sonra hatırlanan bir kadın olmadığını, yaşarken de bir mücadele yürüttüğünü, çalıştığını, ürettiğini, güldüğünü, sevdiğini ve hayatın içinde olduğunu görüyordunuz. Şüphesiz anlatılanlar, onu yalnızca kaybıyla tanımlamaya yetmiyordu.


Geçen yıl ölüm haberi duyulduktan sonra Dilan için ne kadar çok çaba gösterildi, neler yapıldı. Adalet talep edildi, sorular soruldu, açıklamalar yapıldı. Ancak Dilan’ın ve ailesinin yaşarken yalnız bırakıldığı hissi, bugün de peşimizi bırakmadı.


Salonda çok az insan vardı. 


“Baro seçimi vardı”, “yer uzaktı” ve benzeri gerekçeler sıralanabilir. Elbette herkesin kendi koşulları var. 


Dilan, içine düşürüldüğü duygulardan kurtulmak, sesini duyurmak için sesini yükseltmiş ama duyuramamıştı. Bugün, ölümünden sonra adını yaşatmak için bir araya gelenlerin önünde, kocaman konferans salonunun boş sıraları bana bu yalnızlık duygusunu yeniden hatırlattı. Gözyaşlarını tutmakta zorlanan kadınlar, ailesi, onu unutturmamak için emek verenler…


Gönül Karaman: Bu kitap, Dilan’ın yarım kalan 25 Kasım yürüyüşü


Dilan Karaman’ın ablası @GKaraman77252’ın bugün “Dünyanın en güzeli Dilan’ı” kitabının tanıtımında konuştu, dinlemenizi öneririm. https://t.co/wNiwlkXU6f


— Evrim Kepenek (@kepenekevrimm)

October 25, 2026


Dilan’ın ablası Gönül Karaman, kitabın hazırlanma sürecini anlatırken Dilan’ın anısını yaşatmak için bir araya gelen herkese teşekkür etti. Kitabın onun için taşıdığı anlamı, dayanışma ve ortak mücadele üzerinden anlattı:


“Herkes onun anılarının şahidi olarak o kitabın tamamlanmasına katkıda bulundu. Bunun bizim için anlamı çok büyük. Çünkü bu denli korkunç bir karanlık yine ancak bu renklerle aydınlanır. Bu renkler ki bizim sahiplendiğimiz dünyanın yaşanılacak yanı, tutunacak dalı, mücadelenin ışığı ve umududur.


“Aslında bu durum onun adıyla da çok uyumlu. Bu yüzdendir ki dünyanın en güzel Dilan’ı odur. Biran, Türkçede halay demektir. Halay çekmek kolektif bir eylemdir. İnsanlar bütün renkleriyle, stranlarıyla el ele tutuşmasını bilir. Yüz yüze bakar, adımlarla birlikte atılır ve en güzel şarkılar, en güzel ritimlerle tek bir ses olup söylenir.


“Dilan isminin bütün özelliklerini gerçekten de ruhunda taşıyordu. Onun anısına dair herkesin kendi ritmi ve rengiyle kalem tuttuğu bu eser, tam da onun isteyeceği gibi koroların tuttuğu bir dayanışma içerisinde hayata geçiyor. Bu yolculukta kalemleriyle onun yürüyüşünü sürdüren bütün yoldaşlarıma yürekten teşekkür ederim.


“Bu eser, onun yarım kalan, aslında hiç kalmayacak 25 Kasım yürüyüşüdür.”

title: Turkish military blocks protest against solar power plant in Amed
content:
Resistance against the planned “Zenkar 2” solar power plant continues in the province of Amed (Turkish: Diyarbakır). For four days, residents of Arzoxlî (Kervanpınar), a village in the Sur district, have maintained a protest vigil in a tent after company employees entered the project site accompanied by Turkish gendarmerie and police forces. Meanwhile, legal proceedings are ongoing against the favorable environmental impact assessment decision for the project, which includes both a photovoltaic power plant and an energy storage facility.


On the third day of the protest, villagers gathered in front of their tent and set off together toward the site where the company had begun its work. Chanting slogans such as “We will prevail through resistance” and “If you remain silent, you will be next,” they marched toward the project area.


Soldiers stopped the protest march and prevented residents from entering the site. The demonstrators then returned to the protest tent, where they are continuing their vigil. They emphasize that their resistance is not directed against solar energy itself. Rather, they criticize the fact that the facility is planned for grazing land that is essential for livestock farming and, consequently, their economic survival. The construction of the solar power plant threatens to deprive them of a vital source of livelihood.

author: anred
title: De Stonewall a  la Argentina que gobierna Milei
content:
El ajuste, los discursos de odio y el debilitamiento de las políticas públicas ponen en tensión derechos conquistados por décadas de lucha. En este contexto mundial de vanzada de la ultraderecha, la organización de la Comunidad LGBTIQ+ vuelve a las calles el próximo 7 de noviembre para realizar la 35 Marcha del orgullo. «Cuando el odio avanza, el orgullo en las calles es resistencia».

Por Rocío Cisterna para ANRed 


Hay momentos históricos en los que luchar por existir deja de ser solamente una reivindicación y se convierte en una disputa política contra el orden establecido. Cuando el hambre, el ajuste, la discriminación, la persecución y la violencia institucional amenazan las condiciones de vida, los derechos conquistados dejan de parecer garantizados y las calles vuelven a ser escenario de resistencia.


La

rebelión de Stonewall

 fue uno de esos momentos. Hoy, en la Argentina gobernada por Javier Milei, su historia adquiere una renovada vigencia: cuando el Estado debilita las políticas de protección, desfinancia derechos y promueve discursos estigmatizantes, la resistencia se convierte en una necesidad colectiva.


Pero esta disputa no se limita a nuestras fronteras. También se inscribe en un escenario internacional marcado por el avance de las ultraderechas, las alianzas geopolíticas y las confrontaciones en torno a la libertad, la democracia, la soberanía y los derechos humanos.


Stonewall: cuando la resistencia rompió el silencio


En junio de 1969, las personas homosexuales, lesbianas, trans y otras identidades disidentes sufrían distintas formas de criminalización, hostigamiento y persecución en Estados Unidos. Las redadas policiales contra los bares frecuentados por estas comunidades formaban parte de un sistema que buscaba controlar los cuerpos, las identidades y los afectos que desafiaban la norma dominante.


La madrugada del 28 de junio, quienes estaban en el Stonewall Inn, en Greenwich Village, Nueva York, se negaron a someterse pasivamente a la violencia policial. El hartazgo frente a años de persecución se transformó en una rebelión que se extendió durante varias jornadas y se convirtió en un símbolo internacional de las luchas por la liberación sexual y los derechos de las diversidades.


Stonewall no fue solamente una revuelta contra una redada policial. Fue una ruptura con el silencio impuesto y con la idea de que las personas LGBTIQ+ debían aceptar la violencia como una condición inevitable de su existencia.


Su legado recuerda que los derechos no fueron concesiones generosas del poder, sino conquistas de quienes se organizaron y resistieron. Esa memoria sigue presente cada vez que una persona trans encuentra obstáculos para acceder a la salud, cuando se produce una situación de discriminación o cuando un gobierno pretende convertir el odio en sentido común.


Argentina: del avance de derechos al ajuste


Argentina construyó una historia de conquistas en materia de derechos humanos, diversidad y ampliación de derechos civiles. El Juicio a las Juntas, el Nunca Más, la Ley de Educación Sexual Integral (ESI), el matrimonio igualitario y la legalización de la interrupción voluntaria del embarazo forman parte de un recorrido colectivo que demuestra que las transformaciones sociales son posibles mediante la organización popular.


Ninguna de esas conquistas fue resultado de una concesión espontánea. Todas fueron producto de décadas de militancia, debate público y movilización. Por eso, tampoco pueden darse por garantizadas.


Desde la asunción de Javier Milei, las organizaciones feministas, transfeministas, LGBTIQ+ y de derechos humanos denuncian un escenario de retroceso, ajuste y debilitamiento de las políticas públicas. La eliminación del Ministerio de las Mujeres, Géneros y Diversidad y los recortes presupuestarios expresan un cambio en las prioridades del Estado nacional.


También preocupan el financiamiento y la implementación de la ESI, las políticas vinculadas con la interrupción voluntaria y legal del embarazo (IVE e ILE) y el acceso efectivo a la salud integral de las personas trans y no binarias.


No se trata de discusiones abstractas ni de diferencias meramente ideológicas. Se trata de recursos, profesionales, tratamientos, acompañamiento y prevención. Cuando las políticas públicas desaparecen o pierden capacidad de respuesta, las consecuencias recaen sobre vidas concretas y profundizan desigualdades que ya existen.


El ajuste no impacta de la misma manera en todos los sectores …

author: Wir bleiben alle Friedrichshain
title: Protestkundgebung gegen Wohnraumzerstörung und Vertreibung in der Gürtelstraße 39-41
content:
Mehrere Jahre standen die beiden ehemaligen Hotels in der Gürtelstraße 39-41 leer. In den letzten Jahren sind dort Menschen eingezogen, die auf den überteuerten Berliner Wohnungsmarkt keine Chance gehabt hätten. Sie nannten das von ihnen besetzte Gebäude Hugo-Haus. Ende September wurden die Bewohner*innen mit einem großen Polizeiaufgebot auf die Straße gesetzt. Aber sie verschwanden nicht einfach. Direkt gegenüber dem


geräumten Haus errichteten sie ein Zeltdorf. So konnten sie zusammenbleiben und sich gegenseitig beim Leben auf der Straße unterstützen. Gleichzeitig konnten alle sehen, wie in der Gürtelstraße 39-41 Wohnraum vernichtet wird. Fenster und sanitäre Anlagen wurden herausgerissen, Mauern zerstört.Das Hugo-Dorf, wie die Bewohner*innen ihre Zeltstadt nannten, war ein im Straßenbild sichtbares Zeichen. In Berlin wird weiter Wohnraum vernichtet, werden weiter Menschen auf die Straße geworfen. Am 14. Oktober musste auch diese Zeltstadt verschwinden. Eine weitere Genehmigung hatten die zuständigen Ämter verweigert. So wurden die Bewohner*innen zum zweiten Mal innerhalb weniger Wochen vertrieben und zerstreut. Wir sehen es auch als große Schwäche, dass es nicht gelungen ist, mehr Druck von unten aufzubauen, damit die Bewohner*innen nicht vertrieben werden. Jahrelang wurde darüber diskutiert, ob es nicht an der Zeit wäre, wieder Häuser zu besetzen. Wo blieb dann die Unterstützung für die Besetzer*innen in der Gürtelstraße? Diese Frage stellen wir auch selbstkritisch an uns. Blicken auch wir schon zu viel auf angeblich „progressive“ Senatsmehrheiten, die Berlin bezahlbar machen wollen?


Haben wir dabei vergessen, dass es ohne Widerstand von unten keine Verbesserung in unserem Sinne geben wird? Wir verstehen unsere Kundgebung gegen Wohnraumzerstörung und Vertreibung von Menschen auch als einen kleinen Beitrag, diesen Widerstand wieder sichtbar zumachen. Nicht nur in der Gürtelstraße wurden zu Beginn der kalten Jahreszeit Menschen auf die Straße gesetzt. Auch in Habersaathstraße 40-48 wurden am 13. Oktober Menschen mit einem großen Polizeiaufgebot geräumt und aufdie Straße gesetzt. Dort hatten vor 5 Jahren wohnungslose Menschen mit Unterstützer*innengruppen leerstehende Wohnungen besetzt. Sie konnten sogemeinsam mit einigen Altmieter*innen verhindern, dass der


Eigentümer die gut erhaltenden Gebäude abreißt, um Luxuswohnungen zu errichten. Genau das droht auch in der Gürtelstraße Überall werden Menschen vertrieben für das Privatinteresse von Wohnkonzernen.


Wir sind wütend, dass zu Beginn der kalten Jahreszeit erneut Wohnraum vernichtet wird und Menschen auf die Straße geworfen werden. Wir hoffen, wir sind nicht die Einzigen, die dagegen protestieren. Kommt am zur Kundgebung in die Gürtelstraße 39-41!

author: Julius Gavroche
title: John Berger: “Demonstrations are protests of innocence”
content:
Paris, October 17, Guillaume Saligot / AFP


With all of those who continue to demonstrate against injustice and who imagine a different world …


The Nature of Mass Demonstrations


John Berger


This article originally appeared in

New Society

, 23 May 1968.


Seventy years ago (on 6 May 1898) there was a massive demonstration of workers, men and women, in the centre of Milan. The events which led up to it involve too long a history to treat with here. The demonstration was attacked and broken up by the army under the command of General Beccaris. At noon the cavalry charged the crowd: the unarmed workers tried to make barricades: martial law was declared and for three days the army fought against the unarmed.


The official casualty figures were 100 workers killed and 450 wounded. One policeman was killed accidentally by a soldier. There were no army casualties. (Two years later Umberto I was assassinated because after the massacre he publicly congratulated General Beccaris, the ‘butcher of Milan.’)


I have been trying to understand certain aspects of the demonstration in the Corso Venezia on 6 May because of a story I am writing. In the process I came to a few conclusions about demonstrations which may perhaps be more widely applicable.


Mass demonstrations should be distinguished from riots or revolutionary uprisings although, under certain (now rare) circumstances, they may develop into either of the latter. The aims of a riot are usually immediate (the immediacy matching the desperation they express): the seizing of food, the release of prisoners, the destruction of property. The aims of a revolutionary uprising are long-term and comprehensive: they culminate in the taking over of State power. The aims of a demonstration, however, are symbolic: it

demonstrates

 a force that is scarcely used.


A large number of people assemble together in an obvious and already announced public place. They are more or less unarmed. (On 6 May 1898, entirely unarmed.) They present themselves as a target to the forces of repression serving the State authority against whose policies they are protesting.


Theoretically demonstrations are meant to reveal the strength of popular opinion or feeling: theoretically they are an appeal to the democratic conscience of the State. But this presupposes a conscience which is very unlikely to exist.


If the State authority is open to democratic influence, the demonstration will hardly be necessary; if it is not, it is unlikely to be influenced by an empty show of force containing no real threat. (A demonstration in support of an already established

alternative

 State authority – as when Garibaldi entered Naples in 1860 – is a special case and may be immediately effective.)


Demonstrations took place before the principle of democracy was even nominally admitted. The massive early Chartist demonstrations were part of the struggle to obtain such an admission. The crowds who gathered to present their petition to the Tsar in St Petersburg in 1905 were appealing – and presenting themselves as a target – to the ruthless power of an absolute monarchy. In the event – as on so many hundreds of other occasions all over Europe – they were shot down.


It would seem that the true function of demonstrations is not to convince the existing State authority to any significant degree. Such an aim is only a convenient rationalisation.


The truth is that mass demonstrations are rehearsals for revolution: not strategic or even tactical ones, but rehearsals of revolutionary awareness. The delay between the rehearsals and the real performance may be very long: their quality – the intensity of rehearsed awareness – may, on different occasions, vary considerably: but any demonstration which lacks this element of rehearsal is better described as an officially encouraged public spectacle.


A demonstration, however much spontaneity it may contain, is a

created

 event which arbitrarily separates itself from ordinary life. Its value is the result of its artificiality, for therein lies its prophetic, rehearsing possibilities.


A mass demonstration distinguishes itself from other mass crowds because it congregates in public

to create its function

, instead of forming in response to one: in this, it differs from any assembly of workers within their place of work – even when strike action is involved – or from any crowd of spectators. It is an assembly which challenges what is given by the mere fact of its …

author: Cecília Melo
title: Aluno da UFRN espancado em protesto envolvendo Girão: “Não tem alternativa senão a luta”
content:
Quando chegou na Universidade Federal do Rio Grande do Norte (UFRN) no fim da tarde da segunda-feira (19), Henrique Neiva não sabia que terminaria o dia em um exame de corpo e delito, com hematomas pelo corpo e um dente fraturado. O estudante de 28 anos fez parte do grupo que tentou resistir ao avanço de um protesto organizado pelo perfil “Endireita RN” no grupo de WhatsApp “UFRN Anti Lula”, administrado pelo secretário do gabinete do deputado federal

General Girão

 (PL-RN), Allison Lobato. O parlamentar Girão esteve envolvido na ação junto à vereadora de Natal recentemente eleita deputada estadual Camila Araújo (PL-RN).


“Era pra ter quebrado mais uns três”, dizia uma mensagem no grupo, após o fim do protesto. “Apanhou pouco”, completava outro integrante, após as notícias de

agressões

 começarem a se popularizar na Grande Natal. A

Agência Pública

 teve acesso a mensagens trocadas no grupo administrado pelo secretário de gabinete do deputado da extrema direita. O caso foi registrado na 1ª Delegacia de Plantão da Polícia Civil.


A noite que não terminou


Henrique Neiva ainda estava em casa quando começou a ouvir um paredão automotivo reproduzindo: “Um caminho novo pra gente seguir. Agora é Flávio presidente”, parte da letra de um dos jingles do candidato à presidência pelo PL. Por volta das 17h, o universitário chegou à unidade de ensino, onde foi avisado que as aulas estavam sendo interrompidas e os estudantes, liberados, devido à aglomeração que se formava em frente à UFRN.


“Quando eu cheguei, já estava tendo violência, né? Eles já estavam xingando e instigando as pessoas a irem pra cima”, conta o estudante que disse ter acompanhado quando as ofensas passaram de verbais à físicas. “O que a gente tava fazendo era uma corrente humana, dizendo que daquele lado eles não passavam”, disse o estudante.


“Recua, fascista, recua”, gritavam alunos, como pode ser visto em vídeos divulgados nas redes sociais. Em outros registros, o deputado General Girão (PL), cercado por seguranças privados, aparece dizendo: “Avança, avança. Esse ambiente é meu também” e “muitos de vocês ficam na vadiagem vendendo drogas aqui dentro”, acusava.


Henrique conta que o portão do campus estava sendo fechado quando as agressões tiveram início. “Fui segurar o portão. E aí do outro lado a galera estava gritando, xingando e chamando para a violência. Quando eu saio com o meu celular para gravar quem é que estava fazendo isso eu levo um chute na perna. É nesse momento que eu vou atrás de quem me chutou e quando eu vou para cima sou agredido”, narrou o estudante que recebeu chutes e pontapés ao cair no chão, momento registrado em vídeos por colegas.


Após ser submetido por um exame de corpo de delito, Neiva foi para casa, mas não conseguiu dormir direito. “Eu estava sentindo dores e fiquei com uma angústia muito grande do que tinha acontecido, que eu tinha ido pra lá para ser agredido. Fiquei pensando que não vale de nada, né? Nada vai tirar as agressões que eu sofri”, conta. “É necessário ter responsabilização para que isso não volte a acontecer”, opina.


Estou me recuperando física e mentalmente, também temendo pela segurança, mas não tenho deixado esse medo me paralisar. Mesmo eu recebendo esses comentários de ódio nas minhas redes sociais, eu continuo seguindo a minha vida. […] Não acho que é o momento de parar. Eu acho que é na verdade um momento de intensificar, de a gente ocupar mais as ruas, de a gente disputar a consciência das pessoas, de a gente mostrar que não tem outra alternativa senão a luta política”


Henrique Neiva


estudante universitário.


Os lados da moeda


Em sua curta jornada política, Henrique Neiva já vivenciou lados opostos do espectro político e disse ter votado em Jair Bolsonaro em 2018, motivado pelo sentimento antipetista. Foi com a efervescência política de junho de 2013 que Neiva começou a se interessar por política. O jovem contou que começou a buscar na internet informações sobre o cenário político brasileiro, e foi quando teve contato com o pensamento liberal. Foi no MBL que Henrique começou sua trajetória na militância, e chegou a se candidatar a vereador de Natal pelo Novo, mas diz que o sentimento mudou durante o mandato de Bolsonaro.


“Eu vi que não era um governo que tava sendo feito para governar para todas as pessoas, era um governo feito de atacar as instituições públicas e aí essa desesperança começa e se amplifica em 2020”, avalia o jovem, que disse ter sentido na pandemia o divisor de …

author: webdev@democracynow.org (Democracy Now!)
title: "A Spark from the Cockroaches": Arundhati Roy on India's Youth Protests & Modi's Crackdown
content:
A court in India on Wednesday ordered the release of two leaders of the Cockroach Janta Party, the youth-led movement that has led historic waves of protests in India since the summer. Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das were detained amid massive protests last week after they scaled a barricade to enter a site popular for protest, unfurled the national flag and called for the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Kumar oversaw the deletion of 130 million names from the voter rolls in India since June of last year. Opposition parties say those impacted are primarily Muslims and other minorities less likely to support the

BJP

, the Hindu nationalist ruling party of Prime Minister Narendra Modi.


“You have a deep and wide — an ideologically wide — historical culture of resistance in India,” says acclaimed writer and activist Arundhati Roy. At the same time, the Modi government “has three things in its playbook: One is false-flag attacks, two is engineering communal riots, and the third is massive repression. And I don’t think we’ve seen its hand yet.”

title: Lettre ouverte de prisonniers du 17 octobre 2026
content:
Depuis des semaines, la répression contre le mouvement en cours s'intensifie. Au lendemain du 17 octobre, le Garde des sceaux Gérald Darmanin, foulant toute séparation des pouvoirs, enjoignait la magistrature à condamner le plus durement possible les manifestant interpellés et poursuivis. Nombre d'entre eux, dorment donc désormais en prison. Des prisonniers du 17 octobre sont parvenus à nous transmettre cette lettre ouverte, comme un aveux et un appel à continuer la lutte.


Nous vous écrivons depuis une prison d'Ile-de-France dont ne nous vous communiquerons pas le nom, ceci afin de nous protéger des risques de représailles et surtout des administrations judiciaires et pénitentiaires.


Nous sommes étudiants, lycéens, professeurs, chômeurs, restaurateurs, petits entrepreneurs, livreurs, gangsters, de tous les quartiers et de toutes les villes de la région, de Créteil, de Bobigny, de Belleville, de Montreuil, de Bagnolet, de Noisy-le-Sec, de Seine-et-Marne, de Seine-Saint-Denis et de Paris. Nous sommes de tous les âges, de toutes les couleurs de peau et de toutes les nationalités, nous sommes des Arabes, des Blancs, des Noirs, des Tziganes, des Turcs, des Allemands, des Français.


Nous avons été accusés à tort ou à raison d'avoir pillé, d'avois commis des violences contre les forces de l'ordre, de nous être attroupés illégalement, d'avoir dissimulé nos visages. Peu importe finalement nos situations ou ce qu'on pouvait nous reprocher, car les tribunaux se sont pliés aux ordres de la macronie pour nous envoyer tous en taule. Même si les prisons sont toutes plus insalubres et surpeuplées les unes que les autres, tant que ça rentre !


Cela nous rappelle à quel point ce que l'on nomme la Justice, n'est en rien une institution indépendante, d'autant moins lorsque l'État et la bourgeoise se sentent menacés.


En prison, nous avons le privilège de pouvoir nous abrutir toute la journée devant BFMTV, CNEWS et les chaînes des autres chiens de garde du régime. L'offensive idéologique sur ces plateaux télé vient soutenir la politique répressive de ceux qui pensent nous gouverner. Cette offensive est à la hauteur de la peur qui les traverse depuis samedi dernier. Il s'agissait d'un véritable avertissement révolutionnaire. Partout, ils essayent désormais de nous faire regretter, fléchir, de nous dissuader de revenir les samedis suivants. Ils taisent le soutien, la fierté et tous ces petits mots que nous avons pu lire et entendre depuis ces derniers jours du type « j'aurais aimé être là » ou bien encore « vous leur avez fait payer ». Ils veulent nous faire croire que notre violence est comparable aux milliers de vie broyées par le capitalisme au quotidien.


Si les serviteurs médiatiques du pouvoir ne parviennent pas à déterminer le « profil type » des insurgés, c'est que nous autres sommes le peuple qui s'est soulevé. Le peuple qui souffre et qui désormais se bat pour ne plus souffrir. Ils tentent de nous diviser, de nous catégoriser en manifestants, casseurs, pilleurs, racailles ou d'ultra-gauche. Mais ils n'ont pas compris que nous sommes tout cela à la fois ! Nous sommes unis par notre colère et notre désir de révolution. Une révolution qui nous redonne la possibilité de respirer et d'espérer, de partager et de mettre en commun. De nous permettre enfin de décider de la manière dont nous voulons vivre. Une révolution qui mette fin à cette humiliation qui dégueule de luxe.


Cette rage sociale nous a poussé dans la rue samedi dernier, c'est la même que l'on retrouve dans les couloirs et les cellules de la prison où nous sommes enfermés. Cette rage explique aussi le soutien et le respect des autres détenus pour les insurgés du 17 octobre. Nous n'accepterons pas non plus que nous soyons séparés entre d'un côté les prisonniers politiques et les prisonniers de droit commun car nous avons tous été poussés dans les prisons de ce régime par ce monde injuste.


Pour toutes ces raisons, nous vous le disons avec force, nous ne regrettons rien ! Rien si ce n'est de ne pas nous être suffisamment protégés contre la violence répressive qui allait s'abattre sur nous.


Nous appelons donc toutes celles et ceux qui sont dehors à continuer à tenir face à l'État et à retourner dans la rue chaque samedi, jusqu'à la chute de Macron et de tout son monde pourrissant.


Nous vous appelons à vous organiser entre chaque samedi, à vous vous rencontrer, à vous préparer et à prendre vos vies en main dès maintenant.


Nous vous appelons à soutenir tous les …

title: Après la débâcle policière, les tribunaux montrent les muscles. Récit des comparutions immédiates à Marseille après la manif du 17 octobre
content:
Le ministère de la Justice a demandé à ses agents de la dureté. Alors l'ambiance est à la punition collective, yeux fermés marteau à la main !


On parle de 100interpellations, dont 80%des majeurs. Beaucoup d'entre eux seront transféré au tribunal pour des comparutions immédiates. C'est une forme de justice expéditive, expliquée

ici


Plusieurs salles sont réservées au tribunal de Marseille rien que pour ça, de lundi à jeudi.


Le procureur général est là en personne, Nicolas Bessonne, il peut faire son show et déballer ses analyses politico-stratégiques… on l'entendra dire « Il est établi qu'il y a eu une action concertée entre deux types de populations de nature différentes. La catégorie black-bloc attaque des institutions avec pour objectif de fixer les CRS, tandis qu'au même moment arrive, de manière concertée, un autre type de population : des personnes sans papier et des jeunes des quartiers, dans le but de piller ». Le tribunal est décidément un monde clos, coupé de la société.


On va voir pendant ces 4jours d'audiences exceptionnelles de comparutions immédiates le théatre de la justice raciste, classiste, sexiste, moralisante et qui se voit comme dernier rampart républicain à la barbarie… des juges envoyer des gens en prison après 20minutes de pseudo débat contradictoire. Envoyer des gens en prison direct le jour même, après 48h de garde à vue, pour avoir été arrêté en possession d'objets volés samedi soir.


Et comme d'habitude les débats sont incompréhensibles pour les personnes jugées qui sont non francophone tellement aucune place n'est laissé à la possibilité d'une traduction . Les plaidoirie des avocat.e.s commis d'office font souvent mal aux oreilles tellement ils rabaissent leur client.es. Et bien sûr personne ne parle dans les micros donc même si les audienes sont sensées être publiques on entend rien, c'est caché.


On a aussi vu La métropole venir faire la victime et se porter partie civile dans chaque audience dans le but de demander de l'argent à chaque personne jugée, et déployer son discours du désastre et des millions d'euros de dégâts. On avait vu les mêmes pleurs de l'avocat de la métropole en 2023 après les révoltes suite à l'assassinat de Nahel : dire que la personne en possession d'une paire de chassure volé serait coupable complice des millions d'euros supposés de dégâts en ville…


Il y a beaucoup de similitudes avec 2023, des audiences où la justice se donne en spectacle et veut montrer à tout le monde sa force sa rigueur son intransigeance : on voit surtout des gens aller en prison pour des chaussures ou du maquillage : la justice au service de l'État en panique qui veut taper fort !


On connaît l'état des prisons surchargés. Mais les peines de prison sont la norme pendant ces audiences.


On voit des dossiers confus (le gars arrêté parce qu'il fait une vidéo des pillages, ou le gars qui court, etc.) où les flics ont fait n'importe quoi, taper dans le tas : y'a pas d'objets volés, y'a des témoignages de flic contradictoire, y'a pas de victime, donc jugement final : relaxe.


Mais c'est minime.


On voit quelques personnes demander le renvoi de l'audience le temps de préparer sa défense, donc commence un débat sur leur maintien en détention jusque cette date ou leur sortie et sous quelles conditions. Donc certaines sortent avec un contrôle judiciaire (pointage au commissariat, interdiction de manif ou de présence à Marseille, couvre feu individuel de 22h à 6h, etc) jusqu'a leur procès en décembre. Et certaines sont maintenues en détention, elles sont donc envoyées aux Baumettes en détention provisoire jusqu'à fin novembre/décembre.


Pour celleux qui accepte d'être jugées le jour meme on voit :


Une meuf arrêtée avec une paire de chaussure neuve et du maquillage prend 12mois de prison dont 6 avec sursis, est condamnée à payer 1000€ aux 2policiers qu'elles aurait insulté lors de son interpellation et en plus elle doit payer leur avocat qui vient porter plainte contre elle : 1000€ en plus.


Pour des histoires où y'a pas de vol, mais des délits liés au fait même qu'ils se sont fait interpellé.es par les flics. Des histoires de rebellion ou d'outrage : des peines de prison 6mois avec sursis simple et en plus des amendes de 500€ environ.


Pour des possession d'objets volés, du recel : on voit par exemple des peines de 6-10mois avec sursis pour des jouets ou des chaussures, du maquillage etc. Et en plus des fois des interdiction de manifester pendant 2 ans.
