title: Movimento 24 ottobre: la generazione Z rompe i divieti e si prende le piazze
content:
Italia-

Città blindate, quasi 5mila identificati, 371 fermati di cui 110 minorenni, 9 persone arrestate, tensioni e scontri in diverse piazze al termine di manifestazioni pacifiche molto partecipate.


da

Radio Onda d’Urto


La genZ scesa in piazza ieri in mezza Italia si è presa le strade nonostante divieti e militarizzazione dei territori.

 Non si sono verificati saccheggi e devastazioni ma i cortei sono stati comunque attaccati da uomini in divisa con idranti e lacrimogeni a Bologna, Torino, Firenze , Roma e Padova. A Bologna una persona è stata portata in ospedale in codice giallo. Diecimila in corteo a Milano che ha rotto il divieto di manifestare in una città blindata e presidiata da 1400 uomini in divisa. 

Prossimo appuntamento lo sciopero generazionale del 30 ottobre

.


Sulla composizione e le modalità di azione delle piazze di sabato 24 ottobre abbiamo raccolto alcune considerazioni:


Da Bologna Federico della nostra redazione emiliano-romagnola 


Da Torino Martina di Askatasuna 


Da Milano Luciano nostro collaboratore 


Francia-

Una marea di manifestanti ha invaso le città francesi, con cortei festosi, popolari e pacifici, ma esattamente come in Italia, nel tardo pomerioggio attaccati da polizia e gendarmeria con idranti e gas lacrimogeni. Ad attaccare i manifestanti nelle piazze in diverse citta’ si sono visti anche gruppi di estrema destra lasciati agire indisturbati. Secondo il sindacato Cgt, in piazza tra sindacati, studenti, gilet gialli c’erano 800mila persone in tutta la Francia, a Parigi 250mila. Mobilitati 70mila fra poliziotti, gendarmi e agenti dei servizi speciali. Il ministro dell’Interno parla complessivamente di circa mille fermi. Atto terzo il prossimo fine settimana , 30 31 ottobre e 1 novembre in concomitanza con un raduno nazionale dell’estrema destra a Parigi.


Albania-

Violenti scontri ieri a Tirana tra la polizia e i manifestanti durante l’ennesima giornata di protesta convocata dagli studenti. I manifestanti chiedono le dimissioni del premier Edi Rama. Gli agenti hanno caricato il corteo con gli idranti e i gas lacrimogeni, disperdendo la folla raggruppata inizialmente davanti al ministero dell’educazione e subito dopo di fronte al Palazzo di governo. Le forze dell’ordine a fatica sono riuscite a prendere il controllo del principale viale di Tirana con la folla dispersa tra le vie del centro della capitale, lasciando dietro cassonetti di immondizia dati alle fiamme. Ai manifestanti oggi si sono aggiunti gruppi ultras della capitale.


Portogallo-

A Lisbona e Porto il sabato di protesta contro il carovita e per il diritto alla casa si è concluso con lo sgombero dei manifestanti che hanno tentato di prolungare i cortei in nuovi presidi permanenti nel centro delle due città. Sabato pomeriggio migliaia di persone hanno partecipato alle manifestazioni nelle due principali città del Portogallo, a cui si sono uniti dei raduni più piccoli a Coimbra, Braga e Faro. In serata, gruppi di manifestanti hanno provato a occupare, come già avvenuto nei giorni scorsi, le piazze del Rossio, a Lisbona, e João I a Porto. Le autorità avevano avvisato che non sarebbero stati permessi nuovi accampamenti in centro; così, nelle prime ore di domenica, la polizia ha sgomberato le due piazze con la forza. Secondo l’ultimo comunicato emesso dalle forze di polizia, il bilancio provvisorio parla di una trentina di fermi per resistenza a pubblico ufficiale.


Spagna-

E’ di 128 persone arrestate, delle quali 73 minorenni, e 15 agenti delle forze dell’ordine feriti il bilancio degli episodi di disordini e tafferugli registrati nel tardo pomeriggio di ieri a Barcellona. Tale situazione si è sviluppata dopo che c’è stata una manifestazione di protesta non autorizzata partita dalla centralissima Plaza Catalunya, nata da iniziative sui social e che ha visto radunati diverse centinaia di giovani.


Germania-

 Per il 31 ottobre 2026 l’iniziativa “Gen Z steht auf“, ossia “la Gen Z si solleva”, ha convocato manifestazioni in numerose città tedesche, con rivendicazioni che si concentrano soprattutto sui temi dell’istruzione, della giustizia sociale, del carovita e del rifiuto della leva obbligatoria. Il movimento dichiara di ispirarsi alle proteste degli studenti francesi che, in questi giorni, sono state brutalmente represse, anche con l’uso di armi da guerra. Non in tutte le città sono ancora state annunciate ufficialmente mobilitazioni specifiche con appositi percorsi.

title: PJAK member remains forcibly disappeared following arrest by IRGC
content:
More than three months after Khaled Barzanji, a Sanandaj-born member of the Kurdistan Free Life Party (PJAK), was arrested by the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) Intelligence Organisation in the village of Uch Tappeh, Bukan, his fate and whereabouts remain unknown. Despite repeated enquiries by his family, security and judicial authorities have refused to acknowledge his detention.


The Kurdistan Human Rights Network (KHRN) has learned that on 10 July 2026, IRGC forces surrounded a garden house in the village of Uch Tappeh in Bukan and arrested Barzanji along with two other individuals who owned the property.


The identities of the two other detainees remain unknown, although one of them was reportedly released after some time.


Since his arrest, Barzanji has been denied access to a lawyer and all contact and visits with his family. Despite repeated visits and enquiries by his family to judicial authorities and security agencies in Bukan and Orumiyeh, the authorities have denied any knowledge of his arrest or whereabouts.


On 22 October 2026, PJAK issued a statement confirming the arrest of its member and stating that no information about his fate had been obtained.


According to information compiled by KHRN, since June 2025, at least six other Kurds – Mohsen Ghaderi, Sara Rashidi Kachalanlou, Arman Khaleghpanah, Zahra Pirdehghan, Parvin (Akhtar) Rasegh Ghizilbash and Sirwan Habibi – have been subjected to enforced disappearance following their arrests by the Ministry of Intelligence and the IRGC Intelligence Organisation in Baneh, Paveh, Saqqez, Orumiyeh and Kamyaran.


KHRN’s findings indicate that the arrests of these individuals have not been officially registered with the judicial authorities or Iran’s Prisons Organisation. By refusing to acknowledge their detention or disclose their whereabouts, security and judicial authorities have effectively denied responsibility for their fate.

author: Brian Hioe
title: Car Crash Plot on Comedian Shows Increasing Violence of China’s Transnational Repression
content:
FIVE MEN WERE indicted earlier this week over a plot to run down stand-up comic Huang Yi-hao, in retribution for a comedy show in which Huang mocked Chinese president Xi Jinping.

The five men slammed into Huang with a car, injuring his pelvis, after being ordered to hurt Huang enough to hospitalize him. Subsequently, they acted as though the incident was an accident and assisted Huang with an insurance claim. They then forwarded the picture of the insurance documentation to their handler, a Chinese man referred to in media reporting as K., who refused to pay them the full 450,000 NT promised because Huang was not injured sufficiently.

News of the plot to attack Huang follows suit from the indictment of two men over a May attack on a comedy club where Huang was performing, during which the comedy club had a mixture of feces and paint thrown at its entrance. A 35-year-old man surnamed Kuo was reportedly paid 50,000 NT by a 33-year-old man surnamed Liu to carry out the attack. It is unclear whether the two were acting at China’s behest. The incident was not widely known before the indictment.

Since news of the plot broke, there have been calls to strengthen national security laws to deal with Chinese threats. In particular, the attack on the comedy club and the plot to run down Huang highlight China’s growing transnational repression within Taiwan itself.

It can be seen that there are several recurring tactics used by China when it comes to transnational repression. For example, attacks with feces and paint have occurred on several occasions. In 2020, Hong Kong pro-democracy singer Denise Ho and bookstore owner and publisher Lam Wing-kee, one of the Causeway Bay booksellers, were splashed with red paint by attackers. Some of these attackers were linked to Taiwanese pro-China organized crime groups such as the Bamboo Union gang.

Likewise, the same year, Aegis, a restaurant that assisted Hongkongers seeking refuge in Taiwan, was splashed with chicken feces by men who were paid by a Chinese national to carry out the act.

Earlier this year, a gym owned by a pro-democracy Hongkonger who had previously stood as an electoral candidate was splashed with red paint by two individuals who arrived from Hong Kong. The two individuals departed back to Hong Kong before they could be caught.

Nor would this be the only case in which China has apparently flown individuals to Taiwan to carry out actions that they try to quickly flee from in short order. This was also the case when political commentator Akio Yaita was attacked in a Taichung hotel where Yaita was giving a speech, with the individual in question having been flown in for the attack from Hong Kong, and subsequently attempting to flee abroad. The use of Taiwanese and Hongkongers, or Chinese nationals with Hong Kong passports, for such attacks, however, allows for plausible deniability that avoids being directly traced back to the Chinese government.

In other cases, China simply hires Taiwanese individuals to carry out such attacks, as occurred with Huang. But the attack on Akio Yaita, as well as the attempted ramming of Huang Yi-hao, shows that the level of violence of China’s transnational repression directed at critics may be increasing. Indeed, one notes that in 2025, news broke of a plot by the Chinese military attaché in Prague to ram a vehicle into the motorcade of Hsiao Bi-khim during a visit to the city, during a period when Hsiao was the vice president-elect. The plot could have been construed as either an act of intimidation or even an assassination attempt.

Presumably, the aim with such acts as the car crash plot against Huang would be to depict the Chinese government’s reach as inescapable and penetrating deep into Taiwan, meting out retribution for even simply making fun of the Chinese leader. Still, it is possible that such actions ultimately end up pushing Taiwanese further away from China, in showing the dangers of unification, rather than cowing Taiwanese into submission.

author: Shan Kenshin Ecaldre
title: ‘Release tortured Mangyan organizer’
content:
“He needs immediate medical attention for injuries and trauma allegedly sustained during his detention.”

Indigenous Mangyan farmer and organizer Miguel Magbata was reportedly beaten and tortured while in military custody after his arrest in Bulalacao, Oriental Mindoro, on October 14, prompting human rights groups to call for his immediate release and to hold accountable those responsible.

According to Karapatan Southern Tagalog, Magbata was arrested after a reported armed encounter between the Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) and alleged New People’s Army (NPA) members in Sitio Badyang, Barangay San Roque in Bulalacao. He was reportedly subjected to physical abuse and interrogation by the 1st Infantry Battalion (IB) under the command of the 203rd Infantry Brigade (IBde).

After days of uncertainty over his whereabouts, reports emerged that Magbata was transferred to Roxas Municipal Police Station. Defend Mindoro said that he needs immediate medical attention for injuries and trauma allegedly sustained during his detention.

The group also raised concerns over a Facebook post from 203rd Infantry Brigade of Philippine Army about Magbata’s children and family, published without their consent, which it said could compromise their safety.

Despite his reported transfer to police custody, the military reportedly sought to retain custody of Magbata. Defend Mindoro demanded his immediate release and called for accountability from the 203rd IBde led by Brig. Gen. Melencio Ragudo, and the 1st IB, under Lt. Col. Edwin Mirador.

Defend Mindoro said that Magbata’s case shows a pattern of harassment and abuses against Indigenous Peoples, farmers, and community organizers in Mindoro where those asserting their rights are often accused of links to the communist armed movement.

The group cited the killings of Indigenous and peasant individuals Jay-el Maligday, Hulyo Agtay, and Juan Sumilhig which it attributed to military abuses. It also stressed the case of Dolores Solangon, an elderly Mangyan-Iraya woman who reportedly endured illegal arrest and nine hours of torture at the hands of elements from the 76th IB.

Maligday, a young Hanunuo-Mangyan, was allegedly killed by soldiers of the 4th IB while sleeping in his home. The same unit was accused of beating another Hanunuo-Mangyan, Minggo, in Mansalay early this year.

For Defend Mindoro, these abuses are inseparable from the land disputes and economic hardships confronting Indigenous communities and farmers.

In Bulalacao, the group said that large-scale mining and renewable energy projects threaten ancestral lands and local livelihoods. These include developments associated with CleanTech Global Renewables and Singapore-based The Blue Circle which is reportedly planning an offshore wind project involving 100 turbines across a proposed 40,050-hectare area.

Meanwhile, drought has exacerbated the farmers’ hardship. In 2024, an estimated 864 hectares of farmland in Bulalacao were damaged, resulting in P87 million (US$1.37 million) in agricultural losses and affecting around 1,000 registered farmers, according to Defend Mindoro. With another severe El Niño episode looming, communities face renewed threats of crop failure and water shortage.

The group criticized the government for prioritizing counterinsurgency operations over addressing rural poverty, landlessness, and the climate crisis. It said that militarization further endangers communities already struggling to protect their livelihoods and ancestral territories.

Defend Mindoro demanded an independent investigation into the allegations of torture and illegal detention. Torture is prohibited under international law and civilians must be protected from violence and cruel treatment in situations of armed conflict.

The group held the 203rd IBde and the Marcos Jr. administration accountable for the alleged violations, calling for an end to military harassment of Indigenous Peoples and farmers.

For Defend Mindoro, Magbata’s case underscores the dangers faced by community organizers defending the rights of rural communities. “No allegation of insurgency can justify torture or the denial of due process,” the group wrote in a statement. (DAA)

title: José Ángel Martins Mendoza, Peque, preso social anarquista y enfermo de cáncer, en huelga de hambre desde el 9 de octubre porque los servicios médicos de la cárcel de Teixeiro se niegan a administrarle la medicación prescrita por el oncólogo
content:
visto en

+ carta de Peque


José Ángel Martins Mendoza, Peque, actualmente en la cárcel de Teixeiro (A Coruña), alcanza hoy los 12

Nuestro compañero, preso de  larga duración, siempre dispuesto a la lucha por la dignidad de las personas encarceladas, ha participado, entre otros intentos colectivos, en la campaña Cárcel=Tortura y en todo lo que se hizo dentro de 2015 a 2021 por las 14 reivindicaciones. En abril de 2023, cuando estaba en la cárcel de Campos del Río (Murcia),  fue operado de cáncer de garganta en el Hospital de la Arrixaca, cuyo departamento de oncología le prescribió un tratamiento, renovado al ser  trasladado a la cárcel de Villena (Alicante II) por el oncólogo del hospital de referencia. Pero, cuando llegó hace más de seis meses a la cárcel de Teixeiro, le fue retirado primero el tratamiento y después drásticamente reducido. Peque se encontraba mal, con fuertes dolores en el cuello, hasta tal punto que tuvo que abandonar sus estudios universitarios recién iniciados porque así es imposible estudiar. El compañero pedía una y otra vez su tratamiento,  y las médicas de la cárcel gallega, de siniestra fama, se lo negaban una vez y otra. Sólo recientemente, consiguió cita con un especialista en oncología del hospital Juan Canalejo de A Coruña, que le prescribió un tratamiento parecido al que tenía antes de llegar a Teixeiro y una serie de pruebas diagnósticas.


En las primeras pruebas, se ha descubierto que se le ha reavivado el cáncer del que había sido operado y ahora está a la espera de otras exploraciones para un diagnóstico más concreto. Aún así, el tratamiento se lo siguen negando, y de malas maneras. Pero ahora ya no se trata sólo de enfrentarse a unas caprichosas restricciones en su medicación. Peque se ve a merced de la arbitrariedad de unos servicios médico-carcelarios inoperantes, casi inexistentes, cuya autoridad y poder de decisión prevalecen, por lo visto, por encima de los de los especialistas del servicio nacional de salud, que debería ser, según una ley que el mismo Estado que la dictó desobedece, el que se hiciera cargo integralmente del cuidado de la salud de lxs presxs. Cárcel de Teixeiro, septiembre de 2026

Soy JAMM, Peque, y me comunico desde la cárcel de Teixeiro, procedente de la cárcel de Villena, para informaros del atentado que sobre mi persona están cometiendo las médicas fascistas de esta cárcel. La subdirectora médica de esta cárcel, Julia, me conoce desde hace treinta y cinco años, cuando llegué a la cárcel de Monterroxo en 1991.


Habiéndome salido un cáncer en la prisión de Murcia, fui operado en esa comunidad en abril de 2023, sacándome las amígdalas y medio tiroides más trece tumores que me estaban subiendo por la cabeza. title: Terminal Kadıköy’ün reklam ekranı hack’lendi: “Bu bina kent suçudur”
content:
İstanbul'un Kadıköy Söğütlüçeşme’deki Terminal Kadıköy’de bulunan bir reklam ekranı, “BU BİNA KENT SUÇUDUR” yazısıyla hack’lendi. Kent hakkı savunucuları, deprem toplanma alanı ve yeşil alanın alışveriş merkezine (AVM) dönüştürülmesine tepki göstererek kentlerin her alanının kâr maksimizasyonuna göre planlandığını vurguladı.


ETHA’daki habere göre, Söğütlüçeşme Tren İstasyonu’nun viyadük altındaki alanında kurulan Terminal Kadıköy, Nisan 2025’ten bu yana işletiliyor. Açıldığı günden bu yana onlarca dükkânın faaliyet gösterdiği alan, yeni bir tüketim merkezine dönüştü.


Kent hakkı savunucuları, ekoloji örgütleri ve Kadıköylüler, projeye karşı yıllardır itirazlarını sürdürüyor. Haydarpaşa Dayanışması, projeyi “soylulaştırma merkezi” olarak nitelendirerek “Kamusal alanlar ticarileşiyor, bu bir kent suçudur” açıklamasını yapmıştı.


Savunucular, AVM’ye dönüştürülen alanın geçmişte sokakta yaşayan hayvanların kent sakinleri tarafından beslendiği geniş bir yeşil alan olduğunu belirtiyor. Bölgenin yıllarca “izbe bir alan, güvensiz bir yer” olarak tanımlandığını aktaran kent hakkı savunucuları, bu söylemle projeye toplumsal rıza oluşturulmaya çalışıldığını ifade ediyor.


500’den fazla ağaç kesildi


Proje kapsamında bölgede 500’den fazla ağaç kesildi. Kent hakkı savunucuları, Söğütlüçeşme’deki alanın deprem toplanma alanı niteliği taşıdığını ve projenin bu işlevi fiilen ortadan kaldırdığını belirtiyor.


Savunucular, “Hem bir deprem toplanma alanı hem kentsel bir yeşil alanın tümü, bir avuç AVM’ye kurban edildi” diyerek kamusal alanın sermayeye peşkeş çekilmesine tepki göstermişti.


Çevre, Şehircilik ve İklim Değişikliği Bakanlığı ise proje için “ÇED Gerekli Değildir” kararı vermişti.


Terminal Kadıköy sonrası Kadıköy’de artan yoğunluk ve trafik baskısı


14 Nisan 2026

author: Cooper Quintin
title: The Vulnerability Apocalypse and Why We Should Fund Open Source
content:
If you use the internet at all, you may have noticed that a large percentage of sites suddenly went down earlier this week

—

and all your nerdiest friends were talking about "The Vulnerability Apocalypse” and this thing called PHP that

powers nearly 70% of the websites on the internet

. You may find yourself wondering: what is PHP, what just happened, what is the vulnerability apocalypse, and what do I need to do? 

 


To find out what you can personally do read the

first blog post

 in this series!

 


What Is PHP? 

 


PHP is a programming language used mainly to create interactive websites. Facebook, Wordpress, Wikipedia, Etsy, and other major sites all use or were originally built on PHP. It is a long-established mainstay of web development. But because it is open-source, maintenance of these critical systems depends on a small number of volunteers working on this in their free time. The disaster scenario that happened this past week is the perfect example of why we need more money and people supporting open-source projects. Corporations should be contributing both.

 


What Is the Vulnerability Apocalypse? 

 


Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs) are the way that security professionals file reports about vulnerabilities in software. The

National Vulnerability Database

 (NVD), run by NIST, is the official national database of CVEs. In other words, CVE reports managed by NIST are the closest thing we have to a canonical database of security vulnerabilities in software. The NVD currently has around 400,000 CVEs that have been filed and accepted since 1988. In just the month of October, 13,000 new CVEs have been submitted. This means that 3% of critical software security bugs that have ever been officially logged were found in the last month alone. And it's likely that by the end of the year over a quarter of the software vulnerabilities that have ever been found will be from 2026.

 


 

Computer vulnerabilities reported are rising exponentially. Source: CVE Tracker


This research is being driven almost entirely by the cybersecurity capabilities of major AI models from companies like Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google. Historically it has been popularly assumed by cybersecurity experts that finding unknown (zero-day) exploits in any specific project and turning them into exploits was expensive. The knowledge to discover them was not widespread, and it was a hard task even for those initiated into the arcane ways of vulnerability hunting. Google even dedicated

an entire team to it

. 

 


But now thanks to major AI models, vulnerabilities are cheap, and anyone of moderate technical skill with a few dollars and access to a frontier AI model can find vulnerabilities in a few minutes. For example, recent vulnerabilities in PHP were found with a prompt to an AI model that literally said "

find bad vulnerabilities in PHP

."

 


What Happened This Week?

 


In 2024, a potentially severe vulnerability in PHP was

discovered during an external security audit

. PHP’s maintainers couldn’t agree on a solution, but more importantly, they couldn’t find a way to exploit the vulnerability. Because it didn’t seem like an active threat, they ended up deprioritizing a fix in favor of working on more urgent security issues. Then, in August 2026, security researchers working with the latest models from OpenAI and Anthropic independently discovered the vulnerability again, and another one

—

and now, with a way to exploit them.

 


We now know that the vulnerabilities 

were so severe that they would have allowed even moderately inventive hackers to take over any website that uses PHP and then steal customer data, launch further malware attacks, spy on users, take websites offline, or launch a massive denial of service attack.

[

1

]

 


Because of the severity of these vulnerabilities, several of the involved researchers got together with the makers of PHP to patch the vulnerabilities and disclose them in a coordinated manner. The idea was that hopefully everyone would get a chance to quietly release and then apply fixes for the vulnerabilities before the whole world found out about it.

 


But news already started to leak on October 20th. There was a

post on a widely read forum

 “Hacker News” and other posts elsewhere. One of the researchers accidentally published a video early. Companies reported seeing active exploitation of the vulnerabilities going back as far as October 17th. On October 21st, six …

author: Blanca Missé
title: As More Unions Oppose ICE and Israel, the Right Is Cracking Down
content:
The right is trying to gain access to labor unions’ minutes, membership lists, and Zoom chats.

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

On September 22, The Free Press attacked the California Faculty Association (CFA), which represents about 29,000 faculty, librarians, counselors, and coaches across the California State University (CSU) system. Drawing on private discussions about a proposed Jewish caucus, including communications from a union Zoom meeting, the article accused CFA of antisemitism. How those communications reached the publication remains unclear. Two days later, the Jewish Journal amplified those allegations, urging Gov. Gavin Newsom to consider them as he weighed California Assembly Bill (AB) 2551, CFA-sponsored legislation challenging campus protest restrictions imposed after the 2024 Palestine solidarity encampments. Less than a week after The Free Press story was published, Newsom vetoed the bill.

Pro-Israel and Jewish advocacy organizations had already campaigned against AB 2551 before the union’s internal deliberations were targeted, arguing that greater scrutiny would weaken rules needed to protect Jewish students from harassment and intimidation. Newsom’s veto does not prove coordination, but the campaign portraying CFA as hostile to Jewish students had become entangled with the union’s fight against campus protest restrictions.

The CSU’s systemwide policy prohibits encampments, overnight demonstrations, and unauthorized structures. The CSU Academic Senate immediately condemned the restrictions as undermining academic freedom when it was instituted in 2024, while CFA warned that vague definitions of disruption threatened constitutionally protected speech, assembly, protest, and future strike activity. A major 2026 ACLU-Amnesty study, investigating 80 campuses over two years, documented sweeping repression of Palestine solidarity protests. As the report found, universities “have imposed sweeping restrictions on student speech, initiated disciplinary actions against students, and imposed severe punishments, including expulsions and suspensions.” The ACLU has insisted that even legitimate time, place, and manner restrictions “must leave ample room for students to express themselves.”

The controversy reaches beyond CFA and CSU. Unions and rank-and-file organizations committed to Palestine solidarity have been forced to relitigate, again and again, whether anti-Zionism and solidarity with Palestinians constitute antisemitism — and whether such organizing should be systematically policed, investigated, or surveilled. At stake is a more fundamental right of the exploited: Can workers democratically connect economic struggles with Palestine solidarity, resistance to anti-immigrant and anti-Black racism, and the defense of civil liberties without exposing their organizing and deliberations to external pressure or repression?

We already have a word for the use of legal process as a political weapon: lawfare. You do not necessarily have to win. Investigation, expense, compelled disclosure, and possible sanctions can exact their own price.

Call its media counterpart pressfare: leaked material, selective or doctored quotations, and public identification can turn people into political targets and invite pressure on employers, universities, or government agencies.

The leaked CFA meeting should not be adjudicated through fragments selected for publication, especially when CFA’s statewide record contradicts the portrayal of a union indifferent to antisemitism. During the 2024 encampments, CFA opposed antisemitism and Islamophobia “in all forms” while supporting the encampments. Amid a 2025 federal antisemitism investigation, it stated that “as CFA members, we are united against antisemitism; it has no place in our communities,” while defending members’ academic freedom. CFA’s Palestine, Arab, and Muslim Caucus likewise defines its mission as confronting racism “in all its manifestations,” explicitly including antisemitism. The Free Press story — a clear example of pressfare — sought to overwrite this legacy with weaponized accusations, undermining the trust that workers place in the sanctity of their union spaces and processes.

Antisemitism demands to be taken seriously — which is why accusations of anti-Jewish discrimination should not be instrumentalized. Kenneth Stern, director of the Bard Center for the Study of Hate, has …

author: Franco Giandana Gigena
title: Openness in AI development: a path to long-term independence
content:
As concerns grow over

deepening dependencies

 on a handful of Big Tech companies and the

outsized influence

 of the U.S. and China, UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Türk used his speech during July’s inaugural

Global Dialogue on AI Governance

 to call on humans to

“take back our agency”

 over AI. But what does agency over AI really mean? What policies and practices can allow people to shape AI in ways that respect, rather than undermine,

human rights

? 


This blog post unpacks concrete initiatives that show how openness in AI development can increase people’s agency over AI and advance the development of public interest technology. At the same time, we reflect on how openness is not the same thing as mere access, and how short-term pragmatism can pave the way toward long-term independence.


Why is AI development so concentrated? 


Last year, the UN formally established an

Independent International Scientific Panel on AI

, intended to “advance scientific understanding and ensure that international deliberations are informed by the best available evidence.” The panel’s

preliminary report

, published this past July, contained a stark warning about the concentration of AI capabilities in a small number of firms and countries, which it says “could enable authoritarian capture and undermine democratic accountability.” But how has this concentration of power come about? 


One of the main reasons is that

building

 a complete, multilayered “

AI stack

” is both an astronomical investment and a complex technical challenge. This technological stack comprises:


The hardware layer, which provides the computing power that AI demands, mainly via advanced chips known as graphics processing units, or GPUs; 


The data layer, used for training and post-training; 


The model layer, which consists of the models themselves, such as GPT-4 or Claude, and the tools to service them; 


And finally, the application layer, which is the interface that users interact with. 


Currently, the U.S. and China are the only two countries realistically capable of building a fully national version of the entire stack, where they build and control all necessary infrastructure within their borders. However, even then, they would continue to depend on other countries for some elements, whether that’s for sourcing the chips or the critical minerals used in the hardware layer. Meanwhile, most other countries’ reliance on U.S. or Chinese companies creates critical safety and accessibility vulnerabilities. 


However, all is not lost for other countries and regions that want to build agency across the stack. There are several parts in the AI stack — notably

the data, model, and application layers

 — where greater openness and geopolitical collaboration could help foster collective agency. In this way, we can work towards what Martin Tisné, founder and CEO of the Collaborative for AI in the Public Interest, calls a “

global, open, resilient, non-aligned stack

” adaptable to local needs. 


How does openness support greater agency over AI? 


When considering how to gain more agency over AI, it’s worth looking at the free and open source software (FOSS) movement; a longstanding and major driver pushing for increased agency over technology, from the software running the internet, to the tools millions of people rely on every day, such as the Firefox internet browser. Although definitions of FOSS vary from

source

 to

source

, the essential principle means ensuring that anyone can access a given technology’s source code, study how it works, modify it, and share modified or unmodified copies with others.


The Open Source Initiative (

OSI

) has already applied this in the context of AI, with their

open source AI definition (OSAID)

 according to which an open source AI system is one that enables four key freedoms:


Use

 the system for any purpose and without having to ask for permission.


Study

 how the system works and understand how its results were created.


Modify

 the system for any purpose, including to change its output.


Share

 the system for others to use with or without modifications, for any purpose.


None of the offerings from major AI tool providers, such as OpenAI or Anthropic, currently enable any of these freedoms. Until now, the overwhelming preference in AI development has been for closed systems, accessible only through online interfaces or

application programming interfaces (APIs)

. This …

author: EDRi
title: EDRi celebrates Global Encryption Day 2026
content:
On 21 October 2026, we celebrate the Global Encryption Day! Part of EDRi’s KISS campaign, we celebrate this day with our partners, online, in Brussels and in different European capitals.

On 21 October 2026, we celebrate the Global Encryption Day! Part of EDRi’s KISS campaign, we celebrate this day with our partners, online, in Brussels and in different European capitals.

A recent survey conducted by CDT Europe shows that across several European countries (France, Sweden, Poland, and Ireland), people consistently oppose measures that would compromise encrypted communication platforms. In France, 92% of respondents agree they have the right to have private conversations online, while the figure goes to 94% in Poland, 88% in Sweden and 93% in Ireland.

Encryption is great for protecting the way our messages travel on the internet. Through “end to end encryption”, anyone can make sure that the content of an online conversation can not be intruded upon, not even the server that facilitates the transmission.

This year, we have coordinated several campaign actions to celebrate encryption.

1. Raising awareness in European Capitals through LED “Encryption trucks” driving around Paris, Berlin and Dublin and a metro poster campaign in Prague.

To visibilise people’s support for encryption, we partnered with the Irish Council for Civil Liberties, Féministes contre le cyberharcèlement and Digitale Gesellschaft who are in the streets today, talking to people and press about the “Encryption trucks” and the importance of encryption. In Prague, our partner Iure has been supporting the Metro Posters campaign for the past weeks.

2. Working across silos with groups promoting gender justice, and sex workers rights in the digitalised society.

In the case of women defenders, land defenders from indigenous groups, racial justice activists, sex workers defenders and defenders of migrants, unsafe communications can have life or death consequences. For human rights defenders, secure and trusted communication is often a matter of physical safety and democratic organising.

For 21 October 2026, we have partnered with European Sex Workers Alliance and Féministes contre le cyberharcèlement (France) to raise awareness on the importance of safe and secure communications for sex workers as well as womens’ rights. Check ESWA’s Instagram video and

3. Visibilising the testimonials of activists from Privacy Camp and across Europe

During 14th edition of Privacy Camp gathering that happened recently in Brussels, EDRi asked a few participants why encryption mattered for them. The people we interviewed came from a variety of causes: those fighting for a healthy European civic space, and for digital rights in Netherlands, Portugal and Germany. More, we asked EDRi’s over 35.000 supporters why encryption mattered to them too. Their answers inspired us to post some of them, and we will post them during the next couple of weeks. Check the content on EDRi’s social media channels – on Instagram , Mastodon or LinkedIn.

4. Connecting with global experts to advocate for encryption

During the Global Encryption Summit taking place at 4pm CET, EDRi’s expert Chloé Berthélémy will join a panel in an event organised by Internet Society, the Center for Democracy and Technology, Mozilla, and Global Partners Digital.

Europol and law enforcement are pushing to legalise hacking methods that weaken encryption. These methods rely on ordering a service provider (those who develop or maintain the software, computer system, network, or electronic device) to build vulnerabilities in their systems. With this demand, state actors want to enable the police or intelligence agencies to have access to our data and break encryption. Client-side scanning (scanning of all content such as text,images, videos, etc. on a device or shared in a communication channel) is a method proposed under the EU CSA Regulation. Key escrows or “key recovery”, involves placing decryption keys in a “vault” managed by a trusted authority or group of trusted authorities, who can break them out when access to the encrypted data is needed. Finally, ghost proposals refer to the modification of the encryption system to enable a third-party listener to be silently added to encrypted conversations.

In democratic societies, communication systems are vital for our lives and connections with others. Safe and secure communications and devices allow us to work, socialise, organise, express ourselves, and connect …

author: Fundi Skweyiya-Gushu
title: Africa’s Cybersecurity Gap Is Not a Treaty Problem. It Is a Readiness Problem
content:
Africa’s digital economy is expanding faster than its ability to protect it.

INTERPOL’s African Cyberthreat Assessment Report 2026

, drawing on information from 36 countries, found that artificial intelligence was involved in 55 per cent of reported cybercrimes across the continent. Reported losses rose from $192 million in 2024 to $484 million, while 72 per cent of surveyed countries reported scam centres operating within their borders.


The figures expose a growing vulnerability. Africa’s digital transformation is creating economic opportunities but also expanding the terrain on which criminals operate. The question is whether African institutions can respond collectively when attacks cross borders, exploit financial systems and use AI to target victims at scale.


Morocco Cybersecurity Week

, held in Rabat from 12 to 14 October 2026, placed regional cooperation firmly on the agenda. The emphasis was appropriate. Yet Africa’s challenge extends beyond convening officials and announcing strategies. It is making institutions cooperate effectively under pressure.


Africa does not lack legal frameworks.

The African Union Convention on Cyber Security and Personal Data Protection

, known as the

Malabo Convention,

 entered into force in June 2023 after years of delays. Morocco, meanwhile acceded to the

Council of Europe’s Budapest Convention on Cybercrime

 in 2018 and signed its

Second Additional Protocol on electronic evidence

 in 2022.


These instruments provide important foundations for criminal investigations, data protection and cross-border cooperation. But legal commitments cannot, on their own, ensure that investigators obtain evidence quickly, financial institutions exchange actionable intelligence or police services coordinate an effective response.


Cybercrime crosses institutional boundaries. A fraudulent transaction may involve a mobile-money provider, a bank, a telecommunications company, a cryptocurrency exchange and digital infrastructure spread across several jurisdictions. Each holds part of the evidence. When requests are delayed or responsibilities are unclear, investigators lose valuable time while criminals move money and erase their tracks. African institutions must therefore measure cooperation by what they can accomplish together, not by the number of agreements they endorse.


There is evidence that coordinated action works.

INTERPOL’s Operation Serengeti 2.0

, conducted between June and August 2025, brought together law-enforcement authorities from 18 African countries and the United Kingdom. It resulted in 1,209 arrests, the dismantling of 11,432 malicious infrastructures and the recovery of $97.4 million. Private-sector partners contributed intelligence and technical expertise.


The lesson is not that treaties are unnecessary. Investigations still require lawful powers, admissible evidence and safeguards. Rather, Serengeti demonstrates the value of shared objectives, established channels and institutions equipped to act on intelligence together.


This is where Africa should look beyond calls by some of its leaders for a continental equivalent of

NATO’s Article 5

. On 19 May 2025, Rwandan President Paul Kagame made these remarks in his keynote address at the inaugural

International Security Conference on Africa (ISCA)

, held at the Kigali Convention Centre. Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni has also raised related questions at the

African Defence Chiefs Conference on Military Operations

. While these calls reflect growing interest in collective African security, NATO’s experience offers a more specific lesson for cybersecurity governance.

NATO recognises cyberspace as an operational domain

, and significant cyberattacks may, in certain circumstances, constitute an armed attack. However, invoking collective defence is not automatic: each case is assessed individually by the North Atlantic Council.


For African governments confronting cyber-enabled fraud, ransomware and attacks on public services, the more immediate lesson is not collective retaliation. It is collective preparedness.


Consider

NATO’s annual Locked Shields exercise

, organised by its

Cooperative Cyber Defence Centre of Excellence

. The 2026 exercise brought together approximately 4,000 participants from 41 countries to defend simulated digital systems against complex attacks. Participants tested technical responses while confronting the coordination challenges that emerge during a crisis. The …

author: Dulce Amor Rodriguez
title: Social media ban may exclude children instead of protecting them, advocates warn
content:
Child rights advocates have warned that a proposed social media ban could restrict children’s access to information, education, expression, and participation without addressing the perpetrators and platforms responsible for online abuse.


The warning followed the Senate’s approval of Senate Bill No. 2424, or the proposed Safe Media Access and Responsible Technology for Kids in Digital Spaces (SMART KIDS) Act, on third and final reading on October 8.


The Senate approved the measure by a vote of 16-1, with no abstentions, advancing a proposal sponsored by Sen. Robinhood Padilla that would restrict minors’ access to digital services classified as high-risk.


Salinlahi Alliance for Children’s Concerns argued that the government must protect children from online exploitation, grooming, bullying, and other forms of digital harm without treating their access to digital spaces as the problem.


“Banning children from social media does not make the internet safe. It impedes children’s right to participation while the perpetrators remain,” said Teacher Elle Buntag, Salinlahi secretary general.


The group warned that restricting children’s access would not, by itself, establish whether platforms would respond more effectively to abuse or whether authorities would investigate and prosecute offenders more consistently.


Instead, Salinlahi called on the government to strengthen investigations into online sexual abuse and exploitation, require platforms to detect and remove abusive content, improve reporting and rescue mechanisms, and provide survivors with psychosocial and legal support.


“If the government’s answer to online abuse is simply to remove children from the platform, then we are asking children to bear the burden of a problem created by perpetrators and enabled by weak systems,” Buntag said.


The group maintained that children have rights to information, expression, education, participation, and connection in digital spaces, and urged the government to protect these rights while making online environments safer.


“The state must not confuse restricting children’s access with protecting children. Protection means making the digital spaces they inhabit safe and holding those who exploit them accountable,” Salinlahi said.


Different approaches


The debate over the Senate measure centers partly on whether an under-18 restriction offers a proportionate response to online harm or whether lawmakers should adopt age-specific safeguards.


Sen. Risa Hontiveros, the sole senator who voted against the measure, argued for a more targeted approach that would allow older adolescents to use social media with adequate safety measures.


Hontiveros had proposed restricting access for children under 13 while allowing those aged 13 to 18 to use social media if platforms provided adequate safeguards.


The Child Rights Network Philippines’ explainer questioned the basis for setting the minimum age at 18, and urged lawmakers to examine the evidence behind a blanket restriction before limiting children’s digital rights.


Sen. Win Gatchalian, a co-author and co-sponsor of the Senate measure, argued that aligning the age threshold with the legal definition of a child under existing laws would make enforcement more consistent and easier for authorities, according to the network’s explainer.


Padilla, meanwhile, said lawmakers could amend the measure after assessing its effects, and cited other countries’ experiences with restrictions and subsequent policy reviews, the explainer said.


The Child Rights Network challenged the idea that ease of enforcement should determine the age threshold, arguing that lawmakers must also consider the measure’s effects on children’s rights and daily lives.


The debate therefore goes beyond whether authorities can enforce an age restriction and asks whether the restriction would protect children effectively without imposing unnecessary limits on their participation.


Beyond entertainment


Child rights advocates said children use social media for more than entertainment, including research, learning, creative work, communication, and maintaining relationships.


The Child Rights Network noted that children also use digital platforms to connect with friends and peers and to communicate with parents working overseas.


Salinlahi argued that the government must account for these uses when designing online safety policies, rather than assuming that removing children from platforms would resolve the …

title: Mısır da 'Suudi bataklığına' sürükleniyor
content:
Dışişleri Bakanı Hakan Fidan, Mısır Dışişleri Bakanı Bedir Abdulati (solda) ve Suudi Arabistan Dışişleri Bakanı Faysal bin Ferhan 23 Ekim'de İstanbul'da bir araya gelmişlerdi. (Fotoğraf: AA)

Mısır Cumhurbaşkanı Abdulfettah Sisi’nin Ensarullah’a (Husiler) karşı Suudi Arabistan’a her türlü askeri destek vermeye hazır olduklarını açıklaması, haftanın öne çıkan gündemlerinden biri oldu. Kahire, şimdiye kadar Yemen’deki çatışmalardan uzak durmaya ve diplomatik çözüm arayışlarında ara bulucu rolü üstlenmeye öncelik veriyordu. Suudi Arabistan’ın güvenliğini korumak amacıyla askeri destek sağlama yönündeki açıklama ise Mısır’ın bölgesel çatışma karşısındaki tutumunda önemli bir değişime işaret ediyor.

Sisi’nin bu çıkışıyla birlikte Mısır basınında Suudi Arabistan’la tarihsel bağlara, iki ülkenin bölgesel ağırlığına ve Arap dünyasının güvenliği açısından taşıdıkları öneme yapılan vurgular öne çıkıyor. Bu yayınlarda Kahire ile Riyad arasındaki ilişkiler, geçici siyasi çıkarların ötesinde, Arap ulusal güvenliğinin temel dayanaklarından biri olarak sunuluyor. Suudi Arabistan’ın geçmişte Mısır’a sağladığı destek de bu anlatının önemli bir parçasını oluşturuyor.

1973 Arap-İsrail Savaşı sırasında Suudi Arabistan’ın İsrail’i destekleyen ülkelere karşı petrol ambargosu uygulaması ve Mısır’a mali yardım sağlaması, iki ülke arasındaki tarihsel dayanışmanın örnekleri arasında gösteriliyor. Arap Baharı döneminde Kral Abdullah yönetiminin Sisi yönetimine verdiği destek de bu tarihsel bağın devamlılığına kanıt olarak sunuluyor. Macid Münir’in kaleme aldığı ve Mısır ile Suudi Arabistan’ı “doğunun kalesi” olarak nitelendiren yazı da bu söylemin güncel bir örneği. Yazıda iki ülke, bölgesel dengeleri koruyan, Arap ulusal güvenliğini savunan ve daha geniş çaplı bir çatışmayı önleyebilecek iki temel güç olarak tanımlanıyor. Böylece Suudi Arabistan’a destek verilmesi, yalnızca güncel güvenlik kaygılarıyla değil, ortak kader, Arap dayanışması ve bölgesel sorumluluk söylemiyle de meşrulaştırılıyor.

Mısır’ın içinde bulunduğu ekonomik kriz ve Suudi Arabistan’a olan vadesi gelen yüklü borçları tutum değişikliğine gitmesinde önemli unsurlar olarak değerlendiriliyor. Riyad’ın Mısır Merkez Bankasındaki mevduatları ve Kahire’ye sağladığı mali destek, iki ülke arasındaki ilişkinin güvenlik boyutunun ötesine uzandığını gösteriyor. Ancak Mısır’ın tarihsel Yemen tecrübesi, doğrudan bir savaşa katılma konusunda önemli bir çekince oluşturuyor.

1962’de Yemen’e cumhuriyetçileri desteklemek amacıyla asker gönderen Mısır, yıllarca süren çatışmalarda ağır kayıplar verdi. Bazı analistler bu durumu “Yemen sendromu” olarak nitelendiriyor. Aynı dönemde Suudi Arabistan monarşi yanlılarını destekliyordu; dolayısıyla iki ülke Yemen’de karşıt saflarda yer alıyordu. Bugün ise aynı ülkenin güvenliğini savunma gerekçesiyle ortak bir çizgide buluşuyorlar.

Mısır yönetimi bu nedenle askeri desteğin savunma amaçlı olacağı ve Yemen’e yönelik bir saldırıya dönüşmeyeceği mesajını öne çıkarıyor. Mısır Ulusal Savunma Konseyi, Suudi Arabistan’ın güvenliğini, istikrarını, toprak bütünlüğünü ve kutsal mekanlarını korumak için gerekli ve mümkün olan her türlü desteğin sağlanması yönünde karar aldı. Mısır basınında yer alan haberlere göre, olası katkının Suudi Arabistan’a savunma güçleri ve Kızıldeniz’e deniz unsurları gönderilmesiyle sınırlı tutulması seçenekler arasında. Ancak bu çerçevenin fiilen nasıl uygulanacağı ve hangi askeri görevleri kapsayacağı henüz açıklığa kavuşmuş değil. Öte yandan Sisi’nin aynı konuşmada 2030’da yapılacak olan başkanlık seçimlerinde yeniden aday olmayacağını açıklaması da dikkat çekti. Ancak 2017’de üçüncü kez aday olmayacağını söylemesine rağmen 2019’da anayasa değişikliğine giderek 2030’a kadar görevde kalmasının önünü açtı. Üstelik 2030’a daha üç yılı aşkın bir süre var. Bu nedenle kimse bunu ciddiye almadı. Ancak beklenmedik bir şekilde yapılan bu açıklamanın Suudi Arabistan’a askeri destek konusuyla ilişkili olduğuna işaret ediliyor.

Mısır parlamentosundaki tartışmalar da bu belirsizliği yansıtıyor. Anayasa Partisi, Kerame Partisi, Sosyalist Halk İttifakı Partisi ve Yaşam ve Özgürlük Partisi gibi muhalif partileri bünyesinde barındıran Demokratik Sivil Hareket, Mısır ordusunun bölgesel bir savaşa, taraflardan birinin lehine çatışmaya katılmasına karşı çıktı. Mısır Sosyal Demokrat Partisi ise Suudi Arabistan’ın güvenliğine destek verilmesine karşı çıkmamakla birlikte, askeri görevin amaçları, süresi, maliyeti ve askerlerin güvenliğine ilişkin …

title: Roma: alcune riflessioni sul corteo di ieri contro carovita ed economia di guerra
content:
Ripubblichiamo il comunicato di

controsapienza e coordinamento studentesco autonomo romano


Ieri mattina il clima a Roma era surreale per giorni non avevano fatto altro che militarizzare sempre di pro la città e cercare di dissuadere le persone dallo scendere in piazza.


Non ci sono riusciti e per tutta la giornata migliaia di giovani hanno attraversato le piazze e le vie chiedendo un futuro migliore. Ieri in piazza non si é scesi per una chiamata di un partito, sindacato o associazione, nella piazza di ieri non vi erano striscioni né bandiere. Ma semplicemente giovani e lavoratrici che si sono rotte il cazzo del carovita e dell’economia di guerra. Si sono rotte il cazzo di vedere le scuole cadere a pezzi di vedere il loro studio all’università per gli sporchi fini delle aziende belliche che hanno le mani sporche di sangue del popolo palestinese, del prezzo della benzina. di salari da fame, affitti alle stelle e di sentire sempre la solita retorica che indica come problema l’immigrato.


Il corteo di ieri é stato vivo, fluido e agile in modo da evitare tutti i vari blocchi che lo stato di polizia ha messo nelle nostre città, evitando più volte la celere centinaia di giovani sono entrate nel Colosseo e poi dopo aver costretto la polizia ad indietreggiare e bloccare la stazione hanno chiesto a gran voce di arrivare a Montecitorio e verso i palazzi del potere. Il corteo dopo numerose ore e deviazioni e stato fermata a largo santa Susanna dalle forze dell’ordine con massiccio utilizzo di manganelli e idrante.


Noi siamo il futuro del paese e non ci fermeremo, siamo giovani e non vogliamo pagare sulla nostra pelle le scelte di politici che non ci rappresentano. Vogliamo essere ascoltate per davvero, ma ogni volta che proviamo a farci sentire la risposta é sempre la repressione.


Ieri é stato solo l’inizio ora sta noi lottare per cambiare questo presente infame in in un futuro migliore.


NOI VOGLIAMO TUTTO. A NOI CI SPETTA TUTTO, NOI CI PRENDEREMO TUTTO.


CI VEDIAMO NELLE SCUOLE, NELLE UNIVERSITA E VENERDI E SABATO


DI NUOVO IN PIAZZA

title: İsrail, iki askerin öldürüldüğü saldırının ardından El Halil’de kuşatma ve yıkım başlattı
content:
İsrail ordusu, işgal altındaki Batı Şeria’nın El Halil kentinde iki İsrail askerinin öldürüldüğü silahlı saldırının ardından geniş çaplı bir operasyon başlattı.


Dün (23 Ekim) El Halil yakınlarındaki geçici bir kontrol noktasına ateş açan iki Filistinli, iki İsrail askerini öldürmüş ve üçünü de yaralamıştı. Ateş açan Filistinliler yaklaşık 20 dakika süren çatışmada öldürülmüştü.


Saldırının ardından İsrail Başbakanı Binyamin Netanyahu, El Halil ile komşu Halhul’un kuşatma altına alınmasını istedi. İsrail güçleri kentin giriş ve çıkışlarını kapatırken bazı mahallelerde yaşayan Filistinlilerin evlerinden çıkarıldığı bildirildi.


İsrail ordusu operasyonun “saldırganların faaliyet gösterdiği bölgeyle sınırlı” olduğunu ve birkaç gün sürmesinin beklendiğini açıkladı. Ordu ayrıca bölgede silah ve “terör altyapısı” arandığını ve onlarca kişinin sorgulandığını duyurdu.


Netanyahu: Daha büyük operasyon yolda


The Guardian’ın aktardığına göre Netanyahu, Batı Şeria’da 1967’den bu yana gerçekleştirilecek en kapsamlı İsrail askeri operasyonu için planların hazırlandığını söyledi.


Operasyon için tarih açıklamayan Netanyahu, El Halil’de tahliyelerin ve yıkımların süreceğini, Batı Şeria’daki İsrail yerleşimlerinin de genişletileceğini belirtti.


İsrail Savunma Bakanı Israel Katz da saldırganların geldiği mahallelerin boşaltılacağını açıkladı.


Katz, El Halil’de uygulanacak yöntemi Gazze ve Cenin Mülteci Kampı’ndaki İsrail operasyonlarıyla karşılaştırarak, “Cenin Mülteci Kampı modeli El Halil’e geliyor” dedi.


“Bugün teröristlerin çıktığı El Halil’deki her aşiret mahallesi sakinlerinden boşaltılacak. Gazze’de olduğu gibi, Lübnan’da olduğu gibi.” İfadelerini kullandı.


Smotrich yıkım görüntülerini paylaştı


İsrail Maliye Bakanı Bezalel Smotrich ise saldırının ardından bir Filistinliye ait evin buldozerle yıkıldığı sırada çekilen görüntülerini sosyal medya hesabından paylaştı.


Smotrich, ruhsatsız olduğu belirtilen yapının yıkılmasının amacını “caydırıcılık yaratmak ve bedel ödetmek” sözleriyle açıkladı.


Yıkılan evin sahipleriyle saldırganlar arasında herhangi bir bağlantı bulunduğuna ilişkin açıklama yapılmadı.


İsrail Yüksek Mahkemesi, yıkımlar başladıktan kısa süre sonra işlemlerin geçici olarak durdurulmasına karar verdi. İnsan hakları avukatı Mohammed Dahleh, bölgedeki iki fabrika sahibinin adına yaptığı acil başvuruda yıkımların uluslararası hukuktaki kolektif cezalandırma yasağına ve İsrail idare hukukuna aykırı olduğunu savundu.


Dahleh, yaşananları şöyle değerlendirdi:


“Bugün gördüğümüz şey, Gazze’de kullanılan hukuka aykırı uygulamaların Batı Şeria’nın kalbinde tekrarlanması girişimiydi. Gazze’de ve Batı Şeria’daki mülteci kamplarında yaptıkları gibi tüm bölgeleri ortadan kaldırmak istiyorlar.”


İsrailli insan hakları avukatı Michael Sfard da Smotrich’in açıklamasının yıkımların “kolektif cezalandırma” amacı taşıdığına ilişkin doğrudan bir kabul olduğunu söyledi.


Filistinlilerin hareketi kısıtlandı

author: webdev@democracynow.org (Democracy Now!)
title: Nobel Peace Laureate Navi Pillay on ICC, Gaza, Rape as War Crime, Her South African Roots & Mandela
content:
We speak with the acclaimed South African human rights lawyer and international jurist Navi Pillay, who was awarded this year’s Nobel Peace Prize. Pillay has been the United Nations high commissioner for human rights and a judge at both the International Criminal Court and at an international tribunal investigating the 1994 genocide in Rwanda. Most recently, she led the U.N. Independent International Commission of Inquiry that concluded Israel had committed genocide in Gaza. Hours after Pillay was announced as winner of the Nobel Prize, the United States imposed sweeping new sanctions against the International Criminal Court.


“It’s extremely shocking to me, totally unacceptable, that the United States administration can today impose sanctions against the International Criminal Court,” says Pillay, speaking to

Democracy Now!

 from The Hague.


Navi Pillay is now 85 years old. She was born into an Indian Tamil family in apartheid South Africa in 1941. The first woman to start a law practice in Natal, South Africa, in 1967, Pillay began her legal career defending anti-apartheid activists including Nelson Mandela, exposing torture, and helping establish key rights for prisoners on Robben Island. Mandela, as president, later appointed Pillay to the High Court of South Africa, making her the first woman of color on that bench.

author: Ash Sarkar
title: Does Wes Streeting Want Us Ready for War?
content:
Like many long-eyelashed men before him, Andy Burnham is sending mixed-messages. On the one hand, the prime ninister is keen to differentiate himself from his predecessor. Where Keir Starmer carried himself like a doctor who could only break bad news, Burnham is keen to stress that there is a role for the state in the improvement of people’s lives (even if it’s just capital punishment for playing reels without earbuds in). 


But how does the PM’s sunny disposition square with this Cabinet urging us to stock up for the apocalypse?


Wes Streeting – defence secretary, and creature hatched under a jar by the Labour Right – has urged Britons to

prepare for crisis

. The public has been advised to stock up with three days worth of water, food, non-mains light sources and stuff to keep warm, in case of disruption to supply chains caused by cyber-attacks, terrorism, or extreme weather events. You can find the government’s ‘Be Ready Checklist’

here

, and books you can burn in lieu of central heating

here

.


How big of a deal is this? Ordinarily, governments tend to prioritise the prevention of panic-buying. Readers may remember the toilet paper craze in the early days of the Covid pandemic, in which shoppers cleared shelves of loo roll because a rumour had gone round alleging that the Chinese had switched Andrex-production to the manufacturing of paper masks. It doesn’t take huge swings in consumer behaviour to put a dent in just-in-time supply chains – and the sight of depleted aisles can send people scurrying to buy even more. If ministers are advising people to stock up, it’s a sign that they sincerely think something scary is on the horizon.


The government’s resilience programme wasn’t a brainchild of Andy Burnham. It got going during

Keir Starmer’s time in office.

 Some critics say that Burnham hasn’t actually made

enough

 noise about it, pointing to

the lack of a big, shiny rollout

. But regardless of its prominence in No. 10’s grid, the instructions to the public to stock up in case of crisis is dominating the headlines today – and it’s perhaps meaningful that Wes Streeting’s public comments about the issue were made at the opening of a

new weapons manufacturing site

 in Shropshire.


As FT journalist Gideon Rachman noted on Newsnight last night, the language used by leaders in the West has been markedly hawkish on the prospects of World War III. Keir Starmer warned of a Nato war with Russia

as soon as 2030

; Mark Rutte, head of Nato, has said that we have to be prepared for wars of the scale that

our grandparents fought in

 (that’s the Second World War, not

the 2005 Ikea riots

). Rachman has warned that we could be

sleepwalking into World War III

 – I can’t help but wonder if some of our leaders are tapdancing there.


Threats to food supply – not least due to the

‘Godzilla’ El Niño

 superpowering extreme weather events – are real. But it might be the case that the government’s urging of preparedness is both a prudent message to the public in the face of an increasingly chaotic global order, and part of an effort to normalise the prospect of the UK being pulled into a brutal, meat-grinding war. It’s worth minding some of the lessons of the 20th Century: you can only manufacture so many weapons before they get used.

author: Amadou Diarra
title: Wood for War: How Wagner Was Paid in Central African Forest
content:
On 9 February 2021, as government troops and Russian mercenaries pushed rebels back from Bangui, the Central African Republic (CAR) signed Decree No. 21.044. It gave a young company called Bois Rouge a forestry permit covering 186,596 hectares in the south-western Lobaye region –

roughly 1,866 km² of tropical forest, an area larger than Greater London

.


Bois Rouge had never logged a tree. What it had, according to the

US Treasury

, was a patron: the concession was granted in exchange for services the Wagner Group provided to the CAR, at about the same time Wagner fighters and government forces were recapturing territory from the rebels.


Pieced together from sanctions files, customs data and transparency reports, the story shows how Wagner turned battlefield gains into commodities – and why timber proved a poor currency for a sanctioned militia.


A Russian Company with a Central African Face


Flag of the Central African Republic


Bois Rouge SARLU was

registered in Bangui in March 2019

. On paper it was a local firm with a Central African boss.

By October 2019

, at a forestry forum in Shanghai, Bois Rouge was listed under ‘Russia’, represented by Russians Artem Tolmachov and ‘Mike’ Vdovin.


A

UK parliamentary inquiry into the Wagner network

 later named Tolmachov as Bois Rouge’s commercial director. The research group All Eyes on Wagner

found he was also paid

 by two other companies tied to Wagner founder Yevgeny Prigozhin: Service K, which also financed the diamond firm Diamville, and Ferrum Mining, active in Madagascar. The pattern is familiar: a local shell in front, Russian managers behind.


The paperwork moved fast. The

CAR’s 2021 report to the Extractive Industries Transparency Initiative (EITI)

 and a

forestry sector review

 record the permit, PEA 193, with 137,585 exploitable hectares and a management plan approved on 28 April 2021 – less than three months after the decree. The terms were generous: the newcomer received a moratorium on concession rent and export tax, which researchers consider unlawful and which cost the state and communities revenue.


The company built its sawmill in Boda, a town

government forces and Wagner had cleared of rebels

 shortly before the permit was issued. This sets the case apart from ordinary illegal logging. The wood was not smuggled out of a lawless forest. It was licensed by the state, as payment for war.


From Boda to Douala


The export route, as reconstructed by the Global Initiative Against Transnational Organized Crime (GI-TOC), ran from Boda to the ‘Kassaï’ military base in Bangui, then by road through Cameroon to the port of Douala. A GI-TOC photograph from 7 June 2023 shows a loaded company truck at Kassaï. That logs were staged at a military base says much about who ran the business.


The Treasury lists the species exported: azobé, iroko, mukulungu, tali and, above all, sapele. Supplies flowed the other way through Broker Expert, a St Petersburg firm long used by Prigozhin, which made dozens of deliveries for Bois Rouge and, according to the Treasury, also moved the network’s money. Trade data showed

hundreds of imports

 of Russian machinery and logging equipment.


Most timber went to Turkey, the UAE and China, but some reached Europe.

Earthsight found

 that in 2022 the Danish firm WoodGroup ApS, a subsidiary of London-based Woodbois, took six shipments – 465 m³ of sapele worth an estimated €3.4 million at retail. One shipment was recorded as going to France’s Tropica-Bois, whose manager

told Earthsight

 the company had never bought the wood – a discrepancy, not proof of complicity.


New Names, Same Wood


After All Eyes on Wagner began publishing in 2022, Bois Rouge became Wood International Group (WIG) and

hired a new Central African director and a new Russian commercial director

. It did not help. In 2023,

CBS News filmed

 timber convoys heading from a Wagner-linked base to Cameroon and obtained about 100 WIG export documents whose details matched those of Bois Rouge.


OFAC, the Treasury’s sanctions office,

designated the company in September 2023

. In March 2024 the Treasury detailed its Wagner ties and sanctioned Broker Expert, after a joint probe with

Homeland Security Investigations

. Britain followed on 13 June 2024 (

UK sanctions list

; notices in the

Isle of Man

 and

Guernsey

). In Douala, WIG cargo was already being held up in June 2023.


GI-TOC counts 839 m³ exported in 2022 and a peak of 5,810 m³ …

author: Unknown
title: Elisée Reclus - The Vivisection of China
content:
Author

: Elisée Reclus

Title

: The Vivisection of China

Date

: 1898

Notes

: From the September 1898 issue of The Atlantic

Source

: Retrieved on October 22, 2026 from an archived copy of https://www.theatlantic.com/magazine/archive/1898/09/the-vivisection-of-china/636369/


 THE great events which are creating such an excitement in the West Indies over the last shreds of the ancient colonial empire of Spain will undoubtedly have consequences of extreme importance, and become, in the fullest sense of the term, a part of history. But, however intense their interest, and however marked the change which they are certain to occasion in the equilibrium of the world, they remain altogether inferior in real significance to the revolutions which are taking place in the Far East.


 War of some sort between America and Spain on the subject of Cuba had long been unavoidable. No less than a century ago, — at the time when France lost her plantations in San Domingo, and the republic of Hayti was born, — it was easy to foresee the rupture of the ties which had bound to the Spain of Cortez and Pizarro the insular fragments of the great hemisphere appropriated by Pope Alexander VI. The various colonies were sure to break away, one by one, from their metropolitan stepmother, set up for themselves, and live their own life. Cuba and Porto Rico, sucked into the whirlpool of war, are but accomplishing their “manifest destiny,” and fulfilling the prophecies repeatedly uttered by the historians of the last generation but one.


 The progress of events in the eastern portion of the Asian continent had by no means been so fully anticipated. One might certainly have ventured to predict that there, also, populations long crushed by civil and military oppression would one day lay claim to the rights of free men; but it could never have been foreseen under what amazingly dramatic conditions the claim would be asserted. Our ancestors, at the beginning of the nineteenth century, would never have harbored, in their wildest dreams, the fantastic notion that Japan, the empire of the Rising Sun, would spontaneously transform itself into a “European power;” European, at least, if not in language, history, and traditions, in the complete recasting of its administration, institutions, customs, and theories, in its devotion to science, and in its entire and unreserved acceptance of a policy based on observation and experience.


 This is the great event of the century, — one which casts into the shade all the other occurrences of an epoch which has nevertheless been rich in memorable events. And it will be no solitary

avatar;

 there are unmistakable signs that other transformations of the same character are about to take place in the vast empire of China, and in all those countries where inhabitants of different race, yellow, red, or black, are brought into close contact with the men of our own Aryano - Greco - Latin civilization. So vanishes that oft-repeated assertion of the ethnologists, that

race

 is a final and irreducible fact, and that no possible progress in the perception of scientific or moral truths can ever prevail against it. It is from this point of view that the recent history of the Far East presents phenomena to which it behooves us to devote our most serious attention.


 There are those, of course, who tell us that all these events are illusory; that the prodigious changes which have taken place in the Japanese world are a lying phantasmagoria and a vain show; that the national mind and character have undergone no real modification; and that the Japanese are sure to escape, sooner or later, from the sphere of European attraction. We hear them compared to savages, who, having learned in the schools of London or Paris the customs of civilization, make haste, as soon as they get back to their forests and savannas, to cast aside their conventional garments, and array themselves in the toggery consecrated by ancestral instinct and hereditary custom.


 Such assertions appear to us to rest on a complete misconception of indisputable facts. The Japanese have most certainly entered into that realm of civilization on which Bacon and Darwin have set their seal; for if imperial caprice and the spread of bourgeois fashions have power to alter the external aspect of a nation, such influences can have but little effect on its underlying moral sense, its religious beliefs, its educational theories, and the essential principle of its …

title: HORROR AS FLEEING HUNTED STAG COLLIDES WITH CAR CARRYING WOMAN AND CHILD
content:
On the 12

th

 of October the Quantock Staghounds met in West Bagborough, an area which falls within the constituency of Liberal Democrats MP Rachel Gilmour. Rachel has recently spoken publicly about her support for “trail” hunting, presenting what is a grim and violent reality as something that reads like a Disney fairytale.


MP Rachel Gilmour at last year’s BHSA “trail” hunting day, reported in the West Somerset Free Press.


Although stag hunts do not profess to “trail” hunt, like their fox hunting counterparts, they too manipulate the current law, exploiting loopholes to ensure the continuation of barbarism that brings terror to the countryside.


Rachel’s comments come at a time when sickening reports of hunting in the area are piling up, and you would think someone who has previously worked as Head of Strategy at the Environment Agency, would have a greater understanding of the countryside and the views of those that live there.


12th of October 2026


North Dorset Hunt Sabs and Mendip Hunt Sabs were joined by Holford Against Hunting as they sabbed the Quantock Staghounds.

Reports and video footage

 from the day detail how a hunted stag crossed the path of sabs and was subsequently seen to safety, thanks to them calling the hounds off.


More stags were chased throughout the day, with one seeking refuge on land owned by the League Against Cruel Sports. Reports also detail how two pairs of hounds were out at the same time; only two hounds are permitted to be used under the relevant legal exemptions within the Hunting Act.


However, since the reports were published there has been a disturbing update.


A stag crosses the path of sabs as he desperately tries to escape the Quantock Staghounds.

© North Dorset Hunt Sabs


At 4:30pm, two members of the public were travelling along the A39 between Nether Stowey and Holford when they came across the hunt. As we continue to see, rabid hunt supporters will line roads, making as much noise as possible to prevent stags from crossing as they seek safety. This incident was no different, except that what was described as a “gigantic stag” ran across the road and collided with a vehicle.


A witness described how the terrified stag “

was flipped over the top of the car. Its leg kicked out smashing the rear nearside window. The Stag landed heavily on the verge.”


The driver of the vehicle was a young woman with a small child on board, and thankfully, neither of them sustained any injuries, but both were badly shaken up. The hunt, showing absolutely no concern or regard for the members of the public who had been involved in or witnessed this horrific incident, fled the scene as police were called.


The witness went on to say that, despite looking for the stag, they couldn’t see him. Sabs have since reported that it is believed the stag did get away and was not killed by the hunt. However, after being hit by the car, there is no way of knowing what injuries he sustained or whether or not he ultimately survived this horrifying ordeal.


Quantock Staghounds causing chaos and terror in an area of “outstanding natural beauty.”

© North Dorset Hunt Sabs


Excuses, excuses


Stag hunts often try to use the excuse of dispatching an injured or sick deer to justify their barbaric actions. However, on this occasion, when there was clearly an injured stag, albeit as a result of their actions, they were quick to flee the scene. 


In her recent defence of “trail” hunting, Rachel Gilmour has claimed that hunt meets offer “

companionship to retirees and widowers who might otherwise face isolation and loneliness.”

 She also added that hunting “

forms part of a long and richly woven rural social fabric that binds farms, villages and families together through shared work, ritual, and memories.”


Her comments are a far cry from the realities of hunting. Many people living within these communities are not only opposed to it but are also put in grave danger every time these hunts go out.


It’s not just stag hunting taking place under Rachel’s nose


As well as stag hunts operating in Rachel’s constituency, the Tiverton Foxhounds’ kennels are also located within it.

report

 from the day details how “

one fox after another”

 was chased as they kept watch from the ground and used their drone.
