title: Lies the Fur Industry Tells!
content:
Mink and fox killers and their apologists often say the most ridiculous things to try and mitigate their losses after raids like the two we have seen in the last couple of months, in which 3000 or more captive mink were liberated from horrific captivity. Sample absurdities spouted as fact include:

Lie #1: Many or most of the escaped animals were run over and killed by cars.

– The absurdity of this statement is that before liberation, death was 100% certain. Every animal on the farm was bred to die by the end of November. While it is true a small number may be hit by cars after being released, most will not, and if nothing else they have been given a chance at freedom. In reality, fox and mink farms are located in rural areas with little traffic, the animals are quick and solitary animals, and it beggars belief to imagine them aggregating in the road waiting to be run over by the rare passing vehicle.

– Mink are in fact only a few generations removed from their wild cousins and have not yet had their wild instincts bred out. The “Mink Rehabilitation Project” led by convicted ALF liberator Rod Coronado proved this decades ago. Mink legally purchased from a fur farm were released into the wild and shown through observation to retain natural survival instincts and thrive in the wild after a lifetime in a cage. Studies with radio-collared mink demonstrate clearly the animals are capable of surviving in the wild. No, they won’t starve or freeze to death or die from dehydration. Most areas where mink are imprisoned are actually native habitat for American mink.

Lie #3: Most of the mink are recaptured

– Mink normally travel several miles a day. Most mink have dispersed into the surrounding fields before the liberation is even complete. A few may be recaptured, but only a handful at most. Its absurd to imagine hundreds of wild animals being recaptured by lunkhead farmers running around looking for them. Our hearts go out to those few recaptured who were given a shot at life and now have only suffering ahead.

– Captive, now free and wild fox and mink have no desire to be anywhere near humans and their “livestock” or pets. There may be some minimal impact on the local ecosystems temporarily while the animals disperse and learn their way around, but no habitats are decimated or overrun or rendered free of other small animals. And no, the animals do not kill wantonly and more than they need to survive, and they certainly don’t attack human bystanders, as some apologists have had the audacity to suggest.

Liberationists break the law in adherence to a higher law – one which states animals are not commodities, not objects, but sentient creatures with a right to live. They will fight for the lives of these animals “as if they were our own.”

The Animal Liberation Front and other anonymous activists utilize economic sabotage in addition to the direct liberation of animals from conditions of abuse and imprisonment to halt needless animal suffering. By making it more expensive to trade in the lives of innocent, sentient beings, they maintain the atrocities against our brothers and sisters are likely to occur in smaller numbers; their goal is to abolish the exploitation, imprisonment, torture and killing of all innocent, non-human animals.

Join the ALF – Historically, those wishing to participate in direct action have either acted alone or gotten together with others they could trust of like mind and just started doing actions. ALF cells of 1 or more persons operate independently, and typically are begun locally by like-minded individuals who decide to take action against animal abusers. To begin learning about direct action, start here and follow the links where they may take you. Only you can decide what action to take, when to get started, and how much longer the animals must wait for liberation.

The number of fur farms in America has dwindled from more than 300 in the 1990s to less than 100 today, as the fur industry continues its steady decline into oblivion. A listing of all known fur farms in North America, is available here: https://finalnail.com/

author: Sylvie Bunz
title: Nach Aufdeckungen: Rumäniens grausamste Hundetötungsstation schließt
content:
Update vom 21. Oktober 2026


PETA und seine Partnerorganisation sind schockiert über die behördliche Entscheidung, die Wiedereröffnung der Tierheime VetMedan und Daeni zu genehmigen. Seit Monaten kämpfen unsere NGO-Partner vor Ort gemeinsam mit PETA und anderen Tierschützenden sowie Organisationen mit aller Kraft dafür, dass diese Einrichtungen dauerhaft geschlossen bleiben.


Gemeinsam mit unseren Partnern prüfen wir nun erneut, ob es juristische Möglichkeiten gibt, gegen diese Entscheidungen vorzugehen und die Umsetzung der Beschlüsse auszusetzen. Solange mit Hunden erhebliche finanzielle Gewinne erzielt werden, stoßen Tierschutzbemühungen immer wieder auf massive Widerstände und es wird deutlich, wie stark das System ist, das an dem Leid der Hunde viel Geld verdient.


Update vom 22. Juni 2026


PETAs Partner im Einsatz gegen Rumäniens Hundetötungsstationen: Uzunu von Aspa Ivets für immer geschlossen


Nach Jahren voller Leid, Gewalt und systematischer Tötungen wurde das von einem Privatunternehmen geführte Tierheim Uzunu im Juni 2026 dauerhaft geschlossen. Die Entscheidung markiert einen Wendepunkt – für die Tiere, für die Tierschutzbewegung und für alle Menschen, die sich unermüdlich gegen diese Grausamkeiten eingesetzt haben. PETAs Partner in Rumänien, der Verein Eduxanima, hat sich zusammen mit weiteren lokalen und internationalen Vereinen dafür seit Monaten intensiv eingesetzt.


Das Tierheim Uzunu im Kreis Giurgiu war über Jahre hinweg ein Ort des Schreckens: Hunde wurden auf den Straßen eingefangen, in der Tötungsstation unter widrigsten Bedingungen eingesperrt und grausam getötet. Die jüngsten Pathologieberichte bestätigen, was Tierschützer:innen seit Langem vermutet haben: Viele der Tiere starben durch Vergasung – ein qualvoller Tod.


Hintergrund: Aufdeckungen über massives Tierleid


Erst als die Polizei des Kreises Prahova im März 2026 eingriff, kam Bewegung in den Fall. Die Ermittlungen führten zur Entdeckung von über 105 Hundekadavern, die trotz eines Tötungsverbots im Kühlcontainer des Lagers aufbewahrt worden waren. Die anschließenden Untersuchungen der toten Hunde belegten eindeutig, dass die Tiere an schwerer Methämoglobinämie und Hypoxie starben – ein klarer Hinweis auf Vergasung.


Auf Grundlage dieser Ergebnisse ordnete die Veterinärbehörde schließlich die endgültige Schließung der Einrichtung an.


Das derzeitige massive Tierschutzproblem ist, dass an diesem Ort weiterhin rund 240 Hunde vor sich hin vegetieren und kaum versorgt werden. Nur zwei Mitarbeiter kümmern sich um die Hunde, die an diesem Ort an Krankheiten leiden, sich gegenseitig verletzten und sterben. Es gibt weder medizinische Hilfe noch Unterstützung für die Vierbeiner. Unser Partner vor Ort setzt sich für die Hunde ein und fordert von den zuständigen Behörden, dass diese dringend und sofort die Verantwortung übernehmen müssen. Die Behörden und die Polizei sind nach der offiziellen Schließung für die Hunde verantwortlich.


Tierfreundliche und nachhaltige Lösungen sind erforderlich


Einrichtungen wie Uzunu existieren, weil Gemeinden weiterhin Verträge mit kriminellen Firmen abschließen, die Hunde einfangen und töten – finanziert mit öffentlichen Geldern, ohne nachhaltige Wirkung. Die einzige wirksame Lösung gegen Überpopulation bleibt: Kastration, Aufklärung und Bildung. Seit vielen Jahren hat unser Partner ein entsprechendes Konzept, welches immer wieder Gemeinden und Behörden vorgelegt wird und mit dem Rumänien innerhalb von zehn Jahren – statistisch berechnet – nahezu keine heimatlosen Hunde mehr hätte.


Dieses Konzept fußt auf ethischen Maßnahmen und weist geringere Ausgaben auf. Es ist an der Zeit, dass dieses Konzept Beachtung findet und das „System Hund“ sich endlich zum Positiven verändert. Die Schließung von Uzunu zeigt, dass Veränderung möglich ist, wenn Behörden handeln und die Öffentlichkeit hinschaut.


Hundetötungsstation Rumänien: So arbeitet PETA weiter


Nachdem wir von PETA Deutschland uns mit einem nachdrucksvollen Brief an die zuständigen Politiker, die Polizei und die oberste Veterinärbehörde gewandt haben, ist klar: Der Fall ist noch nicht abgeschlossen. Wir werten aktuell die Antworten mit allen Informationen aus, um weiter in den Austausch mit den Behörden zu gehen. Wir erhöhen den Druck und bleiben weiter an dem Fall Uzunu dran und kämpfen für die verbleibenden Hunde und deren Versorgung.

Aktionsaufrufe

“Para lxs políticxs, la justicia y quienes comercializan con la vida de lxs animales hay diferencias entre que un animal sea asesinadx dentro de un matadero para vender su cuerpo y generar el capital o que mueran por inanición en las granjas, eso es pérdida del capital invertido.

Para nosotrxs la vida de cada individuo vale, así que tenemos una sola oportunidad y no la vamos a perder esperando que la justicia decida.

Tampoco la vamos a desaprovechar pidiendo clemencia y que sus asesinos nos entreguen una vida.


Y ahí estamos a plena luz del día a la vista de algunxs curiosxs cortando el plástico para darles libertad, esa que se les nego apenas nacieron. Solo nos cuidamos entre nosotrxs para que ellxs sean libres, porque solo nos tienen a nosotrxs de su lado para romper la jaula”

author: Benji
title: Töten im Takt – Die grausamste Maschine bei Tönnies
content:
Töten im Takt – Die grausamste Maschine bei Tönnies

Tiere leiden vor dem Schlachten Höllenqualen bei CO₂-Betäubung

ARIWA veröffentlicht jetzt erstmals umfangreiche Aufnahmen aus einem Schlachthof von Tönnies. Schlachthöfe gehören zu den schwierigsten Herausforderungen für Undercover-Aufnahmen, da sie extrem gut gesichert sind. Die Betreiber setzen alles daran, dass das, was dort geschieht, nicht an die Öffentlichkeit gelangt.


19.10.2026, Deutschland


 NDR berichtet mit Videomaterial von ARIWA.


Er ist Deutschlands größter Schlachtkonzern und gilt als eines der mächtigsten Unternehmen der europäischen Fleischindustrie: Tönnies. Als Marktführer produziert er 30 Prozent des gesamten deutschen Schweinefleischs. Allein 2023 meldete der Konzern einen Jahresumsatz von über 7 Milliarden Euro. Dafür tötet Tönnies jedes Jahr 16 Millionen


Schweine. 


Das uns vorliegende Material zeigt, wie Mitarbeiter*innen die Tiere beim Zutrieb schlagen und sie unter automatischen Toren eingeklemmt werden. Es zeigt den grausamen Erstickungskampf in der CO₂-Anlage mit Tieren, die in Gondeln vor Angst schreien und versuchen zu fliehen. Und es zeigt zahlreiche Verstöße gegen die gesetzlichen Vorschriften vor und während der Schlachtung.


Von der Ankunft bis zum Tod:

Erste Undercover-Aufnahmen aus Tönnies Schlachthof


Das vorliegende Material dokumentiert erstmals unabhängig den gesamten Ablauf der Schlachtung von der Ankunft der Tiere im Schlachthof bis zur Tötung. Die Aufnahmen zeigen, wie leidvoll die letzten Stunden im Leben der Tiere sind. Das liegt auch an einer Maschine im Schlachthof, die grausamer nicht sein könnte: Die sogenannte CO₂-Betäubungsanlage.


Die Betäubung vor dem Schlachten ist gesetzlich vorgeschrieben. Die Tiere sollen so vor Schmerzen und Stress geschützt werden. Auch zur Betäubung selbst gibt es eindeutige Vorgaben: Paragraf 12 der Tierschutz-Schlachtverordnung legt fest, dass Tiere “schnell und unter Vermeidung von Schmerzen oder Leiden in einen (…) Zustand der Wahrnehmungs- und Empfindungslosigkeit” versetzt werden müssen. Der Betäubungsvorgang darf also keine Schmerzen oder Leid auslösen und muss bis zum Tod des Tieres anhalten. Doch die Aufnahmen zeigen eindeutig, dass die Betäubung mit CO₂ gegen diese Vorschrift verstößt!


Ankunft im Schlachthof


Am frühen Morgen kommen die ersten LKWs auf dem Schlachthof an. An den aufgenommenen Tagen werden mindestens fünftausend Schweine pro Tag hier angeliefert und getötet. Tönnies verfügt über ein riesiges Netz von Zulieferbetrieben in ganz Deutschland.


Nach ihrer Ankunft werden die Tiere in enge Wartebuchten gebracht. Hier läuft sanfte Musik, sie soll die Tiere entspannen. Es wirkt makaber. Neunzig Minuten lang sollen sich die vom Transport und Ausladen gestressten Schweine hier beruhigen, dabei ist zu erkennen, wie ängstlich sie sind.


Doch das wahre Grauen kommt erst noch. Nach anderthalb Stunden öffnet sich ein Tor. Ein Mitarbeiter beginnt, die Tiere in einen Treibgang zu scheuchen. Dabei kommt Gewalt zum Einsatz: Wenn die Schweine panisch versuchen zu fliehen, schlägt der Mitarbeiter mit der Treibstange zu, auch ins Gesicht. Die Schweine werden nach und nach in Sechsergruppen aufgeteilt. Als nächstes geht es für sie in die Betäubungsanlage.


Per Gondel in den Erstickungskampf


Die Schweine sind jetzt in einem engen Abteil, aus dem es kein Zurück gibt. Ein Mitarbeiter treibt die Gruppen nacheinander in die Gondelkäfige, mit denen es in wenigen Augenblicken gut 9 Meter nach unten in eine mit CO₂ gefüllte Grube geht. Manche Tiere werden von den schweren hydraulischen Trenngittern eingeklemmt und können sich nicht alleine befreien. Sie schreien vor Schmerz.


Sobald die erste Gruppe von Schweinen in ihre Gondel getrieben wurde, schließt sich der Käfig aus dicken Metallstangen. Kurze Zeit später setzt sich die Gondel in Bewegung. Die versteckte Kamera fährt mit. Innerhalb weniger Sekunden reagieren viele Schweine mit Panik. Viele schreien, schnappen nach Luft, werfen sich gegen die Gitterstäbe und steigen aufeinander. Die Fluchtversuche können so heftig sein, dass manche Tiere sich verletzen und Blutspuren an der Anlage zurücklassen.


Je tiefer die Tiere in den Schacht fahren, desto heftiger werden ihre Fluchtversuche. Die CO₂-Konzentration beträgt nach wenigen Metern schon 80 Prozent. Zeitgleich wird oben die nächste Gruppe in die Gondeln getrieben. Sie können die Angstschreie ihrer Artgenossen aus den Gondeln unter ihnen hören.

author: Brian Hioe
title: Animal Rights Advocates Call for Referendum on Snare Traps
content:
ANIMAL RIGHTS ADVOCATES are currently campaigning for a referendum to be held on the use of wild boar snares.

In particular, animal rights advocates have long criticized wild boar snares as overly cruel. Such traps use spring-loaded mechanisms to tighten around animals’ limbs when triggered.

Nevertheless, such traps have also been criticized for ensnaring other species, as they do not distinguish. Endangered species such as Formosan black bears and leopard cats had also been killed by such traps, as have cats and dogs, sometimes resulting in their losing limbs if they survive.

Though claims had been made that Indigenous hunters used such traps as part of traditional hunting rights, animal rights groups have generally cited that this was rarely the case, in that Indigenous hunters generally do not use such traps. By contrast, such animal rights advocates state that Indigenous hunters more commonly use traps made from wood, bamboo and vines, and other natural materials. In the past, the Central Election Commission turned down calls for a referendum on the use of wild boar snares on the basis that the referendum was unclear as to whether it pertained to traps used by Indigenous hunters.

Otherwise, such traps are sometimes used by farmers as a means of preventing damage to their crops. Animal rights advocates have called on the government to provide electric fencing, protective netting, or other means for farmers to protect their livestock and crops.

The proposals called for by animal rights advocates are relevant to the use, display, and sale of wild boar snares, as well as their import and export. It is thought that China is a major source of some of the wild boar snares used in Taiwan.

It is unclear as to whether the Central Election Commission will approve the referendum currently called for by animal rights advocates. At the same time, without a major political party endorsing it as an issue, such a referendum is unlikely to gain traction. It is to be seen if either the DPP or KMT, or perhaps even both parties, throw their weight behind the proposal.

One notes that there have been cases of political bipartisanship between both major parties on the issue of animal rights in past years, as seen with politicians of both parties supporting enshrining animal rights in the constitution. Even so, such politicians ultimately did not prove serious about such promises outside of election campaigning, as a result of which neither the KMT nor DPP acted on claims in past election cycles that animal rights would see constitutional protection.

author: Sophie Lemcke
title: So ist es, als weibliches Rind in der Milchindustrie zu leben
content:
Die Milchindustrie ist ein grausamer Kreislauf des Leids und endet mit einem gewaltvollen Tod.


Wie fühlt es sich an, in dieses System hineingeboren zu werden, ohne die Möglichkeit, dem zu entkommen?


Der einzige Grund, weshalb die Industrie dich „produziert“ hat: Auch du sollst Kinder gebären, immer wieder, damit du Milch produzierst. Milch, die dann von Menschen, statt von deinem Kalb konsumiert werden kann.


Du wirst fixiert, während jemand das Besamungsgerät in deine Vagina sowie seinen Arm in deinen Anus einführt. Wenn die Zwangsbefruchtung nicht beim ersten Mal zur Trächtigkeit führt – was oft der Fall ist –, wird dieser Vorgang mehrfach wiederholt.


Neun Monate – wie bei uns Menschen – wächst dein Kalb in dir heran. Du spürst eine Verbindung, merkst, wie es sich bewegt und immer größer wird. Je schwerer du selbst wirst, umso stärker werden deine Gelenkprobleme. Die rutschigen und harten Spaltenböden, auf denen du fast dein ganzes Leben verbringst, führen oft zu Verletzungen.


Dann bringst du dein Kalb zur Welt. Um dich herum riecht es extrem nach Kot und Ammoniak, von den Ausscheidungen der Tiere.


Endlich ist es da, noch ganz nass und schwach. Du leckst ihm über das Fell, um es zu wärmen. Es sucht deine Nähe und will an deinem Euter die für ihn so wichtige Erstmilch trinken. Sie stärkt sein noch schwaches Immunsystem und gibt ihm Kraft. Doch dann kommen die Arbeiter*innen.


Sie zerren dein noch ganz wackelig stehendes Kalb weg von dir. Es ruft nach dir. Du versuchst, bei ihm zu bleiben, aber du hast keine Chance. Die Menschen haben es weggebracht – du wirst es wahrscheinlich nie wiedersehen und nach nur zwei Monaten direkt wieder gewaltvoll befruchtet.


Du wirst nach der Geburt monatelang mehrmals täglich in den Melkstand getrieben – und die meiste Zeit davon bist du bereits wieder schwanger. Dein Körper muss gleichzeitig ein neues Kalb versorgen, das in dir heranwächst, und täglich über 22 Liter Milch produzieren. Dein Euter und deine Zitzen schmerzen. Aufgrund der extremen Überzüchtung produzierst du viermal so viel Milch, wie du es natürlicherweise für dein Kind tun würdest.


Die Prozeduren und Haltungsbedingungen zehren stark an deinem Körper. Dein Euter ist entzündet und schmerzt bei jeder Berührung. Andere Tiere humpeln, weil ihnen jeder Schritt wehtut. Viele sind schwach und ausgelaugt.


Wenn du nicht schon vorher stirbst oder getötet wirst, weil dein Körper nicht mehr kann, dann wirst du voraussichtlich nach nur fünf Jahren getötet – obwohl du unter natürlichen Bedingungen 25 Jahre alt werden könntest.


Dann kommt der Tag, an dem du als nicht mehr profitabel giltst. Du wirst aus dem Stall getrieben – das erste Mal nach Jahren verlässt du ihn, aber das ist kein Grund zur Freude.


Zusammen mit anderen erschöpften „ausgedienten Milchkühen“ wirst du auf einen Transporter verladen. Du hast Mühe, über die Rampe zu gehen. Deine Gelenke schmerzen vom jahrelangen Stehen auf Spaltenböden. Im engen Transporter stehst du dicht an dicht mit den anderen Tieren, der Lkw wackelt. Manche fallen hin und werden versehentlich getreten. Eure Fahrt in den Schlachthof dauert mehrere Stunden, ohne Wasser, ohne Nahrung, ohne Pause.


Angekommen erwartet dich ein brutaler Tod. Überall riecht es nach Blut, du bekommst Panik, aber es gibt keinen Ausweg. Dann ein Bolzenschuss in deinen Kopf. Wenn die Betäubung korrekt durchgeführt wurde und wirkt, brichst du zusammen. Wenn nicht, kann es sein, dass du bei Bewusstsein und unter extremen Schmerzen erlebst, wie dir deine Kehle aufgeschnitten wird und du verblutest.


Es ist unvorstellbar, was Mutterrinder in der Milchindustrie erleiden müssen.


Der wahre Preis von Milch


Ein Ermittler von Animal Equality hat mehrere Monate undercover in einem deutschen Milchgewinnungsbetrieb gearbeitet und den Alltag der Tiere dokumentiert. Was unsere Undercover-Recherche zeigt, ist der wahre Preis von Milch: Ausbeutung, Gewalt, Schmerz, Leid und Tod.


Auf unserer Webseite erfährst du mehr und kannst die Stellungnahme des Betriebs nachlesen:


Zur Undercover-Recherche


Unterstütze dieses grausame System nicht!


Entscheide dich konsequent für pflanzliche Lebensmittel. Im Supermarkt findest du zahlreiche Alternativen zu Milch, wie:


Hafermilch – mild, cremig, perfekt für Kaffee und Müsli (oft die günstigste Option!)


Sojamilch – proteinreich, ideal zum Kochen und Backen


Mandelmilch – leicht nussig, besonders lecker in Smoothies


Reismilch – süßlich und gut verträglich …

author: admin
title: Solidarität mit nichtmenschlichen Tieren im Klimakollaps
content:
Am 2. November ist Friederike Schmitz zu Gast in Leipzig. Ihr Vortrag beschäftigt sich mit der Frage von Solidarität mit nichtmenschlichen Tieren im Klimakollaps.

Plaque, Industriestraße 101, Leipzig

Orga: tierbefreier*innen Leipzig

Die Erderhitzung schreitet voran und wir müssen damit rechnen, dass Wetterextreme und Katastrophen unsere Gesellschaften massiv unter Druck setzen werden. Es ist daher realistisch, von Kollapsszenarien auszugehen – das bedeutet nicht zwingend ein einmaliges Ereignis, das plötzlich alles verändert. Es kann auch bedeuten, dass etablierte Systeme und Sicherheiten zunehmend instabil und unverlässlich werden.>

Die Kollapsbewegung fordert, dass wir uns gemeinsam darauf vorbereiten und solidarische Strukturen aufbauen, denn wer gegen Umweltzerstörung und Faschismus kämpft, kann sich auf den Staat nicht verlassen. Doch inwieweit sind nichtmenschliche Tiere dabei eingeschlossen? Und wie könnte es aussehen, wenn die Solidarität nicht an der Speziesgrenze haltmacht? Der Vortrag liefert einen Einstieg in diese Fragen und lädt zu Austausch und Diskussion ein.

Friederike Schmitz ist eine deutsche Philosophin und Publizistin mit dem Schwerpunkt Ethik und Politik der Mensch-Tier-Beziehung. Zu ihrem Schwerpunkt gehört die Klimagerechte Transformation von Landwirtschaft und Ernährung. In dem Podcast “Was zu retten ist?” thematisiert sie zusammen mit Annemarie Botzki (Campaignerin und Aktivistin) Klima, Kollaps und Ernährung.

title: Smokescreen Saturday Exposed: Chris Packham Blasts The Quorn Hunt Over Sickening Fox Cruelty That Blows Apart Trail Hunting’s Biggest Lie
content:
When we showed wildlife campaigner Chris Packham the sickening footage of the Quorn Hunt, his response was damning:


“Another bloody year, another bloodied body, another animal tortured and torn to pieces to gratify the bloodlust of savages. Where is the damned consultation and where is the damned ban?”


Chris Packham condemns the Quorn Hunt footage.


The footage lays bare the brutal reality of cub hunting – the practice of using foxes to train young hounds to hunt and kill.


WARNING: DISTURBING FOOTAGE


Cub hunting is not some isolated activity. It is the preparation for the hunting season ahead. Throughout the autumn, young hounds are taught what to chase, what to kill and how to respond to the huntsman’s commands. What they learn – or fail to learn – during these crucial weeks sets the tone for the entire season.


This is what makes the Quorn Hunt footage so damning. It shows hounds being deliberately encouraged to seize and tear at a fox, with hunt staff repeatedly intervening to reinforce that behaviour.


On the eve of National Trail Hunting Day aka Smokescreen Saturday – as the British Hound Sports Association (BHSA) and the Countryside Alliance prepared to showcase so-called ‘trail hunting’, the Quorn Hunt provided a horrifying glimpse of the reality behind the myth of trail laying.


On Friday 16 October, 2026 Northants Hunt Saboteurs visited The Quorn Hunt’s kennel meet at Kirby Bellars, near Melton Mowbray, Leicestershire.


The Quorn has a long history of royal connections. King Charles regularly rode with the hunt when he was Prince of Wales. His association with the Quorn came to an end following the emergence of footage showing

hunt members pulling a fox cub from its den

 and throwing them to the hounds to be torn apart.


The footage begins with the saboteurs’ drone approaching a group of barns stacked with bales. Mounted riders are positioned around the outside of the covert – a classic cub hunting tactic designed to frighten fleeing foxes back into cover, where the hounds can kill them.


Riders surround the covert which forces the fox back towards the barns.


As the drone circles to the far side of the barns, a group of hounds comes into view. A quad bike can be seen approaching, alongside another rider. More hounds appear on the track, along with a riderless horse.


Two terriermen jump off the quad bike and run towards the hounds, which have gathered in a narrow passageway between two barns.


Trapped. The fox is between the two barns.


What the drone captures next is utterly horrific – and exposes the brutal reality behind the hunting industry’s claims about scent trails.


The huntsman is already on foot, surrounded by excited hounds. He is swinging something towards them, encouraging them to grab hold. As the footage unfolds, it becomes clear that he is swinging a fox.


First the huntsman is alone shaking the fox to excite the hounds.


The hounds are repeatedly encouraged to seize the fox. Eventually, several begin to grab hold, and the huntsman encourages them further, pulling and tugging against them as though playing a game.


The huntsman blows on his horn over the hounds reinforcing the sound of the horn call with the kill.


When the hounds finally take the fox from him, he bends over them as they tear at it and then blows his hunting horn – most likely sounding the traditional call for a kill, reinforcing the hounds’ association between the horn and their quarry.


He then gives one of the terriermen a thumbs-up.


Thumbs-up.


When the hounds begin to lose interest again, the terrierman picks up the fox’s body and repeatedly shakes it in front of them, encouraging them to take hold once more. He appears to push the fox towards the hounds jaws.


The terrierman also has a go with the fox – shaking the body into the hounds jaws.


When the dogs finally grip it, he pulls against them in a grotesque tug-of-war. Once the hounds take the fox from the terrierman, the huntsman again blows his horn over them.


As more hounds join in, the terrierman pats one of the dogs. But as he does so he appears to hear the drone and looks up.


The terrierman suddenly notices the drone. Too late.


Suddenly everything changes.


The fox’s body is hurriedly retrieved from the hounds, and the two terriermen scramble to stuff it beneath the hay bales.

title: DEM Party launches “Budget for Bread, Peace and Justice” campaign
content:
The Peoples’ Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party) launched its “Budget for Bread, Peace and Justice” campaign in Kurtalan district of Siirt province. At the launch event in Ehmedê Xanê Park, Co-Chair Tuncer Bakırhan and a party delegation first listened to the demands of farmers, shopkeepers, pensioners, and other sections of society. The discussions focused on rising living costs, lack of jobs, and the economic neglect of the region. Bakırhan announced that the party would accompany the upcoming 2027 budget deliberations with a nationwide mobilization. The party will campaign both in parliament and on the streets for a different allocation of public funds.


Agriculture under pressure: Rising costs and declining yields


Statements from local residents painted a picture of the economic difficulties facing the region. Farmers and livestock breeders reported that high production costs were making it increasingly difficult for them to earn a living. “We are being forced to slaughter our animals, primarily because of rising feed prices. A liter of diesel, which we need to cultivate our fields, now costs more than 100 lira,” the people explained.


As a result, residents said, more and more agricultural land is being left uncultivated. This is compounded by environmental changes caused by the Ilisu Dam. According to local residents, the regional climate has changed, affecting the pollination of pistachio trees and leading to declining yields. Pistachio cultivation is an essential source of livelihood for many families.


Bakırhan described these accounts as a reflection of social conditions in Turkey. He stated that millions of people were unable to pay their rent, adequately provide for their children, or make ends meet despite being employed. “If this state also belongs to farmers, workers, the poor, and pensioners, then it must finally listen to the demands voiced by our brothers and sisters here in Siirt,” the DEM Party Co-Chair said.


Budget funds must benefit the people


Bakırhan was particularly critical of the planned railway connection between Siirt and Kurtalan. He questioned the project’s economic benefits for the local population and accused the government of primarily serving the interests of mining companies. “Why is this railway being built? So that the mining companies destroying our environment in Şirvan and Siirt can make even more money. The railway wagons are intended to transport their raw materials to factories,” he said.


Instead, Bakırhan said, the government should reduce the tax burden on small businesses, provide relief to indebted enterprises, introduce free school meals, and increase the incomes of workers and pensioners. “The budget must be drawn up for workers, the people, and the poor. Under your government, the budget has never been prepared for workers or minimum-wage earners. But this time, we will not accept it. We will put up the strongest possible resistance against it in parliament.”


Mining and dams, but few prospects for young people


Bakırhan highlighted the contradiction between the intensive economic exploitation of the region and the persistent poverty of its population. He remarked that Siirt was dominated by dams and mining projects, while young people from Kurtalan struggled to find even minimum-wage jobs in tourist destinations in western Turkey, such as Marmaris. He also criticized the unequal tax burden. According to the budget figures he cited, workers, minimum-wage earners, and small business owners are expected to contribute around five trillion lira in taxes, while approximately two trillion lira is expected from wealthier sections of society.


“Whose taxes are these, and whose budget will it be? It will be a budget for the rich,” Bakırhan said. He also addressed the inadequate public infrastructure, saying: “Although the province is surrounded by dams, Kurtalan has suffered from water supply problems for decades. Instead of building a railway for the mines in Şirvan, finally make sure that Kurtalan has access to water. There are dams everywhere, there is water everywhere.”


Bakırhan also pointed to the shortage of doctors in public hospitals and the lack of economic infrastructure. While numerous university graduates remain unemployed, hospitals in Siirt and Pervari are unable to secure sufficient medical staff, he noted.

author: Unknown
title: Duvara tutturulmak ya da duvarın içinde kalmak
content:
Bir bedene yer açmak ile onu bir mekana yerleştirmek aynı şey midir? Görünür olmak, hareket edebilmek anlamına gelir mi? Dilan Cudi Saruhan’ın

Beden

 adlı yerleştirmesiyle Maurizio Cattelan’ın

A Perfect Day

’i, bu soruları duvarın önünde yeniden kurar. Birinde canlı beden dışarıdan sabitlenir; diğerinde beden imgesi, kendisini kuşatan yüzeyle aynı maddede oluşur. Duvar her iki yapıtta da varlığın yerini belirler. Fakat o yerin içinde nasıl kalındığı değişir.


Şeritlerin merkezde yoğunlaşıp çevreye yayılması, iki çalışma arasında çarpıcı bir görsel yakınlık yaratır. Bu benzerlik, doğrudan etkilenmenin kanıtı değildir. Karşılaştırmayı verimli kılan, benzer düzenlerin farklı toplumsal deneyimler içinde ürettiği ayrımdır: bedenin hareketini durdurmak ile sınırı bedenin içine yerleştirmek arasındaki ayrım.


Saruhan’ın figürü cenin formunda kendi üzerine kapanmıştır. Başı gövdesine yaklaşır, uzuvları merkezde toplanır; beden, dışarıya açılmak yerine kendi içine çekilir. Bu duruşu yalnızca sıkışmanın sonucu saymak, figürün kendini koruma hareketini gözden kaçırır. Ancak korunmanın daralarak mümkün oluşu da başlı başına bir sorudur. Beden burada hem sığınak hem sığınılandır.


Kuşatan ile kuşatılan


Beden’de oluklu karton şeritler merkezde düğümlenerek hacim kazanır, kenarlarda uzayıp seyrelir. Figürün çevresini izlerken bir noktadan sonra bedeni mi, onu içine alan dokuyu mu gördüğümüz belirsizleşir. Çünkü kuşatan ile kuşatılan aynı maddeden yapılmıştır. Karton, figürün çevresindeki engel olduğu kadar onun varlık koşuludur. Sınırı kaldırdığımızda altında özgürleşmeyi bekleyen, önceden tamamlanmış bir beden bulacağımızdan emin olamayız.


Cenin formu bu maddesel ortaklığı daha da yoğunlaştırır. Başın eğilmesi, gövdenin kıvrılması ve uzuvların içe çekilmesi, bedeni kendi sınırları içinde yeniden toplar. Anne rahmini çağrıştıran bu biçimde korunma ile kuşatılma birbirine yaklaşır. Yine de burada güvenli bir başlangıca dönüşten söz etmek güçtür. Figür, onu taşıyan dokunun içinde saklanırken aynı dokunun baskısını da taşır. Bir sığınağın ne zaman kapatılma mekânına dönüştüğünü, formun içinden sorar.


Cattelan’ın 1999 tarihli

A Perfect Day

’inde ise galerici Massimo De Carlo, yapışkan bantlarla kendi galerisinin duvarına sabitlenmiştir. Yüzü, giysisi ve ayakkabıları, kuşatmanın içindeki kişinin kimliğini görünür tutar. Düşey gövde ayakta durma hâlini anımsatır; fakat ayaklar yere değmez. Bedenin ağırlığını taşıma işi zeminden bantlara aktarılmıştır. Başın yana düşüşü, bu duruşun kişinin kendi dengesiyle sürdürülemediğini açığa çıkarır (MASSIMODECARLO, 1999; Phillips, t.y.).


Maurizio Cattelan, A Perfect Day, 1999. Massimo De Carlo’nun yapışkan bantlarla galeri duvarına sabitlendiği eylemin fotoğrafik belgesi. Görsel kaynağı: Phillips, yapıt kaydı, lot 23.


Duruşun izleyicide bıraktığı iz


Cattelan’ın bedeni dışarıdan tutulur; Saruhan’ın bedeni kendi üzerine kapanır. Birinde düşeyliğin dayanağı alınmış, diğerinde bedenin kapladığı alan daralmıştır. Bu ayrım, bakışın yönünü de değiştirir. De Carlo’nun açıkta kalan yüzü bizi belirli bir kişiye götürürken Saruhan’ın yüzü dokunun içinde geri çekilir. Karşılaştığımız, portresinden tanıyabileceğimiz bir kişi kadar, duruşunu kendi bedenimizde yoklayabileceğimiz bir varlık hâlidir.


Görmek, burada bedenden bağımsız bir etkinlik değildir. Merleau-Ponty’nin bedensel algı yaklaşımıyla düşünüldüğünde, izleyici gördüğü duruşu kendi hareket olanakları içinden kavrar (Merleau-Ponty, 2012). Cattelan’ın karşısında kendi ayaklarının yere bastığını fark edebilir; Saruhan’ın figürüne bakarken dizlerini kendine çekmeyi, başını eğmeyi, omuzlarını daraltmayı hatırlayabilir. Cenin formunun tanıdıklığı, bu yakınlığı güçlendirir. Bununla birlikte tanıdıklık, bütün izleyicilerin aynı duyguyu yaşayacağı anlamına gelmez.


Saruhan’ın kapanan bedeninde özdeşlik, yüz benzerliğinden önce bir korunma jesti üzerinden kurulabilir. Kendi kırılganlığımızı o kıvrımın içinde düşünürüz. Fakat “Ben de böyle kıvrılabilirim” demek ile “Ben de aynı kapatılmayı yaşadım” demek arasında aşılması kolay olmayan bir mesafe vardır. Yakınlık, başkasının tarihini kendimize mal etme hakkı vermez. Bakışın sorumluluğu, bu mesafeyi koruyarak yaklaşabilmektir.

author: Julie Zenderoudi
title: New Study Finds EPA May Be Vastly Underreporting PFAS Levels in Drinking Water
content:
The researchers found the Environmental Protection Agency’s minimum reporting levels masked widespread contamination.

Truthout is an indispensable resource for activists, movement leaders and workers everywhere. Please make this work possible with a quick donation.

US drinking water could contain double the PFAS levels currently reported by regulators, according to a new study from Texas Christian University.

The study, published in Cell Reports Sustainability, used computer modeling to estimate that the latest reports from the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) capture only 44% of the average combined concentration of 25 polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) in US water systems.

PFAS, also known as “forever chemicals,” are known to persist in the environment and are linked to some cancers, high cholesterol, reproductive issues, and other health problems.

Researchers analyzed more than 1.8 million PFAS measurement records from the EPA’s January 2026 release of monitoring data from water systems across the country. They found most individual PFAS test results in the dataset fall below the EPA’s minimum reporting levels (MRLs).

These data points are often treated as zero when agencies and researchers summarize average PFAS levels in drinking water.

The authors found that 98% of PFAS test results were below the MRL. The MRL generally means a concentration that most laboratories can reliably measure and report. However, the study’s authors argue that this doesn’t mean that the water tested is PFAS-free or that it’s safe.

“Below the reporting limit does not mean zero. Our study shows why that distinction matters when summarizing PFAS concentrations,” said lead author Gehendra Kharel, associate professor of environmental and geological sciences at Texas Christian University.

Kharel and his team used computer models applied to data from the EPA’s Fifth Unregulated Contaminant Monitoring Rule (UCMR 5), a nationwide program that requires public water systems to test drinking water for specific PFAS. They used this dataset to estimate possible concentrations for PFAS records listed below the EPA’s MRL.

They averaged hundreds of data points to come up with an estimate, performing this calculation for all 25 PFAS that had been detected at least once in the EPA’s dataset.

Under the study’s primary statistical model, they found that treating below-limit results as zero captured only 44% of the average combined concentration of the 25 PFAS monitored across 9,991 community water systems.

Jesse Goodrich, assistant professor in the division of environmental health at the University of Southern California, said that while municipal drinking water data explains why certain people have elevated chemical levels, these findings clarify why so many Americans, regardless of location or water source, have detectable PFAS in their blood.

“People traditionally have thought that drinking water is a large source of exposure to different PFAS compounds. And so when you look at the UCMR results, you see a lot of zeros, and that is hard to reconcile based on the human biomonitoring studies, where you see that everyone is actually exposed,” Goodrich said.

The results of this study are model-generated predictions rather than measurements of actual concentrations. However, Goodrich believes the results explain how trace contamination builds up.

“There’s very low levels of PFAS in drinking water, and over time, since compounds have such a long half life, that can add up to measurable, kind of ubiquitous exposure in the population,” Goodrich said.

Kharel believes the study could help provide a more complete picture of PFAS levels in US drinking water and improve how environmental monitoring data are interpreted, bridging the gap between official estimates and the actual level of chemicals in our water.

Alissa Cordner, co-director of the PFAS Project Lab at Northeastern University, said the EPA takes a more conservative approach by treating unmeasurable chemical samples as zero, which results in the lowest possible contamination estimates.

Cordner argues scientists can use better methods. Instead of assuming zero, researchers often estimate low-level presence by dividing the lab’s detection limit by either two or the square root of two.

“Either of those approaches are going to give you a less conservative and potentially more environmentally relevant measure of what’s actually going on in these samples,” she said.

title: Zonguldak’taki maden patlaması: 3 işçi toprağa verildi, 3 kişi tutuklandı
content:
Zonguldak’ta 3 işçinin yaşamını yitirdiği madendeki metan gazı birikmesi sonucu yaşanan patlamada yaşamını yitiren 3 işçi toprağa verildi. Gözaltına alınan işletme sahibi ile iş sağlığı ve güvenliği uzmanı ve maden mühendisi ise tutuklandı.

Zonguldak’ın Kilimli ilçesine bağlı Gelik beldesinin Dereiçi mevkiinde, Demir Madencilik AŞ’ye ait maden ocağında dün saat 10.00 sıralarında grizu patlaması meydana geldi. Olayda madende bulunan 8 işçiden 3’ü hayatını kaybetti. 2’si ağır, 5 yaralı ise ambulansla Zonguldak Atatürk Devlet Hastanesine kaldırılarak tedaviye alındı.

Zonguldak Atatürk Devlet Hastanesi morgundan sabah saatlerinde alınan maden işçisi Cengizhan Bükrübaş’ın cenazesi, cenaze aracıyla Çaycuma ilçesinin Perşembe beldesi Muharremşah köyüne getirildi. Bükrübaş, daha sonra Muharremşah Camisi’nde kılınan cenaze namazının ardından gözyaşları arasında toprağa verildi. Bükrübaş'ın bekar olduğu, babası İsmail Bükrübaş'ın da aynı ocaktan emekli olduğu belirtildi.

İşçilerden Murat Kaya’nın cenazesi ise Saltuokova beldesine bağlı Sarmaşık köyü Kartoğlu Mahallesi’ne götürüldü. Murat Kaya, aile mezarlığına defnedildi.

İşçilerden 3 çocuk babası Recep Çolakoğlu (45) için de Alibüyük Mahallesi’nde cenaze töreni düzenlendi. Çolakoğlu mahalle mezarlığında son yolculuğuna uğurlandı.

Olayın ardadan işletme sahibi Mehmet Salih Demir, iş sağlığı ve güvenliği uzmanı Ercüment Yalçın ile maden mühendisi Yusuf Çavdar, gözaltına alındı. Jandarmadaki işlemlerinin ardından adliyeye sevk edilen 3 kişi, savcılık sorgularının ardından çıkarıldıkları sulh ceza hakimliğinde ‘Bilinçli taksirle öldürme ve yaralama’ suçundan tutuklandı.

İşletme müdürü Mustafa Kapanşahin hakkında ise yakalama kararı çıkarıldı.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: Emma Honeybun
title: ‘Something big is coming’: climate advocates say Bill C-39 is a new version of an old issue
content:
First Nations activists say a federal bill approaching its third reading will fast-track environmental impacts that Indigenous communities have already been feeling for decades — with the same lack of consent.


Michel Koostachin, founder of Indigenous-led advocacy group

Friends of the Attawapiskat River

, said that prophecies are a part of many First Nations cultures and he viewed the bill as that.


“There was an Elder that spoke about what was coming to us as First Nations. If you look at this legislation… he said that there’s something big coming, something that has no ears, no brain, no eyes, no mouth, no legs, no feet, no hands. And that’s that legislation,” Kootstachin said.


“You know, bulldozing the environment without primary informed consent, which is our Indigenous right, and contaminating the environment.”


Bill C-39, the

Building Canada Strong Act

,

 is currently being studied by a special committee in the House of Commons, and pre-studied by the Senate.


If passed, the law would aim to expand on the government’s “one-project, one-review, within one-year approach” to major projects, such as mines and ports, that are predicted to have a positive effect on Canada’s economy.


Bill C-5, the

Building Canada Act

,

 passed in 2025, introduced “projects of national interest,” which gives ministers the authority to fast-track major projects if they meet certain criteria.


According to the Major Projects Office set up to deal with proposed infrastructure, a project must “strengthen Canada’s autonomy, resilience, and security”; “provide economic or other benefits”; “advance the interests of Indigenous Peoples”; and “contribute to clean growth and to meeting Canada’s climate change objectives.”


If a project presents a case that aligns with those guidelines, it may be exempt from permits pertaining to different laws, such as the

Species at Risk

 and

Heritage

 Acts.


However, several First Nation governments, advocates and environmentalists have raised the concern that these projects of national interest do not align with their own criteria — specifically, advancing the interests of Indigenous Peoples and contributing to clean growth — due to the bill’s implications for the environment, as well as inherent and Treaty rights.


On Wednesday, 56 scientist fellows from the Royal Society of Canada

published an open letter

 “concerning environmental stewardship and the proposed

Building Canada Strong Act.

”


Among other points, the letter recommended that “additional time may be required to evaluate less harmful alternatives and impacts not yet studied by the proponents,” and to remove the “concentration of power” from a single minister “to dismiss conditions for permits and Impact Assessments.


“This is an extraordinary power,” the scientists wrote, “with potentially far-reaching consequences for the environment.”


They said that they “fully agree” with the goal of creating economic growth while protecting the environment, referencing Canada’s Force of Nature announcement, which included adding protective environmental measures when it came to the development of large-scale projects.


“As written, however, Bill C-39 countermands the environmental protections currently in place in Canadian law, laws written to avoid irreparable harms to species, ecosystems, natural resources, and human wellbeing and health,” the letter continued. “We call upon the House and Senate to uphold these laws and to consider our recommendations for the benefit of nature, Canadians, and the rest of the world.”


Webequie First Nation, approximately 60 km from the Ring of Fire mineral deposit in the James Bay lowlands of northern Ontario, is seen from the air in 2025. Photo: Christopher Katsarov/The Canadian Press.


Koostachin said that the bill is part of a larger issue of projects being approved without consent from First Nations.


This was in response to Ottawa’s announcement to invest $1 billion in the construction of the

Webequie Supply Road

, an all-season gravel road into the Ring of Fire, a mineral-rich section of the James Bay Lowlands.


Currently, the Ring of Fire is only accessible by ice road or plane, and James Bay, more than 68,000 square kilometres and holding approximately 30 billion tonnes of carbon — is largely untouched.


The investment was only one line in a larger announcement about a “new action plan to protect workers from tariffs and strengthen Ontario industries,” done in collaboration …

author: Zeit Online
title: Warum die Deutschen nicht ausrasten?
content:
Während in Frankreich Barrikaden brennen, bleibt es hierzulande ziemlich ruhig. Geht’s den Deutschen so viel besser? Nein, sie sind nur die Summe ihrer Ängste.


Verschwitzte Gesichter hinter Sturmhauben, ein Rathaus, das lichterloh in Flammen steht, Ascheberge am Straßenrand. Die Bilder der Ausschreitungen in Frankreich, die in diesen Tagen zu uns herüberschwappen, können bei deutschen Betrachtern für gemischte Gefühle sorgen. Im ersten Moment kann man erschrecken; die Franzosen, meine Güte! Oder aber man macht einen Schritt zur Seite. Und fragt: Warum blieben wir in Deutschland von solchen Ausschreitungen bislang verschont? Warum rasten die Deutschen nicht aus, wie Menschen in anderen Ländern der Welt, zumindest nicht in diesen Massen? Und das, obwohl radikale Einstellungen auch hierzulande zunehmen?


Beobachtet man die Protestkultur in Deutschland in den vergangenen Jahren, kann man sich fühlen wie in einer düsteren Variante von Samuel Becketts Warten auf Godot. Man spürt, da baut sich etwas auf, der Unmut, so erwartet man, muss bald eskalieren, das Aufbegehren steht vor der Tür. Und alle fürchten es schon. Doch dann? Bleibt es aus.


So war es, als die Gelbwesten in Frankreich durch die Straßen zogen und die Zeitungen ein baldiges deutsches Pendant prophezeiten. So war es, als die Klimaaktivisten ihre Hände auf die Autobahn klebten; CSU-Politiker Alexander Dobrindt sah damals gar die Entstehung einer »Klima-RAF« voraus. Und auch auf die Pegida-Demonstrationen und die Bauernproteste schaute die Öffentlichkeit voller Angst vor flächendeckender Eskalation. Nur kam diese nie. In Deutschland gibt es den Zorn der Masse. Aber er kocht selten über.


Bevor sich jetzt jemand wütend in die Kommentarspalte verabschiedet: Ja, auch hierzulande kommt es zu Gewalt bei Protesten. Linksradikale schmissen in den vergangenen Jahren Steine auf Polizisten, Rechtsradikale griffen Gegendemonstranten an, Corona-Demonstrierende kletterten über das Gitter zum Reichstag, Pro-Palästina-Demos endeten mit Verhaftungen. Aber im Vergleich zu Frankreich etwa rasteten die Deutschen zuletzt selten richtig aus, zumindest nicht in Gestalt einer gewaltbereiten Masse, die landesweit durch die Straßen zieht, öffentliche Gebäude in Brand steckt und Läden plündert.


Das vielleicht bekannteste Beispiel für gewaltsame Ausschreitungen bei Demonstrationen der letzten Jahre sind die linksradikalen Proteste rund um den G20-Gipfel 2017. Aber auch diese blieben auf einen Ort und den Anlass beschränkt. Und es war kein allein deutscher Protest, er war international. Aus ganz Europa reisten Demonstrierende an, um ihrer Wut Ausdruck zu verleihen.


Was also passiert mit der deutschen Wut auf der Straße? Unmut gibt es hier schließlich auch. Die AfD macht längst mit der mangelhaften Infrastruktur, der übertriebenen Bürokratie, dem Aussterben von Kleinstädten und der Verelendung von Großstädten Politik.


Wenn man in die Zahlen schaut, gibt es viele der Probleme, die in Frankreich beklagt werden, auch hier: Der Anteil derer, die armutsgefährdet sind, liegt hier wie dort bei 16 Prozent. Die Preise für die Verbraucher sind in beiden Ländern um ziemlich genau drei Prozent gestiegen. Die hohen Mieten sind in Deutschland sogar ein größeres Problem als in Frankreich. Beim letzten Pisa-Test schnitt Deutschland so schlecht ab wie noch nie. Die Jugendarbeitslosigkeit ist in Frankreich zwar deutlich höher, aber auch hierzulande haben Jugendliche, was ihre Zukunftsaussichten angeht, allen Grund, die Fassung zu verlieren. Steht uns der Kipppunkt also vielleicht doch nur noch bevor?


Telefoniert man Protestforscher im Land ab, rechnet keiner von ihnen damit, dass Ausschreitungen, wie wir sie in Frankreich sehen, in nächster Zeit bei uns drohen könnten. Strukturelle Gründe werden da genannt. Die Tatsache, dass hierzulande Gewerkschaften regelmäßig mit Unternehmern am Tisch sitzen und Kompromisse aushandeln, bevor alles eskaliert. In Frankreich gehe die Polizei viel härter gegen Demonstrierende vor, auch das befördere die Eskalation eher, als dass es sie verhindere. Der vielleicht größte strukturelle Unterschied ist, dass es in Deutschland keine Zentralregierung gibt, die von oben alles entscheidet und auf die sich die geballte Wut einer ganzen Bewegung entladen kann. Im föderalen System bleibt der Protest eher lokal, statt sich im Land auszubreiten.

Die Zahl der Krankheitstage durch Hitze und Sonnenlicht hat sich im Zeitraum von 2008 bis 2017 verdoppelt. Zudem werden mittlerweile jährlich Tausende Fälle von Hautkrebs als Berufskrankheit anerkannt. Hitzschlag, Sonnenstich, Krämpfe, Ödeme, Probleme durch Salz- und Wasserverlust – das sind einige der Gesundheitsschäden, die durch Hitze und Sonnenlicht ausgelöst werden können. Wie aus Angaben der Bundesregierung auf eine Anfrage der Linksfraktion hervorgeht, gab es 2017 etwa 40.000 Arbeitsunfähigkeitstage „auf Grund von Schäden durch Hitze und Sonnenlicht“. An der Hitze in Europa starben im Sommer 50.000 Menschen. Eine britische Analyse zeigt: Die Folgen des menschengemachten Klimawandels werden deutlicher


„Der Hitzesommer 2026 kostete nach Schätzung britischer Wissenschaftler in europäischen Städten etwa 50.000 Menschen das Leben – mehr als je zuvor. Fast zwei Drittel (65 Prozent) der Todesfälle führen die Forscher direkt auf den von Menschen verursachten Klimawandel zurück. (…) Die Wissenschaftler vom Imperial College London und der London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine entwickelten eine Methode zum Berechnen von Hitzetoten aus historischen Daten seit dem Jahr 2000 und verglichen sie mit tatsächlich gemeldeten Statistiken. (…) „Wir können mit ziemlicher Sicherheit sagen, dass der Sommer 2026 der schlimmste seit Beginn der Aufzeichnungen war, was die hitzebedingte Sterblichkeit in weiten Teilen Europas angeht“, sagte Clair Barnes, Forscherin für Extremwetter und Klimawandel am Imperial College. „Hinter diesen Statistiken stecken echte Menschen, die ihr Leben verloren haben, und Familien, die um sie trauern“, so die Forscherin weiter. Den Wissenschaftlern zufolge starben nicht nur ältere Menschen an den Folgen der Hitze. Schätzungsweise 6.000 der 50.000 Hitzetoten seien unter 65 Jahre alt gewesen, betonten sie. „Es wird immer deutlicher, dass unsere Städte schlecht an die steigenden Temperaturen angepasst sind, und es ist entscheidend, dass wir unsere Anpassungsbemühungen verstärken“, betonte der Epidemiologe Pierre Masselot von der London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine. „Das bedeutet, die Städte durch mehr Grünflächen und weniger Umweltverschmutzung zu kühlen und die Bevölkerung medizinisch zu versorgen.“

author: Bulatlat Contributors
title: Farmers decry government’s lack of preparation for Super El Niño
content:
Farmers, scientists and environmentalists, held a forum, October 18 on the impacts of Super El Niño on farmers and fisherfolk and the government’s lack of preparations for it.

A Super El Niño is a stronger El Niño where the temperature of the Pacific Ocean increases to 2C above the average. In the Philippines, it leads to the extreme shifting of weather conditions, bringing in severe drought, or stronger rainfall events. For farmers, it is the government’s unpreparedness that turns it into an even greater calamity, made even worse by the climate crisis.

Farmers Geraldine Patriarca and Ginny Nabia from Bicol and Negros expressed how their communities are already experiencing extreme drought, and are unable to sustain themselves and their families. They demanded Marcos Jr. to give genuine solutions to farmers’ struggles, not his proposed buckets that they say “will barely even catch any rain.”

Irish Cuaresma of Advocates of Science and Technology for the People (Agham), added that farmers and Indigenous peoples are further undermined by “disaster capitalism,” where corporations benefit from humanitarian crises.

Sharl Lopez of Philippine Network of Food Security Programs (PNFSP) meanwhile, criticized the government for not upholding their obligation to uphold the people’s right to food security, and advocated for the passing of the Right to Adequate Food Bill.

After the forum, farmers held a flash mob calling for national industrialization, genuine agrarian reform. (RVO)

El 12 de octubre, las calles de la Ciudad de Buenos Aires volvieron a ser escenario del contrafestejo, una jornada de lucha y memoria frente a la celebración de la conquista de América. Sin embargo, no logró detener la columna, que resistió la imposición policial y sostuvo su derecho a ocupar la calle.

author: Rob Wipond
title: A Biological Psychiatrist Wins the Nobel
content:
O

ne could be forgiven for feeling wary rather than celebratory this October when

Stanford University neuroscientist and psychiatrist Karl Deisseroth

, along with two German scientists,

received the Nobel Prize

 for inventing a new, invasive brain technology dubbed “optogenetics.”


After all, the last time a psychiatric treatment garnered a Nobel Prize for Physiology or Medicine was in 1949—for the lobotomy technique of severing the arteries into the brain’s frontal lobes. The award further boosted excitement among psychiatrists worldwide, who ultimately administered lobotomies to tens of thousands of people (often by, infamously, hammering an icepick through both eye sockets) as a “calming treatment” for hundreds of different mental and emotional conditions. Mainstream psychiatry later moved on from lobotomies with the emergence of new drugs. But

protest campaigns

 led by family members of lobotomized patients continued for decades as they tried (in vain) to get the Nobel Foundation to rescind its award for a practice that had killed an estimated 5 percent of patients and left countless others permanently stripped of major emotional, mental, and functional capacities.


So, in 2026, is optogenetics biological psychiatry’s long-sought breakthrough for understanding and rectifying dysfunction in the mechanisms of the brain? Or is it another damaging, dangerous tool? Reading some of the leading researchers in the field reveals that it could be a bit of both.


Karl Deisseroth: From Poetic Emoting to Policing Emotion


To understand the roots and likely future of this “revolutionary” new brain technology, it helps to first understand a little about its founder and leading developer.


In his book,

Projections: A Story of Human Emotions

, and in a wide-ranging, three-hour

interview

 with computer scientist Lex Fridman, Karl Deisseroth shows his appreciation for both scientific and artistic ways of viewing the human condition.


Alongside his neuroscientific research, Deisseroth works in both hospital inpatient and private outpatient psychiatric practice, and writes literary nonfiction. He believes in the value of talk therapy, is interested in extreme states of consciousness, frequently fuels his thinking with poets and novelists such as Jorge Luis Borges, Toni Morrison, and James Joyce and, when describing his conversations with his patients, uses words like “empathy” and “communion.”


Karl Deisseroth. Photo by Cmichel67, CC BY-SA 4.0


Yet Deisseroth also writes that he was “trained to see brains as biological objects, as they indeed are.” He describes many of those same patients as having “diseases” or “disorders” of the brain, and not infrequently authorizes that they be involuntarily committed and forcibly drugged against their protests. And he appears to have no serious sociological or scientific critique of common psychiatric research and practices. For example, he regularly discusses the lack of reliable lab tests in psychiatry to verify any diagnoses or positive emotional impacts from treatments, yet he also describes electroconvulsive shock therapy (ECT) as “very effective” for depression—with no acknowledgement of the

dearth

 of quality scientific evidence supporting such a view. He describes lithium as “highly effective for bipolar”—despite

broad scientific questions about such claims

. And he says studies in twins have proven that depression, bipolar, and other mental disorders have major genetic drivers—with no acknowledgement of the

scientific gaps and biases

 common in twin and other behavioral genetics studies.


One of many stories from Deisseroth’s book that vividly illustrate these seemingly contradictory tendencies is that of a 67-year-old retired insurance executive he calls Alexander. After witnessing the 9/11 attacks on the World Trade Center, the man becomes swept up in a whirlwind of new interests and activities, hoping to find ways to help his country. Alexander’s family is worried about these dramatic changes and get into conflicts with him, but Alexander himself regards what’s happening as exciting, positive, a revitalizing surge of youthful energy, and a new, more meaningful lease on life. Deisseroth reflects on how a similar experience came over him after a rush to escape an armed robbery left him hyper-energized for weeks. Deisseroth also relates Alexander’s impassioned convictions and behaviors to those of literary figures, historical leaders, and mythical heroes of …

author: Tam Saavedra
title: ¡Las Directrices de la CDPD de la ONU sobre Interseccionalidad están aquí!
content:
Las Directrices de la CDPD de la ONU sobre Interseccionalidad acaban de cambiar las reglas del juego para los derechos de las personas con discapacidad: Esto es lo que necesitas saber

 


¡Grandes noticias para las mujeres con discapacidad y para todas las personas defensoras, aliadas y organizaciones feministas y con discapacidad en todo el mundo!

 


Durante su 35º Período de Sesiones en agosto de 2026, el

Comité de las Naciones Unidas sobre los Derechos de las Personas con Discapacidad

 (CDPD de la ONU)

 adoptó oficialmente las

Directrices sobre la Identificación y Abordaje de la Discriminación Interseccional Contra las Niñas, Adolescentes, Mujeres y Mujeres Mayores con Discapacidad

.

 


Este hito representa un paso gigante para los derechos de las personas con discapacidad. Por primera vez, los Estados Partes cuentan con orientación explícita y accionable para respaldar sus obligaciones en la intersección entre género y discapacidad.

 


Lee las Directrices oficiales de la CDPD de la ONU aquí

 


¿Qué son las Directrices de la CDPD sobre Discriminación Interseccional?

 


Las Directrices constituyen un marco internacional autorizado, desarrollado por la CDPD de la ONU, para ayudar a los Estados a prevenir, supervisar y abordar de mejor manera la discriminación interseccional.

 


A lo largo de años de procesos de revisión de países por parte de la CDPD de la ONU, el Comité identificó una brecha persistente y crítica:

los derechos humanos específicos de las mujeres con discapacidad y la discriminación interseccional y compleja que experimentan, rara vez son comprendidas o abordadas por los gobiernos.

 


Al celebrar el 20º aniversario de la CDPD de la ONU

, e

stas Directrices fueron emitidas para cerrar esa brecha, garantizando que la convención se aplique a favor de

todas

las mujeres y niñas con discapacidad, y las personas de género diverso con discapacidad a lo largo de sus vidas.

 


¿Por qué estas Directrices cambian las reglas del juego?

 


Los documentos internacionales rara vez se centran de forma explícita en las experiencias de vida y los derechos de las mujeres con discapacidad. Estas Directrices nombran y explican las barreras sistémicas que las mujeres y personas de género diverso con discapacidad enfrentan a diario en todo el mundo, incluyendo:

 


Salud y Derechos Sexuales y Reproductivos (SDSR):

 Abordar y prevenir la esterilización forzada, la anticoncepción forzada, la falta de atención médica accesible, las restricciones al aborto y la falta de atención perinatal, menstrual y menopáusica.

 


Violencia de Género y Basada en la Discapacidad:

 Exponer la violencia institucional, el abuso digital/en línea y la falta generalizada de servicios de apoyo para las víctimas.

 


Reconocimiento de las labores de cuidado:

 Validar a las mujeres con discapacidad como cuidadoras activas y madres, en lugar de tratarlas únicamente como receptoras de cuidados.

 


Exclusión económica y educativa:

 Destacar las barreras en el mercado laboral y la exclusión de la educación durante la pubertad.

 


Respuesta a crisis y cambio climático:

 Combatir la exclusión agravada durante desastres ambientales, emergencias climáticas y esfuerzos de ayuda humanitaria.

 


Por nombrar sólo algunas.

 


7 avances clave en el enfoque de las Directrices

 


Lo que hace que este documento sea un instrumento transformador único es su enfoque estructural y progresista:

 


Inclusión explícita de la diversidad de género:

 Las Directrices abarcan explícitamente los derechos de las personas transgénero, intersexuales, no binarias y de otras diversidades de género con discapacidad, y solicitan una interpretación inclusiva de la diversidad de género de todas las obligaciones descritas.

 


Reconocimiento de las raíces históricas:

 El Comité aborda explícitamente el legado y los impactos continuos del colonialismo y la esclavización, estableciendo que los Estados que se benefician de estos sistemas históricos tienen la responsabilidad particular de reparar sus efectos actuales.

 


Un catálogo abierto de diversidad:

 El texto reconoce que las mujeres con discapacidad pertenecen a comunidades multimarginalizadas —incluidos grupos indígenas, afrodescendientes/negros, dalit, adivasi, refugiados, solicitantes de asilo, minorías religiosas, pastoriles o personas que viven en asentamientos informales, entre otros— dejando espacio para todas las identidades interseccionales.

author: Sara Luterman
title: Nursing Home Residents Have a Right to Vote — Despite What Trump CMS Agency Says
content:
The Nursing Home Reform Act of 1987 requires facilities to support their residents in exercising their rights.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

Cindy Napolitan and her daughter Melissa have multiple sclerosis, a degenerative condition in which the immune system attacks the brain, spinal cord and nerves. They have lived together at a nursing home in Mesquite, Texas, for nine years. In previous elections, Cindy and Melissa Napolitan voted by mail, but this year they took an unusual step: They voted in person. They worried their mail-in ballots — and even their in-person votes — may not be counted.

“I’ve never worried like this before. I’ve never worried that I don’t have the proper ID. I’ve never worried that somebody is going to intimidate me. Will I encounter somebody that’s going to threaten me or make me feel less than? So yeah, I’m very worried, and I shouldn’t be,” Cindy Napolitan said. “I shouldn’t have to be worried about stuff like that. This is the 19th Amendment. I’m allowed to vote.”

Nursing home residents are guaranteed the right to vote. Around two-thirds of all nursing home residents in the United States are women, making aging and long-term care gendered issues.

There is no data on how many nursing home residents exercise that right. Cindy, 70, and Melissa Napolitan, 48, at least, feel like they’ve had good experiences with voting at their facility. Cindy Napolitan, in particular, has worked with the activities coordinator to organize rides to the polls for her, her daughter and other interested residents.

“We are scheduled to go on the first day of early voting. So in case there are any issues that we come across, we still have time to rectify the situation and be allowed to vote,” Cindy Napolitan said.

Cindy and Melissa Napolitan are more concerned this year than in previous years about government interference and voter suppression. Their fears are not unfounded: Experts and advocates for the rights of nursing home residents, older adults and people with disabilities are worried too.

In July, the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services rescinded previous guidance affirming that nursing home residents have the right to vote.

“The memo does not alter the underlying law. Nursing homes are governed by the Nursing Home Reform Act of 1987 and its implementing regulations,” said Nina Kohn, a professor at Syracuse University and expert on elder law. “That law still requires facilities to support their residents in exercising their rights as Americans.”

The memo also emphasized voter fraud in nursing homes, specifically around mail-in ballots. For years, President Trump has disparaged mail-in ballots, insisting without evidence that fraudulent votes by mail had a role in his loss during the 2020 presidential election. His comments have led to some states restricting who can use a mail-in ballot and in what contexts.

According to experts, including Kohn, there is no evidence that voter fraud is a serious or widespread problem in nursing homes. Instead, Kohn is concerned about the chilling effect that it may have on residents’ rights.

“The language in the memo itself is intimidating, and it may understandably make staff think that they could face criminal prosecution or be in some other form of legal trouble if they help residents vote,” Kohn said.

Cindy and Melissa Napolitan do everything together — and on Monday, they voted together. They are also roommates at the facility; most people living in nursing homes are assigned roommates who are strangers.

“Unlike other people that have roommates that don’t get along, I’m very lucky and fortunate that I have somebody that loves me and I love her,” Cindy Napolitan said.

This is the second time Cindy and Melissa Napolitan have voted in person since entering a nursing home. The first time was during the 2024 presidential election.

“I’ve been checking my status weekly to make sure that I haven’t been dropped off the voter rolls, making sure my daughter and I don’t have some sort of issue that says that we can’t vote,” Cindy Napolitan said.

People living in nursing homes and other long-term care facilities face specific barriers. Some residents may need assistance filling out their ballots because they lack the movement or dexterity to hold a pen or press buttons on a computer screen. People with dexterity or coordination issues may also be unable to produce the same signature twice …

author: Mostafa Hosny
title: ‘Citizens’ health’ session at Egypt Forum 2026 boasts spending success with no mention of declining hospital bed numbers
content:
On Tuesday, the second day of Egypt Forum 2026, Health Minister Khaled Abdel Ghaffar described the political leadership’s support for the healthcare sector as unprecedented.


Speaking at the “citizen’s health”

session

 of Egypt Forum 2026, he said the approach dated back to the beginning of President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi’s presidency in 2014, when, he

said,

 Egypt faced a massive “disease burden,” with a lack of data and years of inadequate budget allocations that had failed to meet developmental ambitions for the system, particularly as population growth accelerated.


The minister said the state’s development plan had delivered gains in the sector, citing 16 presidential initiatives that had benefited 95 million citizens at a cost of LE44 billion. 


Abdel Ghaffar stressed that success in healthcare should not be measured by spending levels, but by the results citizens ultimately experience.


Mada Masr looked into some of those results, drawing from government

data

 published by the Central Agency for Public Mobilization and Statistics (CAPMAS).


One clear result over the time period is the notable decline in the number of beds in public hospitals between 2013 and 2024, with a drop from around 98,291 to 84,225. 


Over the same period, the number of beds in private hospitals rose from 26,009 to 36,014. 


Still, the combined total of beds in public and private hospitals fell from 124,300 in 2013 to 120,239 in 2024.


While Abdel Ghaffar portrayed inadequate budget allocations as a problem of the past, the state

has consistently fallen short

 of the constitutionally mandated minimum for healthcare spending.

 Article 18 of the Constitution requires the state to allocate at least three percent of gross national product to public healthcare starting in FY 2016/17 and gradually increase spending over time. The state has not met this threshold since the Constitution was adopted in 2014. Since then, healthcare spending has not exceeded 1.7 percent of GNP in most years.


The government allocated 1.51 percent of GNP to healthcare in the current fiscal year’s budget, half the constitutional minimum. 


Meanwhile, the government has

introduced

 a different method for calculating budget allocations that allows it to claim it is meeting the minimum spending threshold.

 


Rather than using its previous classification, which was based on the Health Ministry’s expenditure, the government now uses a “broader and more comprehensive” definition. Under this new definition, healthcare expenditure also encompasses spending by a number of off-budget economic authorities and companies as well as “any other entities providing healthcare services, such as police and military hospitals, Al-Azhar hospitals, the comprehensive health insurance system and its associated programs,” a Finance Ministry source previously told Mada Masr. Without publicly available data on these entities’ healthcare spending, it is impossible to verify whether they bring total annual healthcare spending to the constitutionally mandated minimum.


The same expansion of what constitutes annual “health spending” also allows the government to include the budgetary allocation for these entities’ debt repayments as investment in the sector, according to the same source.


The president

confessed

 three years ago that the state is not meeting the constitutional requirements, saying in a public address that “the required numbers aren’t available, folks.”

 His comment came days after the government’s assertion that it was meeting the required spending levels.


Aside from its commentary on expenditure, the government’s Egypt Forum 2026 also highlighted the Universal Health Insurance System, one of the leading presidential health initiatives.


Egypt’s Healthcare Authority head, Ahmed al-Sobky,

described

 the system as a comprehensive reform of Egypt’s healthcare sector, capping an “enormous leap forward” under Sisi, following earlier historic transformations under King Fouad I and former President Gamal Abdel Nasser.


Shortly before the forum, the government began promoting the second phase of the Universal Health Insurance System, launching a pilot phase in Minya Governorate. 


The first phase launch in the governorates of Port Said, Ismailia, Suez, South Sinai, Luxor and Aswan began in 2018 and was

completed

 in 2025.

author: Unknown
title: Ulus: Healthcare must be free and accessible to all
content:
Structural problems in public hospitals and shortcomings in healthcare services are making it increasingly difficult for citizens to access medical care. People struggling to secure appointments through the Central Physician Appointment System (MHRS) sometimes have to wait at least 15 days just to submit an appointment request. Patients who eventually manage to obtain appointments after considerable effort must then try to explain their health problems within limited consultation times due to overcrowding in hospitals.


Difficulties in securing appointments and restrictions on consultation times are further deepening problems concerning the quality and accessibility of healthcare services.


Mehmet Nuri Ulus, Co-Chair of the Diyarbakır (Amed) Branch of the Health and Social Service Workers’ Union (SES), spoke to ANF about the problems facing public hospitals.


‘Healthcare is not being transformed, it is going backwards’


Ulus recalled that the Justice and Development Party (AKP) government has introduced healthcare reform and transformation programmes since 2002. He said that the policies implemented in recent years have caused serious problems in healthcare services and continued: “The AKP government has announced numerous programmes under the names of healthcare reform and healthcare transformation. However, particularly over the past 10 to 15 years, what has been called healthcare transformation has, from our perspective, meant collapse and regression. We have experienced both the COVID-19 pandemic and the earthquake during this period. These major crises showed us just how inadequate the healthcare system was in responding to the problems that arose.


The healthcare system should have been prepared for these crises and should have had the capacity to meet society's healthcare needs. Healthcare is a service that must be provided within the framework of the social welfare state. Everyone must be able to receive healthcare services equally, accessibly and in their mother tongue.


However, in recent years, we have seen healthcare services increasingly turn into a system in which those who have money can access care more easily. The proliferation of private hospitals is one aspect of this. Another is the emergence of an approach in which even public hospitals link faster access to certain tests, radiological examinations, medical reports and surgical procedures to payment. This undermines the principle that healthcare services should be equal for everyone.”


‘Physical queues have been replaced by virtual queues’


Ulus addressed the appointment crisis in the healthcare system, pointing out that the queues once seen outside hospitals now continue through the Central Physician Appointment System. He said appointment systems should make healthcare more accessible, but many citizens are currently unable to secure appointments.


Ulus said: “The AKP government used to say that people had to go to hospitals early in the morning and wait in queues to see a doctor. Today, physical queues have been replaced by virtual queues. Instead of waiting for hours outside hospitals, people now try to book appointments on their phones or online. However, when you access the system, you cannot find an available appointment. The queues have therefore not disappeared; they have simply changed form. Citizens now find themselves waiting in front of digital systems to access healthcare.


People face serious difficulties securing appointments, particularly in departments such as ear, nose and throat, ophthalmology and dermatology. Citizens who cannot obtain appointments are then forced to turn to private hospitals. However, considering the economic crisis, the struggle to make ends meet and the housing problems in Turkey, not everyone has the financial means to seek treatment at private hospitals.


As a result, the inability to access healthcare has become another dimension of economic hardship. Healthcare should be free and accessible, yet citizens are forced to stretch their financial resources to obtain the medical care they need.”


‘The budget is not allocated to preventive healthcare services’


Ulus said that the problems facing the healthcare system are not limited to difficulties in securing appointments. He drew attention to the following issues: “When we look at the Ministry of Health's budget and healthcare policies, we see that preventive healthcare services are consistently pushed into the background.
