author: India McKinney
title: Computer Security Is About to Get a Lot Worse, Here’s What You Can Do
content:
It is a commonly held truth among computer geeks that there is no such thing as bug free software, or a secure computer. Any piece of software that anyone actually uses

will have a security vulnerability somewhere in the code

. The more complex that software is, the more likely there will be a vulnerability. Fortunately for everyone, finding severe vulnerabilities was generally considered an expensive and difficult task requiring years of training and deep knowledge of how computers and software worked. Until recently there was a steady background hum of vulnerabilities being found and patched, with major vulnerabilities that could cripple the entire internet only happening every few years. Now that is no longer the case. 

 


You may have noticed your nerdiest friends freaking out about the “Vulnerability Apocalypse” this week and waving their arms in panic about something called PHP. You may have also noticed that some of your favorite websites were down for a bit. In the last two weeks of October alone, there have been multiple, potentially internet-breaking vulnerabilities reported and patched. Many of those vulnerabilities were in the open-source software that is the foundation of the vast majority of the internet.


For more detailed information on what happened, and why supporting open-source projects matters, 

check out our other blog

.


This is all because frontier AI models, such as those created by OpenAI, Anthropic, and others, have made it incredibly cheap and easy to find previously unknown vulnerabilities (zero-days) in open- and closed-source code.

Three percent of all software vulnerabilities ever found in history were found just in the month of October. This year alone researchers have found nearly a quarter of all software security issues which have ever been discovered.

 


If exploiting critical software is now cheaper and easier than ever, what does that mean for us as individuals and what does that mean for society as a whole?

TL; DR

: It’s going to get worse before it gets better. But you can protect yourself with basic digital security hygiene that is now more important than ever. 

 


What Do I Need to Do?

 


There absolutely needs to be a bigger conversation about how we got here and how to fix the systemic issues involved, including how corporations that depend on open-source code should contribute to their upkeep, and how big tech should be regulated. 

 


But for now, this news is a compelling reason to tighten up your digital hygiene.

A lot of computers are going to get hacked a lot more often, and unfortunately, it isn’t going to get better any time soon.

Thankfully, EFF has compiled a comprehensive set of security advice in

our Surveillance Self-Defense guides

.


To start

,

we recommend making sure your browser and all applications are

always up to date

 with the latest patches.  

 


You should also consider installing a tracker blocking tool, like EFF’s

Privacy Badger (now on Safari),

 and remain vigilant for

phishing attempts

. Additionally,

install a password manager

 and

use unique passwords

 for each website, so that if one site is compromised, the rest of your passwords are safe. You should also be aware that

data breaches

 may now be more likely, and the websites you visit may experience more attacks than usual, which means that some services may be disrupted.

 


If you host a blog or other website, make sure that either you or your hosting provider has

patched

 this particular issue. 

 


For additional tips on protecting yourself and others, head over to our

Surveillance Self-Defense site

. Additionally, if you’d like to support any of EFF’s open-source projects like

Privacy Badger

,

Rayhunter

, and

Certbot

, visit our

donate page

.

author: Keelan Jacobs
title: Few details released as First Nations–First Ministers meeting approaches
content:
With the first dedicated

 First Nations–First Ministers Meeting (FN-FMM)

 set for Monday, a number of key issues are still being worked out with the Prime Minister’s Office, according to the Assembly of First Nations. 


On Friday, chiefs gathered in downtown Ottawa to discuss strategy and rehearse speeches ahead of the meeting. 


The gathering is scheduled for Oct. 26 on unceded Algonquin territory in Ottawa, preceded by a day of ceremony on Sunday. 


Prime Minister Mark Carney, provincial and territorial premiers and a limited First Nations delegation are expected to discuss rights, treaties, jurisdiction, economic partnerships, major projects and other shared priorities. 


The main table is reported to seat 28 people, with additional First Nations invitees outside that room.


In an interview with APTN News on Friday, AFN National Chief Cindy Woodhouse Nepinak said First Nations have waited a long time for a seat at this table.


“I’m sorry that it took 119 years to get to this point, and hopefully it doesn’t take another 119 years, that it’s not a one-and-done,” Woodhouse Nepinak said. “We are thankful for rights holders, Elders, and provincial delegations traveling from across the country. We’re also looking forward to Sunday’s ceremony.”


The government once banned First Nation ceremonies, she noted. She framed the moment against a longer history of First Nations standing with Canada through wars, the pandemic and recent unity votes.


“The trust is very fragile, and the relationship is very fragile,” she said. “This is another one of those times where we can really make things or break things.”


Asked about her highest priority coming from the meeting with Carney and the premiers, Woodhouse Nepinak returned to permanence.


“To make sure that this isn’t a one and done, because one meeting isn’t going to solve 119 years of FMM meetings, but even before that, since the creation of this country,” she said. 


She said First Nations are the original landowners “of every square inch of this country,” and have traditionally been partners in its creation without receiving the corresponding respect.


COO-Grand-Chief-Abram-Benedict in 2025. Photo by APTN.


Abram Benedict, chief of the Chiefs of Ontario, told APTN everything is still evolving.  


“The agenda is still an evolving document,” he said. “Our regions will have an opportunity to make three-minute opening remarks and reflections.” 


“There are still some negotiations happening on who’s doing opening remarks overall for the entire forum,” he added. “There has been a request for additional time for the regions to speak. So right now we have three minutes per region. They’re going to try to push that up a little bit. Some of the logistical information has not all been solidified yet, and we’re doing the best as we receive that to share that with the leadership.”


Benedict said his region’s high-level ask is to advance the relationship under Section 35 of the Constitution, including the treaty relationship with Ontario and Canada, and to establish a trilateral process to support nations on program delivery and jurisdiction issues that will continue after Monday’s meeting.


Relations between First Nations and Ontario Premier Doug Ford have been strained since the passing of Bill 5 – the Protect Ontario by Unleashing our Economy Act, that gives the province sweeping powers to ignore laws to get infrastructure projects built. 


It’s expected that Carney’s proposed Building Canada Strong Act will get a lot of attention. Like Ontario’s building law – it will give the federal cabinet massive powers to push projects “of national interest” through the regulatory phase while ignoring laws that protect the environment. 


Recently, Carney added the proposed Pacific Link pipeline as a national interest project. It will carry Alberta bitumen to the B.C. coast. Carney said there was two months of “rigorous” consultation but chiefs along the pipeline route complained Canada came to the table with little information. 


Another issue that may be raised was contained in a draft AFN paper obtained by APTN. It proposes a First Nations National Benefits Sharing Framework and a First Nations-controlled sovereign wealth fund fed in part by contributions from projects of national interest, both leaders were measured.


Woodhouse Nepinak said there is no commitment yet.

title: Eski SPK Daire Başkanı Erman Çete hakkında gözaltı kararı
content:
Eski Sermaye Piyasası Kurulu (SPK) Daire Başkanı Erman Çete hakkında İstanbul Cumhuriyet Başsavcılığınca yürütülen fon soruşturması kapsamında gözaltı kararı çıkarıldı. Ayrıca Çete'nin mal varlığına tedbir kararı da istendi. Çete'nin henüz gözaltına alınmadığı bildirildi.

Soruşturma kapsamında eski SPK Başkanı İbrahim Ömer Gönül hakkında da işlem yapılmıştı. İstanbul Cumhuriyet Başsavcılığı, Gönül hakkında "görevi kötüye kullanma" suçlaması kapsamında soruşturma yürütülebilmesi için Hazine ve Maliye Bakanlığına başvurmuştu. Hazine ve Maliye Bakanı Mehmet Şimşek, yapılan ön incelemenin ardından 14 Ekim'de Gönül hakkında soruşturma izni vermişti. Gönül, 30 Eylül'de de soruşturma kapsamında şüpheli sıfatıyla savcılığa ifade vermişti.

title: Merinos işçisinden sosyal medya yasağına tepki: Köle değil, işçiyiz!
content:
Biz Merinos’ta gecesini gündüzüne katıp alın teri döken işçiyiz. Fabrikada zaten hakkımızı ararken binbir türlü zorluk yaşıyoruz, şimdi bir de elimizdeki telefonu, kişisel sosyal medya hesaplarımızı kontrol altına almak istiyorlar. Biz patronun niyetini çok iyi biliyoruz. Amaç içeride yaşadığımız haksızlıkları, ağır çalışma koşullarını veya bir iş kazasını dışarıya duyurmamızı engellemek istiyor. Yarın bir gün haksızlığa ses çıkardığımızda, bizi tazminatsız işten atmak için şimdiden kılıf hazırlıyor. Hatta işten ayrılsak bile arkasından konuşmayalım diye gözdağı veriyorlar. Bu kağıdı imzalatmalarında, iş yerindeki ağır çalışma koşullarının sosyal medyada paylaşılmasının ve bundan dolayı da yeni işçi alımlarında işçi bulmakta zorlanmalarının etkisi de var.

Bu taahhütnameyle bizi tamamen susturmak istiyorlar. ‘Hakaret, iftira, yanıltıcı bilgi’ diyerek tazminatsız işten atılmanın altyapısını oluşturuyorlar. Düşük zam karşısında yapacağımız grevlerin önünü kesmek istiyorlar. Haksızlıklar karşısında basına, sendikaya ya da sosyal medyaya açıklama yapmamızı engellemek istiyorlar. ‘İşten ayrıldıktan sonra da benim kölemsin’ anlamına geliyor. Yani biri işten ayrılsa bile, Merinos hakkında tek kelime edemeyecek. Haksız şekilde işten atılsa hakkını arayamayacak. Hak arayan, taahhütnamedeki kurallara uymayan işçiler de tazminatsız işten atılmakla, şirkete tazminat ödemekle tehdit ediliyor.

Ama bu belgenin hukuki bir geçerliliği yok, biliyoruz. Tamamen bizi korkutmak için yapılan bir uygulama. Biz köle değiliz, işçiyiz. Anayasal hakkımız olan ifade özgürlüğümüzün ve hak arama hürriyetimizin elimizden alınmasını kabul etmiyoruz. Sendikamızın ve basının bu sansür dayatmasına karşı sesimizi duymasını ve yanımızda durmasını istiyoruz.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: Caio de Freitas
title: PF acha nota de Willer Tomaz citando indiciado no caso Abin Paralela e “180 mil dólares”
content:
Uma anotação salva no aplicativo de notas usado pelo advogado Willer Tomaz de Souza, amigo do candidato a presidente Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), chamou a atenção dos investigadores da Polícia Federal (PF).

A nota continha um valor de “180 mil dólares” (R$ 908 mil, na cotação atual) atrelado às palavras “Corregedoria”, “Agosto/21” e ao nome Paulo Maurício Fortunato.


Naquele mesmo mês, Paulo Fortunato havia deixado o comando do Departamento de Operações de Inteligência (DOINT) da Agência Brasileira de Inteligência (Abin) do governo de Jair Bolsonaro, em um período de atividade da chamada “Abin Paralela”, como ficou conhecido o grupo que fazia uso, principalmente, do DOINT para comandar buscas contra adversários políticos, e até mesmo aliados, de Jair Bolsonaro (PL) por meio do

software

 israelense de espionagem First Mile – o que a PF classificou como “organização criminosa”.


Ao resumir as acusações contra Paulo Fortunato, o

relatório final da PF

 no caso “Abin Paralela” aponta que “o DOINT, sob sua direção [Fortunato], era a unidade central para a execução de buscas no sistema First Mile”, com “uso da estrutura para fins políticos e a perseguição de servidores”. A PF apontou que Fortunato teria sido “a autoridade demandante e o principal gestor da aquisição do sistema First Mile” em 26 de dezembro de 2018, nos últimos dias de governo Michel Temer (MDB) – imputação negada pela defesa de Fortunato, segundo apurado pela

Agência Pública

.


Para os investigadores, o ex-diretor da Abin “omitiu-se dolosamente no seu dever de implementar controles efetivos sobre o uso do First Mile e evitar a execução de ações clandestinas no DOINT. Sua omissão foi crucial para a continuidade das atividades clandestinas” e que “havia conhecimento, desde a origem, da ‘real natureza’ e das ‘características intrusivas’ da ferramenta

, que permitiam a localização de dispositivos móveis sem autorização judicial por meio de interceptação de sinais, explorando vulnerabilidades do sistema de telefonia nacional”.


Segundo a PF, o DOINT “era o principal demandante e utilizador da ferramenta para monitorar alvos de interesse da ORCRIM [organização criminosa], incluindo políticos, jornalistas, advogados e servidores públicos, muitas vezes sem amparo em investigações formais ou finalidades institucionais legítimas”. Como já se sabe hoje,

um dos alvos

 foi a então repórter da

Agência Pública

 Alice Maciel.


Em 2025, Fortunato foi indiciado pela PF por seu suposto envolvimento com a Abin Paralela, pelos crimes de organização criminosa, realizar interceptação de comunicações sem autorização judicial ou com objetivos não autorizados em lei, peculato, prevaricação de forma continuada e violação de sigilo funcional. Ele foi desligado oficialmente do governo somente

em 9 de janeiro deste ano

, com a conclusão do processo administrativo disciplinar contra ele por parte da Controladoria-Geral da União (CGU).

O que dizem Paulo Fortunato e Willer Tomaz


O advogado responsável pela defesa do ex-diretor da Abin, Oscar Luís de Morais, disse à

Pública

 que a decisão da CGU foi “protocolar”, pois referia-se a um processo de exoneração de cargo em comissão na Abin. “O próprio senhor Paulo Maurício Fortunato pediu seu afastamento do órgão após a operação da Polícia Federal em outubro de 2023, e à época ele já estava aposentado, após 38 anos de serviço público sem qualquer registro de punição disciplinar durante sua carreira”, disse, acrescentando que ele é inocente no caso Abin Paralela e que seus atos à frente do DOINT se respaldam em um parecer técnico elaborado pelo próprio órgão de inteligência à época. 


“Não tem nenhum ato que implique ele a não ser os atos de ofício, determinados por seus superiores naquele período”, afirmou. Além disso,

a defesa alega que o ex-diretor da Abin “não conhece, nem tem qualquer relação com os senhores Willer Tomaz e Flávio Bolsonaro” e desconhece qualquer contato do ex-diretor da Abin com o escritório de Willer Tomaz.

author: Daron Letts
title: Hudson Bay MLA raises alarm over proposed Port of Churchill expansion
content:
Newly

elected

 Hudson Bay MLA Jason Iqaluq hit the ground running during his first week representing his Sanikiluaq constiuents in the

fall session

 of the legislative assembly.


When it was his turn to question Premier John Main on Friday, Iqaluq raised an alarm over his community’s concerns about proposed upgrades to the Port of Churchill, located about 900 kilometres northwest in Manitoba.


“This project has the potential to have impacts on the Hudson Bay ecosystem and the waters surrounding Sanikiluaq,” Iqaluq said.


He was following up on correspondence shared with the government in May by his predecessor, Daniel Qavvik, who resigned from the legislature in June, spurring t

he Sept. 28 byelection in which Iqaluq was elected.


Iqaluq pressed the Premier for a response to the correspondence before the end of the fall session on Nov. 5.


Main assured Iqaluq the government would reply prior to that date.


The project, dubbed Port of Churchill Plus, was referred to the federal government’s new

Major Projects Office

 in September 2025,

 which means it has the ability to speed up the permitting process.


The project seeks to upgrade the Port of Churchill, Canada’s only deep-water Arctic port, and “expand trade corridors with an all-weather road, an upgraded rail line, a new energy corridor, and marine ice-breaking capacity,” according to the federal government’s website.


While Nunavut is not a direct proponent of the project, the territory is a stakeholder, Main said.


“It is an exciting time to look at the concept of strengthening transport links to benefit Nunavut residents,” Main said. “Nunavut needs to be connected to the rest of the country.”


However, Main said he agrees it’s important Nunavummiut’s environmental concerns be heard during the process.


Iqaluq followed up by asking if the Nunavut Impact Review Board would have an opportunity to assess the project.


Main said that would be clarified in the government’s written response later in the session.


“As it is a transboundary issue, it’s quite complex,” he said.


Iqalu

q said he was satisfied with Main’s response to his question, in an interview in his office following the session.


However, he does not share Main’s optimism for the project.


“If it scares off wildlife, it is definitely going to be a bad thing for our community,” Iqaluq said.

“We have to make sure that nothing is going to be disturbed.”

author: Rafael Custódio
title: ‘Judicialização freestyle’ de Kassio mira Exército do Lula e ajuda Flávio, diz professor
content:
A dois dias do

segundo turno

, o Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE) atuou para impedir que fosse derrubado o principal canal de comunicação da campanha digital de reeleição do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) — o Exército do Lula.

O ministro Floriano de Azevedo Marques ordenou nesta sexta-feira, 23 de outubro, que Kassio Nunes Marques, que comanda a Corte, se abstenha de suspender por via administrativa o canal de WhatsApp, criado e administrado pelo deputado federal André Janones (Rede).


Floriano escreveu que a presidência do TSE não tem competência para tirar do ar canais de pessoas físicas e viu o risco de abuso de poder. A resposta veio após um pedido do presidente da Corte, na última quinta-feira, 22 de outubro, para que a Meta – dona do Instagram, Facebook e WhatsApp –, o Google e o X (antigo Twitter) entregassem um relatório sobre a atuação do canal Exército do Lula, que reúne quase 10 milhões de pessoas. O prazo vence no início da noite desta sexta-feira, 23 de outubro. 


A decisão de Nunes Marques foi avaliada como “desastrosa” pelo professor Afonso Albuquerque, do curso de Estudos de Mídia da Universidade Federal Fluminense (UFF).

“[O TSE] atribui a uma empresa privada estrangeira o poder de produzir diagnóstico capaz de orientar a vida pública no Brasil”

, criticou. 


Professor Afonso Albuquerque, do curso de Estudos de Mídia da Universidade Federal Fluminense (UFF)


O docente também descreveu como “judicialização freestyle” a forma como o principal órgão eleitoral do país tem atuado, por estabelecer um desequilíbrio na forma como analisa os movimentos das duas campanhas eleitorais e por favorecer a campanha de Flávio Bolsonaro (PL). 


O canal de Janones entrou na mira de Nunes Marques após o fim do primeiro turno, depois que a campanha do candidato Flávio

pediu

 a suspensão do grupo por suposta disseminação de desinformação – fato que não foi constatado por peritos do próprio TSE. A equipe do candidato do PL também foi responsável pelo pedido ao ministro para que as plataformas fornecessem um relatório completo sobre a atuação do Exército do Lula, que estaria promovendo ações coordenadas. 


Às 10h12 desta sexta-feira, 23 de outubro, Janones avisou aos seguidores do canal de que eles estavam prestes a perder o lugar que os reunia. No Exército do Lula, o parlamentar mineiro disse que a página “deverá sair do ar ainda hoje” e que seria perto do horário do último debate entre presidenciáveis, que será realizado nesta noite na TV Globo, e que o pedido teria vindo do TSE. 


Com o anúncio de uma suposta restrição, os integrantes do grupo começaram a se mobilizar nas redes sociais, por conta própria, e disparar hashtags que apontavam para uma possível censura administrada por Nunes Marques. 


Uma minuta de resolução – que proibiria canais com mais de 200 mil seguidores nas 48 horas anteriores à votação – chegou a circular entre os ministros, mas foi abandonada por falta de maioria. 


A reportagem procurou o TSE que “não determinou a retirada de nenhum canal de WhatsApp do ar. Os prazos dos processos de propaganda são sempre curtos. Ilações a partir desses despachos que pedem informação em tempo curto são absolutamente indevidos.” 


A nota acrescentou ainda que “na manhã de hoje, os ministros da propaganda do TSE se reuniram  com as plataformas Meta, X, Google, TikTok e Kwai. Em pauta, as providências para o atendimento da legislação eleitoral. O ministro Kassio Nunes Marques, pediu reforço de pessoal e atuação isonômica por parte das plataformas a fim de garantir o cumprimento do plano de conformidade assinado por todas as empresas.”


A

Agência Pública

 entrevistou o professor Afonso Albuquerque, leia as principais respostas aqui.

title: Boğaziçi'nde Nurettin Yıldız protestosu davasında gazeteci Öztürk'e beraat, 14 öğrenciye ceza talebi
content:
Mayıs 2025'te  Boğaziçi Üniversitesi'ndeki protesto sırasında gözaltına alınan 14 öğrenci ve T24 muhabiri Can Öztürk'ün yargılandığı davanın beşinci duruşmasında savcı esas hakkındaki mütalaasını sundu.


Medya ve Hukuk Çalışmaları Derneği'nden (MLSA) Canan Coşkun'un haberine göre İstanbul 69. Asliye Ceza Mahkemesi'ndeki duruşmada savcı, dosyadaki görüntülerde Can Öztürk'ün protestoyu görüntülediğinin anlaşıldığını belirterek suçlamaların kanıtlanamadığını bildirdi.


Mütalaada, Öztürk'ün cezalandırılması için “her türlü şüpheden uzak kesin ve inandırıcı delil” elde edilemediği belirtilerek beraatine karar verilmesi talep edildi.


Öztürk, Mayıs 2025'te Boğaziçi Üniversitesi'ndeki protestoyu takip ederken polisler tarafından gözaltına alınmış, daha sonra yurt dışına çıkış yasağı ve karakola imza verme yükümlülüğüyle serbest bırakılmıştı.


14 öğrenciye dört ayrı suçlama


Savcı, protestoya katılan 14 öğrencinin ise polislerin oluşturduğu güvenlik hattına yüklenerek bazı polislerin inşaat çukuruna düşmesine ve yaralanmasına neden olduğunu ileri sürdü.


Mütalaaya göre olayda bir polisin parmağı kırılmış, diğerleri ise basit tıbbi müdahaleyle giderilebilecek ölçüde yaralanmışlardı. 


Savcı, öğrencilerin 2911 sayılı Toplantı ve Gösteri Yürüyüşleri Kanunu'nun 32. Maddesinde yer alan direnme suçunun yanı sıra Türk Ceza Kanunu'nun 265, 86 ve 87. Maddelerindeki görevi yaptırmamak için direnme, kasten yaralama ve neticesi sebebiyle ağırlaşmış yaralama suçlarından cezalandırılmasını istedi.


Öğrenciler ise suçlamaları reddetti. Daha önceki savunmalarında da öğrenciler, polislerin kendilerini çember içine aldığını ve sıkışıklık nedeniyle nefes alamadıklarını anlatmışlardı.


Avukatlar: "Polislerin sağlık raporları çelişkili"


Duruşmada öğrencilerin avukatı Özge Durdu, müşteki polis amiri Mustafa Ermenek'in sağlık raporları arasında çelişki bulunduğunu ileri sürdü.


Durdu, ilk sağlık raporunda herhangi bir yaralanma tespit edilmemesine rağmen sonraki raporda Ermenek'in basit tıbbi müdahaleyle giderilebilecek şekilde yaralandığının belirtildiğine dikkat çekti.


Ermenek'in dosyasında 26 Haziran 2026 tarihli bir fizik tedavi raporu da bulunduğunu hatırlatan Durdu, raporların birbirini doğrulamadığını savundu.


Öğrencilerin avukatlarından Gamze Serin Şimşek de bu çelişkileri ayrıntılı savunmalarında ele alacaklarını söyledi.


Mahkeme, avukatlara mütalaaya karşı savunmalarını hazırlamaları için süre vererek duruşmayı 11 Ocak 2027 saat 09.30'a erteledi.


6 öğrenci tutuklanmıştı


Dava, çocuk yaşta evliliği meşrulaştıran

açıklamalarıyla

 tepki çeken ilahiyatçı Nurettin Yıldız'ın 13 Mayıs 2025'te Boğaziçi Üniversitesi'ne konuşmacı olarak davet edilmesi üzerine başlayan protestolarla ilgili.


Öğrenciler üniversitede basın açıklaması yapmak isterken polis müdahalesiyle karşılaşmış, 14 öğrenci ve protestoyu izleyen T24 muhabiri gazeteci Can Öztürk gözaltına alınmıştı.


Öğrencilerden 6'sı olaydan hemen sonra tutuklanmış, 8'i adli kontrolle serbest bırakılmıştı.


Boğaziçi'nde 'Nureddin Yıldız'ı protesto eden 6 genç tutuklandı


14 Mayıs 2025


Tutuklu öğrenciler de daha sonra tahliye edildi.


Dava sürerken polislerin şikâyetleri üzerine açılan ikinci dosyanın ilk davayla birleştirilmesi sonucunda öğrenciler yeniden savunma vermek zorunda kalmışlardı.


(AEK)

author: Natalia Viana
title: EXCLUSIVO: Eduardo Bolsonaro abriu empresa no Bahrein com passaporte italiano
content:
Em 30 de janeiro deste ano, Eduardo Bolsonaro postou uma foto com o Príncipe Herdeiro e Primeiro-Ministro do Reino do Bahrein, Sheik Salman bin Hamad Al Khalifa, ao lado do seu irmão, o candidato à presidência Flávio Bolsonaro (PL). Ambos apareciam vestidos nos trajes tradicionais do país. “No mundo árabe, a

candora

 é o equivalente ao terno e gravata. Vestir a roupa tradicional é mais do que estilo, é respeito. Diplomacia se faz com gestos. E gestos constroem confiança, proximidade e resultados reais para Bahrein e Brasil”, escreveu Eduardo, que tem pretensões de assumir o Ministério de Relações Exteriores se seu irmão vencer as eleições no próximo domingo.


Eduardo participava da comitiva oficial do candidato ao lado de Paulo Figueiredo e dos deputados federais Paulo Bilynskyj (PL-SP) e Rodrigo Valadares (União Brasil-SE). A viagem incluiu uma visita ao palácio e um festival de corridas de cavalos promovido pela monarquia.


Mas o que Eduardo não mencionou no post do Instagram é que ele mantinha uma relação bem mais firme com o país.


Uma investigação da

Agência Pública

 constatou que ele manteve uma empresa no Bahrein para realizar atividades de consultoria em gestão. Aberta em 19 de setembro de 2024, a The Next Level LLC funcionou oficialmente por pouco mais de um ano e teve suas atividades encerradas em setembro do ano passado por não ter renovado o registro de companhia limitada. O capital inicial era de cerca de R$ 130 mil.


Um detalhe chama a atenção: o irmão do candidato presidencial Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) registrou a empresa como cidadão italiano. Tanto Eduardo quanto seu irmão Carlos possuem passaporte italiano, fruto dos antepassados dos Bolsonaro na cidade de Anguillara Veneta, no norte do país.


A informação pode ampliar controvérsias em torno do lobby de Eduardo para gerir o Itamaraty e liderar a diplomacia brasileira. E abre dúvidas se ele não teria aberto empresas em outros países como cidadão italiano e não brasileiro.


Eduardo Nantes Bolsonaro, cujo nome, em árabe, aparece

no Portal de Registro Comercial (SIJILAT)

 no Bahrein como ورانوسلوب ستنان ودراودإ, não respondeu aos questionamentos da

Agência Pública

 sobre qual era a finalidade da empresa.


Mas ela foi aberta exatamente no mesmo período em que ele e o irmão Flávio buscavam fundos para viabilizar a realização do filme “Dark Horse”, cinebiografia de Jair Bolsonaro, que recebeu aporte de US$ 13 milhões do banqueiro Daniel Vorcaro. Foi em dezembro de 2024 que Flávio conheceu Daniel Vorcaro em uma reunião online, e nos meses seguintes, até meados de 2025, Fabiano Zettel passou a coordenar o repasse dos valores em parcelas de cerca de US$ 2 milhões. Foi um período de grande mobilização para buscar apoio para o projeto familiar.


Em maio deste ano, o deputado federal Mário Frias Filho (PL-SP), produtor do filme e detentor dos direitos sobre a história de vida de Bolsonaro – como

revelou

 a

Pública

 – acompanhou Eduardo em uma nova viagem até o Bahrein. Realizada entre 12 e 18 de maio, segundo Mário Fias, a visita ocorreu a convite do Conselho de Desenvolvimento Econômico do país (EDB, na sigla em inglês).


Jornalismo investigativo é antídoto contra a desinformação. Ajude a garantir informação acessível e gratuita para mais pessoas. Faça um Pix para

contato@apublica.org

 ou doe em

apoie.apublica.org

.


Segundo levantamento da jornalista Juliana Dal Piva na sua

coluna

 no ICL Notícias, Eduardo Bolsonaro esteve ao menos nove vezes no Bahrein desde 2019. Quatro destas viagens ocorreram durante o governo de Jair Bolsonaro. Depois disso, outras três coincidiram com momentos de pressão judicial do STF contra o ex-deputado federal.


A mais recente ocorreu em 8 de outubro, entre o primeiro e o segundo turno das eleições. Ele voltou a visitar o palácio e a se encontrar com o Sheikh Salman bin Hamad Al Khalifa, além do ministro de economia e finanças, para discutir cooperação econômica e comercial. 


As fotos foram feitas no mesmo dia em que o ministro do STF Alexandre de Moraes decretou sua prisão pelo crime de coação no curso do processo, devido ao lobby realizado junto ao governo Trump por retaliações contra o Brasil. Alexandre mandou ainda cancelar os passaportes de Eduardo. 


O ex-deputado, foragido da justiça brasileira, usou seu passaporte italiano para entrar no país e postou vídeos xingando o ministro do STF e passeando pelo aeroporto do Bahrein e dos EUA livremente.

author: The Canadian Press
title: Atikamekw baby to be reburied in home community more than 70 years after death
content:
More than 70 years after his death, an Atikamekw baby buried far from his family in Quebec City will be laid to rest in his home community.


After 12 years of searching, the family of Maxime Ottawa has located his burial site, exhumed his remains and confirmed his identity, bringing what relatives describe as “immense relief.”


“On Oct. 26, 2026, Baby Maxime will finally come home to Manawan, to his mother and father, to his brothers and sisters,” his niece, Manon Ottawa, said Thursday at a news conference in Montreal.


Maxime was the brother of her father, Henri Ottawa, whose wish to find out what happened to the child prompted her to begin searching in 2014.


Manawan is an Atikamekw community located about 250 kilometres north of Montreal.


In 1954, when Maxime was just six months old, he was taken from Manawan to La Tuque, Que., for medical treatment without his parents.


He was later transferred to Quebec City without his family being informed. He died on Oct. 5, 1954, after 43 days in the hospital, without his loved ones having the chance to see him one last time.


His parents only learned of his death two years later and were unable to hold a funeral or bury him according to their traditions and beliefs.


“In 2014, four years after the death of my father Henri, I began searching, according to his wishes, to find my uncle,” Ottawa told reporters.


“I wanted to understand what had happened to him … I wanted to know the truth.”


The family’s search eventually led them to Saint-Charles Cemetery in Quebec City, where Maxime had been buried.


In October 2025, Quebec Superior Court authorized the exhumation of his remains so that forensic testing could confirm his identity and, if successful, allow him to be reburied in Manawan.


The exhumation proved particularly complex.


Read More: 


Quebec’s special advisor on ‘ghost babies’ expects number of missing children to rise 


Cemetery records indicate Maxime was buried in a plot containing five people, while the two neighbouring plots contained four and five people, respectively, all of them Indigenous.


One body was eventually exhumed and transferred to Quebec’s forensic laboratory for identification testing.


Nearly a year later, on Sept. 30, Canada’s National Day for Truth and Reconciliation, the family received confirmation that the remains belonged to Maxime Ottawa.


“Receiving this confirmation precisely on the National Day for Truth and Reconciliation gave it an even deeper meaning in our story,” Manon Ottawa said.


She added that reconciliation goes beyond words and requires seeking truth and respecting the dignity of families.


Maxime’s story is one of several involving Indigenous children who disappeared or died after being sent to Quebec hospitals decades ago, leaving families searching for answers.


In 2020, First Nation leaders called for separate legislation to help families access medical records and religious archives to learn what happened to their children. The province passed a law the following year allowing families to access certain records held by health institutions, government bodies and religious organizations.


Maxime’s remains are expected to return to Manawan on Monday, ahead of a reburial ceremony on Wednesday that will honour his memory and the traditions of his community.


In a statement Thursday, the family thanked those who helped bring Maxime home after decades of uncertainty.


“While their search for truth is coming to an end, the journey toward possible reconciliation can now begin,” the family said in a statement issued through their lawyer, Olivia Malenfant.


Story by Frédéric Lacroix-Couture

Atikamekw baby to be reburied in home community more than 70 years after death

APTN News

author: Bruno Fonseca
title: Flávio Bolsonaro turbina anúncios na Meta com suspeita de uso irregular de IA
content:
O candidato à presidência Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) aumentou — e muito — a quantidade de dinheiro gasto com impulsionamentos nas redes da Meta nessa reta final das eleições. A

Agência Pública

 apurou que

na última terça-feira, dia 20 de outubro, a campanha do bolsonarista veiculou mais de meio milhão de reais com anúncios nessas plataformas.


Nessa última cartada, a campanha também está apostando em anúncios micro direcionados para os eleitores — chegando a fazer vídeos direcionados para bairros específicos de quem mora na cidade de São Paulo.


Nessa outra leva de anúncios, todos veiculados em sequência entre ontem, 22 de outubro e hoje, 23 de outubro, o apresentador diz, ao lado de Flávio Bolsonaro, para:


“Você que mora em Higienópolis, é com você que que eu quero falar hoje”.


“Você que mora no Brooklin, é com você que que eu quero falar hoje”.


“Você que mora no Grajaú, é com você que que eu quero falar hoje”.


Ao todo, a reportagem contou ao menos 26 vídeos, cada um direcionado a um morador de bairro diferente de São Paulo.

 Em apenas um deles, o direcionado a moradores de Higienópolis, a campanha pagou mais de R$ 150 mil para impulsionar o conteúdo. O bairro, um dos mais caros da capital paulista, foi palco de uma manifestação pró-Flavio no último final de semana.


Os vídeos têm indícios de terem sido alterados por Inteligência Artificial, visto que o apresentador fala todas essas apresentações realizando o mesmo movimento — o que indicaria o uso desse tipo de ferramenta.

 A reportagem, contudo, não encontrou nenhum alerta feito pela campanha de que houve esse tipo de interferência, o que é previsto pelas regras do TSE.


Além disso, há um outro problema. As regras eleitorais proíbem impulsionamento de material eleitoral usando imagens de pessoas públicas ou candidatos alteradas por IA das 17h de quinta-feira, dia 22 de outubro, até o pós votação.


Como explica Cynthia Picolo, Diretora executiva do Laboratório de Políticas Públicas e Internet – LAPIN, “o TSE proíbe, nas 72 horas anteriores e nas 24 horas posteriores ao término da votação, a publicação, republicação ou impulsionamento de novos conteúdos produzidos ou alterados por IA que usem imagem, voz ou manifestação de candidatos ou pessoas públicas, mesmo quando o uso de IA estiver devidamente identificado”. As regras podem ser consultadas

aqui

.


A reportagem teve acesso à veiculação dessa propaganda na noite de quinta, ou seja, depois do período. A biblioteca de anúncios da Meta também indica que a propaganda foi veiculada até hoje, dia 23.

contato@apublica.org

 ou doe em

apoie.apublica.org

.


“O TSE permite determinados usos de IA na propaganda eleitoral. Desde que sejam respeitadas essas obrigações, essas restrições previstas nas próprias regulamentações do TSE. Já o deepfake na propaganda eleitoral é proibido, mesmo que haja identificação de conteúdo que foi gerado por IA. E essa decisão, inclusive, que proibiu o uso de deepfake é bem recente. O que a gente vê, de forma bem contraditória, é o uso massivo de conteúdo sintético, inclusive de imagem, voz, som”, complementa Picolo.


O TSE já havia se manifestado à

Pública

 de que “não se manifesta sobre casos concretos, que podem vir a ser objeto de análise pela Justiça Eleitoral”.


Reportagem

 do Intercept mostrou que a campanha de Flávio pagou R$ 600 mil para a empresa Elytron, que tem sistema que usa inteligência artificial para manipulação política em eleições.


A reportagem procurou a assessoria do candidato para se posicionar. O espaço segue aberto. A assessoria do apresentador também foi procurada.


Flavio abre bolso para propagandas na Meta


O gasto recente de Flávio na Meta é surpreendente até para os padrões da própria campanha.

Em comparação, quando se pega todo o período eleitoral, desde 4 de agosto, a Meta já veiculou R$ 8,5 milhões de anúncios da campanha do bolsonarista. Isso dá uma média de R$ 110 mil por dia.

 Nesta reta final, com o aumento dos gastos, a campanha do bolsonarista está pagando quase cinco vezes esse valor por dia.


Os dados sobre valores pagos para anúncios que a

Meta

 divulga vão sendo atualizados diariamente. Eles são diferentes do que o Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE) apresenta, que são atualizados de acordo com a prestação de contas de cada campanha. Esses dados também mostram um aumento de …

author: Marcelo Oliveira
title: Justiça eleitoral muda até 4 vezes ao dia local de votação às vésperas do 2° turno
content:
Na última semana, o número de seções de votação alteradas pelos Tribunais Regionais Eleitorais (TREs) entre o primeiro e o segundo turno mudou drasticamente. No dia 17 de outubro, eram

4352 alterações

 de seção eleitoral. No dia 19, o número caiu para

2033 seções alteradas

. No dia 20, um levantamento feito pela

Agência Pública

 contou 453 alterações em 22 estados. 


Nesta quinta-feira, 22, às 11h27, eram 300 as seções alteradas e, às 15h25, passaram a 314 as modificações. Sim, as mudanças podem ocorrer de 4 em 4 horas e são anunciadas, em turnos, no

sistema de informações eleitorais

 do site do Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE).  


A

Pública

 comparou nos últimos dois dias, as seções de votação cuja alteração estava prevista na tabela do TSE no dia 20 de outubro, com o número de votos obtidos, nessas urnas, pelos dois candidatos que avançaram para o segundo turno da eleição presidencial: Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) e Lula (PT). 


Nas 453 seções cuja alteração estava prevista, Lula venceu em 249, Bolsonaro em 202 e em duas houve empate. Em números absolutos, o presidente Lula recebeu 51.890 votos nessas seções e o adversário, 43.282. A abstenção foi semelhante à apurada nacionalmente, que chegou a 21,08%: 29.311 eleitores deixaram de comparecer às urnas (21,59% do total). 


As 453 seções, juntas, têm apenas 135.742 eleitores, 0,08% do total. Pouco diante dos 158,7 milhões de eleitores do país, mas pode ser muito em um cenário em que os dois candidatos estão em

empate técnico

 na maior parte das pesquisas eleitorais. 


Na nota mais recente no site do TSE sobre o assunto,

publicada na quinta-feira,

 a corte se exime do problema e diz que exigiu dos TREs o preenchimento de um formulário para informar as mudanças e que o TSE “não solicita” as alterações, definidas pelos TREs em virtude de questões climáticas, problemas na estrutura dos prédios e para garantir a segurança de eleitoras e eleitores. 


No início desta semana, o Colégio de Presidentes dos Tribunais Regionais Eleitorais divulgou um

comunicado

 em que se comprometeu a manter o eleitorado informado sobre os locais de votação do 2º turno das Eleições 2026. 


De acordo com os dados da quinta-feira, 22 de outubro, , divulgados às 15h45, o TRE de Minas Gerais liderava as alterações, com 50 seções modificadas de local em diferentes partes do Estado (eram 119 no dia 20). Em segundo, estava o Pará, com 32, e em terceiro o Piauí, com 29 mudanças. O número de estados afetados caiu de 22 para 20 nos últimos dois dias. 


São Paulo é o quarto estado com mais mudanças. Na última terça-feira, dia 20,  eram 31 seções alteradas. Na pesquisa de quinta-feira à tarde, 22, eram 27 alterações, entretanto, três seções tinham sido trocadas. Elas estavam localizadas na EMEI Lourdes Heredia, e passaram para a CEI Indir Jabaquara, ambas localizadas na região do Jabaquara, na capital paulista.

contato@apublica.org

 ou doe em

apoie.apublica.org

.


Más condições de escola e problema climático


Uma das principais mudanças em São Paulo foi a substituição da Escola Estadual Conselheiro Ruy Barbosa pelo Recanto Nossa Senhora de Lourdes, no Horto Florestal, com 12 seções no endereço. Em entrevista à CBN, alunos da escola contaram que o espaço alaga completamente em caso de chuva, o que pode danificar as urnas eletrônicas. 


Na cidade de Confresa, no Mato Grosso, por exemplo, fortes chuvas e ventos danificaram a cobertura de uma escola utilizada como local de votação. Após uma avaliação técnica, o imóvel foi interditado preventivamente, e as oito seções eleitorais que funcionavam no local precisaram ser transferidas.


Em Santa Catarina, circulou a informação que 65 locais de votação foram alterados. As mudanças ocorreram antes do primeiro turno devido a questões emergenciais, como problemas de estrutura e clima. A informação continuou circulando e, para o segundo turno, o TRE local teve que esclarecer que as mudanças do primeiro turno estavam mantidas para o segundo. 


Como saber se o local de votação mudou?


Para checar se o seu local de votação mudou, o TSE recomenda duas opções: consulta no aplicativo

e-Título

 ou no menu

Autoatendimento Eleitoral

 do Portal do TSE, na aba onde votar. Segundo o TSE, as alterações realizadas pelos TREs têm reflexo imediato nesses canais oficiais. 


Caso opte pelo autoatendimento …

author: Nicole Santos
title: Política e monetização: como ativistas se tornam alvo de violência dentro e fora das redes
content:
Os perfis nas redes sociais do jornalista e comunicador popular Mateus Fernandes, de 26 anos, sempre articularam debates sobre raça, meio ambiente e participação política a partir da periferia de São Paulo. A decisão de declarar o voto no presidente Lula no segundo turno das eleições custou a liberdade e tranquilidade de Mateus. Conhecido nas redes como

@omateuso

, seu perfil divulgou uma

nota

 pública no dia 12 de outubro informando que ele havia recebido oito ameaças de morte e tortura, com referências à Ku Klux Klan e saudações nazistas. Além disso, seu endereço residencial foi exposto em comentários no Facebook, o que motivou o jornalista a sair de casa por medo de ser assassinado.  


As ameaças surgiram após a participação de Mateus na campanha de “vira-voto” com centenas de criadores de conteúdo. Sem respostas efetivas às denúncias enviadas à Meta, Mateus e sua equipe jurídica de apoio registraram boletim de ocorrência por racismo, apologia ao nazismo, intolerância religiosa e ameaça. Também levou o caso ao Ministério Público de São Paulo (MP-SP) e à Polícia Civil.


O caso de Mateus não é isolado. Ele se soma a episódios de intimidação contra parlamentares e agentes políticos registrados em diferentes estados durante o período eleitoral.

Os dados após o primeiro turno confirmaram o diagnóstico: segundo levantamento da organização de Direitos Humanos Terra de Direitos e da Justiça Global, divulgado no dia 7 de outubro, o Brasil registrou 134 episódios de violência política em 50 dias de campanha, uma média de um caso a cada nove horas.


Segundo a pesquisa, dos 134 episódios registrados no primeiro turno, 102 foram dirigidos a pessoas com candidaturas registradas, o que equivale a 76,1% do total. Os outros 32 casos atingiram quem não disputava eleições: foram vítimas 19 vereadores, 3 prefeitos, um vice-prefeito e dois secretários. Também houve quatro casos contra dirigentes partidários e dois contra sedes do PT e a equipe de uma candidata.  


Um exemplo foi da deputada federal eleita com a melhor votação de Minas Gerais, Ana Elisa (PT-MG), de 21 anos, a mulher mais jovem da história do país e assumir uma cadeira na Câmara dos Deputados. Logo após a confirmação do resultado das urnas, ela passou a ser alvo de perseguição e ameaças de morte.


No Amazonas, a deputada estadual e candidata a vice-governadora Alessandra Campêlo (PSD) denunciou ter sido ameaçada durante um debate eleitoral promovido pela TV Norte Amazonas. Alessandra disputa o segundo turno ao Governo do Estado ao lado de Omar Aziz (PSD) contra a chapa da Professora Maria do Carmo (PL). 


Um homem da coligação adversária foi flagrado, nos bastidores, fazendo um gesto de degolamento enquanto a encarava. Tratava-se de Kidson Maia, que buscou uma vaga de deputado estadual no Amazonas, mas não foi eleito, ficando como 1° suplente.

Segundo o portal G1

, Alessandra apresentou uma representação criminal e, com isso, a juíza eleitoral Bárbara Folhadela Paulain determinou que Kidson e o deputado federal eleito Sargento Salazar (PL) mantenham distância mínima de 200 metros da parlamentar, proibiu qualquer tipo de contato e suspendeu o porte de armas da dupla. A

Agência Pública

 solicitou um posicionamento do Tribunal Regional Eleitoral do Amazonas mas não obteve retorno até o fechamento desta reportagem. O espaço segue aberto.


Além de candidatas, minorias políticas tornam-se alvo


A violência política segue um padrão na escolha das vítimas: atingem sobretudo pessoas negras, mulheres, populações periféricas, entre outros grupos marginalizados que ocupam o debate público. Em setembro, uma articulação de quase 70 organizações da sociedade civil (entre elas o

Instituto Marielle Franco

,

Terra de Direitos

,

Justiça Global

,

Articulação de Mulheres Negras Brasileiras

author: Joe Mullin
title: Two States Can Now Restrict Social Media Access—Here’s What To Do Next
content:
Last week, two federal appeals courts

issued


opinions

 that will allow Florida and Georgia to start enforcing laws that will age-gate and block young people from accessing social media. The laws do not adequately respect minors’ rights to play, speak, and learn online. More fundamentally, these laws don’t help young people stay safe online—a goal that lawmakers should pursue.


Age-Gated? Email EFF at

agegates@eff.org

. 


Because of the new laws, some young people will lose their ability to access lawful information, find their online communities, and even engage with school board members. Others will need parental permission to stay online. And adults will face increased demands to prove their age, which will put their privacy at increased risk simply to continue to use the services they already use. 


We

opposed

 these laws because they threaten the free expression and privacy of both minors and adults.  Even though these lawsuits are not over, the injunctions that paused enforcement have been lifted, and the states of Florida and Georgia will now be able to enforce broad restrictions on social media use. 


The restrictions that these states will start enforcing are a setback for the rights of all internet users, but they are not written in stone. That’s why EFF is encouraging internet users - and particularly young people – to start keeping a record of how they are affected. If you are a teenager who loses access to an online discussion, can’t participate in a political campaign, or stop seeking information because you don’t want to upload personal information, document what happened. The same is true for adults who may be mistakenly blocked by age checks, and parents who may encounter obstacles to authorizing their children's use of online services. These experiences matter. They can help us show courts, policymakers, and the public what government restrictions on online expression actually cost the people who live under them. 


Hopefully, with enough proof of the expressive harms these laws cause, we can push lawmakers to rescind them. That’s why we’re encouraging folks to reach out to EFF once they’ve documented these harms. You can write to us about this issue at the email address

agegates@eff.org

. 


The Decisions


These two opinions, issued by the same panel from the U.S. Court of Appeals for the 11th Circuit, allow Florida and Georgia to enforce restrictions on social media accounts for people under 16 years old. The requirements differ by state. 


In

Florida

,

 the judges allowed that state’s

H.B. 3

 to move forward, which requires covered platforms to ban anyone under 14 from opening or keeping accounts—even with parental permission. Teenagers who are 14 or 15 can have accounts only with parental consent. To be covered, a platform has to use algorithms, allow content uploads or the viewing of other peoples’ content, and have at least one feature on a list of features the state considers bad, including livestreaming, engagement metrics, autoplay, infinite scrolling, or push notifications. These requirements effectively apply to every major social media service that young people use.


To the extent there is a silver lining in the ruling on Florida’s law, it’s that the panel recognized that H.B. 3 targets expression protected by the First Amendment. The problem is that the ruling uncritically accepts the idea that a social media service is addictive in a clinical sense, even if just 10% of users under 16 are using the platform for two or more hours per day (the standard set in H.B. 3). The court simply accepts that time spent online is a proxy for harm. The bill doesn’t distinguish doomscrolling or compulsive use from organizing a campaign, making art, or talking with friends. 


In

Georgia

,

S.B. 351

 can now be enforced. That law requires parental consent for anyone under 16 to hold an account on social media platforms. It also requires platforms to make “commercially reasonable efforts” to check users’ ages, which creates a hurdle for adults as well as under-16s. 


The ruling acknowledges that S.B. 351 “overwhelmingly applies to platforms that overwhelmingly host protected speech.” But the ruling faults the plaintiffs for not being able to show that “invalid applications substantially outweigh the valid ones.” That asks the groups challenging the law to meet a virtually impossible standard—to make their case, they would have to measure and evaluate the content hosted by all …

author: Amy Goodman
title: At Least 59 People Have Died in ICE Custody Since Start of Trump’s Second Term
content:
Meanwhile, the GEO Group announced that DHS purchased two immigration jails in Adelanto, California, for $950 million.

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

At least 59 people have died in ICE custody since the start of President Donald Trump’s second term, the highest number in more than a decade. Many deaths have been linked to medical neglect, including four of five recent deaths at California’s Adelanto Processing Center, according to a 2026 report by the state attorney general. Al Jazeera English’s Fault Lines investigated deaths at the facility, which is operated by the private prison company GEO Group, in the new documentary Dying in Detention.

“GEO Group has made over a billion dollars in profits from immigration detention. They have given more than a million dollars … to help reelect Donald Trump,” says correspondent Natasha Del Toro. “That raises a lot of questions for us about the relationship between GEO and the federal government, and some of these conflicts of interest.”

This is a rush transcript. Copy may not be in its final form.

author: Julius Gavroche
title: Giorgio Agamben: Hope and desire
content:
Evelyn De Morgan, “Hope in a Prison of Despair”, 1887


Our condition, in terms of hope and desire, resembles that of those who, in Dante’s

Divine Comedy

, remain suspended in Limbo and who, in Virgil’s words, desire without any longer hoping (

sanza speme vivemo in disio

). We too, like the inhabitants of Limbo, are suspended between desire and hope: we have lost hope in a better world and yet we continue to desire it in vain and cannot do without it. To emerge from this liminal state, we must direct our hope not towards a good that we lack and wish to possess, but towards that which we already possess, the good that lies within us, so that it may remain alive and give us life. And if faith is, in the words of the Apostle, the assurance of things hoped for [cf.

Hebrews

 11:1], these things are present within us and before us, and the desire for a good in which we believe is always already fulfilled. Hope in what we have is, therefore, a special form of memory, which is not limited to recalling a past good, but which ceaselessly works to ensure that it remains present and alive. And this transformation of hope into memory is thought, the life of the mind.


Quodlibet

, 20/10/2026

author: Julius Gavroche
title: Ian Alan Paul: The Disorder of Things
content:
from

Ill Will

, 22/10/2026


On the final pages of his

Republic

, Plato presents us with the image of a perfect, total order that no earthly city could ever achieve. Ian Alan Paul’s “The Disorder of Things” begins where Plato’s text leaves off. Yet far from an indictment of earthly life, Paul argues that the imperfection highlighted by Plato does not mark the failure of order but serves as its condition of possibility. This is true existentially as it is politically: just as existence has no essence, no intrinsic form or foundation, political orders operate by ordering a disorder they can never fully extinguish. The state, capital, algorithmic control societies: as these orders attempt to ward off their own inevitable death, they give shape to an increasingly dying world, from ecological collapse to genocide to ever-intensifying security. The task of contemporary political insurgency is to bring about the death of this order.


Order is thus something different than form, which has an anarchic plasticity to it. Anarchy, for Paul, refers to a constitutive non-coincidence of life with itself that serves as the ground of our autonomy, one which order seeks at once to appropriate and to suppress. Whereas order fixes hierarchies among forms, deciding thereby which lives are permissible and which disposable, the form-giving anarchy of existence remains irreducible to it. The choice we now face, he concludes, is between anarchy or death, and Atropos, the Fate who severs the thread, must orient us.


“The sea is not less beautiful in our eyes because we know that sometimes ships are wrecked by it.”


Simone Weil


“Is not philosophy the practice of death?”


Plato


In the very last passages of the last book of Plato’s

Republic

, the three fates [

moirai, ?????

] appear, the sisters who together determine the destiny of all living things beyond even the will of the gods. Clotho spins threads so as to begin each life, Lachesis measures threads so as to give each life its length, and the third and final sister Atropos decides where and in what manner each thread and life are destined to end. While most of the

Republic

 concerns the political and economic order of the city state, an order which must strategically counter the various forms of disorder that persistently threaten to undermine and undo it, the fates stand apart as figures of a divine order within which no dissension or desertion is possible, an order that is so comprehensive that no distance remains between its rule and what it rules over. The order of the fates is thus the order that the many autocrats, bureaucrats, and technocrats of our time can only dream of, an order which is imposed upon all things exhaustively and in perpetuity, an orderwithout disorder.


While the divine order of the fates is total, flawless, and eternal, the earthly order of the city-state, in contrast, always remains only partial, deficient, and contingent, relentlessly at risk of eroding, collapsing, or being usurped by another, indefinitely having to fend off the possibility of an insurrection, plague, war, or famine that could decisively wash it away and bring it to its end, as all things on Earth inevitably are. The fates thus appear at the conclusion of the

Republic

 as an image of a harmonious and perfected order that cannot possibly be realized on such a discordant and imperfect Earth. But in the end, this lack of perfection doesn’t make order unattainable in the city-state or any other place, but rather proves to be its very condition of possibility, as all police and politicians already know so well when they survey the disarray of the populations they rule over and see not the limits of their order but its very material. Order does not arise from the elimination of disorder, as if order and disorder were precisely counterbalanced and zero-sum. Order rather arises always as

an ordering of the disordered Earth

. It is disorder itself that order ultimately takes to be its object, a disorder which can never finally be extinguished or neutralized, but which can be guided and shaped, managed and adjusted, even if it must be so indefinitely, without any hope of conclusion or end.


If our existence has an essence, it is disorder. Which is to say that its only essence is its lack of essence, that there is no order which is intrinsic to life or to the Earth. As a consequence, whatever order happens to historically arise does so only at the expense of great amounts of …

author: Unknown
title: IFJ passes motion in support of press freedom and against censorship in Turkey
content:
At its online meeting on 19 and 20 October 2026, the Executive Committee of the International Federation of Journalists (IFJ) unanimously passed a motion expressing solidarity with journalists, trade unions, and professional organisations in Turkey in their fight against censorship, intimidation and the criminalisation of journalism. The European Federation of Journalists (EFJ) also supported the motion.


Considering:


The increasing repression of independent journalism in Turkey, including the detention and prosecution of journalists, restrictions on media outlets, the appointment of government-appointed trustees to media organisations and the blocking of journalists’ social media accounts;


The fundamental right of journalists to report freely, investigate matters of public interest and hold those in power accountable, without intimidation, censorship or criminal prosecution for their legitimate professional activities;


The joint call by Turkish journalists’ professional organisations for nationwide demonstrations on 24 October 2026, marking the first anniversary of the appointment of a trustee to TELE 1;


Resolves:


First:

 To express its full solidarity with journalists, their trade unions and professional organisations in Turkey in their struggle against censorship, intimidation and the criminalisation of journalism.


Second:

 To strongly condemn all forms of repression targeting independent media and to demand the release of journalists detained solely for carrying out their professional duties.


Third: 

To support the nationwide mobilisation organised by Turkish journalists’ organisations on 24 October 2026 and their legitimate demands for press freedom, editorial independence and the public’s right to information.


Fourth:

 To urge the Turkish authorities to respect their international obligations concerning freedom of expression and press freedom, and to put an end to judicial harassment, arbitrary restrictions and political interference in the media.


The IFJ Executive Committee reaffirms that journalism is not a crime, press freedom is not negotiable, and the public’s right to know must never be denied.

author: Unknown
title: Öcalan’s book ‘Manifesto of the Democratic Communal Society’ banned in prison
content:
The administration of Siverek No. 1 T-Type Closed Prison in Urfa has prohibited political prisoner Tacittin Kalgı from receiving the book

Manifesto of the Democratic Communal Society

. The decision was justified on the grounds that the book allegedly contains material posing a threat to security. DEM Party MP Newroz Uysal Aslan has therefore appealed to the Human Rights Commission of the Turkish Parliament, calling for an investigation into the ban.


The measure is based on a decision issued by the prison administration on October 8, under file number 2026/390. The decision specifically objects to passages addressing the historical and political dimensions of the Kurdish question, Abdullah Öcalan’s ideas, the history of the Kurdish movement, and the paradigm of a democratic society.


The prison’s Education Board maintains that the book damages the reputation of the state, contains terrorist propaganda, and could incite hatred and hostility.


Even Öcalan’s call for peace is deemed objectionable


In her petition, Uysal Aslan pointed out that even passages concerning Öcalan’s February 27, 2025, Call for Peace and Democratic Society were deemed objectionable. The book addresses, among other issues, the transition from armed struggle to democratic politics and perspectives on coexistence within society.


“Banning this content on the basis of a security-oriented assessment contradicts the ongoing Peace and Democratic Society Process,” Uysal stated.


The MP also emphasized that expressing dissenting political views and criticizing state policies do not, in themselves, constitute sufficient grounds for banning a publication. Furthermore, she said, the prison administration had failed to adequately explain what specific threat the book allegedly posed to the security and order of the prison.


Similar bans in other prisons


Uysal Aslan cited Articles 25 and 26 of the Turkish Constitution, which guarantee freedom of thought and expression, as well as Article 62 of Law No. 5275 on the Execution of Sentences and Security Measures, which regulates prisoners’ access to publications. She also referred to a ruling by the Turkish Constitutional Court that found the denial of access to publications for prisoners to constitute a violation of their rights.


The case in Siverek does not appear to be an isolated incident. Political prisoner Ihsan Kartal, held in Tekirdağ No. 1 F-Type Prison, was also denied access to the same book. Uysal Aslan further called for an investigation into restrictions on access to similar publications affecting Metin Yamalak, who is imprisoned in Bolu F-Type Prison.


The MP urged the parliamentary Human Rights Commission to review the prison administration’s decision, request information from the Ministry of Justice, and initiate measures to protect prisoners’ right to access publications. She also called for an investigation into similar bans in other prisons.

author: Dottie Rosenbaum
title: SNAP Participation Losses Far Exceed CBO’s Estimates
content:
About 5.5 million people lost food assistance through SNAP in the year since enactment of the 2025 reconciliation law.

Truthout is an indispensable resource for activists, movement leaders and workers everywhere. Please make this work possible with a quick donation.

About 5.5 million people lost food assistance through SNAP in the year since enactment of the 2025 reconciliation law. This includes about 2 million children, who were not targeted by the law’s eligibility restrictions.

These participation declines have resulted in a sharp drop in SNAP spending, since 90 percent of SNAP spending is for food assistance benefits. (The rest is primarily administrative expenses and Puerto Rico’s nutrition assistance block grant.)

SNAP spending in fiscal year 2026, which ended September 30, was nearly $11 billion lower than the prior year (-10.3 percent). Along with the 5.5 million people who have less money to purchase groceries, this also means people in communities across the U.S. had about $11 billion less for spending on food in fiscal year 2026.

The drop in SNAP participation and spending is considerably more than the Congressional Budget Office (CBO) predicted. The latest U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) data for July 2026 show that monthly SNAP participation in fiscal year 2026 is on track to average about 4.5 million fewer people compared to the average month in fiscal year 2025 — far greater than CBO’s prediction of 2.8 million fewer people in an average month in 2026 versus 2025. (See chart.) CBO projected that SNAP outlays would drop by about $6 billion in 2026; in actuality SNAP outlays dropped by nearly double that amount.

The most likely reason for the larger-than-expected cut is the impact of the 2025 reconciliation law shifting enormous new SNAP costs to states, which they owe starting in fiscal year 2028. CBO estimated the cost shift mandate would have no impact until 2028. But it has already led many states to erect barriers to people’s SNAP participation, such as more paperwork and other requirements that states often don’t have the staff to administer.

The reconciliation law granted a few states a two-year delay for this harmful cost shift. Congress should extend the delay to all states before the end of the year, given SNAP losses outpacing predictions and the high cost of groceries and other basic needs. CBO estimated the reconciliation law would cut SNAP by $187 billion (about 20 percent) through 2034, the largest SNAP cut in history. With far steeper cuts evident in fiscal year 2026, Congress should not further cut SNAP to offset the cost of a delay in the cost shift.

In its most recent February 2026 baseline, CBO projected that 39.3 million people would participate in SNAP in an average month of 2026, compared to about 42.1 million in 2025. But just shy of 36.1 million people participated in SNAP in July 2026, according to the most recent data from USDA, suggesting that fiscal year 2026 participation will average about 37.6 million people, or about 4.5 million below last year’s average.

SNAP spending was also substantially lower than CBO’s forecast. CBO’s most recent baseline assumed a 6 percent drop in SNAP spending between fiscal years 2025 and 2026. But SNAP spending for the fiscal year was more than 10 percent, or nearly $11 billion, lower than it was in 2025.

The outsized drops suggest that people not ostensibly targeted by the 2025 reconciliation law’s eligibility restrictions are losing SNAP anyway. That includes many children, seniors, and people with disabilities, yet another reason for Congress to delay the cost shift.

At the time of the reconciliation law’s enactment, CBPP explained that, based on CBO’s estimate, once the law had fully taken effect about 4 million people would be cut from SNAP entirely or lose a substantial amount of their benefits. Now, with nearly a year of USDA data since the law’s enactment, more than 5.5 million fewer people receive any SNAP. That figure does not include people whose benefits are lower as a result of the new law. More losses are almost certain as the law continues to phase in.

That the losses are coming faster than CBO predicted is likely in large part because CBO’s original estimates did not factor in any effects of the state cost shift mandate until 2028. This is when the law requires states will to start paying for a share of SNAP benefits — 5 to 15 percent of them, potentially hundreds of millions of dollars for many states and …

author: 张皓翔
title: The Dislocation of Vendémiaire (IV): The Misrecognized Socialism and the Resisters Who Refuse Connection 【葡月的错位（四）被误认的社会主义与拒绝联结的抗争者】 【A commentary on the French riots between September and October】
content:
This essay is the fourth part of The Dislocation of Vendémiaire. Drawing on Karl Marx's famous "sack of potatoes" metaphor from 1851, it contrasts the historical inability of the French peasantry to unite with the contemporary resisters of the 2026 French/European movements who actively "refuse connection." The author argues that while previous struggles centered on physiological survival, modern struggles have shifted to the realm of existential subjectivity—the refusal to be treated as mere interchangeable parts ("elementalization") within social machinery. The essay re-examines the Soviet experience, arguing that it substituted market-based elementalization with a planned one, thereby creating a historical illusion that alienated modern resisters from political organizations. Ultimately, the text critiques the movement's decentralized, anti-party stance as "eating the child with the bathwater," arguing that without the vanguard, organization, and discipline, resisting a highly organized capitalist state machine is impossible.

author: Chris Walker
title: Todd Blanche Won’t Rule Out DOJ Disruption of Midterm Elections Certification
content:
Seven in 10 Americans don’t believe President Donald Trump will accept the midterm results.

Truthout is an indispensable resource for activists, movement leaders and workers everywhere. Please make this work possible with a quick donation.

Attorney General Todd Blanche told reporters on Thursday that he wouldn’t rule out the possibility of the Department of Justice (DOJ) refusing to allow states to certify their own election results in this year’s midterm races.

Blanche’s comments come as Americans are expressing deep skepticism that President Donald Trump will accept election outcomes if Republicans lose to Democrats.

According to the U.S. Constitution, states are the managers of elections, not the federal government. But the administration could attempt to dispute the election results by claiming widespread fraud had taken place, refusing to allow states to certify outcomes through extreme measures, including seizing ballots.

As Blanche was boarding a plane in Virginia, he was asked by reporters whether it was possible that the DOJ could disrupt the certification process after the midterms concluded. The attorney general said he wouldn’t rule out the idea.

“It is not DOJ’s intention to, and it’s never our intention to, improperly interfere with elections or the state confirmation process or certification process,” Blanche said, but added that he may feel compelled to do so in a “doomsday scenario.”

“To say that there’s no circumstances that we would ever do that …. of course, I’m not going to say that,” he elaborated.

The DOJ has already taken steps to purportedly root out fraud and ineligible voters in several states, despite evidence suggesting that claims of widespread fraud are unfounded.

There are reports that federal agents have started going door to door to search for supposed noncitizen voters, an action that could intimidate residents who are eligible to participate in the elections. The DOJ has also threatened state election officials, warning them of potential criminal prosecutions if they allow noncitizens to vote this November.

The administration’s claims have fallen apart under scrutiny — for example, a report the White House produced alleging that 24,000 noncitizens participated in the 2020 presidential election (which Trump lost) was deemed deeply flawed due to unusual methodology.

Polling has consistently demonstrated that Democrats are likely to win the House of Representatives in this year’s midterm races. The Democratic Party is also within reach of winning the Senate, some polls have suggested.

If Republicans lose to Democrats, most Americans have doubts that Trump will accept the results.

According to a Washington Post/ABC News/Ipsos poll published this week, only 28 percent of voters said they were “confident” Trump would accept the results of the midterms. Meanwhile, 70 percent said they were “not confident” that he would.

Trump has already indicated that he will only accept the results if he deems them “honest,” saying as much back in February. If he doesn’t believe they are honest, then “something else has to happen,” he said.

Truthout is one of only a few platforms for justice-oriented, grassroots journalism. Today, we face an existential threat.

Due to Google’s launch of AI search, we’ve seen a drastic plunge in our site traffic and, as a result, our revenue. We lost 15 percent of our readership overnight. This was a readership we painstakingly built over decades, and it vanished because Google chose corporate greed over a healthy democracy.

We are fundraising right now to meet our basic operating expenses. If you can support Truthout with a one-time or monthly donation, you will make a significant impact on our work. Anything you can do makes a difference — we appreciate your support.
